children.title: Finite Feature Approximations
children.top_down_role: Explicit finite-dimensional features approximating richer surrogate representations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Posterior computation after fixing a finite feature map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y=\Phi w+\epsilon\), where \(w\sim\mathcal N(0,I_m)\) and \(\epsilon\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2I_n)\). Then \(w\mid y\sim\mathcal N(\mu_w,\Sigma_w)\), where \[\Sigma_w=(I_m+\sigma^{-2}\Phi^\top\Phi)^{-1},\qquad \mu_w=\sigma^{-2}\Sigma_w\Phi^\top y.\] At \(x\), the latent predictive mean and variance are \(\phi(x)^\top\mu_w\) and \(\phi(x)^\top\Sigma_w\phi(x)\). Dense formation and factorization cost \(O(nm^2+m^3)\) time and \(O(nm+m^2)\) storage, or \(O(m^2)\) storage when sufficient statistics are accumulated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-feature Gaussian regression performs posterior inference through an m-dimensional Bayesian linear system.
assumptions_latex: Dense feature-space linear algebra is used.
knowledge_statements.title: Weight-Space Gaussian Regression

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-pair Monte Carlo approximation for normalized shift-invariant kernels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k(x,x')=\kappa(x-x')\) be a real normalized shift-invariant positive-semidefinite kernel. Its normalized spectral measure \(p\) satisfies \(\kappa(\delta)=\mathbb E_{\omega\sim p}[\cos(\omega^\top\delta)]\). For independent \(\omega_j\sim p\) and \(b_j\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,2\pi]\), define \(\phi_j(x)=\sqrt{2/m}\cos(\omega_j^\top x+b_j)\). Then \[\mathbb E[\phi(x)^\top\phi(x')]=k(x,x')\] and, for fixed \(x,x'\), \[\Pr\!\left(\left|\phi(x)^\top\phi(x')-k(x,x')\right|\ge\varepsilon\right)\le2e^{-m\varepsilon^2/8}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Random Fourier features are unbiased for a normalized stationary kernel and have a fixed-pair Hoeffding bound.
assumptions_latex: \(k\) is real, normalized, shift invariant, and positive semidefinite.
Frequencies and phases are mutually independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\phi(x)^\top\phi(x')]=k(x,x')\) with the displayed fixed-pair tail bound.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional feature representation of an approximate Gaussian process.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R^m\) satisfy \(\widetilde k(x,x')=\phi(x)^\top\phi(x')\). If \(w\sim\mathcal N(0,I_m)\) and \(\widetilde f(x)=\phi(x)^\top w\), then \[\mathbb E[\widetilde f(x)]=0,\qquad \operatorname{Cov}(\widetilde f(x),\widetilde f(x'))=\widetilde k(x,x').\] Thus replacing \(k\) by \(\widetilde k\) converts Gaussian-process inference into Bayesian linear inference in \(m\) features. On data \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), the approximate Gram matrix is \(\widetilde K=\Phi\Phi^\top\), where \(\Phi_{i:}=\phi(x_i)^\top\).

children.title: Approximation-Accuracy Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Predictive and uncertainty consequences of reducing computational complexity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage and dense arithmetic scaling for a rank-m covariance factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent an \(n\times n\) approximation as \(\widetilde K=UU^{\mathsf T}\), with \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\), and regularize by \(\lambda I\), \(\lambda>0\). Storing \(U\) costs \(O(nm)\); forming \(U^{\mathsf T}U\) costs \(O(nm^2)\); factoring the resulting \(m\times m\) system costs \(O(m^3)\); and a subsequent Woodbury solve costs \(O(nm+m^2)\) per right-hand side. This improves on dense \(O(n^2)\) storage and \(O(n^3)\) factorization when \(m\ll n\), while introducing rank-approximation error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-m factor reduces dense storage and factorization costs when m is much smaller than n, in exchange for approximation error.
assumptions_latex: \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\).
\(\lambda>0\).
Dense unstructured arithmetic is used.
knowledge_statements.title: Dense Low-Rank Linear-Algebra Tradeoff

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic relation between rank budget and best attainable matrix error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed target matrix \(K\) and matrix norm, define \[E_m=\inf_{\operatorname{rank}(A)\le m}\|K-A\|.\] Since the feasible rank classes are nested, \(E_{m+1}\le E_m\). A particular heuristic sequence need not have monotone realized error unless its approximations are nested or reoptimized.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Best achievable approximation error is nonincreasing with rank, although a heuristic's realized errors need not be.
assumptions_latex: The target matrix and norm are fixed across ranks.

notation.meaning: Best error attainable with rank at most m.

knowledge_statements.title: Nested-Rank Monotonicity
Approximation-Accuracy Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal rank-error tradeoff for positive-semidefinite kernel matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\in\mathbb S_+^n\) have eigenvalues \(\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_n\ge0\), and let \(K_m\) retain its largest \(m<n\) eigenpairs. Among all matrices \(A\) of rank at most \(m\), \[\min_{\operatorname{rank}(A)\le m}\lVert K-A\rVert_2=\lambda_{m+1},\qquad \min_{\operatorname{rank}(A)\le m}\lVert K-A\rVert_F=\left(\sum_{j=m+1}^n\lambda_j^2\right)^{1/2}.\] Therefore smaller approximation error requires retaining enough rank to capture the spectral tail; rapid eigenvalue decay permits accurate low-rank surrogates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The best rank-m kernel approximation error equals the discarded spectral tail, directly linking computational rank to attainable accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb S_+^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_m\) attains the displayed optimal spectral- and Frobenius-norm errors.

children.title: Approximation Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cases where reduced representations miss local, spectral, or posterior structure relevant to search.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Obstruction for approximation features that omit an isolated region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\operatorname{diag}(K_1,K_2)\) with \(K_2\ne0\), and suppose every approximation feature vanishes on the second block. Then \(\widetilde K=\operatorname{diag}(\widetilde K_1,0)\), so \[\|K-\widetilde K\|_2\ge\|K_2\|_2.\] Increasing approximation effort solely within the first block cannot reduce this error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Features confined to one isolated region cannot approximate a nonzero covariance block in an omitted region.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is block diagonal with \(K_2\ne0\).
All approximation features vanish on the second block.

notation.meaning: Covariance block of the omitted region.

knowledge_statements.title: Missed Localized Covariance Block

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of prior uncertainty in a direction omitted by a reduced-rank covariance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\succeq0\) and let \(\widetilde K\succeq0\) have rank below the ambient matrix dimension. For any nonzero \(v\in\ker(\widetilde K)\), the approximation assigns \(v^{\mathsf T}\widetilde Kv=0\). If \(v^{\mathsf T}Kv>0\), it deletes genuine prior variance in direction \(v\); treating \(\widetilde K\) as exact therefore understates prior uncertainty in that direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A low-rank covariance assigns zero variance to its nullspace, including directions where the exact covariance may have positive variance.
assumptions_latex: \(K,\widetilde K\succeq0\).
\(v\in\ker(\widetilde K)\) and \(v^{\mathsf T}Kv>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Unrepresented Covariance-Direction Failure
Approximation Failure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Flat-spectrum obstruction to low-rank kernel approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(K=I_n\), whose eigenvalues are all one. For every matrix \(A\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(A)\le m<n\), \[\lVert I_n-A\rVert_2\ge1,\qquad \lVert I_n-A\rVert_F\ge\sqrt{n-m}.\] Hence no rank-\(m\) approximation achieves spectral-norm error below one, and small relative Frobenius error requires \(m\) close to \(n\). This concrete family marks a failure regime for global low-rank surrogates: absent spectral decay, rank reduction cannot preserve the kernel matrix accurately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identity kernel matrices have no spectral decay, so low-rank approximation remains inaccurate unless the retained rank is nearly full.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct flat-spectrum specialization of optimal low-rank approximation errors
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The identity-matrix lower bounds and infimum values are correct, and failure_boundary is the exact mathematical role for this leaf. The record lacks an inspectable source for the optimal low-rank error result on which the failure claim depends.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General kernel-perturbation result already owned by approximation-error and tradeoff scopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A=K+\lambda I\) and \(\widetilde A=\widetilde K+\lambda I\), with \(K,\widetilde K\succeq0\) and \(\lambda>0\), \[\|A^{-1}-\widetilde A^{-1}\|_2\le \lambda^{-2}\|K-\widetilde K\|_2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small regularization can amplify covariance approximation error in inverse-based calculations.
assumptions_latex: \(K,\widetilde K\succeq0\).
\(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Small-Regularization Error Amplification

children.title: Local Partition Scaling Architectures
children.top_down_role: Neighborhood and divide-and-conquer architectures for scalable prediction.

children.title: Local Surrogates
children.top_down_role: Predictive models fitted or queried within neighborhoods of candidate locations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Query-dependent exact Gaussian-process inference on a selected neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At query \(x\), select the \(k\) nearest observations \(I_k(x)\), form their regularized covariance \(K_x\), and compute the ordinary Gaussian-process posterior using only \((X_{I_k(x)},y_{I_k(x)})\). A fresh dense factorization costs \(O(k^3)\) time and \(O(k^2)\) storage per query, excluding neighbor search. When \(k=n\), the result equals the full-data Gaussian-process posterior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nearest-neighborhood local GP performs exact GP inference on k nearby observations and recovers the full posterior when all observations are retained.
assumptions_latex: The selected regularized covariance is positive definite.
A deterministic tie rule defines \(I_k(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The local factorization costs \(O(k^3)\) time and becomes full-data inference when \(k=n\).

notation.meaning: Indices of the k observations nearest to x.

review_flags: neighbor-search complexity depends on dimension and indexing method
knowledge_statements.title: Nearest-Neighborhood Local Gaussian Process

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise consistency conditions for a local weighted-mean surrogate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_i=m(X_i)+\epsilon_i\), with \(\mathbb E[\epsilon_i\mid X_i]=0\) and uniformly bounded conditional variance. At an interior point \(x\) where the design density is positive and \(m\) is continuous, use normalized nonnegative bounded-kernel weights with bandwidth \(h_n\to0\) and \(nh_n^d\to\infty\). Under the standard kernel-support and denominator regularity conditions, \[\widehat m_n(x)\xrightarrow{p}m(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local weighted-mean surrogate is pointwise consistent when its neighborhood shrinks while its effective sample size diverges.
assumptions_latex: \(h_n\to0\) and \(nh_n^d\to\infty\).
The design density is positive and the regression function is continuous at the interior query.
Noise is conditionally mean zero with uniformly bounded conditional variance.
The kernel and normalization satisfy the standard local-regression regularity conditions.
review_flags: this theorem concerns local weighted regression, not arbitrary local-GP hyperparameter procedures
knowledge_statements.title: Consistency of Shrinking-Neighborhood Local Regression
Local Surrogates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Query-dependent surrogate fitted within a local neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given observations \(D_n=\{(x_i,y_i)\}_{i=1}^n\) and a query \(x\), choose a neighborhood \(N_h(x)=\{i:d(x_i,x)\le h\}\). A local surrogate at \(x\) is a predictive model \(M_x\) fitted using only \(D_x=\{(x_i,y_i):i\in N_h(x)\}\), or equivalently using weights that vanish outside this neighborhood. Its predictive distribution \(p_x(f(x)\mid D_x)\) may vary with the query because both the retained observations and fitted parameters can change with \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local surrogate predicts at each query using only nearby observations or weights supported in a prescribed neighborhood.
assumptions_latex: \(d\) is a distance or dissimilarity on \(\mathcal X\).
\(h>0\) and \(N_h(x)\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_x\) depends on the localized dataset \(D_x\), not necessarily on all of \(D_n\).

notation.meaning: Indices in the radius-h neighborhood of x.
Local observations used at query x.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit neighborhood-based definition; dedicated local-surrogate source pending
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The neighborhood-based definition is coherent, introduces its local objects, and definition is an appropriate content kind for Local Surrogates. A dedicated source is still required to establish that this is the intended standard usage in surrogate modeling.

children.title: Treed Surrogates
children.top_down_role: Hierarchical domain subdivision supporting region-specific surrogate behavior.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Posterior exploration of recursive partitions and leaf-model parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A treed-surrogate sampler may use grow, prune, change, and swap proposals. For a dimension-matched reversible-jump proposal from \(z=(T,\theta)\) to \(z'=(T',\theta')\), including any required auxiliary variables in the proposal densities, the Metropolis--Hastings acceptance probability is \[\alpha(z,z')=1\wedge\frac{p(D\mid z')p(z')q(z\mid z')}{p(D\mid z)p(z)q(z'\mid z)}|J|.\] Valid dimension matching and reciprocal proposals give detailed balance with the tree-and-parameter posterior. If the resulting chain is additionally Harris irreducible and aperiodic, its distribution converges to that posterior from admissible initial states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dimension-matched grow, prune, change, and swap moves can preserve and, under ergodicity conditions, converge to the treed-surrogate posterior.
assumptions_latex: The reversible-jump mapping is dimension matched and has the stated Jacobian.
Forward and reverse proposal densities include required auxiliary variables.
The posterior is proper.
The convergence conclusion additionally assumes Harris irreducibility and aperiodicity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p(T,\theta\mid D)\) is invariant, and the chain converges to it under the stated ergodicity conditions.
review_flags: the compact ratio presumes auxiliary-variable factors are included in q
knowledge_statements.title: Reversible-Jump Tree Exploration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense Gaussian-process cost conditional on a fixed tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Conditional on a tree with leaf sample counts \(n_1,�ldots,n_L\), independent dense Gaussian-process leaves require \(O(\sum_{\ell=1}^Ln_\ell^3)\) factorization time and \(O(\sum_{\ell=1}^Ln_\ell^2)\) storage. If \(n_\ell\asymp n/L\), these become \(O(n^3/L^2)\) and \(O(n^2/L)\), excluding tree-learning or tree-sampling overhead.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed treed partition reduces dense GP algebra through leafwise factorization, while tree exploration adds separate overhead.
assumptions_latex: Leaf models are conditionally independent.
Dense covariance factorizations are used.
The balanced bounds assume comparable leaf sizes.
knowledge_statements.title: Leafwise Treed-Surrogate Scaling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Posterior prediction when the recursive partition is uncertain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) denote a partition tree and \(p(f_*\mid x_*,D,T)\) its conditional predictive distribution. Bayesian averaging gives \[p(f_*\mid x_*,D)=\sum_Tp(f_*\mid x_*,D,T)p(T\mid D),\] with an integral for continuous tree parameters. If \(\mu_T\) and \(s_T^2\) are the tree-conditional mean and variance, then \[\mathbb E[f_*\mid D]=\mathbb E_T[\mu_T],\qquad \operatorname{Var}(f_*\mid D)=\mathbb E_T[s_T^2]+\operatorname{Var}_T(\mu_T).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bayesian tree averaging adds between-tree partition uncertainty to within-tree predictive variance.
assumptions_latex: \(p(T\mid D)\) is proper.
Every conditional predictive distribution has a finite second moment.
knowledge_statements.title: Bayesian Averaging over Surrogate Trees
Treed Surrogates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive-partition representation with leaf-specific surrogate models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite decision tree partition \(\mathcal X\) into disjoint leaves \(R_1,\ldots,R_L\). Associate leaf \(R_\ell\) with a local surrogate \(f_\ell\), and define \[f(x)=\sum_{\ell=1}^L\mathbf 1\{x\in R_\ell\}f_\ell(x).\] If the leaf processes are independent Gaussian processes with kernels \(k_\ell\), then \[k_T(x,x')=\sum_{\ell=1}^L\mathbf 1\{x,x'\in R_\ell\}k_\ell(x,x')\] is positive semidefinite and has zero cross-leaf covariance. The tree supplies the recursive gating structure; the leaves supply local predictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A treed surrogate recursively partitions the domain and assigns a local model to each terminal region.
assumptions_latex: \(R_1,\ldots,R_L\) form a disjoint partition of \(\mathcal X\).
Each \(k_\ell\) is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(k_T\) is positive semidefinite and block diagonal across tree leaves.

notation.meaning: Terminal region of the partition tree.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite gated sum of leaf kernels is positive semidefinite; treed-GP source pending
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: For a fixed partition and independent leaf Gaussian processes, the gated kernel is positive semidefinite and has zero cross-leaf covariance. This is an appropriate treed-surrogate representation, but no specific treed-GP or treed-surrogate source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A local-partition scaling architecture using conditionally independent Gaussian processes in tree leaves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A treed Gaussian-process surrogate recursively partitions the input domain and assigns a conditionally independent Gaussian process, with potentially leaf-specific covariance and noise parameters, to each terminal region. Its local covariance decompositions are smaller than a single global decomposition, while leaf-specific dependence and variance structures represent nonstationarity and heteroskedasticity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A treed Gaussian-process surrogate partitions the domain and fits an independent Gaussian process in each leaf. Smaller local covariance matrices reduce computation, while leaf-specific spatial dependence and noise levels model nonstationarity and heteroskedasticity.
assumptions_latex: The input domain is divided into terminal regions by a tree.
Conditional on the tree, Gaussian-process models in distinct leaves are independent.
Covariance or noise parameters may vary between leaves.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K_{\mathcal T}=\operatorname{diag}(K_\eta:\eta\in\mathcal L_{\mathcal T})\ \text{up to permutation, enabling local computation and region-dependent covariance and variance behavior.}

children.title: Partitioned Surrogates
children.top_down_role: Divide-and-conquer prediction across explicit or learned domain regions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Likelihood factorization and dense computation for independent regional Gaussian-process experts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_1,\ldots,R_L\) be a disjoint partition, and assign observation \(i\) to the unique region containing \(x_i\). If regional latent processes and observation noises are mutually independent, the training covariance is \[K=\operatorname{diag}(K_1,\ldots,K_L)\] and \[\log p(y)=\sum_{\ell=1}^L\log p(y_\ell).\] With \(n_\ell\) observations in region \(\ell\), dense fitting costs \(O(\sum_\ell n_\ell^3)\) time and \(O(\sum_\ell n_\ell^2)\) storage. For exactly balanced counts \(n_\ell=n/L\), these become \(O(n^3/L^2)\) and \(O(n^2/L)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent hard partitions factor covariance and likelihood by region, reducing dense GP cost when region sizes are balanced.
assumptions_latex: The regions form a disjoint partition.
Regional latent processes and noises are mutually independent.
Dense regional factorizations are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\) is block diagonal and fitting costs \(O(\sum_\ell n_\ell^3)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Independent Hard-Partition Factorization
Partitioned Surrogates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hard- or soft-gated composition of region-specific predictive models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_1,\ldots,R_L\) cover \(\mathcal X\), and let gating functions \(w_\ell:\mathcal X\to[0,1]\) satisfy \(\sum_{\ell=1}^Lw_\ell(x)=1\). Given local predictive means \(\mu_\ell(x)\) and variances \(s_\ell^2(x)\), a partitioned mixture surrogate has \[\mu(x)=\sum_{\ell=1}^Lw_\ell(x)\mu_\ell(x),\] \[s^2(x)=\sum_{\ell=1}^Lw_\ell(x)\bigl(s_\ell^2(x)+\mu_\ell(x)^2\bigr)-\mu(x)^2.\] Indicator gates produce a hard partition; overlapping gates produce coordinated interpolation across regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partitioned surrogate combines region-specific predictions through hard indicators or normalized soft gates, with variance given by total variance.
assumptions_latex: \(w_\ell(x)\ge0\) and \(\sum_\ell w_\ell(x)=1\).
Each local model has finite mean and variance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mu(x)\) and \(s^2(x)\) are the mean and variance of the gated predictive mixture.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: mixture mean and total-variance identities; partitioned-surrogate source pending
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed mean and variance are correct for a predictive mixture whose component index has probabilities w_l(x), and representation fits the leaf. A source is required, and the record should clarify how the gates correspond to the stated regions before the architecture-specific interpretation can be relied upon.

children.title: Cross-Region Coordination
children.top_down_role: Information sharing, continuity, or competition across local surrogate regions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient regularity condition for blending overlapping regional predictors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let continuous weights \(w_r:\mathcal X\to[0,1]\) satisfy \(\sum_{r=1}^Rw_r(x)=1\), and let each \(\mu_r\) be continuous on a neighborhood of \(\operatorname{supp}(w_r)\). Then \[\mu(x)=\sum_{r=1}^Rw_r(x)\mu_r(x)\] is continuous. If all relevant weights and predictors are \(C^q\), then \(\mu\in C^q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuous normalized overlap weights preserve continuity, and smooth weights and experts preserve corresponding differentiability.
assumptions_latex: The weights form a finite continuous partition of unity.
Each local predictor has the claimed regularity wherever its weight can be nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mu=\sum_r w_r\mu_r\in C(\mathcal X)\), with the analogous \(C^q\) conclusion.
knowledge_statements.title: Partition-of-Unity Continuity Condition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gated-kernel construction permitting covariance across overlapping regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k_r\) be positive-semidefinite kernels and let \(w_r:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\). Then \[k(x,x')=\sum_{r=1}^Rw_r(x)w_r(x')k_r(x,x')\] is positive semidefinite. It permits nonzero covariance across a regional boundary whenever some gate is nonzero at both inputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gating and summing local kernels gives a valid covariance that can share information across regional boundaries.
assumptions_latex: Every \(k_r\) is positive semidefinite.
The sum contains finitely many terms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(k\) is positive semidefinite and can couple inputs sharing an active gate.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Semidefinite Cross-Region Coupling
Cross-Region Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinates partition-local surrogate acquisitions through normalized regional weights and a common global decision rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X=\bigcup_{r=1}^R\mathcal X_r\), and let \(a_r(x;s_r)\) be the acquisition supplied by the posterior state \(s_r\) in region \(r\). Choose measurable coordination weights \(w_r(x)\ge 0\) satisfying \(\sum_{r=1}^R w_r(x)=1\), with \(w_r(x)=0\) when region \(r\) is irrelevant to \(x\). Form the coordinated acquisition \(A(x)=\sum_{r=1}^R w_r(x)a_r(x;s_r)\), select \(x^+\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X}A(x)\), observe the response, and update every local state whose weight at \(x^+\) is positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Blend local acquisitions with normalized regional weights, maximize the resulting global acquisition, and update every local surrogate participating at the selected point.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) is partitioned or covered by finitely many regions \(\mathcal X_r\).
Each \(a_r(\cdot;s_r)\) is defined wherever \(w_r\) is positive.

notation.meaning: Posterior state of local surrogate r.
Coordination weight assigned to region r.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the cross-region coordination leaf and is internally coherent, but the weighted-acquisition construction and multi-surrogate update rule have no cited evidence.

children.title: Boundary Artifact Risks
children.top_down_role: Prediction or uncertainty distortions near neighborhood or partition boundaries.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Artificial Uncertainty Jump at a Region Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hard regional gating can create an acquisition jump solely through posterior uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let regional posterior means be identically zero and assemble posterior standard deviations as \(s(x)=0\) for \(x\le b\) and \(s(x)=1\) for \(x>b\). The latent objective may nevertheless be the continuous zero function. For \(a(x)=\mu(x)+\sqrt\beta s(x)\), \(\beta>0\), \(a(x)=0\) on the left and \(a(x)=\sqrt\beta\) on the right. Thus \[\lim_{x\downarrow b}a(x)-a(b)=\sqrt\beta>0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regional uncertainty jump can create an artificial acquisition preference even when the objective and posterior means agree across the boundary.
assumptions_latex: Posterior standard deviations are hard-gated as displayed.
knowledge_statements.title: Artificial Uncertainty Jump at a Region Boundary
Boundary Artifact Risks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies discontinuities caused by independently fitted local surrogates at a shared partition boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X_1=(-\infty,b]\) and \(\mathcal X_2=(b,\infty)\), and fit independent local posterior means \(m_1\) and \(m_2\). Define the assembled predictor by \(m(x)=m_1(x)\) for \(x\le b\) and \(m(x)=m_2(x)\) for \(x>b\). If \(m_1(b)\ne\lim_{x\downarrow b}m_2(x)\), then \(m\) is discontinuous at \(b\), even when the latent objective is continuous. Any acquisition depending continuously and nontrivially on the posterior mean can inherit this jump, creating artificial boundary maxima or suppressing genuine candidates near \(b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent regional fits can disagree at a shared boundary, producing discontinuous predictions and spurious acquisition maxima despite a continuous objective.
assumptions_latex: The two regional surrogates are fitted without a continuity constraint at \(b\).
The relevant one-sided limits of \(m_1\) and \(m_2\) exist.

notation.meaning: Posterior mean fitted in region r.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The discontinuity example is mathematically plausible and failure_boundary is appropriate, but the broader acquisition-artifact claim requires an inspectable authoritative source.

children.title: Sequential Numerical Reuse Architecture
children.top_down_role: Sequential computational mechanisms reusing earlier surrogate factorizations and summaries.

children.title: Incremental Posterior Inference
children.top_down_role: Sequential maintenance of surrogate inference as new observations arrive.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact posterior-moment recursion after appending one scalar Gaussian observation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \((f(x),Y_{n+1})\mid\mathcal D_n\) is jointly Gaussian, with conditional means \(m_n(x)\) and \(\mu_n\), cross-covariance \(c_n(x):=\operatorname{Cov}(f(x),Y_{n+1}\mid\mathcal D_n)\), and \(v_n:=\operatorname{Var}(Y_{n+1}\mid\mathcal D_n)>0\). After observing \(Y_{n+1}=y_{n+1}\), \[m_{n+1}(x)=m_n(x)+\frac{c_n(x)}{v_n}(y_{n+1}-\mu_n),\] \[C_{n+1}(x,x')=C_n(x,x')-\frac{c_n(x)c_n(x')}{v_n}.\] These moments equal those obtained by conditioning the full joint Gaussian model on all \(n+1\) observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A new Gaussian observation produces an innovation update of the posterior mean and a rank-one reduction of posterior covariance, exactly matching batch conditioning.
assumptions_latex: \((f(x),f(x'),Y_{n+1})\mid\mathcal D_n\) is jointly Gaussian for all queried \(x,x'\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (m_{n+1},C_{n+1})\text{ equals the batch posterior conditioned on }\mathcal D_n\cup\{Y_{n+1}=y_{n+1}\}.

notation.meaning: Conditional covariance between the latent query and the new noisy observation.
Conditional predictive variance of the new observation.

knowledge_statements.title: Recursive Gaussian Posterior Conditioning
Incremental Posterior Inference
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact rank-one Gaussian-process posterior update after appending one noisy observation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a positive-definite covariance matrix \(K_n=L_nL_n^{\mathsf T}\), append an observation at \(x_{n+1}\) with covariance vector \(k\) and marginal variance \(\kappa\). Compute \(v=L_n^{-1}k\) and \(d=(\kappa-v^{\mathsf T}v)^{1/2}\), then set \[L_{n+1}=\begin{pmatrix}L_n&0\\v^{\mathsf T}&d\end{pmatrix}.\] Solve with \(L_{n+1}\) and \(L_{n+1}^{\mathsf T}\) to obtain posterior coefficients and predictive moments. Stop after the appended datum is incorporated and return the updated factor and posterior state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Append one observation by extending the existing Cholesky factor, then use triangular solves to update the Gaussian-process posterior.
assumptions_latex: \(K_n\) is symmetric positive definite.
The Schur complement satisfies \(\kappa-v^{\mathsf T}v>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_{n+1}=L_{n+1}L_{n+1}^{\mathsf T}\), with an exact-arithmetic update cost of \(O(n^2)\).

notation.meaning: Cholesky factor of the current covariance matrix.
Covariances between the new and existing observations.
Square root of the new Schur complement.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The block Cholesky update is standard and algorithm is the correct kind, but neither the exact GP inference interpretation nor the stated O(n^2) cost is cited.

children.title: Factorization Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of earlier matrix factorizations during successive surrogate updates.

knowledge_statements.title: Factorization Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuses a covariance factor for posterior coefficients, variance calculations, and sequential extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For observations \(y\in\mathbb R^n\) and positive-definite covariance matrix \(K_n=L_nL_n^{\mathsf T}\), compute posterior coefficients by the reused triangular solves \(L_nz=y\) and \(L_n^{\mathsf T}\alpha=z\). For a candidate with covariance vector \(k_x\), reuse the same factor to solve \(L_nv_x=k_x\), giving predictive mean \(m_n(x)=k_x^{\mathsf T}\alpha\) and variance \(s_n^2(x)=k(x,x)-v_x^{\mathsf T}v_x\). The factor may subsequently be extended by a block Cholesky update rather than recomputed from scratch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One Cholesky factor supports posterior coefficients, predictive variances, and later block extensions without repeated full factorizations.
assumptions_latex: \(K_n\) is symmetric positive definite.
The prior mean has been subtracted from \(y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_n(x)=k_x^{\mathsf T}K_n^{-1}y\) and \(s_n^2(x)=k(x,x)-k_x^{\mathsf T}K_n^{-1}k_x\) are obtained using \(L_n\).

notation.meaning: Whitened covariance vector for candidate x.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The factor-reuse formulas are coherent and representation fits the leaf, but the nontrivial GP formulas and sequential-extension claim lack cited evidence.

children.title: Cached Predictive Summaries
children.top_down_role: Reuse of stored quantities supporting repeated prediction or acquisition evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Cached Predictive Summaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Caches reusable Gaussian-process quantities while invalidating summaries affected by posterior updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(K_n\), observations \(y_n\), and a fixed candidate set \(C\), cache \(\alpha_n=K_n^{-1}y_n\) and, for every \(x\in C\), the pair \(m_n(x)=k_x^{\mathsf T}\alpha_n\) and \(s_n^2(x)=k(x,x)-k_x^{\mathsf T}K_n^{-1}k_x\). Reuse a cached pair only while the training data, kernel parameters, noise parameters, and candidate covariance vector remain unchanged. After any of these inputs changes, invalidate the affected entries, recompute them using the current factorization, and return summaries indexed by the posterior-state version.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cache candidate means and variances with a posterior version, and invalidate every entry whose data or covariance parameters have changed.
assumptions_latex: \(K_n\) is invertible.
Each cache entry records the posterior-state version under which it was computed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A returned cache entry equals \((m_n(x),s_n^2(x))\) for the current posterior state.

notation.meaning: Candidate set whose predictions are cached.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cache-versioning algorithm matches the leaf, but its invalidation requirements and GP summary formulas have no authoritative citation.

children.title: Warm-Started Numerical Solvers
children.top_down_role: Initialization of repeated inference computations from earlier fitted states.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Warm Starts Do Not Certify Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating reuse of an initial point from validity of the current numerical solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The condition \(\theta_t^{(0)}=\widehat\theta_{t-1}\) alone implies neither \(R_t(\theta_t^{(0)})=0\) nor convergence of the iterates generated by \(T_t\). If the preceding point lies outside the current solver's convergence region, a warm-started run may stagnate, diverge, or converge to an undesired local solution. Acceptance therefore requires a certificate evaluated for the current problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A previous solution is only an initial point; it need not solve the changed problem or lie in the current solver's convergence basin.
assumptions_latex: The numerical problem or solver map may change from iteration \(t-1\) to \(t\).
knowledge_statements.title: Warm Starts Do Not Certify Convergence
Warm-Started Numerical Solvers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Initializes each sequential numerical solve from the preceding posterior state's solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Theta\) be the solver domain, let \(R_t:\Theta\to\mathbb R^q\) be the residual map for the numerical problem at Bayesian-optimization iteration \(t\), and let \(\widehat\theta_{t-1}\in\Theta\) be the preceding solution. Initialize \(\theta_t^{(0)}=\widehat\theta_{t-1}\), apply the current solver update \(\theta_t^{(j+1)}=T_t(\theta_t^{(j)})\), and stop at the first \(j\) satisfying \(\|R_t(\theta_t^{(j)})\|\le\varepsilon_t\) or a prescribed iteration limit. Return \(\widehat\theta_t=\theta_t^{(j)}\), together with the residual and termination status; warm starting changes initialization, not the stopping certificate. For smooth optimization one may take \(R_t=\nabla F_t\), while for root finding \(R_t\) is the current equation residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start each updated numerical problem from the previous solution, while certifying successful convergence using the current problem's residual rather than the warm start itself.
assumptions_latex: \(R_t\) and the solver map \(T_t\) are defined on \(\Theta\).
The previous solution \(\widehat\theta_{t-1}\in\Theta\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta_t^{(0)}=\widehat\theta_{t-1}\), and termination by the residual test implies \(\|R_t(\widehat\theta_t)\|\le\varepsilon_t\).

notation.meaning: Residual map for the current numerical problem.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic contraction theorem proposed as a warm-start complexity result.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(T_t\) is contractive with factor \(\rho_t\in(0,1)\), then \(\|\theta_t^{(j)}-\theta_t^\star\|\le \rho_t^j\|\widehat\theta_{t-1}-\theta_t^\star\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contractive iteration converges geometrically from the previous solution when that point lies in its invariant contraction region.
assumptions_latex: \(T_t\) is a contraction on an invariant set containing the initial point and fixed point.
knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Contraction Bound

intermediate_metadata.reason: The local inventory is initialization reuse, current-problem termination testing, and the fact that warm starts provide no validity or convergence certificate. The generic contraction bound is deferred because its canonical home is fixed-point convergence. Factor updates, caches, and accumulated numerical error remain outside this leaf.

children.title: Accumulated Numerical Error
children.top_down_role: Stability risks arising from repeated updates, stale summaries, or degraded conditioning.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic safeguard against accumulated error in sequential numerical reuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After a declared number of updates or whenever a factor residual is evaluated, compute a reliable bound \(\rho_t\ge\|K_t-\widehat L_t\widehat L_t^{\mathsf T}\|_2\). Continue reuse only while \(\rho_t\) remains below the prescribed tolerance and any available eigenvalue-margin threshold; otherwise recompute a fresh stable factorization of \(K_t\) and restart residual monitoring. The refresh restores only the guarantees of the chosen full-factorization routine and arithmetic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Monitor the reused factor's residual and replace it with a fresh factorization when the residual or eigenvalue-margin test fails.
assumptions_latex: A reliable residual-norm bound can be computed.
The fresh factorization routine has a declared stability guarantee.
The tolerance and eigenvalue-margin policy are fixed before the decision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho_t\ge\tau_t\ \Longrightarrow\ \text{refresh the factor rather than certify continued reuse}.

notation.meaning: Reliable upper bound on the current factor residual norm.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Triggered Factor Refresh

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual Certificate for a Reused Covariance Factor
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable drift certificate for a sequentially maintained factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_t\succ0\), \(R_t=K_t-\widehat L_t\widehat L_t^{\mathsf T}\), and let \(0<\underline\lambda_t\le\lambda_{\min}(K_t)\) be certified. If \(\|R_t\|_2<\underline\lambda_t\), then \[\lambda_{\min}(\widehat L_t\widehat L_t^{\mathsf T})\ge\underline\lambda_t-\|R_t\|_2>0.\] Failure of the inequality is inconclusive rather than proof of indefiniteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual smaller than a certified eigenvalue margin certifies positive definiteness of the matrix represented by the reused factor.
assumptions_latex: \(K_t\) is symmetric positive definite.
\(\underline\lambda_t\) is a valid positive lower eigenvalue bound.
The residual norm has a reliable upper bound.

notation.meaning: Residual of the current reused factor.
Certified lower bound on the smallest eigenvalue of the exact covariance matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Certificate for a Reused Covariance Factor

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cumulative Backward-Error Boundary for Sequential Factor Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic accumulation boundary under an explicitly additive update-error model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\widehat L_t\widehat L_t^{\mathsf T}=K_t+E_t\) and a sequential update satisfies \(E_t=\operatorname{emb}(E_{t-1})+\Delta_t\), where the embedding preserves the spectral norm. Then \[\|E_t\|_2\le\|E_0\|_2+\sum_{j=1}^t\|\Delta_j\|_2.\] If this upper bound reaches \(\lambda_{\min}(K_t)\), perturbation analysis no longer certifies positive definiteness of the represented nearby matrix or reliable covariance-derived variances. The statement is conditional on the declared additive backward-error model and is not an algorithm-independent roundoff rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under an additive backward-error model, sequential update errors accumulate; once their bound reaches the covariance eigenvalue margin, definiteness and variance guarantees are lost.
assumptions_latex: \(K_t\) is symmetric positive definite in exact arithmetic.
Each update admits the stated additive backward-error model.
The embedding preserves the spectral norm.

notation.meaning: New backward perturbation introduced at update t.

knowledge_statements.title: Cumulative Backward-Error Boundary for Sequential Factor Reuse
Accumulated Numerical Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounds perturbation accumulation under repeated factor updates and identifies loss of positive-definiteness guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a recursively computed factor satisfies \(\widehat L_t\widehat L_t^{\mathsf T}=K_t+E_t\). If update \(t\) embeds the preceding error and introduces a symmetric perturbation \(\Delta_t\), then \(E_t=\operatorname{emb}(E_{t-1})+\Delta_t\), so \(\|E_t\|_2\le\|E_0\|_2+\sum_{j=1}^t\|\Delta_j\|_2\). Once this bound is comparable to \(\lambda_{\min}(K_t)\), perturbation analysis no longer guarantees positive definiteness or reliable posterior variances. Periodic refactorization or residual checks are therefore required before that threshold is crossed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Errors from sequential factor updates can accumulate until they rival the smallest covariance eigenvalue, invalidating positive-definiteness and variance guarantees.
assumptions_latex: Each recursive update admits the stated additive backward-error model.
\(K_t\) is symmetric positive definite in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|E_0\|_2+\sum_{j=1}^t\|\Delta_j\|_2\ge\lambda_{\min}(K_t)\) marks failure of the perturbative definiteness guarantee.

notation.meaning: Embedding of the prior error into the enlarged matrix.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive error bound and loss-of-guarantee threshold are plausible and failure_boundary is appropriate, but the backward-error model and prescribed safeguards require authoritative numerical-analysis support.

children.title: Bayesian Lookahead Policy Family
children.top_down_role: Policies organized by one-step, truncated-horizon, rollout, and approximately nonmyopic decision value.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bellman representation and computational boundary for learning policies whose state records current beliefs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(S^n\) is the current state, \(C(S^n,x)\) is the immediate contribution, and \(S^{n+1}\) is the next state after action \(x\), then
\[
V^n(S^n)=\max_{x\in\mathcal X}\left(C(S^n,x)+\mathbb E\!\left[V^{n+1}(S^{n+1})\mid S^n,x\right]\right).
\]
For \(\mathcal X=\{1,\ldots,M\}\), if the belief about each \(\mu_x\) is normal with mean \(\bar\mu_x^n\) and variance \(\sigma_x^{2,n}\), the belief state is
\[
S^n=\left((\bar\mu_x^n,\sigma_x^{2,n})\right)_{x\in\mathcal X}.
\]
Because these belief parameters are continuous and the state contains parameters for every alternative, direct Bellman computation is intractable for the learning problems described.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A learning policy can be represented by a Bellman recursion whose state contains the current belief distributions. Under independent normal belief summaries, this state consists of every alternative's mean and variance; its continuous, multidimensional form makes direct dynamic programming intractable for the described learning problems.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathcal X\).
\(\mathbb E[V^{n+1}(S^{n+1})\mid S^n,x]\) exists.
For the stated belief representation, \(\mathcal X=\{1,\ldots,M\}\) and the belief about each \(\mu_x\) is normal with mean \(\bar\mu_x^n\) and variance \(\sigma_x^{2,n}\).

children.title: One-Step Bayes-Optimal Policies
children.top_down_role: Myopic policies derived from terminal recommendation or information utility.

knowledge_statements.title: One-Step Bayes-Optimal Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Myopic Bayes rule for one remaining observation followed by a terminal recommendation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s\) be the current belief state, \(x\in\mathcal X\) a sampling action, \(Y\sim P(\cdot\mid s,x)\) its observation, and \(T(s,x,Y)\) the Bayesian update. If \(U(s')\) is the optimal expected terminal recommendation utility in posterior state \(s'\), and \(c(x)\) is sampling cost, then a one-step Bayes-optimal action satisfies \[x^*(s)\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X}\left\{\mathbb E[U(T(s,x,Y))\mid s,x]-c(x)\right\}.\] The expectation integrates over the current posterior predictive distribution and includes no value from observations beyond this single sample.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the sample maximizing expected terminal recommendation utility after one Bayesian update, less its sampling cost.
assumptions_latex: The terminal utility is integrable under \(P(\cdot\mid s,x)\) for every feasible \(x\).
The displayed maximum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*(s)\) maximizes the one-step posterior expected terminal utility net of sampling cost.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact stopping certificate when at most one further observation is permitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G(s,x)\) be the expected increase in optimal terminal utility from sampling \(x\), and let \(c(x)\) be its cost. In a decision problem permitting immediate stopping or at most one final sample, stopping is Bayes-optimal if and only if \(\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}\{G(s,x)-c(x)\}\le0\). This does not certify optimal stopping when two or more observations can have complementary value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonpositive maximal net one-step information value exactly certifies stopping only in the one-sample problem.
assumptions_latex: Only immediate stopping or one final sample is admissible.
The supremum of net one-step value is well-defined.
knowledge_statements.title: One-Step Stopping Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-of-information property when the terminal decision may ignore the observation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U(s)=\sup_{d\in\mathcal D}\mathbb E[u(d,\Theta)\mid s]\) and \(G(s,x)=\mathbb E[U(T(s,x,Y))\mid s,x]-U(s)\). If every pre-observation terminal decision remains available after observing \(Y\), then \(G(s,x)\ge0\). With sampling cost \(c(x)\), sampling \(x\) is strictly preferable to immediate stopping exactly when \(G(s,x)>c(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Information cannot reduce optimal terminal decision value when it may be ignored; sampling is worthwhile only when its expected value exceeds cost.
assumptions_latex: Terminal utilities are integrable.
Every pre-observation terminal decision remains feasible after observation.
The posterior update is coherent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G(s,x)\ge0,\qquad x\text{ strictly beats stopping}\iff G(s,x)>c(x).
knowledge_statements.title: Nonnegative Value of One Observation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a myopic acquisition policy using expected marginal dataset utility and gives its value-of-sample-information interpretation under decision utility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a current dataset \(\mathcal D\), a utility function \(u\) on returned datasets, and a candidate location \(x\in\mathcal X\), let the prospective random observation \(y\) yield \(\mathcal D'=\mathcal D\cup\{(x,y)\}\). The one-step lookahead acquisition function is \[\alpha(x;\mathcal D)=\mathbb E\!\left[u(\mathcal D')\mid x,\mathcal D\right]-u(\mathcal D).\] The next evaluation location is chosen according to \[x_{\mathrm{next}}\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x'\in\mathcal X}\alpha(x';\mathcal D).\] If \(u(\mathcal D)\) is the expected utility of a decision informed by \(\mathcal D\), then \(\alpha(x;\mathcal D)\) is the value of sample information obtained by observing at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Score each candidate evaluation location by the expected increase in dataset utility after incorporating its prospective observation, and evaluate next at a maximizer of that score. When the dataset utility is the expected utility of a data-informed decision, this gain is the value of sample information.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal D=(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\text{ is the currently observed dataset.}
u\text{ is a chosen utility function on returned datasets.}
x\in\mathcal X\text{ is a candidate location and }y\text{ is its prospective random observation conditional on }(x,\mathcal D).
\mathcal D'=\mathcal D\cup\{(x,y)\}.
\mathbb E[u(\mathcal D')\mid x,\mathcal D]\text{ exists for the candidates under consideration.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha(x;\mathcal D)=\mathbb E[u(\mathcal D')\mid x,\mathcal D]-u(\mathcal D),\qquad x_{\mathrm{next}}\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x'\in\mathcal X}\alpha(x';\mathcal D);\quad u\text{ is decision utility}\Rightarrow\alpha(x;\mathcal D)\text{ is value of sample information.}

children.title: Finite-Horizon Lookahead Policy Family
children.top_down_role: Approximate finite-horizon policies accounting for future evaluations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the rolling-horizon approximation obtained by limiting Bayesian-optimization lookahead and gives the conditional complexity of the described tree implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a true remaining horizon \(\tau\) and a computational lookahead limit \(\ell\), an \(\ell\)-step lookahead policy selects each observation by maximizing \(\alpha_{\min\{\ell,\tau\}}(x;\mathcal D)\). Thus, when \(\tau>\ell\), it substitutes the limited-horizon value \(\alpha_\ell\) for the full-horizon value \(\alpha_\tau\), while the minimum prevents lookahead beyond the true horizon. For the described tree-based implementation, the computational cost per decision is \(\mathcal O(n^\ell q^\ell)\). The case \(\ell=1\) maximizes the expected marginal gain from one additional observation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ell-step lookahead, or rolling-horizon, policy chooses the next observation by maximizing the acquisition value for the smaller of the lookahead limit and the true remaining horizon. When the true horizon is longer, it approximates the full-horizon value by the ell-step value. Under the described tree implementation, a decision costs order n to the ell times q to the ell. Ell equal to one is one-step lookahead.
assumptions_latex: \tau\in\mathbb N\text{ is the true remaining observation horizon}
\ell\in\mathbb N\text{ is the imposed lookahead limit}
\alpha_k(x;\mathcal D)\text{ is the }k\text{-step acquisition value}
\text{The complexity bound applies to the tree-based implementation described in the source}

children.title: Rollout Policy Approximations
children.top_down_role: Policies that estimate future value through simulated continuation from candidate evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Rollout Policy Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monte Carlo lookahead using a base policy after each candidate first action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given belief state \(s\), horizon \(H\), base policy \(\pi_0\), and simulation count \(M\), enumerate candidate first actions \(x\). For each \(x\), simulate \(M\) independent posterior trajectories beginning with \(x\) and thereafter following \(\pi_0\) for \(H-1\) decisions. Let \(G^{(m)}_H(s,x;\pi_0)\) be simulated cumulative reward including terminal utility, and compute \(\widehat Q_H(s,x)=M^{-1}\sum_{m=1}^M G^{(m)}_H(s,x;\pi_0)\). After all candidates are evaluated, return any \(x^+\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_x\widehat Q_H(s,x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simulate each candidate first action, follow a base policy afterward, and choose the candidate with the largest estimated finite-horizon return.
assumptions_latex: The simulated returns are integrable and conditionally independent across replications.
The candidate first-action set is finite or the maximization is otherwise solved.

notation.meaning: Base policy used after the first simulated action.
Number of simulated trajectories per candidate.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform sampling-error and selected-action loss certificate for bounded rollout returns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) candidate actions have rollout returns in \([a,b]\), with \(M\) independent replications per action, true means \(Q(x)\), and sample means \(\widehat Q(x)\). With probability at least \(1-\delta\), \(\max_x|\widehat Q(x)-Q(x)|\le(b-a)\sqrt{\log(2K/\delta)/(2M)}=: \varepsilon_M\). Hence every empirical maximizer \(\widehat x\) satisfies \(\max_xQ(x)-Q(\widehat x)\le2\varepsilon_M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many candidates and bounded returns, uniform concentration certifies that the empirically selected rollout action is near-optimal for the rollout objective.
assumptions_latex: There are \(K<\infty\) candidate actions.
For each action, its \(M\) rollout returns are independent and lie in \([a,b]\).
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Candidate Monte Carlo Rollout Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon improvement over a base policy when rollout action values are evaluated exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite-horizon Markov decision problem, let \(V_h^{\pi_0}\) be the value of base policy \(\pi_0\) with \(h\) decisions remaining and \(Q_h^{\pi_0}(s,x)=r(s,x)+\mathbb E[V_{h-1}^{\pi_0}(S')\mid s,x]\). If the receding-horizon rollout policy chooses \(\pi_{R,h}(s)\in\arg\max_xQ_h^{\pi_0}(s,x)\) at every visited state, then \(V_h^{\pi_R}(s)\ge V_h^{\pi_0}(s)\) for every \(s,h\). Simulation error or inexact maximization can invalidate this ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact receding-horizon rollout is no worse than its base policy, but simulation and optimization errors can destroy the guarantee.
assumptions_latex: The base-policy action is feasible at every state.
Conditional expectations and rollout action values are exact.
Every rollout maximization is exact and recomputed after each observation.

notation.meaning: First-action value followed by the base policy.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Rollout Policy Improvement

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines Bayesian-optimization rollout using a tractable base policy and states the conditional complexity for a one-step-lookahead base policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: To score a candidate next location \(x\), a rollout policy considers its possible outcome, applies a tractable base policy to select each subsequent location conditional on the simulated observations, and continues to the terminal horizon. Averaging the resulting terminal utilities over the unknown future outcomes gives a rollout estimate \(\widehat\alpha^{\mathrm{rollout}}_\tau(x;\mathcal D)\), which is maximized over \(x\). If the base policy is one-step lookahead and the described optimization and quadrature routines are used, the running time is \(\mathcal O(n^2q^\tau)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rollout policy evaluates a possible next observation by simulating all later decisions with a tractable, potentially suboptimal base policy. Future locations respond to simulated observations, and terminal utilities are averaged over the unknown outcomes. The next location maximizes this estimated expected gain. With a one-step-lookahead base policy and the described numerical routines, the running time is order n squared times q to the tau.
assumptions_latex: \tau\in\mathbb N\text{ is the remaining decision horizon}
\text{A tractable base policy selects subsequent locations from the simulated information state}
\text{Unknown future observation values are averaged out in the terminal-utility estimate}
\text{The complexity bound assumes a one-step-lookahead base policy and the described optimization and quadrature routines}

children.title: Multistep Lookahead Policies
children.top_down_role: Finite-horizon policies that explicitly value multiple future evaluation stages.

knowledge_statements.title: Multistep Lookahead Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon Bayesian dynamic program over belief states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U(s)\) be terminal utility and set \(V_0(s)=U(s)\). For \(h=1,\ldots,H\), recursively define \[V_h(s)=\sup_{x\in\mathcal X(s)}\left\{r(s,x)+\mathbb E\left[V_{h-1}(T(s,x,Y))\mid s,x\right]\right\}.\] At a state with \(h\) decisions remaining, select any maximizing action \(\pi_h(s)\), observe \(Y\), update the belief through \(T\), decrement \(h\), and stop at \(h=0\) with terminal value \(U\). Thus the policy accounts for the adaptive value of all observations within the chosen horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recursively optimize immediate reward plus expected future belief-state value, selecting actions adaptively until the finite horizon ends.
assumptions_latex: Each conditional expectation is well-defined.
Each supremum used by the policy is attained.

notation.meaning: Optimal value with h decisions remaining.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct enumeration complexity for finite-horizon adaptive lookahead with finite action and observation branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose each belief state admits at most \(A\) actions and each action has at most \(B\) observation outcomes. Direct evaluation of an \(H\)-decision tree without state merging evaluates at most \(A\sum_{d=0}^{H-1}(AB)^d\) action nodes and has at most \(A^H B^{H-1}\) complete action-observation paths. Thus its size is \(O(A(AB)^{H-1})\) when \(AB>1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Direct multistep lookahead grows exponentially with planning depth under persistent action and observation branching.
assumptions_latex: \(A,B<\infty\).
Distinct action-observation branches are explicitly enumerated without merging equivalent states.

notation.meaning: Maximum observation branching factor per action.

knowledge_statements.title: Lookahead-Tree Growth

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Horizon-two extension of an arbitrary one-step Bayesian-optimization acquisition function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a one-step acquisition function \(\alpha(x;\mathcal D)\), its two-step analogue is defined by
\[
\alpha_2(x;\mathcal D)=\alpha(x;\mathcal D)+\mathbb E\!\left[\max_{x'\in\mathcal X}\alpha(x';\mathcal D')\mid x,\mathcal D\right],
\]
where \(\mathcal D'\) is the random updated data set after evaluating \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The two-step acquisition value is the immediate acquisition value plus the conditional expected best acquisition value after observing the result at the current candidate.
assumptions_latex: x\in\mathcal X
\alpha(x;\mathcal D)\text{ is a one-step lookahead acquisition function}
\mathcal D'\text{ is the random data set obtained after evaluating }x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha_2(x;\mathcal D)=\alpha(x;\mathcal D)+\mathbb E\!\left[\max_{x'\in\mathcal X}\alpha(x';\mathcal D')\mid x,\mathcal D\right]

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-step cumulative-reward lookahead, its knowledge-gradient decomposition up to an action-independent constant, and its overexploitation boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For cumulative reward, the two-step acquisition is
\[
\alpha_2(x;\mathcal D)=\mu_{\mathcal D}(x)+\mathbb E\!\left[\max_{x'\in\mathcal X}\mu_{\mathcal D'}(x')\mid x,\mathcal D\right].
\]
After subtracting the current-data global-reward term, which is constant in \(x\), the acquisition is ranking-equivalent to
\[
\mu_{\mathcal D}(x)+\alpha_{\mathrm{KG}}(x;\mathcal D).
\]
The posterior-mean and knowledge-gradient terms express exploitation and exploration, respectively, but this two-step policy can nevertheless become stuck through overexploitation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For cumulative reward, two-step lookahead combines immediate posterior-mean reward with the expected best posterior mean after the observation. Up to an additive constant independent of the candidate, it is posterior mean plus knowledge gradient, yet it can still become stuck by overexploiting.
assumptions_latex: u(\mathcal D)=\sum_i y_i
\mathcal D'\text{ is the random data set after evaluating }x
\alpha_{\mathrm{KG}}(x;\mathcal D)\text{ is the expected increase in the best posterior mean relative to the current best posterior mean}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha_2(x;\mathcal D)\equiv\mu_{\mathcal D}(x)+\alpha_{\mathrm{KG}}(x;\mathcal D)\pmod{\text{an additive constant independent of }x}

children.title: Horizon Truncation Effects
children.top_down_role: Decision-quality changes attributable to limited planning depth.

knowledge_statements.title: Horizon Truncation Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform value-loss bound for truncating an infinite discounted lookahead horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an infinite-horizon discounted belief-state problem with discount factor \(0<\gamma<1\) and rewards satisfying \(|r_t|\le R_{\max}\). If an \(H\)-step approximation discards all rewards from time \(H\) onward and uses zero terminal continuation value, then for every policy \(\pi\) and initial state \(s\), \[|V^{\pi}(s)-V_H^{\pi}(s)|\le\sum_{t=H}^{\infty}\gamma^tR_{\max}=\frac{R_{\max}\gamma^H}{1-\gamma}.\] Without discounting, a finite total-reward bound, or an accurate terminal continuation value, this vanishing truncation guarantee need not hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discounted truncation error decays geometrically with horizon; without discounting or another tail bound, increasing a finite horizon need not control error.
assumptions_latex: Rewards obey \(|r_t|\le R_{\max}<\infty\) almost surely.

notation.meaning: H-step truncated value of policy pi.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of an approximate terminal continuation value in discounted finite-horizon lookahead.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a policy \(\pi\), let \(J_W^\pi(s)=\mathbb E_s^\pi[\sum_{t=0}^{H-1}\gamma^t r_t+\gamma^H W(S_H)]\), and define \(J_{\widehat W}^\pi\) analogously. If \(\|\widehat W-W\|_\infty\le\varepsilon\), then \(\sup_\pi\|J_{\widehat W}^\pi-J_W^\pi\|_\infty\le\gamma^H\varepsilon\). If \(\widehat\pi\) maximizes \(J_{\widehat W}^\pi(s)\) and \(\pi^*\) maximizes \(J_W^\pi(s)\), then \(J_W^{\pi^*}(s)-J_W^{\widehat\pi}(s)\le2\gamma^H\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniformly accurate terminal continuation approximation contributes at most its discounted error, while optimizing against it loses at most twice that amount.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\gamma\le1\).
\(\|\widehat W-W\|_\infty\le\varepsilon<\infty\).
The relevant policy maxima are attained.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Policy Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric state-dependent representation of a policy using a finite acquisition portfolio.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_1,\ldots,a_J\) be acquisition functions defined on belief states and feasible actions. A state-dependent portfolio representation is \[\pi_\theta(s)\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X(s)}\sum_{j=1}^J w_j(s;\theta)a_j(s,x),\] where \(w_j(s;\theta)\ge 0\) and \(\sum_{j=1}^Jw_j(s;\theta)=1\). The parameters \(\theta\) may be fitted by minimizing an empirical policy loss \(\widehat L(\theta)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N\ell(\pi_\theta(s_i),x_i^*)\). This representation includes fixed mixtures and state-dependent acquisition selection as restricted cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent a policy by a state-dependent weighted acquisition portfolio and fit its parameters against target decisions or policy loss.
assumptions_latex: Every \(a_j(s,\cdot)\) is defined on \(\mathcal X(s)\).
The portfolio maximizer exists for each represented state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_\theta(s)\) is a feasible policy determined by normalized state-dependent acquisition weights.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic policy-function-approximation locator does not yet establish the specific normalized acquisition-portfolio representation, empirical fitting formula, or claimed restricted cases. A directly supporting source is needed.

children.title: Acquisition Mixtures
children.top_down_role: Policies combining contributions from multiple acquisition criteria.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of invariance under componentwise rescaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=\{x,y\}\), let \(a_1(x)=1,a_1(y)=0\), \(a_2(x)=0,a_2(y)=2\), and use equal weights. The mixture selects \(y\); replacing \(a_1\) by \(3a_1\) makes it select \(x\), although \(a_1\)'s own ranking is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rescaling one component can reverse a weighted-mixture decision.
assumptions_latex: Equal weights and no compensating normalization are used.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted-Sum Mixtures Are Scale Sensitive

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-declared convex scalarization of acquisitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For acquisitions \(a_k\), positive scales \(s_k\), offsets \(b_k\), and \(w\in\Delta_K\), define \(a_w(x)=\sum_{k=1}^K w_k(a_k(x)-b_k)/s_k\). The normalization parameters are part of the policy because independent positive rescaling generally changes an unnormalized weighted-sum maximizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic acquisition mixture must declare component normalization because its compromise depends on scale.
assumptions_latex: \(K<\infty\), \(w\in\Delta_K\), and \(s_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Deterministic Acquisition Scalarization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive-Weight Mixture Maximizers Are Pareto Undominated
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nondominance property of deterministic scalarization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every \(w_k>0\) and \(x^\star\) maximizes \(\sum_k w_ka_k(x)\), no \(y\) can satisfy \(a_k(y)\ge a_k(x^\star)\) for all \(k\) with strict inequality for at least one component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A maximizer of a strictly positive weighted sum cannot be dominated in all acquisition components.
assumptions_latex: All weights are strictly positive.
The weighted-sum maximum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in X}\sum_k w_ka_k(x)\Rightarrow x^\star\text{ is Pareto undominated}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Weight Mixture Maximizers Are Pareto Undominated

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Proposal Law of a Randomized Acquisition Mixture
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Categorical randomization among finitely many acquisition-policy proposal laws.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_k(\cdot\mid D)\) be Borel proposal probability kernels on a common topological design space and let \(w\in\Delta_K\). Drawing \(J\sim\operatorname{Categorical}(w)\) and then drawing a proposal from \(Q_J(\cdot\mid D)\) induces \[Q_w(\cdot\mid D)=\sum_{k=1}^K w_kQ_k(\cdot\mid D).\] Its support is \[\operatorname{supp}Q_w(\cdot\mid D)=\overline{\bigcup_{k:w_k>0}\operatorname{supp}Q_k(\cdot\mid D)}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Categorical randomization among acquisition policies produces the weighted mixture of their proposal laws and the closed union of their positively weighted supports.
assumptions_latex: \(K<\infty\) and \(w\in\Delta_K\).
All components define Borel proposal kernels on the same topological design space.

notation.meaning: Proposal law induced by component acquisition policy k.
Proposal law induced by categorical randomization.

knowledge_statements.title: Proposal Law of a Randomized Acquisition Mixture

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Averaged-Acquisition Maximization Can Propose a Point Never Chosen by Its Components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit separation of deterministic scalarization from categorical randomization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal X=\{x,y,z\}\), use weights \(w_1=w_2=1/2\), and define
\[a_1(x)=2,\quad a_1(y)=0,\quad a_1(z)=1.1,\]
\[a_2(x)=0,\quad a_2(y)=2,\quad a_2(z)=1.1.\]
The component maximizers are uniquely \(x\) and \(y\), so categorical randomization induces \(\tfrac12\delta_x+\tfrac12\delta_y\). The averaged acquisition has values \(1,1,1.1\) at \(x,y,z\), respectively, and therefore uniquely proposes \(z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two acquisitions can individually choose x and y while their average uniquely chooses a third point z, so randomization and scalarization have different proposal laws.
assumptions_latex: The displayed finite design space and acquisition values are used.
Both components receive weight one half.

notation.meaning: proposal law under categorical component selection
proposal law obtained by maximizing the averaged acquisition

knowledge_statements.title: Averaged-Acquisition Maximization Can Propose a Point Never Chosen by Its Components

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Agreement Criterion for Deterministic and Randomized Acquisition Mixtures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes equality of proposal laws after component and mixture tie rules are fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(s_k(D)\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}a_k(x;D)\) be measurable tie-broken component proposals, let \(w\in\Delta_K\), and let
\[s_w(D)\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}\sum_{k=1}^K w_ka_k(x;D).\]
Conditional on \(D\), deterministic scalarization has proposal law \(\delta_{s_w(D)}\), whereas categorical randomization has law \(\sum_k w_k\delta_{s_k(D)}\). These laws are equal if and only if
\[s_k(D)=s_w(D)\quad\text{for every }k\text{ with }w_k>0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted-average acquisition and categorical randomization induce the same proposal law exactly when every positively weighted component proposes the weighted-average maximizer.
assumptions_latex: \(K<\infty\) and \(w\in\Delta_K\).
All component and scalarized argmax selections use declared measurable tie rules.

notation.meaning: tie-broken proposal of component acquisition k
tie-broken proposal of the weighted acquisition

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Agreement Criterion for Deterministic and Randomized Acquisition Mixtures
Acquisition Mixtures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex randomization or scalarization of finitely many Bayesian-optimization acquisitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_1,\ldots,a_K:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) be acquisition functions and let \(w=(w_1,\ldots,w_K)\) lie in the probability simplex \(\Delta_K\). Their deterministic mixture is \[a_w(x)=\sum_{k=1}^K w_k a_k(x),\qquad x\in\mathcal X,\] and selects any \(x^+\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}a_w(x)\). A randomized mixture instead draws \(J\sim\operatorname{Categorical}(w)\) and selects from \(\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}a_J(x)\). These policies generally differ because maximizing an average acquisition is not equivalent to randomizing among its individual maximizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixture either maximizes a convex combination of acquisitions or randomly chooses one acquisition and maximizes it; these two policies need not agree.
assumptions_latex: \(K<\infty\) and \(w_k\ge 0\) with \(\sum_{k=1}^K w_k=1\).
Each displayed argmax is nonempty or an explicit approximate maximizer is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_w\) and the categorical rule define two distinct acquisition-mixture policies.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the leaf, but the cited general policy-function section does not specifically support Bayesian-optimization acquisition mixtures. Moreover, the conclusion calls the two policies distinct without qualification, although they can coincide in special cases; it should say generally nonequivalent.

children.title: Acquisition Portfolios
