knowledge_statements.statement_title: Acquisition Portfolio as a Finite Expert Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Collection of separately identifiable acquisition policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An acquisition portfolio is a finite family \(\Pi=\{\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_K\}\), where each \(\pi_k\) maps the current Bayesian-optimization state to an eligible action or action distribution. A manager chooses among experts or their proposals while retaining their separate identities and feedback records.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An acquisition portfolio maintains distinct acquisition policies as competing experts.
assumptions_latex: \(K<\infty\).
Each expert returns an eligible action or a distribution supported on eligible actions.
knowledge_statements.title: Acquisition Portfolio as a Finite Expert Set

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Counterfactual Expert Rewards Are Not Automatically Observed
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feedback boundary when only one proposal is evaluated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If expert \(k\) proposes \(x_{t,k}\) but only \(x_{t,J_t}\) is evaluated, the realized objective reward at an unchosen distinct proposal is unobserved. Treating predictions at unchosen points as realized rewards changes the feedback model and requires separate justification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One evaluated proposal does not reveal the objective rewards of distinct unchosen portfolio proposals.
assumptions_latex: Only one proposed candidate is evaluated.
At least one unchosen expert proposes a distinct candidate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{t,k}\text{ is not observed for }k\ne J_t\text{ merely from observing }r_{t,J_t}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Counterfactual Expert Rewards Are Not Automatically Observed

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of expert proposal, manager choice, and feedback attribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At round \(t\), each expert proposes \(x_{t,k}\). The manager forms a history-measurable probability vector \(p_t\), draws \(J_t\sim\operatorname{Categorical}(p_t)\), evaluates \(x_{t,J_t}\), and records feedback under a declared attribution rule. Candidate generation, expert selection, and feedback attribution are distinct stages.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Portfolio experts propose candidates, a manager chooses one, and a declared rule attributes the resulting feedback.
assumptions_latex: Expert proposals and \(p_t\) use only pre-observation information.
The feedback attribution rule is explicitly declared.
knowledge_statements.title: Candidate-Generating Portfolio Round
Acquisition Portfolios
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online allocation among a finite collection of acquisition policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given acquisitions \(a_1,\ldots,a_K\), initialize scores \(G_{1,k}=0\). At round \(t\), form \[p_{t,k}=\frac{\exp(\eta G_{t,k})}{\sum_{j=1}^K\exp(\eta G_{t,j})},\] draw \(J_t\sim\operatorname{Categorical}(p_t)\), and evaluate \(x_t\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}a_{J_t,t}(x)\). After observing a bounded reward vector \(r_t\), update \(G_{t+1,k}=G_{t,k}+r_{t,k}\). Stop at the evaluation budget and return the best incumbent under the chosen objective convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An acquisition portfolio adaptively samples policies using exponential weights, updates their scores from bounded rewards, and returns the final incumbent.
assumptions_latex: The portfolio contains finitely many acquisitions and \(\eta>0\).
Rewards satisfy \(r_{t,k}\in[0,1]\); unobserved rewards require an explicitly specified estimator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recursion defines a budget-limited adaptive acquisition-portfolio policy.

notation.meaning: Probability of selecting acquisition k at round t.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits an acquisition-portfolio leaf, but the cited hybrid value-policy iteration section does not establish this exponential-weights Bayesian-optimization algorithm. The record also alternates between full reward-vector feedback and an unspecified estimator for unobserved rewards, so an authoritative portfolio source and a fixed feedback variant are required.

children.title: Learned Policy Selection
children.top_down_role: Data-driven selection among candidate acquisition policies during search.

knowledge_statements.title: Learned Policy Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Context-dependent selection among acquisition policies using learned predicted utility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_1,\ldots,a_K\) be candidate acquisitions and let \(s_t\) summarize the posterior and evaluation history at round \(t\). Given learned utility predictors \(q_{t,k}(s_t)\), choose \[J_t\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{1\le k\le K}\{q_{t,k}(s_t)+b_{t,k}(s_t)\},\qquad x_t\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}a_{J_t,t}(x),\] where \(b_{t,k}\) is an optional exploration bonus. Observe the evaluation outcome, construct a declared utility target, update the selected predictor, and repeat until the evaluation budget is exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A learned selector maps the current optimization state to a policy choice, optionally adds exploration, and updates from observed utility.
assumptions_latex: The state representation and utility target are measurable and fixed by the implementation.
Every maximization uses a stated tie-breaking or approximation rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recursion defines a context-dependent learned acquisition-selection policy.

notation.meaning: Posterior and history state at round t.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the cited broad policy-approximation section does not support this learned acquisition selector. The utility target, predictor update, and exploration rule remain implementation placeholders whose mathematically intended variant requires a specific source.

children.title: Expected Improvement

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Expected improvement as expected marginal simple reward
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines expected improvement as the conditional expected change in the maximum posterior mean caused by evaluating a candidate point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal D'\) be the random dataset resulting from evaluating \(x\), conditional on the current data \(\mathcal D\). For simple reward, expected improvement is
\[
\alpha_{\mathrm{EI}}(x;\mathcal D)=\mathbb E\!\left[\max_{x'}\mu_{\mathcal D'}(x')\mid x,\mathcal D\right]-\max_{x'}\mu_{\mathcal D}(x').
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected improvement at a proposed point is the conditional expected maximum posterior mean after its evaluation minus the current maximum posterior mean.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal D'\text{ is the random posterior update produced by evaluating }x\text{ conditional on }\mathcal D.
\text{Utility is measured by the maximum posterior mean (simple reward).}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha_{\mathrm{EI}}(x;\mathcal D)=\mathbb E[\max_{x'}\mu_{\mathcal D'}(x')\mid x,\mathcal D]-\max_{x'}\mu_{\mathcal D}(x').

When the improvement region is represented using the stated truncated-normal structure, this expectation can be evaluated in closed form. A Bayesian-optimization policy that scores candidates by this expectation is called Expected Improvement.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Expected Improvement as One-Step Gain in Simple-Reward Utility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Risk-neutral Bayesian optimization with simple-reward utility, one-step lookahead, and a final recommendation selected by posterior mean.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the simple-reward utility of a dataset by \(u(\mathcal D)=\max_{\mathbf x}\mu_{\mathcal D}(\mathbf x)\). If evaluating a proposed location \(x\) yields \(y\sim p(y\mid x,\mathcal D)\) and the augmented dataset is \(\mathcal D'\), then the expected-improvement acquisition is
\[\alpha_{\mathrm{EI}}(x;\mathcal D)=\int \max_{\mathbf x'}\mu_{\mathcal D'}(\mathbf x')\,p(y\mid x,\mathcal D)\,\mathrm dy-\max_{\mathbf x}\mu_{\mathcal D}(\mathbf x)=\mathbb E_{y\mid x,\mathcal D}[u(\mathcal D')]-u(\mathcal D).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With risk-neutral simple-reward utility, a dataset is valued by the largest posterior mean available for the final recommendation. Expected improvement at a proposed evaluation location is the predictive expected value of that utility after the observation minus its current value.
assumptions_latex: u(\mathcal D)=\max_{\mathbf x}\mu_{\mathcal D}(\mathbf x)
\mathcal D'\text{ is }\mathcal D\text{ augmented by the observation }(x,y)
y\sim p(y\mid x,\mathcal D)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha_{\mathrm{EI}}(x;\mathcal D)=\mathbb E_{y\mid x,\mathcal D}[u(\mathcal D')]-u(\mathcal D)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotonicity and Positivity of Gaussian Expected Improvement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Analytic properties of deterministic-observation Gaussian EI.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a=f_n^*-\mu\), \(\sigma>0\), \(z=a/\sigma\), and \[E(a,\sigma)=a\Phi(z)+\sigma\phi(z).\] Then \[\frac{\partial E}{\partial a}=\Phi(z),\qquad \frac{\partial E}{\partial\mu}=-\Phi(z),\qquad \frac{\partial E}{\partial\sigma}=\phi(z)>0.\] Hence EI increases with \(f_n^*-\mu\), decreases with the predictive mean for minimization, and strictly increases with predictive standard deviation. Moreover, \(E(a,\sigma)>0\) for every finite \(a\) when \(\sigma>0\); at \(\sigma=0\), EI equals \(a_+\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gaussian EI favors both lower predicted values and greater uncertainty and is positive wherever predictive variance is nonzero.
assumptions_latex: f_n^*,\mu\in\mathbb R.
\sigma>0\text{ for the derivative identities}.

notation.meaning: Predicted improvement margin f_n^* minus mu.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity and Positivity of Gaussian Expected Improvement

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounds separating deterministic predicted improvement from the contribution of Gaussian uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a=f_n^*-\mu\), let \(Z\sim N(0,1)\), and define \(E(a,\sigma)=\mathbb E[(a-\sigma Z)_+]\) for \(\sigma\ge0\). Then \[a_+\le E(a,\sigma)\le a_++\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{2\pi}}.\] The lower bound is an equality when \(\sigma=0\); for \(\sigma>0\), \(E(a,\sigma)>a_+\) for every finite \(a\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gaussian EI is at least the positive predicted improvement and strictly exceeds it under nonzero uncertainty; the additional contribution is at most sigma divided by the square root of two pi.
assumptions_latex: \(a\in\mathbb R\).
\(\sigma\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Expected positive improvement under a Gaussian predictive error.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounds for Gaussian Expected Improvement

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Deterministic-Observation EI Policy with Approximate Maximization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and additive-approximate maximization of noiseless expected improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact EI policy selects \(x_{n+1}\in\arg\max_{x\in\mathcal X}\operatorname{EI}_n(x)\). An additive-\(\varepsilon_n\) implementation may return any \(x_{n+1}\) satisfying \[\operatorname{EI}_n(x_{n+1})\ge\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}\operatorname{EI}_n(x)-\varepsilon_n.\] This controls acquisition-value error only and does not certify objective regret or distance to an objective optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The policy maximizes noiseless EI; approximate maximization certifies only an acquisition-value gap.
assumptions_latex: \operatorname{EI}_n\text{ exists on }\mathcal X.
\varepsilon_n\ge0.
knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic-Observation EI Policy with Approximate Maximization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expectation definition and Gaussian closed form for noiseless one-point minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With exact observations, let \(f_n^*=\min_{i\le n}f(x_i)\). If \(f(x)\mid\mathcal D_n\sim N(\mu_n(x),\sigma_n^2(x))\), then \[\operatorname{EI}_n(x)=\mathbb E[(f_n^*-f(x))_+\mid\mathcal D_n]=(f_n^*-\mu_n(x))\Phi(z_n(x))+\sigma_n(x)\phi(z_n(x)),\] where \(z_n(x)=(f_n^*-\mu_n(x))/\sigma_n(x)\) for \(\sigma_n(x)>0\). When \(\sigma_n(x)=0\), \(\operatorname{EI}_n(x)=(f_n^*-\mu_n(x))_+\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noiseless EI is the posterior expected decrease below the best exact observation and has a Gaussian closed form.
assumptions_latex: The objective is minimized and observations defining the incumbent are exact.
f(x)\mid\mathcal D_n\text{ is Gaussian at the candidate point}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{EI}_n(x)=\mathbb E[(f_n^*-f(x))_+\mid\mathcal D_n]\text{ with the displayed zero-variance convention}.

notation.meaning: Standard normal distribution and density functions.

knowledge_statements.title: Gaussian Deterministic-Observation Expected Improvement
Deterministic-Observation Expected Improvement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form one-step expected improvement for noiseless minimization under a Gaussian predictive law.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the noiseless incumbent be \(f_n^*=\min_{1\le i\le n}f(x_i)\), and suppose \(f(x)\mid\mathcal D_n\sim N(\mu_n(x),\sigma_n^2(x))\). For minimization, \[\operatorname{EI}_n(x)=\mathbb E_n[(f_n^*-f(x))_+]=(f_n^*-\mu_n(x))\Phi(z_n(x))+\sigma_n(x)\phi(z_n(x)),\] where \(z_n(x)=(f_n^*-\mu_n(x))/\sigma_n(x)\) when \(\sigma_n(x)>0\). If \(\sigma_n(x)=0\), define \(\operatorname{EI}_n(x)=(f_n^*-\mu_n(x))_+\). The next point maximizes \(\operatorname{EI}_n\) over the design domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noiseless expected improvement is the posterior mean positive decrease below the best observed value, with a closed form under Gaussian prediction.
assumptions_latex: Objective observations are exact and the problem is minimization.
The conditional predictive distribution at each candidate is Gaussian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed Gaussian formula equals \(\mathbb E_n[(f_n^*-f(x))_+]\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Improvement, probability of improvement, and expected improvement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic-observation improvement acquisitions for minimizing an expensive black-box objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given data D_n and the best observed value f_{\min}^n=\min\{y_1,\ldots,y_n\}, define I(x)=\max\{0,f_{\min}^n-Y(x)\}, where Y(x)\mid D_n is the predictive response. Then \operatorname{PI}(x)=\Pr(Y(x)<f_{\min}^n\mid D_n) and \operatorname{EI}(x)=\mathbb E[I(x)\mid D_n]. For predictive draws y^{(t)}, Monte Carlo estimates are T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbf 1\{y^{(t)}<f_{\min}^n\} and T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\max\{0,f_{\min}^n-y^{(t)}\}. If Y(x)\mid D_n\sim\mathcal N(\mu_n(x),\sigma_n^2(x)) with \sigma_n(x)>0 and z=(f_{\min}^n-\mu_n(x))/\sigma_n(x), then \operatorname{PI}(x)=\Phi(z) and \operatorname{EI}(x)=(f_{\min}^n-\mu_n(x))\Phi(z)+\sigma_n(x)\phi(z).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Improvement is the positive amount by which a predictive response beats the best observed value. Probability of improvement measures the chance of doing so, and expected improvement measures its expected magnitude. Both can be estimated from predictive samples; a nondegenerate Gaussian prediction gives the stated closed forms.
assumptions_latex: f_{\min}^n=\min\{y_1,\ldots,y_n\}
y^{(t)}\text{ are predictive draws from }Y(x)\mid D_n
\mathbb E[I(x)\mid D_n]<\infty\text{ for the expected-improvement Monte Carlo limit}
Y(x)\mid D_n\sim\mathcal N(\mu_n(x),\sigma_n^2(x)),\quad\sigma_n(x)>0\text{ for the Gaussian formulas}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed form, monotonicity, and gradient of noiseless expected improvement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gaussian predictive values, exact observations, and a maximization objective; includes the zero-variance boundary and the spatial gradient when posterior moments are differentiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Y(x)\sim\mathcal N(\mu,\sigma^2)\) be the predictive objective value under exact observations, and let \(\phi^*\) be the best previously observed value. Then
\[
\alpha_{\mathrm{EI}}(x)=\mathbb E[(Y(x)-\phi^*)_+].
\]
For \(\sigma>0\), setting \(z=(\mu-\phi^*)/\sigma\) gives
\[
\alpha_{\mathrm{EI}}(x)=(\mu-\phi^*)\Phi(z)+\sigma\varphi(z),
\quad
\frac{\partial\alpha_{\mathrm{EI}}}{\partial\mu}=\Phi(z)>0,
\quad
\frac{\partial\alpha_{\mathrm{EI}}}{\partial\sigma}=\varphi(z)>0.
\]
For \(\sigma=0\),
\[
\alpha_{\mathrm{EI}}(x)=(\mu-\phi^*)_+.
\]
If \(\mu(x)\) and \(\sigma(x)\) are differentiable and \(\sigma(x)>0\), then
\[
\nabla_x\alpha_{\mathrm{EI}}(x)=\Phi(z)\nabla_x\mu(x)+\varphi(z)\nabla_x\sigma(x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With exact observations and a Gaussian predictive value, expected improvement has the standard normal-CDF/PDF closed form. At positive predictive standard deviation it is strictly increasing in both the predictive mean and standard deviation. At zero variance it equals the positive-part improvement, and its location gradient follows from the chain rule when the posterior moments are differentiable.
assumptions_latex: Y(x)\sim\mathcal N(\mu,\sigma^2).
\phi^*\text{ is the best previously observed objective value}.
\text{The objective is maximized and observations are exact}.
\sigma>0\text{ for the closed-form derivative identities}.
\mu(x),\sigma(x)\text{ are differentiable and }\sigma(x)>0\text{ for the spatial-gradient formula}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected improvement integrating uncertainty in latent values at previously observed noisy sites.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization with noisy data \(\mathcal D_n\), let \(F_{1:n}=(f(x_1),\ldots,f(x_n))\) denote the latent values and define \(M(F_{1:n})=\min_i F_i\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact finite-domain noisy expected improvement via a Gaussian upper envelope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computes the simple-reward definition of noisy expected improvement on a finite terminal-recommendation domain for a Gaussian-process posterior with additive Gaussian observation noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathbf x'=(x'_1,\ldots,x'_n)\) be the finite set over which the terminal posterior mean is maximized. Suppose an evaluation at \(x\) produces
\[
Y\mid x,\mathcal D\sim\mathcal N(\mu,s^2),\qquad s>0.
\]
Define
\[
\mu^*=\max_i\mu_{\mathcal D}(x'_i),\qquad
\mathbf a=\mu_{\mathcal D}(\mathbf x'),\qquad
\mathbf b=\frac{K_{\mathcal D}(\mathbf x',x)}{s}.
\]
Writing \(Y=\mu+sZ\), where \(Z\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), yields
\[
\mu_{\mathcal D'}(\mathbf x')=\mathbf a+\mathbf bZ,
\qquad
\alpha_{\mathrm{EI}}(x;\mathcal D)=g(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)-\mu^*,
\]
with
\[
g(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)=\mathbb E\!\left[\max_i(a_i+b_iZ)\right].
\]
Delete lines that never attain the upper envelope and order the remaining lines by increasing slope. If line \(i\) dominates on \((c_i,c_{i+1})\), with \(c_1=-\infty\) and \(c_{m+1}=+\infty\), then
\[
g(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\left\{a_i[\Phi(c_{i+1})-\Phi(c_i)]+b_i[\varphi(c_i)-\varphi(c_{i+1})]\right\}.
\]
The envelope preprocessing takes \(\mathcal O(n\log n)\) time. The value is invariant under a common permutation of \(\mathbf a,\mathbf b\) and deletion of always-dominated lines, and the expression reduces to noiseless expected improvement when observation noise vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the simple-reward definition on a finite recommendation domain, noisy expected improvement is the expected upper envelope of affine functions of one standard normal variable. Dominated lines are removed, the surviving lines are ordered by slope, and their dominance intervals are integrated in closed form. Preprocessing costs O(n log n), and the expression recovers noiseless expected improvement in the zero-noise limit.
assumptions_latex: \text{The surrogate is a Gaussian process with additive Gaussian observation noise}.
Y\mid x,\mathcal D\sim\mathcal N(\mu,s^2),\quad s>0.
\mathbf x'=(x'_1,\ldots,x'_n)\text{ is the finite terminal-recommendation domain}.
\mu^*=\max_i\mu_{\mathcal D}(x'_i).
\mu_{\mathcal D'}(\mathbf x')=\mu_{\mathcal D}(\mathbf x')+K_{\mathcal D}(\mathbf x',x)(Y-\mu)/s^2.
\text{Noisy expected improvement is defined as expected marginal gain in maximum posterior mean}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected improvement in the noise-free objective relative to a declared conditionally fixed threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_n\) be a finite \(\mathcal D_n\)-measurable incumbent threshold. For minimization, \(\operatorname{LVEI}_n(x;T_n)=\mathbb E[(T_n-f(x))_+\mid\mathcal D_n]\), where \(f(x)\) is the latent objective. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Future-Response Improvement Is a Different Functional
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between latent improvement and improvement in a future noisy observation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Y(x)=f(x)+\varepsilon_x\), then \(\mathbb E[(T_n-Y(x))_+\mid\mathcal D_n]\) is future-response improvement, not LVEI. Under conditionally independent Gaussian noise with variance \(\lambda^2(x)\), it uses predictive variance \(\sigma_n^2(x)+\lambda^2(x)\), whereas LVEI uses latent variance \(\sigma_n^2(x)\); the values need not agree when \(\lambda^2(x)>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Putting future observation noise inside the positive part changes the acquisition and is not latent-value EI.

\varepsilon_x\perp f(x)\mid\mathcal D_n.
f(x)\mid\mathcal D_n\sim N(\mu_n(x),\sigma_n^2(x)).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_n\) be a posterior-random incumbent, \(b_n\) a \(\mathcal D_n\)-measurable plug-in value, and \(Z_x\) the candidate latent value. Define \(\alpha_{\mathrm{plug}}(x)=\mathbb E[(b_n-Z_x)_+\mid\mathcal D_n]\) and \(\alpha_{\mathrm{joint}}(x)=\mathbb E[(B_n-Z_x)_+\mid\mathcal D_n]\). The tower-property form \(\mathbb E_{B_n\mid\mathcal D_n}[\mathbb E[(B_n-Z_x)_+\mid B_n,\mathcal D_n]]\) equals \(\alpha_{\mathrm{joint}}\) only when the inner conditional law retains the joint posterior dependence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternative deterministic and posterior-integrated treatments of an uncertain minimization incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_n\) be a posterior random incumbent and let \(b_n\) be a data-measurable point estimate. Three distinct treatments are \[\alpha_{\mathrm{plug}}(x)=\mathbb E[(b_n-f(x))_+\mid\mathcal D_n],\qquad \alpha_{\mathrm{joint}}(x)=\mathbb E[(B_n-f(x))_+\mid\mathcal D_n],\] and \[\alpha_{\mathrm{cond}}(x)=\mathbb E_{B_n\mid\mathcal D_n}\!\left[\mathbb E[(B_n-f(x))_+\mid B_n,\mathcal D_n]\right].\] The latter two are equal when the conditional law preserves the joint posterior dependence; independently resampling \(B_n\) and \(f(x)\) generally changes the acquisition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Marginal Bounds and Symmetry of Joint Batch Expected Improvement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distribution-free structural properties of correlated batch improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_j=(f_n^*-Y_j)_+\) be posterior-integrable batch improvements and let \[Q=\mathbb E[\max_{1\leq j\leq q}I_j\mid\mathcal D_n].\] Then \[\max_{1\leq j\leq q}\mathbb E[I_j\mid\mathcal D_n]\leq Q\leq\sum_{j=1}^q\mathbb E[I_j\mid\mathcal D_n].\] Moreover, \(Q\) is invariant under permutations of the batch and equals ordinary one-point expected improvement when \(q=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint batch EI lies between the largest marginal EI and their sum, is permutation invariant, and reduces to ordinary EI for a singleton batch.
assumptions_latex: I_1,\ldots,I_q\text{ are posterior integrable}.
q\geq1.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Joint Batch EI Depends on Cross-Covariance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two Gaussian batches with identical marginal predictive distributions but different joint expected improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the minimization incumbent be \(f_n^*=0\), and let both batch members have marginal law \(N(0,1)\). In batch \(A\), take \((Y_1,Y_2)=(Z,Z)\); in batch \(B\), take \((Y_1,Y_2)=(Z,-Z)\), where \(Z\sim N(0,1)\). Then \[q\operatorname{EI}(A)=\mathbb E[(-Z)_+]=\frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}},\qquad q\operatorname{EI}(B)=\mathbb E|Z|=\sqrt{\frac2\pi}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identical marginal predictions do not determine joint batch EI: perfect positive and perfect negative dependence give different values.
assumptions_latex: Z\sim N(0,1).
The batch utility is the maximum positive improvement among its members.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value comparison when an additional candidate is appended to a joint-EI batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_j=(f_n^*-Y_j)_+\) be posterior-integrable improvements and define \(Q_q=\mathbb E[\max_{1\leq j\leq q}I_j\mid\mathcal D_n]\). After appending a candidate with improvement \(I_{q+1}\), \[Q_{q+1}\geq Q_q.\] Equality holds if and only if \[I_{q+1}\leq\max_{1\leq j\leq q}I_j\quad\text{almost surely conditional on }\mathcal D_n.\]

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributional representation of expected best positive improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_X=\max_{1\le j\le q}(f_n^*-Y_j)_+\) be posterior integrable. Then \[q\operatorname{EI}_n(X)=\mathbb E_n[M_X]=\int_0^\infty\mathbb P_n(M_X>u)\,du=\int_0^\infty\left[1-\mathbb P_n\!\left(Y_j\ge f_n^*-u\ \forall j\right)\right]du.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint batch EI equals the integral of the posterior probability that at least one batch member improves the incumbent by more than each positive amount.
assumptions_latex: \(M_X\ge0\) is posterior integrable.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diminishing returns of joint expected improvement over a finite candidate ground set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be finite and let \(I_x\ge0\), \(x\in V\), be jointly distributed posterior-integrable improvements. Define \(F(\varnothing)=0\) and \(F(S)=\mathbb E_n[\max_{x\in S}I_x]\) for nonempty \(S\). With \(M_A=\max_{x\in A}I_x\) and the convention \(M_\varnothing=0\), \[F(A\cup\{e\})-F(A)=\mathbb E_n[(I_e-M_A)_+].\] Hence, for \(A\subseteq B\subseteq V\) and \(e\notin B\), \[F(A\cup\{e\})-F(A)\ge F(B\cup\{e\})-F(B).\] Thus \(F\) is monotone and submodular without an independence assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected best improvement has diminishing returns as candidates are added, even when their predictive outcomes are dependent.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite.
\((I_x)_{x\in V}\) are jointly defined, nonnegative, and posterior integrable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A\subseteq B,\ e\notin B\Rightarrow F(A\cup\{e\})-F(A)\ge F(B\cup\{e\})-F(B).

Joint Batch Expected Improvement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step expected improvement from evaluating a correlated batch simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For noiseless minimization with incumbent \(f_n^*\), the joint expected improvement of a batch \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_q)\in\mathcal X^q\) is \[q\operatorname{EI}_n(X)=\mathbb E_n\!\left[\left(f_n^*-\min_{1\le j\le q}f(x_j)\right)_+\right].\] Equivalently, \[q\operatorname{EI}_n(X)=\mathbb E_n\!\left[\max_{1\le j\le q}(f_n^*-f(x_j))_+\right].\] The expectation is taken under the joint posterior predictive law of the batch, including cross-covariances. A joint batch-EI policy chooses a maximizing or declared approximate-maximizing element of \(\mathcal X^q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint batch EI is the expected best improvement among all batch members under their correlated joint posterior predictive distribution.
assumptions_latex: The incumbent is exactly known and the objective is minimized.
The batch positive-part improvement is posterior integrable.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical deterministic-proxy variants of greedy sequential batch construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a(x;\mathcal D)\) be a one-point acquisition and \(q\geq1\). Starting with \(\mathcal D^{(0)}=\mathcal D_n\), for \(j=1,\ldots,q\) choose \[x_j\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}a(x;\mathcal D^{(j-1)}).\] Kriging believer uses \(\widetilde y_j=\mu^{(j-1)}(x_j)\); constant liar uses a prespecified constant \(\widetilde y_j=L\). Set \(\mathcal D^{(j)}=\mathcal D^{(j-1)}\cup\{(x_j,\widetilde y_j)\}\) and output \((x_1,\ldots,x_q)\). Temporary proxy observations are discarded when the actual concurrent outcomes arrive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Kriging believer uses the current posterior mean as each temporary outcome, whereas constant liar uses a fixed declared value.
assumptions_latex: q\geq1.
Each acquisition argmax is attained.
The surrogate admits the stated temporary updates.
L\text{ is fixed before constant-liar construction}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x_1,\ldots,x_q)\text{ is a deterministic greedy proxy batch conditional on tie rules}.

notation.meaning: Constant proxy response used by constant liar.
Temporary augmented data after j greedy selections.

knowledge_statements.title: Kriging-Believer and Constant-Liar Batch Approximations

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Proxy and Ordering Dependence of Sequential Batch Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on interpreting greedy proxy batches as solutions of joint batch expected improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q=1\), sequential batch construction returns a maximizer of its underlying one-point acquisition. For \(q>1\), later choices depend on earlier tie rules, selection order, and fantasy or proxy outcomes through the temporary posterior. Without an additional equivalence theorem, the resulting batch cannot be asserted to maximize joint batch expected improvement, and changing the proxy rule can change the unordered selected set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singleton greedy batch agrees with the one-point acquisition, but larger batches depend on ordering and proxy choices and need not maximize joint q-EI.
assumptions_latex: q>1\text{ for the non-equivalence boundary}.
Temporary posterior updates affect subsequent acquisition values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Greedy sequential construction does not by itself certify joint-qEI optimality}.
knowledge_statements.title: Proxy and Ordering Dependence of Sequential Batch Construction
Sequential Batch Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy construction of a batch using fantasies or deterministic surrogate updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given data \(\mathcal D_n\), batch size \(q\), and a one-point acquisition \(a\), set \(P_0=\varnothing\). For \(j=1,\ldots,q\), choose \[x_j\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}a(x;\mathcal D_n,P_{j-1}),\] assign a fantasy or deterministic proxy response \(\widetilde y_j\) at \(x_j\), update \(P_j=P_{j-1}\cup\{(x_j,\widetilde y_j)\}\), and recompute the acquisition conditional on the augmented state. Output \((x_1,\ldots,x_q)\) for concurrent evaluation. The fantasy law or proxy rule is part of the algorithm and determines the approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sequential batch approximation greedily adds points, temporarily conditions on fantasy or proxy outcomes, and dispatches the completed batch concurrently.
assumptions_latex: A batch size \(q\ge1\) and a one-point acquisition are specified.
Each fantasy distribution or proxy-response rule is declared before batch construction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recursion returns a greedy approximate batch without directly maximizing joint batch expected improvement.

notation.meaning: Temporary pending-point data after j selections.

children.title: Parallel Expected-Improvement Execution
children.top_down_role: Expected-improvement policies adapted to simultaneous evaluation capacity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Duplicate Dispatch When Pending Evaluations Are Ignored
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of parallel EI dispatch without pending-point exclusion or conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose no completed observation arrives between two worker-dispatch events, \(\alpha(x;\mathcal D)\) is recomputed from completed data only, and \[\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}\alpha(x;\mathcal D)=\{x^*\}.\] If pending locations are neither excluded from the feasible set nor incorporated into \(\alpha\), both dispatches select \(x^*\). Distinct proposals therefore require an explicit replication policy, pending-point exclusion, or a pending-aware acquisition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If neither the data nor acquisition changes between dispatches, multiple workers select the same unique EI maximizer unless pending points are handled explicitly.
assumptions_latex: \operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}\alpha(x;\mathcal D)=\{x^*\}.
\mathcal D\text{ is unchanged between dispatches}.
Pending sites affect neither the acquisition nor the feasible set.

notation.meaning: Unique acquisition maximizer under unchanged completed data.

knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate Dispatch When Pending Evaluations Are Ignored

knowledge_statements.scope_note: State invariant for synchronous or asynchronous EI execution with a finite worker pool.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_k\) be the set of pending evaluation jobs immediately after event \(k\), and let the worker capacity be \(q\in\mathbb N\). A dispatch event is permitted only when \(|P_k|<q\) and changes the state to \(P_{k+1}=P_k\cup\{j\}\) for one newly launched job \(j\). A completion event for \(j\in P_k\) changes it to \(P_{k+1}=P_k\setminus\{j\}\). If \(|P_0|\le q\), then \[0\le |P_k|\le q\qquad\text{for every event }k.\] If locations already represented in \(P_k\) are ineligible unless a replication flag is set, simultaneous duplicate locations can occur only through the declared replication policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Capacity-checked dispatch and completion transitions keep the number of running evaluations at most q, while pending-location exclusion makes duplicate dispatch an explicit replication decision.
assumptions_latex: \(q\in\mathbb N\).
A dispatch occurs only when \(|P_k|<q\).
A completion removes exactly one pending job.
A pending location is ineligible for dispatch unless replication is explicitly enabled.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall k:\ |P_k|\le q\), and undeclared simultaneous duplicate locations are impossible.

notation.meaning: Pending evaluation jobs after execution event k.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Dispatch Capacity Invariant

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact accounting identity and overshoot boundary for parallel evaluation budgets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At execution event \(k\), let \(L_k\) be the number of launched jobs, \(C_k\) the number completed, and \(P_k\) the pending-job set, with every launched job classified as exactly one of completed or pending. Then \[L_k=C_k+|P_k|.\] Consequently, enforcing \(L_k\leq B\) prevents commitments beyond a launch budget \(B\). If only completed jobs are counted and worker capacity is \(q\), up to \(q\) additional jobs may already be committed when \(C_k=B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Launched jobs equal completed plus pending jobs; a completed-only budget can overlook up to q outstanding commitments.
assumptions_latex: Every launched job is classified as exactly one of completed or pending.
At most \(q\) jobs are pending concurrently.

notation.meaning: Numbers of launched and completed evaluation jobs after event k.

knowledge_statements.title: Launched-Completed-Pending Budget Ledger

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Execution-time consequence of waiting for every job in an EI-selected batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a synchronous batch of \(q\) evaluations is launched simultaneously at time zero with nonnegative completion times \(T_1,\ldots,T_q\), and no new EI decision is made until all results arrive. The next posterior update using the full batch and the next batch dispatch cannot occur before \[T_{\mathrm{barrier}}=\max_{1\le j\le q}T_j.\] If some worker finishes at \(\min_jT_j<T_{\mathrm{barrier}}\), that worker is idle until the barrier unless work outside the synchronous policy is assigned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A synchronous parallel-EI batch advances only when its slowest evaluation finishes, potentially leaving faster workers idle.
assumptions_latex: All q jobs are launched together.
The policy waits for every batch result before its next EI construction.
Completion times are nonnegative.

notation.meaning: Time at which every job in the synchronous batch has completed.

knowledge_statements.title: Synchronous Batch Barrier Completion Time

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier-synchronized execution of a declared batch-EI proposal under a launch budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let worker capacity be \(q\), completed data be \(\mathcal D_k\), and remaining launch budget be \(b_k\). At synchronization epoch \(k\), set \(r_k=\min\{q,b_k\}\). If \(r_k>0\), compute a declared exact or approximate maximizer \(X_k=(x_{k,1},\ldots,x_{k,r_k})\) of the chosen \(r_k\)-point expected-improvement acquisition, launch all \(r_k\) evaluations simultaneously, and make no further acquisition decision until every member completes. Then set \[\mathcal D_{k+1}=\mathcal D_k\cup\{(x_{k,j},y_{k,j}):1\le j\le r_k\},\qquad b_{k+1}=b_k-r_k.\] Stop launching when \(b_k=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Synchronous parallel EI chooses a batch, launches it together, waits for every result, updates once, and repeats without exceeding the launch budget.
assumptions_latex: \(q\in\mathbb N\) and the initial launch budget \(B\) is finite.
The batch-EI acquisition and exact or approximate optimization convention are declared.
Every launched evaluation counted by the loop eventually returns.
The terminal recommendation convention is specified separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_k r_k\le B\), and each new-batch posterior update occurs only after the preceding batch has completed.

notation.meaning: Number of evaluations launched at synchronous epoch k.
Remaining launch budget before epoch k.
EI-selected batch launched at epoch k.

knowledge_statements.title: Synchronous Full-Batch EI Execution

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Immediate worker refill using a declared pending-aware expected-improvement acquisition and a launch budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain completed data \(\mathcal D\), a set of pending jobs \(P\), worker capacity \(q\), launched-job count \(L\), and launch budget \(B\). Initially, and after each completion event, while \(|P|<q\) and \(L<B\), construct the declared pending-aware expected-improvement acquisition \(\alpha(x;\mathcal D,P)\), choose an attained or declared approximate maximizer among eligible locations, launch its evaluation, add its job to \(P\), and increment \(L\). When a job \(j\in P\) completes with result \((x_j,y_j)\), set \(P\leftarrow P\setminus\{j\}\), append \((x_j,y_j)\) to \(\mathcal D\), update the surrogate, and refill the freed capacity by the same loop. Stop launching when \(L=B\), and form the declared terminal recommendation after all counted pending jobs required by the reporting convention finish.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Asynchronous parallel EI updates on each completion and immediately refills available capacity using a specified pending-aware EI rule while respecting the launch budget.
assumptions_latex: \(q\in\mathbb N\) and \(B<\infty\).
The pending-aware acquisition, eligibility rule, tie-breaking, and approximate-optimization convention are declared.
A dispatch occurs only when \(|P|<q\) and \(L<B\).
Each completion identifies its pending job and supplies the observation needed for the surrogate update.
The terminal treatment of still-pending jobs is declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\le |P|\le q,\qquad L\le B,\qquad\text{and every available worker is refilled after a completion whenever }L<B.

notation.meaning: Number of jobs launched under the counted budget.

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Completion-Triggered EI Execution

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Event-time characterization of asynchronous execution with pending evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(m\ge1\) EI-selected evaluations are pending at time \(s\), their residual completion times are \(T_1,\ldots,T_m\ge0\), and the asynchronous policy updates its posterior and refills available capacity immediately after the first completion. Ignoring policy-computation latency, the next update and refill event occurs at \[s+\min_{1\le j\le m}T_j.\] A full barrier using all \(m\) results cannot occur before \(s+\max_jT_j\). This execution-time comparison does not order the policies' statistical solution quality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Asynchronous EI can update and refill at the first pending completion instead of waiting for the slowest job; this is not a regret comparison.
assumptions_latex: At least one evaluation is pending.
A completion immediately triggers updating and refill.
Policy-computation latency is ignored in the displayed times.
The stated residual completion times are finite.

notation.meaning: Residual completion time of pending job j.

knowledge_statements.title: Completion-Triggered Refill Time
Parallel Expected-Improvement Execution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asynchronous or synchronous dispatch of expected-improvement-selected evaluations to parallel workers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain completed data \(\mathcal D_t\), pending locations \(P_t\), and at most \(q\) workers. Whenever a worker is available, construct an expected-improvement acquisition \(\alpha_t(x;\mathcal D_t,P_t)\), choose \(x_t\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X\setminus P_t}\alpha_t(x;\mathcal D_t,P_t)\), dispatch its evaluation, and add \(x_t\) to \(P_t\). Upon completion, remove the point from \(P_t\), append its observation to \(\mathcal D_t\), and update the posterior. Stop dispatching at the budget and return the declared incumbent after all counted evaluations finish.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel EI repeatedly fills available workers, accounts for pending points, updates on completed evaluations, and returns an incumbent when the budget finishes.
assumptions_latex: At most \(q<\infty\) evaluations run concurrently.
The pending-point treatment inside \(\alpha_t\) and the budget accounting convention are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dispatch rule defines synchronous execution when updates await a full batch and asynchronous execution when each completion triggers selection.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: parallel Bayesian optimization maintains completed and pending evaluation sets with capacity-limited dispatch

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits parallel EI execution, and the completed/pending-set dispatch description is coherent. An authoritative source is required, particularly because the pending-point acquisition and synchronous versus asynchronous execution conventions determine the actual algorithm.

children.title: Pending-Point Batch Treatments
children.top_down_role: Batch criteria that incorporate locations whose outcomes remain unavailable.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variance reduction obtained by treating pending locations as future observations while retaining the current posterior mean.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a Gaussian-process posterior based on completed data have mean \(\mu_n\) and covariance \(k_n\). For pending locations \(P=(p_1,\ldots,p_m)\) with declared observation-noise covariance \(\Sigma_P\), define \[\widetilde\mu_n(x)=\mu_n(x),\qquad \widetilde k_n(x,x')=k_n(x,x')-k_n(x,P)\bigl(K_n(P,P)+\Sigma_P\bigr)^{-1}k_n(P,x').\] If \(K_n(P,P)+\Sigma_P\succ0\), then \[0\leq\widetilde k_n(x,x)\leq k_n(x,x).\] This is not ordinary posterior conditioning because the outcome-dependent conditional-mean update is deliberately omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A covariance-only pending update reduces GP variance as if pending sites were observed while deliberately leaving the mean unchanged.
assumptions_latex: K_n(P,P)+\Sigma_P\succ0.
k_n\text{ is a positive-semidefinite posterior covariance}.

notation.meaning: Posterior covariance matrix at pending sites.

knowledge_statements.title: Gaussian-Process Covariance-Only Pending Update

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fantasy integration for selecting one additional point while evaluations remain unresolved.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Draw conditionally i.i.d. joint fantasies \(Y_P^{(1)},\ldots,Y_P^{(K)}\sim\mathcal L(Y_P\mid\mathcal D_n)\), update the posterior and every outcome-dependent acquisition state under each fantasy, and compute \[\widehat a_K(x)=\frac1K\sum_{k=1}^K a(x;\mathcal D_n\cup\{(P,Y_P^{(k)})\}).\] For each fixed \(x\) having an integrable fantasy acquisition, \(\widehat a_K(x)\to a_{\mathrm{int}}(x)\) almost surely. For EI, the fantasy-dependent incumbent must also be updated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Average acquisitions under joint pending-outcome fantasies, fully updating both the surrogate and acquisition state for every fantasy.
assumptions_latex: Y_P^{(k)}\mid\mathcal D_n\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\mathcal L(Y_P\mid\mathcal D_n).
\mathbb E[|a(x;\mathcal D_n\cup\{(P,Y_P)\})|\mid\mathcal D_n]<\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Monte Carlo Pending-Outcome Integration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two principal treatments of unresolved evaluations when selecting an additional point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) denote pending locations and \(Y_P\mid\mathcal D_n\) their joint predictive outcomes. For a measurable acquisition \(a(x;D)\), define \[a_{\mathrm{int}}(x)=\mathbb E[a(x;\mathcal D_n\cup\{(P,Y_P)\})\mid\mathcal D_n],\qquad a_{\mathrm{plug}}(x;\widehat y_P)=a(x;\mathcal D_n\cup\{(P,\widehat y_P)\}).\] The integrated form averages fully updated acquisitions, whereas the plug-in form conditions on declared proxy outcomes. Generally \(a_{\mathrm{int}}(x)\ne a_{\mathrm{plug}}(x;\mathbb E[Y_P\mid\mathcal D_n])\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pending outcomes can be integrated over or replaced by declared proxy values; the two treatments generally differ.
assumptions_latex: a(x;\mathcal D_n\cup\{(P,Y_P)\})\text{ is measurable and integrable}.
\widehat y_P\text{ is fixed conditional on }\mathcal D_n.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a_{\mathrm{int}}\text{ and }a_{\mathrm{plug}}\text{ are generally nonequivalent pending-point acquisitions}.
knowledge_statements.title: Posterior-Integrated and Proxy-Conditioned Pending Acquisitions
Pending-Point Batch Treatments
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Posterior and acquisition approximations for evaluations dispatched but not yet observed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=(p_1,\ldots,p_m)\) be pending sites and \(Y_P\) their unknown outcomes. A posterior-integrated pending-point acquisition is \[\alpha_{m int}(x)=\mathbb E_{Y_P\mid\mathcal D_n}\!\left[\alpha(x;\mathcal D_n\cup\{(P,Y_P)\})\right].\] A plug-in treatment selects a declared proxy \(\widehat Y_P\) and uses \[\alpha_{m plug}(x)=\alpha(x;\mathcal D_n\cup\{(P,\widehat Y_P)\}).\] A covariance-only treatment conditions the surrogate variance on locations \(P\) while leaving its mean unchanged. These constructions are distinct approximations unless special posterior or acquisition identities make them coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pending evaluations may be integrated over, assigned proxy outcomes, or used only to reduce covariance; the resulting acquisitions generally differ.
assumptions_latex: The predictive distribution of pending outcomes exists conditional on completed data.
The acquisition is measurable and integrable under the pending-outcome law.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_{m int}\), \(\alpha_{m plug}\), and covariance-only conditioning define generally nonequivalent pending-point treatments.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: fantasy integration, plug-in outcomes, and covariance-only updates are standard pending-point constructions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation appropriately distinguishes posterior integration and plug-in pending outcomes. A source is required for these named treatments, and the covariance-only construction needs a sourced formal specification because conditioning variance on locations while leaving the mean unchanged is an approximation rather than ordinary posterior conditioning.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Integrated, Plug-In, and Covariance-Only Pending Treatments Can Rank Differently
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed Gaussian ranking construction for three pending-point treatments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider noiseless minimization with incumbent \(0\), one pending outcome \(Y\sim N(0,1)\), and two candidates \(a,b\). Conditional on completed data, let \(F_a=Y\) and let \(F_b\sim N(0,1)\) be independent of \(Y\). After observing \(Y=y\), one-point EI at \(a\) is \((-y)_+\), while EI at \(b\) is \(1/\sqrt{2\pi}\). Therefore posterior integration gives equal scores. A plug-in value \(\widehat Y=-1\) ranks \(a\) above \(b\), while a covariance-only update ranks \(b\) above \(a\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposed example claims that integrated, plug-in, and covariance-only pending treatments produce three different rankings.
assumptions_latex: \(F_b\sim N(0,1)\) independently of \(Y\).
The minimization incumbent before resolving the pending point is zero.
The plug-in proxy is \(\widehat Y=-1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The claimed ranking separation is not established under standard fantasy-updated expected improvement.

notation.meaning: Latent objective values at the two candidate locations.

knowledge_statements.title: Integrated, Plug-In, and Covariance-Only Pending Treatments Can Rank Differently

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf owns how unresolved locations alter a subsequent acquisition through outcome integration, proxy conditioning, or covariance-only variance reduction. Only the covariance-only formula is accepted. The proposed ranking counterexample is deferred because standard fantasy EI must update both the incumbent and posterior after the pending outcome. Generic fantasy computation and worker dispatch remain excluded adjacent scopes.

children.title: Feasibility-Coupled Improvement Family
children.top_down_role: Improvement policies coupled to modeled feasibility or violation information.

children.title: Feasibility-Weighted Improvement
children.top_down_role: Improvement criteria modulated by modeled feasibility likelihood.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite posterior example separating feasibility-weighted improvement from exact joint constrained improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let posterior improvement \(I\) and feasibility indicator \(Z\) satisfy \(\Pr((I,Z)=(2,1))=\Pr((I,Z)=(0,0))=1/2\). Then \(\mathbb E[IZ]=1\), whereas \(\mathbb E[I]\Pr(Z=1)=1/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When objective improvement and feasibility are dependent, EI times feasibility probability can differ from exact constrained improvement.
assumptions_latex: I\ge0.
knowledge_statements.title: Dependence Breaks Product Factorization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural properties of product-form feasibility-weighted improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\operatorname{EI}_n(x)\ge0\), \(p_F(x)\in[0,1]\), and \(\alpha_{\mathrm{FWI}}(x)=\operatorname{EI}_n(x)p_F(x)\), then \(0\le\alpha_{\mathrm{FWI}}(x)\le\operatorname{EI}_n(x)\). Moreover, \(p_F(x)=0\) implies \(\alpha_{\mathrm{FWI}}(x)=0\), while \(p_F(x)=1\) implies \(\alpha_{\mathrm{FWI}}(x)=\operatorname{EI}_n(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility weighting attenuates ordinary expected improvement, suppressing zero-feasibility points and recovering EI at certainly feasible points.
assumptions_latex: \operatorname{EI}_n(x)\ge0.
0\le p_F(x)\le1.
knowledge_statements.title: Range and Feasibility-Zero Suppression

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-form expected improvement modulated by posterior joint-feasibility probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a declared finite incumbent threshold \(T_n\), let \(I_n(x)=(T_n-Y(x))_+\), \(F(x)=\{C_j(x)\le0\ \forall j\}\), and \(p_{F,n}(x)=\Pr(F(x)\mid\mathcal D_n)\). Then \(\alpha_{\mathrm{FWI},n}(x)=\mathbb E[I_n(x)\mid\mathcal D_n]p_{F,n}(x)\). It equals \(\mathbb E[I_n(x)\mathbf1_{F(x)}\mid\mathcal D_n]\) when \(I_n(x)\) and \(\mathbf1_{F(x)}\) are conditionally independent given \(\mathcal D_n\); otherwise the product is generally only a factorized criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility-weighted improvement is EI times joint feasibility probability and equals exact feasible improvement only under the stated conditional independence.
assumptions_latex: T_n\text{ is finite and }\mathcal D_n\text{-measurable}.
I_n(x)\text{ is conditionally integrable}.
F(x)\text{ is posterior measurable}.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Weighted Improvement

children.title: Constrained Expected Improvement
children.top_down_role: Expected-improvement policies targeting objective progress within modeled feasible regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Constrained Expected Improvement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step constrained improvement for minimization with posterior-random objective and inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal X\) be the design space, let \(Y(x)\) and \(C_1(x),\ldots,C_m(x)\) denote posterior predictive objective and constraint values, and let \(f_{\min}^{\mathrm{feas}}\) be the best observed feasible objective. Constrained expected improvement is
\[\operatorname{CEI}(x)=\mathbb E\!\left[(f_{\min}^{\mathrm{feas}}-Y(x))_+\prod_{j=1}^m\mathbf 1\{C_j(x)\le 0\}\mid\mathcal D\right].\]
If \(Y(x)\) is conditionally independent of the constraint vector \((C_1(x),\ldots,C_m(x))\) given \(\mathcal D\), then
\[\operatorname{CEI}(x)=\operatorname{EI}(x)\,\mathbb P\!\left(C_j(x)\le0\text{ for all }j\mid\mathcal D\right).\]
If, additionally, \(C_1(x),\ldots,C_m(x)\) are mutually conditionally independent given \(\mathcal D\), then
\[\operatorname{CEI}(x)=\operatorname{EI}(x)\prod_{j=1}^m\mathbb P(C_j(x)\le0\mid\mathcal D).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constrained expected improvement averages objective improvement over feasible posterior outcomes. Under conditional independence of the objective from the constraint vector, it equals expected improvement times joint feasibility probability; mutually independent constraints permit the joint probability to be factored into marginal probabilities.
assumptions_latex: \(f_{\min}^{\mathrm{feas}}\) exists and is finite.
All displayed posterior expectations and probabilities are well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{n+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}\operatorname{CEI}(x)\) defines the corresponding one-step policy.

notation.meaning: posterior predictive value of constraint j

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dependence Invalidates Product-Form Constrained Expected Improvement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp counterexample to marginal factorization without conditional independence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), let the random objective improvement be \(I=B\), and let the feasibility indicator be \(F=B\). Then \[\mathbb E[IF]=\mathbb E[B]=\tfrac12,\qquad \mathbb E[I]\,\mathbb P(F=1)=\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac12=\tfrac14.\] Thus constrained expected improvement \(\mathbb E[IF]\) need not equal ordinary expected improvement times marginal feasibility probability when improvement and feasibility are posterior dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perfect positive dependence between improvement and feasibility makes true constrained EI twice the product of its marginal quantities in this example.
assumptions_latex: B\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2).
I=F=B.
knowledge_statements.title: Dependence Invalidates Product-Form Constrained Expected Improvement

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Undefined Incumbent Before Any Feasible Observation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain boundary of incumbent-based constrained expected improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The canonical incumbent-based quantity \((f_{\min}^{\mathrm{feas}}-Y(x))_+\) is undefined when no feasible objective value has been observed, because \[f_{\min}^{\mathrm{feas}}=\min\{Y(x_i):x_i\text{ is observed feasible}\}\] then minimizes over an empty set. Standard incumbent-based CEI therefore requires an initial feasible observation or an explicitly declared alternative utility; assigning an arbitrary numerical incumbent changes the acquisition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard constrained EI requires a feasible incumbent or an explicitly defined replacement utility.
assumptions_latex: The set of observed feasible points is empty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_{\min}^{\mathrm{feas}}\text{ and canonical incumbent-based CEI are undefined}.
knowledge_statements.title: Undefined Incumbent Before Any Feasible Observation

children.title: Violation-Aware Improvement
children.top_down_role: Improvement policies that use predicted constraint-violation severity.

knowledge_statements.title: Violation-Aware Improvement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Improvement computed from a scalar merit function that explicitly penalizes predicted constraint violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For minimization over \(\mathcal X\), define aggregate violation \(V(x)=\sum_{j=1}^m w_j(C_j(x))_+\), with \(w_j>0\), and posterior-random merit \(M_\rho(x)=Y(x)+\rho V(x)\), with \(\rho>0\). Given an incumbent merit value \(m_n\), the violation-aware improvement acquisition is
\[\alpha_{\mathrm{VAI}}(x)=\mathbb E[(m_n-M_\rho(x))_+\mid\mathcal D].\]
Thus objective reduction and violation reduction are compared on the common merit scale; increasing \(\rho\) places greater acquisition value on reducing violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Violation-aware improvement applies expected improvement to a merit function combining objective value and weighted positive constraint violation.
assumptions_latex: \(Y(x)\) and every \(C_j(x)\) are jointly integrable under the posterior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{n+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}\alpha_{\mathrm{VAI}}(x)\) is a violation-aware improvement decision.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but “violation-aware improvement” does not uniquely determine this particular weighted positive-part penalty construction. A source must establish the intended canonical variant and the role of the penalty parameter.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Penalties Need Not Enforce Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed boundary for the unsupported finite additive-penalty variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite \(\rho>0\), let deterministic candidates \(a,b\) satisfy \((Y(a),V(a))=(0,0)\) and \((Y(b),V(b))=(-2\rho,1)\). Then \(Y(b)+\rho V(b)=-\rho<0=Y(a)+\rho V(a)\), so this additive merit can prefer infeasible \(b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite additive violation penalty need not make a merit rule prefer a feasible candidate.
assumptions_latex: \rho\in(0,\infty).
Lower additive merit values are preferred.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Penalties Need Not Enforce Feasibility

intermediate_metadata.reason: The leaf should own acquisitions using predicted violation severity, but its canonical variant is materially ambiguous. The additive-penalty counterexample is therefore deferred with the underlying seed. Feasibility weighting, exact constrained improvement, and feasibility-first switching were excluded as sibling scopes.

children.title: Feasibility-First Search Regimes
children.top_down_role: Policies emphasizing discovery of usable feasible regions before objective refinement.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary requiring a separate feasibility-discovery convention before feasible-incumbent improvement is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal I_n=\{i\le n:C_j(x_i)\le0\ \forall j\}\). The best observed feasible value \(f_n^{\mathrm{feas}}=\min_{i\in\mathcal I_n}f(x_i)\) is finite only if \(\mathcal I_n\ne\varnothing\). If \(\mathcal I_n=\varnothing\), an acquisition containing \((f_n^{\mathrm{feas}}-Y(x))_+\) is undefined unless an explicit threshold or extended-value convention is supplied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Before a feasible observation exists, improvement relative to the best feasible observation has no finite data-defined incumbent.
assumptions_latex: Sampled designs can be classified as feasible or infeasible.
No artificial incumbent threshold has been declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal I_n=\varnothing\implies f_n^{\mathrm{feas}}\text{ is not a finite data-defined incumbent}.
knowledge_statements.title: Undefined Feasible-Incumbent Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-regime search distinguished by whether an observed feasible incumbent exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal I_n=\{i\le n:C_j(x_i)\le0\ \forall j\}\) and \(p_{F,n}(x)=\Pr(C_j(x)\le0\ \forall j\mid\mathcal D_n)\). While \(\mathcal I_n=\varnothing\), choose a maximizer of \(p_{F,n}\), or a minimizer of an explicitly declared restoration score. Once \(\mathcal I_n\ne\varnothing\), terminate restoration and use a declared feasible-improvement acquisition based on \(f_n^{\mathrm{feas}}=\min_{i\in\mathcal I_n}f(x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasibility-first policy restores feasibility until a feasible observation exists and then switches to a separately declared feasible-improvement policy.
assumptions_latex: Observed constraints determine membership in \(\mathcal I_n\).
The restoration score, post-switch acquisition, and tie or approximation rules are declared.
All choices use only \(\mathcal D_n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal I_n=\varnothing\text{ selects restoration, whereas }\mathcal I_n\ne\varnothing\text{ selects feasible improvement}.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-First Switching Policy

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A fully specified pre-feasibility restoration score.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C_j(x)\le0\), positive weights \(w_j\), and \(\mathcal I_n=\varnothing\), define \(V_n(x)=\sum_{j=1}^m w_j\mathbb E[(C_j(x))_+\mid\mathcal D_n]\) and choose \(x_{n+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathcal X}V_n(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One feasibility-restoration variant minimizes weighted posterior expected positive constraint violation.
assumptions_latex: w_j>0\quad(j=1,\ldots,m).
\mathbb E[(C_j(x))_+\mid\mathcal D_n]<\infty.
The minimization has a declared exact or approximate solution rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Expected-Violation Restoration Variant
Feasibility-First Search Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lexicographic constrained search used before and after discovery of a feasible observation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given posterior constraint models, define \(p_F(x)=\mathbb P(C_j(x)\le0\text{ for all }j\mid\mathcal D_n)\). If no observed design is feasible, choose
\[x_{n+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}p_F(x),\]
or, when feasibility probabilities are uninformative, minimize a specified posterior violation score. Once a feasible observation exists, set \(f_n^{\mathrm{feas}}\) to the best feasible objective and choose
\[x_{n+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}\mathbb E[(f_n^{\mathrm{feas}}-Y(x))_+\mathbf1\{C(x)\le0\}\mid\mathcal D_n].\]
Update the posterior after each evaluation and stop under a prespecified budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search first maximizes feasibility until a feasible point is observed, then switches to improvement restricted to feasible posterior outcomes.
assumptions_latex: The constraint event \(C(x)\le0\) is posterior measurable.
Each acquisition maximization has an admissible maximizer or an approximation rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The policy uses feasibility as the primary objective precisely while the feasible incumbent is undefined.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role fits the leaf, but the precise feasibility-first switching policy lacks a source. The post-switch expression also uses an undefined vector notation \(C(x)\le0\) after defining scalar constraints \(C_j\), and the fallback violation score is not specified.

children.title: Probability of Improvement
children.top_down_role: Acquisition policies based on the posterior chance of exceeding a target.

knowledge_statements.title: Probability of Improvement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold-improvement acquisition for one-step minimization under a predictive distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Y(x)\) be the posterior predictive objective at \(x\in\mathcal X\), and let \(\tau\in\mathbb R\) be a target level. The probability-of-improvement acquisition for minimization is
\[\operatorname{PI}_\tau(x)=\mathbb P(Y(x)\le\tau\mid\mathcal D).\]
If \(Y(x)\mid\mathcal D\sim\mathcal N(\mu(x),\sigma^2(x))\) and \(\sigma(x)>0\), then
\[\operatorname{PI}_\tau(x)=\Phi\!\left(\frac{\tau-\mu(x)}{\sigma(x)}\right).\]
For \(\sigma(x)=0\), its value is \(\mathbf1\{\mu(x)\le\tau\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Probability of improvement is the posterior probability that the objective falls below a chosen minimization target.
assumptions_latex: \(Y(x)\) is posterior measurable for every \(x\in\mathcal X\).
The Gaussian formula assumes a conditionally normal predictive distribution.

notation.meaning: posterior predictive mean and standard deviation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limitation intrinsic to threshold-event scoring.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If two posterior predictive laws \(P_1,P_2\) satisfy \(P_1(Y\le\tau)=P_2(Y\le\tau)\), then they have equal probability-of-improvement scores even if \(\mathbb E_{P_1}[(\tau-Y)_+]\ne\mathbb E_{P_2}[(\tau-Y)_+]\). For \(\tau=0\), the laws placing probability \(1/2\) on each of \((-1,1)\) and \((-100,1)\), respectively, both have PI \(1/2\), whereas their expected improvements are \(1/2\) and \(50\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PI records the chance of crossing the target but not how far a successful outcome crosses it.
assumptions_latex: Improvement for minimization is \((\tau-Y)_+\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{PI}_{P_1}=\operatorname{PI}_{P_2}\) need not imply equal expected improvement.
knowledge_statements.title: PI Ignores Improvement Magnitude

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mean and uncertainty sensitivity for fixed-target Gaussian PI.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(z=(\tau-\mu)/\sigma\) and \(\sigma>0\), \(\operatorname{PI}_\tau=\Phi(z)\) satisfies \[\frac{\partial\operatorname{PI}_\tau}{\partial\mu}=-\frac{\phi(z)}{\sigma}<0,\qquad \frac{\partial\operatorname{PI}_\tau}{\partial\sigma}=-\frac{z\phi(z)}{\sigma}.\] Thus greater predictive uncertainty raises PI when \(\mu>\tau\), lowers PI when \(\mu<\tau\), and has zero first-order effect when \(\mu=\tau\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PI always favors a lower Gaussian predictive mean, while the effect of uncertainty changes sign at the target.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\mid\mathcal D\sim\mathcal N(\mu,\sigma^2)\).
\(\sigma>0\) and \(\tau\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.title: Gaussian PI Sensitivity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scoring rule for a maximization-oriented Bayesian-optimization policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given data $\mathcal D$ and incumbent value $f^{\mathrm{inc}}$, the Probability-of-Improvement acquisition score of a candidate $x$ is \[\alpha_{\mathrm{PoI}}(x)=\Pr\!\left(Y(x)>f^{\mathrm{inc}}\mid\mathcal D\right).\] Thus each candidate is scored by its posterior probability of strictly improving upon the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Probability-of-Improvement policy scores each candidate by the posterior probability that its function value will exceed the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \text{The objective is maximized.}
f^{\mathrm{inc}}\text{ is the incumbent value.}
Y(x)\mid\mathcal D\text{ is the posterior predictive function value at }x.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If $Y(x)\sim\mathcal N(\mu(x),\sigma^2(x))$ with $\sigma(x)>0$, then the probability that the function value at $x$ exceeds the incumbent value $f^{\mathrm{inc}}$ is the normal-tail area \[\Pr\!\left(Y(x)>f^{\mathrm{inc}}\right)=\int_{f^{\mathrm{inc}}}^{\infty}\frac{1}{\sigma(x)\sqrt{2\pi}}\exp\!\left(-\frac{(y-\mu(x))^2}{2\sigma^2(x)}\right)\,dy.\]

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold-based probability of improvement for the stated simple posterior-mean utility in Bayesian optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an already gathered dataset \(\mathcal D=(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\), let \(u(\mathcal D)=\max \mu_{\mathcal D}(\mathbf x)\). Given a proposed observation location \(x\), an improvement margin \(\varepsilon\), and the threshold \(\tau=u(\mathcal D)+\varepsilon\), the probability-of-improvement acquisition function is \[\alpha_{\mathrm{PI}}(x;\mathcal D,\tau)=\Pr\!\left(u(\mathcal D')>\tau\mid x,\mathcal D\right),\] where \(\mathcal D'\) is the dataset updated by the proposed observation. This criterion accounts for the probability, but not the magnitude, of improvement beyond the threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the stated utility—the maximum posterior mean associated with the gathered dataset—the probability-of-improvement acquisition function scores a proposed observation location by the conditional probability that the updated utility strictly exceeds the current utility plus a chosen margin. It ignores how large an improvement beyond that threshold would be.

u(\mathcal D)=\max \mu_{\mathcal D}(\mathbf x)
\tau=u(\mathcal D)+\varepsilon
\mathcal D'\text{ is the dataset updated by an observation at }x

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Probability of Improvement under a Gaussian predictive distribution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the minimization-oriented Probability of Improvement value and preserves the stated boundary convention at noiseless measured points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Y be the predictive objective value at a query point, with Gaussian mean \widehat{\mu} and variance \widehat{\sigma}^{2}, and let y_{\min} be the minimum sampled value. If \widehat{\sigma}>0, then \Pr(Y<y_{\min})=\int_{-\infty}^{y_{\min}}\mathcal{N}(y\mid\widehat{\mu},\widehat{\sigma}^{2})\,dy=\Phi\!\left((y_{\min}-\widehat{\mu})/\widehat{\sigma}\right). If \widehat{\sigma}=0 at a noiseless measured point, the probability of improvement is set to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a Gaussian predictive model and positive predictive standard deviation, Probability of Improvement is the standard normal CDF evaluated at the standardized best-so-far threshold. At a noiseless measured point with zero predictive standard deviation, the source assigns it value zero.
assumptions_latex: y_{\min}=\min\{\text{objective values sampled so far}\}
\widehat{\sigma}>0\implies Y\sim\mathcal{N}(\widehat{\mu},\widehat{\sigma}^{2})
\Phi\text{ is the standard normal cumulative distribution function}

children.title: Quantile Improvement
children.top_down_role: Improvement policies driven by selected posterior objective quantiles.

knowledge_statements.title: Quantile Improvement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Improvement scored using a lower posterior objective quantile rather than a tail probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For minimization, let \(q_\alpha(x)=\inf\{y:\mathbb P(Y(x)\le y\mid\mathcal D)\ge\alpha\}\) be the posterior \(\alpha\)-quantile, where \(0<\alpha<1\), and let \(\tau\) be a target. Define quantile improvement by
\[\operatorname{QI}_{\alpha,\tau}(x)=(\tau-q_\alpha(x))_+.\]
Under a Gaussian predictive distribution,
\[q_\alpha(x)=\mu(x)+\Phi^{-1}(\alpha)\sigma(x).\]
A maximizer favors locations whose selected posterior quantile lies farthest below the target.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quantile improvement measures how far a selected lower posterior objective quantile falls below a target.
assumptions_latex: The posterior distribution of \(Y(x)\) has a well-defined lower quantile.

children.title: Fixed Target Levels
children.top_down_role: Threshold-oriented policies using externally specified aspiration levels.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation between an unchanging aspiration level and changing posterior threshold scores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\tau\in\mathbb R\) be fixed before sequential sampling and let \(A_n(x;\tau)\) be a threshold score determined by the posterior law of \(Y(x)\mid\mathcal D_n\) relative to \(\tau\). Updating \(\mathcal D_n\) may change \(A_n(x;\tau)\), but the minimization success event remains \(\{Y(x)\le\tau\}\) at every round.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a fixed target, posterior scores change as data arrive but the aspiration level defining success does not.
assumptions_latex: \tau\text{ is selected independently of sequential observations}.
The same minimization objective scale is used at every round.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \tau_n=\tau\ \forall n\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\text{only the posterior law, not the benchmark, is updated}.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Target Posterior Updating Invariance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: History-independent aspiration threshold retained throughout sequential search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A threshold policy has fixed target \(\tau\in\mathbb R\) when \(\tau\) is selected before sequential sampling and \(\tau_n(\omega)=\tau\) for every round \(n\) and every admissible history \(\omega\). Data update the posterior threshold score but not the benchmark defining success.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed target is a preselected aspiration level that remains constant across rounds and histories.
assumptions_latex: \tau\in\mathbb R\text{ is selected before sequential observations}.
Every round uses the same objective scale and optimization direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Target Level
Fixed Target Levels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Target policy in which the improvement threshold remains independent of sequential data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A threshold-improvement policy has a fixed target level if there exists \(\tau\in\mathbb R\), selected before sequential sampling, such that \(\tau_n=\tau\) for every round \(n\). For minimization, the associated improvement event and magnitude are respectively
\[\{Y_n(x)\le\tau\}\quad\text{and}\quad(\tau-Y_n(x))_+.\]
Consequently, observations update the predictive distribution of \(Y_n(x)\) but do not change the benchmark defining improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-target policy keeps the improvement threshold constant across rounds while posterior predictions change with the accumulated data.
assumptions_latex: The target \(\tau\) is chosen independently of future observations.
All rounds use the same objective scale and minimization convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau_n=\tau\) for all \(n\) is the defining fixed-target predicate.
