children.title: Adaptive Target Levels
children.top_down_role: Threshold-oriented policies whose aspiration levels change during search.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information constraint for an implementable sequentially updated target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F_n=\sigma(\mathcal D_n)\). A target \(\tau_n\) used to construct the round-\(n\) acquisition must be \(\mathcal F_n\)-measurable. A target depending on \(Y_{n+1}\) or another unrevealed response is anticipative and does not define an implementable sequential policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An adaptive target must be computable from current information; using a future response is not implementable.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal F_n\text{ is the information available before selecting }x_{n+1}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \tau_n\in L^0(\mathcal F_n)\text{ is necessary for nonanticipative target selection}.

notation.meaning: target used for the next acquisition

knowledge_statements.title: Predictability of Adaptive Targets

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical minimization update using a declared incumbent and margin schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(b_n\) be a declared \(\mathcal F_n\)-measurable incumbent and \(\xi_n\ge0\) a declared \(\mathcal F_n\)-measurable margin. Set \(\tau_n=b_n-\xi_n\), evaluate the chosen sibling-owned threshold score relative to \(\tau_n\), select its maximizer under a declared tie rule, observe the response, and update \(\mathcal F_{n+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A standard adaptive target sets the next minimization aspiration level to the current incumbent minus a nonnegative margin.
assumptions_latex: b_n,\xi_n\in L^0(\mathcal F_n).
\xi_n\ge0.
The threshold score and acquisition optimization rule are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \tau_n=b_n-\xi_n\text{ is a nonanticipative adaptive minimization target}.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent-Minus-Margin Target Update

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonanticipative threshold levels recomputed from sequential information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(\mathcal F_n=\sigma(\mathcal D_n)\), an adaptive target regime is a sequence \((\tau_n)\) in which every \(\tau_n\) is \(\mathcal F_n\)-measurable and at least one \(\tau_n\) is not a preselected history-independent constant. The round-\(n\) threshold acquisition is evaluated relative to \(\tau_n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive targets are nonanticipative thresholds that may change with the observed history.
assumptions_latex: \tau_n\in L^0(\mathcal F_n)\quad\text{for every }n.
The objective scale and minimization or maximization convention are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \tau_n=T_n(\mathcal D_n)\text{ distinguishes adaptive targets from a constant preselected target}.

notation.meaning: information available before the next selection

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Target Sequence
Adaptive Target Levels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential threshold policy whose target is recomputed from the current data or posterior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose a measurable target rule \(T_n\). At round \(n\), set \(\tau_n=T_n(\mathcal D_n)\), form
\[\alpha_n(x)=\mathbb P(Y_n(x)\le\tau_n\mid\mathcal D_n)\]
or another specified threshold-improvement score, select \(x_{n+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}\alpha_n(x)\), observe the response, and update \(\mathcal D_{n+1}\). A common minimization rule is \(\tau_n=f_n^{\min}-\xi_n\), where \(f_n^{\min}\) is the best observed value and \(\xi_n\ge0\) is a prescribed margin. Stop at the evaluation budget and return the best observed design.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An adaptive-target policy recomputes its improvement threshold from current data, such as the incumbent minus a round-dependent margin.
assumptions_latex: Each \(T_n\) is measurable with respect to \(\mathcal D_n\).
The acquisition maximization uses only information available at round \(n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dependence \(\tau_n=T_n(\mathcal D_n)\) distinguishes adaptive from fixed target levels.

notation.meaning: best objective observed through round n

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Parameter-dependent correspondence between GP-UCB and probability of improvement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correspondence in the noiseless Gaussian predictive setting on points with positive predictive standard deviation, together with the failure of fixed-parameter sequential equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(\sigma(x)>0\) on \(\mathcal X\). For \(\beta\in\mathbb R\), suppose \(\tau(\beta)=\max_{x'\in\mathcal X}\{\mu(x')+\beta\sigma(x')\}\) is attained. Then every \(x\in\arg\max_{x'\in\mathcal X}\{\mu(x')+\beta\sigma(x')\}\) minimizes \((\tau(\beta)-\mu(x'))/\sigma(x')\) and therefore maximizes noiseless Gaussian probability of improvement for target \(\tau(\beta)\). Conversely, if \(x\) maximizes probability of improvement for a target \(\tau\), then, with \(\beta=(\tau-\mu(x))/\sigma(x)\), the point \(x\) maximizes \(\mu+\beta\sigma\). This parameter correspondence does not make sequential GP-UCB with fixed \(\beta\) equivalent to probability of improvement with a fixed target, because \(\tau(\beta)\) depends on the current data and model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the noiseless Gaussian setting, a UCB maximizer for a given exploration parameter is a probability-of-improvement maximizer when the target is chosen as the optimal UCB value. Conversely, each probability-of-improvement maximizer determines an exploration parameter for which it maximizes UCB. The correspondence is iteration-dependent: fixing the UCB parameter does not fix the probability-of-improvement target as data and the model change.
assumptions_latex: \mu,\sigma:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R
\sigma(x)>0\quad\text{for all }x\in\mathcal X
\tau(\beta)=\max_{x'\in\mathcal X}(\mu(x')+\beta\sigma(x'))\text{ exists and is attained}
\text{Probability of improvement is computed from a noiseless Gaussian predictive distribution.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise predictive-quantile representation, Gaussian closed form, exploration interpretation, and gradient for a fixed confidence parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a predictive distribution at \(x\) and a fixed confidence level \(\pi\in(0,1)\), define \(\alpha_{\mathrm{UCB}}(x;\mathcal D,\pi)=q(\pi;x,\mathcal D)\). If \(Y(x)\mid\mathcal D\sim\mathcal N(\mu(x),\sigma^2(x))\), then \(\alpha_{\mathrm{UCB}}(x;\mathcal D,\pi)=\mu(x)+ eta\sigma(x)\), where \( eta=\Phi^{-1}(\pi)\). If \(\mu\) and \(\sigma\) are differentiable at \(x\), then \(
abla_x\alpha_{\mathrm{UCB}}(x)=
abla_x\mu(x)+ eta
abla_x\sigma(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a fixed confidence level, GP-UCB is the corresponding predictive quantile. For a Gaussian predictive distribution, it is the posterior mean plus the standard deviation multiplied by the associated standard-normal quantile. Its spatial gradient is the same linear combination of the mean and standard-deviation gradients when both are differentiable.
assumptions_latex: \pi\in(0,1)\text{ is fixed with respect to }x
Y(x)\mid\mathcal D\sim\mathcal N(\mu(x),\sigma^2(x))
\beta=\Phi^{-1}(\pi)
\mu\text{ and }\sigma\text{ are differentiable at }x\text{ for the gradient formula}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lower Confidence Bound Acquisition for Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization-oriented confidence-bound acquisition using a surrogate predictive mean and standard deviation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a surrogate predictive mean \(\widehat{\mu}\), predictive standard deviation \(\widehat{\sigma}\), and \(\alpha\ge 0\), define \(\operatorname{LB}(x)=\widehat{\mu}(x)-\alpha\widehat{\sigma}(x)\). The next sample is selected by minimizing \(\operatorname{LB}\). The case \(\alpha=0\) is prediction-based optimization; larger \(\alpha\) places greater emphasis on predictive uncertainty, approaching error-based exploration as \(\alpha\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize the surrogate mean minus a nonnegative multiple of predictive uncertainty. The multiplier controls the exploration–exploitation trade-off: zero uses only the predicted mean, while larger values increasingly favor uncertain points.
assumptions_latex: \widehat{\mu}:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R
\widehat{\sigma}:\mathcal X\to[0,\infty)
\alpha\ge 0
\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x\in\mathcal X}\left[\widehat{\mu}(x)-\alpha\widehat{\sigma}(x)\right]\neq\varnothing

children.title: Classical GP-UCB Policy Family
children.top_down_role: Canonical confidence-bound policies for sequential Gaussian-process search.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating a GP-UCB score from a valid confidence-based regret guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The score \(\mu_{t-1}(x)+\sqrt{\beta_t}\sigma_{t-1}(x)\) supports the classical regret argument only when its confidence band is simultaneously valid over the required points and times. An arbitrary or undersized \(\beta_t\), model misspecification, or unaccounted data-dependent hyperparameter fitting can invalidate that event; the sampling formula alone then implies no stated regret bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mean-plus-standard-deviation score is not itself a regret certificate; its confidence schedule and model assumptions must make the band simultaneously valid.
knowledge_statements.title: Confidence Calibration Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: GP-UCB Confidence and Information-Gain Regret Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical cumulative-regret bound conditional on simultaneous confidence and bounded kernel variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(|f(x)-\mu_{t-1}(x)|\le\sqrt{\beta_t}\sigma_{t-1}(x)\) simultaneously for all required \(x,t\), \(\beta_t\) is nondecreasing, and GP-UCB maximizes its score exactly. Then \(r_t\le2\sqrt{\beta_t}\sigma_{t-1}(x_t)\). If observations have independent Gaussian noise variance \(\lambda>0\), \(k(x,x)\le1\), and \(\gamma_T=\max_{|A|=T}I(y_A;f_A)\), then \[R_T\le2\sqrt{C_\lambda T\beta_T\gamma_T},\qquad C_\lambda=\frac{2}{\log(1+\lambda^{-1})}.\] Hence \(R_T/T\to0\) whenever \(\beta_T\gamma_T=o(T)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a valid simultaneous confidence event, classical GP-UCB has information-gain-controlled cumulative regret and vanishing average regret under sublinear confidence-capacity growth.
assumptions_latex: A maximizer \(x^*\) exists.
The simultaneous confidence event holds.
\(\beta_t\) is nondecreasing and acquisition maximization is exact.
Noise is independent Gaussian with variance \(\lambda>0\), and \(k(x,x)\le1\).

notation.meaning: Maximum information gain from T observations.

knowledge_statements.title: GP-UCB Confidence and Information-Gain Regret Bound
Classical GP-UCB Policy Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical sequential confidence-bound policy, stated for maximization with a fixed Gaussian-process model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) be maximized and place a Gaussian-process prior with fixed kernel and noise model on \(f\). After data \(\mathcal D_{t-1}\), compute posterior mean \(\mu_{t-1}(x)\) and standard deviation \(\sigma_{t-1}(x)\). For a prescribed sequence \(\beta_t>0\), choose
\[x_t\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}\left\{\mu_{t-1}(x)+\sqrt{\beta_t}\,\sigma_{t-1}(x)\right\},\]
observe the noisy response, and update the posterior. After a fixed budget, return a specified recommendation, such as the sampled point having largest posterior mean.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classical GP-UCB repeatedly maximizes posterior mean plus a confidence-scaled posterior standard deviation under a fixed GP model.
assumptions_latex: The kernel and observation-noise model are fixed during the run.
The posterior mean and variance exist at every candidate point.
Each acquisition maximization is solved exactly or by a declared approximation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed upper confidence bound determines the classical GP-UCB sampling policy.

notation.meaning: posterior standard deviation before round t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed sampling rule is the standard classical GP-UCB algorithm and the content kind fits, but no citation is supplied. An authoritative source is required, particularly if the policy is to carry any confidence or regret interpretation tied to \(\beta_t\).

children.title: Hyperparameter-Adaptive GP-UCB Regimes
children.top_down_role: Confidence-bound policies adapting kernel, noise, or confidence calibration during search.

children.title: Adaptive-Kernel GP-UCB
children.top_down_role: Confidence-bound policies that revise kernel structure or parameters during search.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive-Kernel GP-UCB
knowledge_statements.scope_note: GP-UCB with kernel hyperparameters updated from sequential observations and uncertainty propagated into the acquisition bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Theta_t\) be a data-dependent confidence set for kernel hyperparameters after \(\mathcal D_{t-1}\). For each \(\theta\in\Theta_t\), compute posterior quantities \(\mu_{t-1,\theta}(x)\) and \(\sigma_{t-1,\theta}(x)\). Select
\[x_t\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_t}\left\{\mu_{t-1,\theta}(x)+\sqrt{\beta_t}\,\sigma_{t-1,\theta}(x)\right\},\]
observe the response, update \(\mathcal D_t\), and reconstruct \(\Theta_{t+1}\). If \(\Theta_t\) is a singleton containing a plug-in estimate, the rule reduces to plug-in adaptive-kernel GP-UCB rather than uncertainty-robust GP-UCB.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive-kernel GP-UCB updates kernel hyperparameters sequentially and may maximize confidence bounds over a data-dependent set of plausible kernels.
assumptions_latex: Every \(\Theta_t\) is nonempty and measurable from past data.
Posterior quantities exist for all \(\theta\in\Theta_t\).
The supremum-based acquisition is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Kernel uncertainty enters the decision through optimization over \(\Theta_t\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The supremum over a hyperparameter confidence set defines a coherent robust variant, but it is not implied uniquely by the title Adaptive-Kernel GP-UCB. A source must identify this variant and state conditions under which its confidence bounds are valid.

children.title: Unknown-Noise GP-UCB
children.top_down_role: Confidence-bound policies operating with learned or uncertain observation noise.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Noise-Regularization Monotonicity and Its Coverage Limitation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact monotonicity of GP posterior latent variance in an assumed homoskedastic noise variance, without claiming confidence validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix training inputs, a positive-semidefinite Gram matrix \(K\), covariance vector \(k_x\), and prior variance \(k(x,x)\). For \(0<\lambda_1\le\lambda_2\), define \[s_{\lambda}^2(x)=k(x,x)-k_x^{\top}(K+\lambda I)^{-1}k_x.\] Then \((K+\lambda_2 I)^{-1}\preceq(K+\lambda_1 I)^{-1}\), hence \[s_{\lambda_1}^2(x)\le s_{\lambda_2}^2(x).\] The posterior means \(\mu_\lambda(x)=k_x^{\top}(K+\lambda I)^{-1}y\) have no analogous universal ordering. Therefore replacing unknown noise by an upper estimate enlarges latent posterior variance but does not by itself prove coverage of \(\mu_\lambda(x)\pm c s_\lambda(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Larger assumed homoskedastic noise increases GP latent posterior variance, but changes the posterior mean without a universal direction; a noise upper bound alone is not a coverage proof.
assumptions_latex: \(K\succeq0\).
\(0<\lambda_1\le\lambda_2\).
The same kernel, training inputs, and response vector are used in both posterior calculations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s_{\lambda_1}^2(x)\le s_{\lambda_2}^2(x),\quad\text{while no universal ordering of }\mu_{\lambda_1}(x)\text{ and }\mu_{\lambda_2}(x)\text{ follows}.

notation.meaning: Kernel Gram matrix at the training inputs.
Posterior latent variance computed using noise variance lambda.

knowledge_statements.title: Noise-Regularization Monotonicity and Its Coverage Limitation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unknown-noise GP-UCB for independent homoskedastic Gaussian noise using prespecified replicate calibration groups.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At calibration update \(r\), use a prespecified finite replicate group to compute an upper bound \(\overline\sigma_{\varepsilon,r}^2\) at conditional failure level \(\delta_r\). Form GP posterior summaries \((\mu_t^+,s_t^+)\) using the current bound and choose an attained or declared approximate maximizer of \(\mu_t^+(x)+\sqrt{\beta_{t+1}}s_t^+(x)\). If \(\sum_r\delta_r\le\delta_\sigma\), then all calibration bounds hold simultaneously with probability at least \(1-\delta_\sigma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use prespecified Gaussian replicate groups to maintain a simultaneous upper bound on constant noise variance, then construct GP-UCB with that bound.
assumptions_latex: Observation errors are independent, homoskedastic, and Gaussian.
Each calibration group and its size are fixed before observing the responses used in that group, or its bound is otherwise conditionally valid.
Each update has conditional failure probability at most \(\delta_r\), with \(\sum_r\delta_r\le\delta_\sigma\).
The acquisition optimizer returns an exact or declared approximate maximizer.

notation.meaning: Failure allocation for calibration update r.

knowledge_statements.title: Replication-Calibrated Unknown-Noise GP-UCB

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probability composition required for unknown-noise GP-UCB optimism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_\sigma=\{\forall t:\sigma_\varepsilon^2\le\overline\sigma_{\varepsilon,t}^2\}\) satisfy \(\mathbb P(E_\sigma)\ge1-\delta_\sigma\). If \(\mathbb P(E_f^c\cap E_\sigma)\le\delta_f\), where \(E_f=\{\forall t,x:f(x)\le\mu_{t-1}^+(x)+\sqrt{\beta_t}s_{t-1}^+(x)\}\), then \(\mathbb P(E_\sigma\cap E_f)\ge1-\delta_\sigma-\delta_f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unknown-noise optimism requires both noise-scale coverage and a function-envelope guarantee valid on the calibration event.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb P(E_\sigma^c)\le\delta_\sigma\).
\(\mathbb P(E_f^c\cap E_\sigma)\le\delta_f\).
knowledge_statements.title: Joint Noise-and-Function Confidence Composition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gaussian Replication Upper Confidence Bound for Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-sample upper bound for unknown homoskedastic Gaussian noise variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(m\ge2\) independent replicates at one fixed design satisfy \(Y_j=f(x)+\varepsilon_j\) with \(\varepsilon_j\overset{\mathrm{iid}}\sim N(0,\sigma_\varepsilon^2)\), and let \(S_m^2=(m-1)^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^m(Y_j-\bar Y)^2\). For \(0<\delta<1\), define \[\overline\sigma_{\varepsilon,m}^2=\frac{(m-1)S_m^2}{\chi^2_{m-1,\delta}},\] where \(\chi^2_{\nu,\delta}\) is the lower \(\delta\)-quantile. Then \(\mathbb P(\sigma_\varepsilon^2\le\overline\sigma_{\varepsilon,m}^2)=1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replicated Gaussian observations give an exact finite-sample upper confidence bound for an unknown constant noise variance.
assumptions_latex: The replicate errors are independent \(N(0,\sigma_\varepsilon^2)\).
The noise variance is common across design locations.
The replicate group size \(m\ge2\) is fixed independently of the responses in that group.

notation.meaning: Lower delta-quantile of a chi-square distribution with nu degrees of freedom.

knowledge_statements.title: Gaussian Replication Upper Confidence Bound for Noise

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Noise Upper Bound Alone Does Not Ensure GP Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Undercoverage from posterior-mean shrinkage despite conservative noise substitution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Take one training input with \(k(x,x)=1\), zero prior mean, observation \(y=f(x)=10\), and true noise variance \(0\). Compute the posterior using \(\lambda=1\). At the same input, \(\mu_\lambda(x)=5\) and \(s_\lambda(x)=1/\sqrt2\). With multiplier \(c=2\), \(\mu_\lambda(x)+cs_\lambda(x)=5+\sqrt2<10=f(x)\), although \(\lambda\ge\sigma_\varepsilon^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An assumed noise variance above the truth can still under-cover a fixed function when the confidence multiplier does not account for posterior-mean shrinkage.
assumptions_latex: There is one noiseless observation \(y=f(x)=10\).
The prior mean is zero and \(k(x,x)=1\).
The posterior is computed with assumed noise variance \(\lambda=1\) and multiplier \(c=2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Noise Upper Bound Alone Does Not Ensure GP Coverage
Unknown-Noise GP-UCB
knowledge_statements.scope_note: GP-UCB using sequential upper confidence control for an initially unknown observation-noise scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose observations satisfy \(y_t=f(x_t)+\varepsilon_t\), but the noise scale is unknown. From \(\mathcal D_{t-1}\), construct an upper confidence estimate \(\overline\sigma_{\varepsilon,t-1}\) for that scale and compute GP posterior quantities \(\mu_{t-1}^{+}(x)\) and \(s_{t-1}^{+}(x)\) using this conservative value. Choose
\[x_t\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}\left\{\mu_{t-1}^{+}(x)+\sqrt{\beta_t}\,s_{t-1}^{+}(x)\right\},\]
observe \(y_t\), and update both the noise bound and GP posterior. A valid confidence claim additionally requires simultaneous coverage of the noise bound and function envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unknown-noise GP-UCB updates a conservative noise-scale bound and uses it when constructing each Gaussian-process upper confidence acquisition.
assumptions_latex: The noise process belongs to a stated family permitting an upper confidence estimate.
\(\overline\sigma_{\varepsilon,t}\) is measurable from observations through round \(t\).
The GP posterior is well defined under the conservative noise value.

notation.meaning: upper confidence estimate of noise scale
posterior standard deviation under the conservative noise value

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role fits, but no noise family, estimator, or finite-sample confidence construction is specified. Consequently the conservative posterior rule and simultaneous coverage conclusion cannot be assessed reliably without a source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unrestricted Mean Confounds Noise Estimation Without Replication
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed identifiability boundary for estimating observation noise from singly observed adaptive locations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose distinct locations \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) are each observed once under \(Y_i=f(x_i)+\varepsilon_i\), while \(f(x_i)\) is unrestricted. For every realized vector \(y\), the noiseless model \(f(x_i)=y_i\), \(\varepsilon_i=0\) fits the data, and for every \(\sigma^2>0\) a Gaussian-noise model with means \(f(x_i)=y_i\) assigns positive density near the same vector. Hence the noise variance is not identifiable from single observations without restrictions coupling the values of \(f\), replication, or other information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With an unrestricted latent mean and no replication, variation across observations cannot be uniquely attributed to noise.
assumptions_latex: Each sampled location is observed once.
The latent values \(f(x_i)\) are unrestricted nuisance parameters.
No external noise information is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_\varepsilon^2\) is not identifiable from \((x_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^n\) under this unrestricted model.
knowledge_statements.title: Unrestricted Mean Confounds Noise Estimation Without Replication

intermediate_metadata.reason: The local inventory covers exact Gaussian replicate calibration, a replication-calibrated GP-UCB specialization, noise-regularization monotonicity, joint event composition, and a concrete coverage failure. The proposed unrestricted-mean nonidentifiability claim is deferred because its likelihood argument does not prove statistical nonidentifiability. Adaptive-kernel selection, generic confidence recalibration, heteroskedastic modeling, and broad hyperparameter uncertainty are excluded as sibling or adjacent scopes.

children.title: Adaptive Confidence Calibration
children.top_down_role: Policies that revise exploration confidence as evidence accumulates.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Confidence Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predictable calibration condition ensuring sequential GP confidence envelopes retain simultaneous coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(w_t>0\) be a confidence width chosen using only \(\mathcal D_{t-1}\). Adaptive confidence calibration at error level \(\delta\in(0,1)\) holds when
\[\mathbb P\!\left(\forall t\ge1,\ \forall x\in\mathcal X:\ |f(x)-\mu_{t-1}(x)|\le w_t\sigma_{t-1}(x)\right)\ge1-\delta.\]
Writing \(w_t=\sqrt{\beta_t}\), the associated GP-UCB rule uses \(\mu_{t-1}(x)+w_t\sigma_{t-1}(x)\). Pointwise or fixed-time empirical coverage alone does not satisfy this simultaneous sequential condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive calibration requires predictable confidence widths whose GP envelopes cover the unknown function simultaneously over all rounds and candidate points.
assumptions_latex: \(w_t\) is measurable with respect to \(\mathcal D_{t-1}\).
Posterior standard deviations are defined on \(\mathcal X\).
The probability is taken under the declared prior or frequentist data-generating model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The simultaneous event has probability at least \(1-\delta\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind correctly expresses a calibration condition, but simultaneous coverage over all times and all points is a strong claim whose validity depends on the domain, kernel, noise assumptions, and whether probability is Bayesian or frequentist. These must be specialized and sourced.

children.title: Hyperparameter-Uncertainty Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Reliability limits caused by uncertain or unstable surrogate hyperparameters.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Data-Dependent Hyperparameter Selection Requires Uniform Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary for transferring fixed-hyperparameter GP confidence guarantees to plug-in or adaptively selected hyperparameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat\theta_t\) be selected from past data and let \(E_t(\theta)\) denote validity of the GP confidence envelope constructed with hyperparameter \(\theta\). Bounds of the form \(\mathbb P(E_t(\theta))\ge 1-\delta\) for every fixed \(\theta\in\Theta\) do not, without uniform or selection-adjusted control, imply \(\mathbb P(E_t(\widehat\theta_t))\ge1-\delta\). A sufficient transfer condition is \[\mathbb P\!\left(\bigcap_{\theta\in\Theta_t}E_t(\theta)\right)\ge1-\delta,\qquad \widehat\theta_t\in\Theta_t,\] or another theorem that directly accounts for the data-dependent selection rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Confidence validity for every fixed hyperparameter does not automatically survive data-dependent hyperparameter selection; uniform or selection-adjusted coverage is required.
assumptions_latex: \(\widehat\theta_t\) is measurable with respect to the data available before the confidence bound is used.
\(E_t(\theta)\) denotes the declared confidence event for the posterior constructed with \(\theta\).
\(\Theta_t\) is a measurable candidate set containing \(\widehat\theta_t\).

notation.meaning: Data-dependent kernel or noise hyperparameter used by the GP-UCB policy.
Confidence-envelope validity event under hyperparameter theta.
Data-dependent family over which simultaneous validity is asserted.

knowledge_statements.title: Data-Dependent Hyperparameter Selection Requires Uniform Coverage
Hyperparameter-Uncertainty Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary at which plug-in GP hyperparameters cease to support valid UCB coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider two noiseless observations of the constant function \(f(x)=0\) and a squared-exponential GP with plug-in signal variance \(\widehat a_t^2\). Maximum likelihood may select the boundary value \(\widehat a_t^2=0\), yielding \(\mu_t(x)=0\) and \(\sigma_t(x)=0\) for every \(x\). For any nonzero function compatible with the finite observations, the plug-in envelope
\[\mu_t(x)\pm\sqrt{\beta_{t+1}}\sigma_t(x)\]
then has zero width and cannot cover the function at an unobserved point, regardless of finite \(\beta_{t+1}\). Thus classical GP-UCB coverage and regret conclusions do not transfer without controlling hyperparameter uncertainty or excluding degeneracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Plug-in hyperparameters can collapse posterior variance, making every finite-width UCB degenerate and invalidating classical coverage or regret guarantees.
assumptions_latex: Signal variance is estimated by unconstrained plug-in maximum likelihood.
The admissible hyperparameter space includes zero signal variance.
Only finitely many function values have been observed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat a_t^2=0\Rightarrow\sigma_t(x)=0\), so no finite \(\beta_{t+1}\) repairs missing coverage at unobserved points.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, but whether maximum likelihood admits or selects zero signal variance depends on the exact likelihood, covariance regularization, and treatment of the degenerate boundary. A source is required before accepting the counterexample and its transfer-of-guarantees conclusion.

children.title: Extended-Feedback GP-UCB Regimes
children.top_down_role: Optimistic policies for pending observations, delayed feedback, or drifting objectives.

children.title: Parallel GP-UCB
children.top_down_role: Optimistic policies selecting multiple evaluations for concurrent execution.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel GP-UCB
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Batch confidence-bound selection using pending-location variance updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X\) be a nonempty decision set and let a Gaussian-process posterior after completed observations be \((\mu_t,s_t)\). For a batch size \(q\), initialize \(P_{t,0}=\varnothing\). For \(j=1,\ldots,q\), form \(s_t(x\mid P_{t,j-1})\), the posterior standard deviation after conditioning on the locations in \(P_{t,j-1}\) but not their unknown values, and select \[x_{t,j}\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X}\left\{\mu_t(x)+\sqrt{\beta_{t,j}}\,s_t(x\mid P_{t,j-1})\right\}.\] Set \(P_{t,j}=P_{t,j-1}\cup\{x_{t,j}\}\), evaluate all points in parallel, and update the posterior when their observations return.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build a batch sequentially, retaining the completed-data posterior mean while reducing uncertainty at locations already pending in the batch.
assumptions_latex: \(q\in\mathbb N\) and each displayed argmax is attained.
\(\beta_{t,j}>0\) for every batch position.
The observation model is jointly Gaussian conditional on completed data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{t,q}\) is the batch dispatched at round \(t\).

notation.meaning: First j pending locations in batch t.
Posterior standard deviation conditioned additionally on pending locations P.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the Parallel GP-UCB leaf, and the notation is internally coherent, but no inspectable citation supports this particular pending-location variance-update variant or the required calibration of beta under batch selection. A source is needed to distinguish it from GP-BUCB and other parallel GP-UCB formulations.

children.title: Delayed-Feedback GP-UCB
children.top_down_role: Confidence-bound policies acting before earlier evaluation outcomes arrive.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stale-posterior GP-UCB using exactly the evaluations whose delayed responses have arrived.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At decision time \(t\), let \(A_t\subseteq\{1,\ldots,t-1\}\) contain exactly the evaluations whose responses are available before dispatch. Form the Gaussian-process posterior \((\mu_{A_t},\sigma_{A_t})\) from those responses and choose \[x_t\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X}\{\mu_{A_t}(x)+\sqrt{\beta_t}\sigma_{A_t}(x)\}.\] Dispatch the evaluation without using outstanding responses, and enlarge the available-data set whenever feedback arrives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Available-feedback GP-UCB applies the classical confidence-bound rule to responses received so far while outstanding evaluations remain unavailable.
assumptions_latex: \(A_t\) is measurable before choosing \(x_t\) and contains exactly the arrived feedback.
\(\beta_t>0\), and each argmax is attained or approximated by a declared rule.
Outstanding outcomes are not used in the posterior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_t\text{ is measurable with respect to the feedback available before decision }t.

notation.meaning: Indices whose feedback has arrived before decision t.
Posterior summaries based on arrived feedback.

knowledge_statements.title: Available-Feedback GP-UCB

knowledge_statements.scope_note: No-learning boundary when the delay process need not reveal observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X=\{a,b\}\), suppose no response arrives before any of the first \(T\) decisions, and let deterministic tie-breaking repeatedly select \(a\) from the unchanged posterior. For an objective with \(f(b)-f(a)=\Delta>0\), the cumulative regret is \(R_T=T\Delta\). Thus delayed-feedback GP-UCB has no sublinear-regret guarantee without an arrival condition or another mechanism preventing permanent information loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If feedback may be withheld indefinitely, the posterior can remain unchanged and delayed GP-UCB can suffer linear regret.
assumptions_latex: No dispatched response is available during the first \(T\) decisions.
Tie-breaking repeatedly selects \(a\).

notation.meaning: Objective gap between the optimal and repeatedly selected action.

knowledge_statements.title: Indefinitely Withheld Feedback Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic delay regime for available-feedback GP-UCB.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If evaluation \(s\) is dispatched at decision \(s\) and its response is available before decision \(s+d_s+1\), uniformly bounded delay means \(0\le d_s\le\tau\) for every \(s\). Consequently, before decision \(t\), every response with \(s\le t-\tau-1\) has arrived, and at most \(\tau\) earlier evaluations remain unresolved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic delay bound limits the number of missing earlier responses at every GP-UCB decision.
assumptions_latex: Each dispatched evaluation eventually returns.
There is a deterministic \(\tau<\infty\) satisfying \(d_s\le\tau\) for every \(s\).

notation.meaning: Indices whose responses are available before decision t.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniformly Bounded Feedback Delay

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of stale and fully updated GP uncertainty at fixed dispatched locations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a Gaussian-process prior, observation model, hyperparameters, and dispatched inputs. Let \(A_t\subseteq B_t\) be nested sets of responses available from those inputs. knowledge_statements.title: Time-Varying GP-UCB

children.title: Pending-Observation Confidence Control

knowledge_statements.title: Pending-Observation Confidence Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact GP uncertainty update from pending locations before their values arrive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Condition on completed data \(D\), and let \(P=(p_1,\ldots,p_m)\) be pending evaluation locations with independent Gaussian observation noise covariance \(\Sigma_P\). For any \(x\in\mathcal X\), the variance after the pending values are revealed is already determined by their locations: \[s_D^2(x\mid P)=s_D^2(x)-k_D(x,P)\bigl(K_D(P,P)+\Sigma_P\bigr)^{-1}k_D(P,x).\] Consequently, \(0\le s_D^2(x\mid P)\le s_D^2(x)\), and this controlled variance does not depend on the as-yet unknown numerical observations. A pending-aware confidence bound may therefore use \(s_D(x\mid P)\) while retaining or fantasizing the posterior mean.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pending locations determine the future GP variance exactly, although their unknown values still affect the future posterior mean.
assumptions_latex: The completed and pending observations follow a jointly Gaussian model.
\(K_D(P,P)+\Sigma_P\) is invertible.
Pending observation noises are conditionally independent of the latent process.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le s_D^2(x\mid P)\le s_D^2(x)\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\).

notation.meaning: Completed-data posterior covariance between x and pending locations.

children.title: Posterior-Quantile Policies

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Quantiles Are Not Simultaneous Bands
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coverage boundary for marginal posterior-quantile policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The marginal inequalities \(\mathbb P(f(x)\leq Q_{t,\alpha}(x)\mid D_t)\geq\alpha\) at each fixed \(x\) do not imply \[\mathbb P(f(x)\leq Q_{t,\alpha}(x)\ \forall x\in\mathcal X\mid D_t)\geq\alpha.\] Simultaneous coverage requires a joint construction accounting for dependence and domain multiplicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise posterior quantiles do not automatically form a simultaneous credible band.
assumptions_latex: The quantiles are marginal at individual locations.
No simultaneous-coverage construction is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[\forall x,\ \mathbb P(f(x)\leq Q_{t,\alpha}(x)\mid D_t)\geq\alpha\bigr]\not\Rightarrow\mathbb P(\forall x,\ f(x)\leq Q_{t,\alpha}(x)\mid D_t)\geq\alpha.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Quantiles Are Not Simultaneous Bands

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized-inverse calibration for arbitrary scalar posterior laws.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_{t,\alpha}(x)=\inf\{z:F_{t,x}(z)\geq\alpha\}\). Whenever this quantile is finite, \[F_{t,x}(Q_{t,\alpha}(x)-)\leq\alpha\leq F_{t,x}(Q_{t,\alpha}(x)).\] An atom at the quantile can therefore make posterior coverage strictly larger than \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A generalized posterior quantile reaches at least its requested probability and can overcover at an atom.
assumptions_latex: \(F_{t,x}\) is a distribution function.
\(Q_{t,\alpha}(x)\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.title: Posterior Quantile Calibration at Atoms
Posterior-Quantile Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Confidence acquisitions represented as Gaussian posterior quantiles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the scalar latent response at \(x\in\mathcal X\), conditional on data \(D_t\), satisfies \(f(x)\mid D_t\sim\mathcal N(\mu_t(x),s_t^2(x))\). For \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), its posterior quantile is \[Q_{t,\alpha}(x)=\inf\{z:\mathbb P(f(x)\le z\mid D_t)\ge\alpha\}=\mu_t(x)+\Phi^{-1}(\alpha)s_t(x).\] Thus minimizing a lower posterior quantile uses \(x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x\in\mathcal X}Q_{t,\alpha}(x)\), while maximizing an upper posterior quantile uses the corresponding argmax with \(\alpha>1/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Gaussian posterior quantile equals its mean plus a normal quantile times its standard deviation, yielding confidence-bound policies.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x)\mid D_t\) is Gaussian for every \(x\in\mathcal X\).
The relevant acquisition optimizer exists.

children.title: Risk-Sensitive Quantile Search

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary specification for interpreting quantile search as risk-sensitive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\theta(x)\) be a latent response quantity and \(Y(x)\) a future realized outcome. In general, \(\mathcal L(\theta(x)\mid D_t)\) and \(\mathcal L(Y(x)\mid D_t)\) have different quantiles. A latent posterior quantile ranks epistemic uncertainty, whereas a predictive-outcome quantile also incorporates conditional outcome variability. They coincide only under additional model-specific conditions, such as zero aleatoric noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Latent posterior and future-outcome predictive quantiles represent different risks and generally induce different policies.
assumptions_latex: \(Y(x)\) may contain conditional randomness beyond uncertainty about \(\theta(x)\).
Both conditional laws have the relevant quantiles.
knowledge_statements.title: Epistemic–Aleatoric Quantile Distinction
Risk-Sensitive Quantile Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Posterior-quantile acquisition with an explicit risk-level parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y(x)\mid D_t\) have posterior distribution function \(F_{t,x}\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\). Fix a risk level \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and define \[Q_{t,\alpha}(x)=\inf\{y\in\mathbb R:F_{t,x}(y)\ge\alpha\}.\] For minimization, choose \(x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x\in\mathcal X}Q_{t,\alpha}(x)\); for maximization, choose the corresponding argmax. Observe the response, update \(F_{t,x}\), and repeat until the fixed budget is exhausted. The value of \(\alpha\), together with the objective orientation, fixes which posterior tail governs the search.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize a selected posterior response quantile, with the quantile level controlling which tail influences decisions.
assumptions_latex: Each \(F_{t,x}\) is a right-continuous distribution function.
The selected quantile optimizer exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{t+1}\) optimizes the posterior \(\alpha\)-quantile under the declared objective orientation.

notation.meaning: Posterior response distribution function at x.
Lower alpha-quantile of the posterior response.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the leaf, but the record calls alpha a risk level while optimizing a generic posterior response quantile. Without a source, it is unclear whether the intended quantity represents epistemic posterior uncertainty, aleatoric response risk, or a predictive mixture of both; that distinction changes the mathematical policy.

children.title: Orientation Conventions
children.top_down_role: Sign, tail, and objective-direction conventions used across confidence policies.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the complementary-level identity for generalized quantiles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For generalized-inverse lower quantiles, atoms or flat distribution-function segments can invalidate \(Q_{-Z}(\alpha)=-Q_Z(1-\alpha)\). Reflection then relates a lower quantile to an upper-quantile convention involving distribution-function left limits, so generalized-inverse and tie conventions must be specified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With atoms or flat distribution-function segments, simple complementary lower-quantile conversion can fail.
assumptions_latex: Quantiles are defined by generalized inverses.
The distribution may contain atoms or flat distribution-function segments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Continuity and strict increase cannot be omitted from the simple complementary-quantile identity.}

notation.meaning: Left limit of the distribution function at z.

knowledge_statements.title: Atom Boundary for Quantile-Tail Conversion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tail-index conversion when translating posterior-quantile policies between objective orientations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a real posterior random variable \(Z\), define \(Q_Z(\alpha)=\inf\{z:F_Z(z)\geq\alpha\}\). If \(F_Z\) is continuous and strictly increasing, then \[Q_{-Z}(\alpha)=-Q_Z(1-\alpha),\qquad \alpha\in(0,1).\] Thus objective negation reverses the optimization direction and exchanges complementary tails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negating an objective reverses optimization direction and exchanges complementary posterior-quantile levels.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) is real-valued.
\(F_Z\) is continuous and strictly increasing.
knowledge_statements.title: Quantile Transformation Under Objective Negation
Orientation Conventions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign conversion between maximization UCB and minimization LCB.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be an objective to maximize and define the minimization-oriented objective \(g=-f\). If the posterior of \(f(x)\) has mean \(\mu_f(x)\) and standard deviation \(s_f(x)\), then \(g(x)\) has mean \(\mu_g(x)=-\mu_f(x)\) and standard deviation \(s_g(x)=s_f(x)\). Hence, for every \(\beta>0\), \[\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X}\{\mu_f(x)+\sqrt\beta s_f(x)\}=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x\in\mathcal X}\{\mu_g(x)-\sqrt\beta s_g(x)\}.\] Therefore UCB and LCB labels are meaningful only together with the stated optimization orientation and sign convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negating the objective converts maximization by UCB exactly into minimization by LCB without changing posterior standard deviations.
assumptions_latex: \(g(x)=-f(x)\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\).
Both optimization problems use the same feasible set and confidence parameter.
The relevant optimizer sets are nonempty.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded introductory characterization of the Bayesian knowledge-gradient policy; no formal acquisition formula is supplied.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under a Bayesian belief model, the basic knowledge gradient evaluates the value of a single experiment by the improvement in decision quality obtainable from the resulting better understanding of the problem. knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step value of information when the terminal recommendation maximizes the posterior mean and may be a location never evaluated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal D\) induce posterior mean \(\mu_{\mathcal D}\) and predictive density \(p(y\mid x,\mathcal D)\) on \(\mathcal X\). Define the global-reward utility by \(u(\mathcal D)=\max_{x'\in\mathcal X}\mu_{\mathcal D}(x')\). If observing \(y\) at \(x\) produces \(\mathcal D'=\mathcal D\cup\{(x,y)\}\), then the knowledge-gradient acquisition function is \[\alpha_{\mathrm{KG}}(x;\mathcal D)=\int \max_{x'\in\mathcal X}\mu_{\mathcal D'}(x')\,p(y\mid x,\mathcal D)\,dy-\max_{x'\in\mathcal X}\mu_{\mathcal D}(x').\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The global reward is the maximum posterior mean over the domain. When the terminal recommendation may be an unevaluated point, the knowledge gradient of sampling at x is the expected global reward after observing that sample minus the current global reward.
assumptions_latex: u(\mathcal D)=\max_{x'\in\mathcal X}\mu_{\mathcal D}(x')
y\sim p(\cdot\mid x,\mathcal D)
\mathcal D'=\mathcal D\cup\{(x,y)\}
\text{The terminal recommendation may be any }x'\in\mathcal X\text{, including an unevaluated location.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha_{\mathrm{KG}}(x;\mathcal D)=\mathbb E_{y\mid x,\mathcal D}\!\left[u(\mathcal D')\right]-u(\mathcal D).

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete-Alternative Knowledge Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step value of information for finitely many correlated alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X=\{1,\ldots,M\}\), let \(\mu_n(i)=\mathbb E[f(i)\mid D_n]\), and let \(D_{n+1}^{(i)}\) denote the random posterior data state obtained by measuring alternative \(i\) once. Define \[\operatorname{KG}_n(i)=\mathbb E_n\!\left[\max_{j\in\mathcal X}\mu_{n+1}(j;D_{n+1}^{(i)})\right]-\max_{j\in\mathcal X}\mu_n(j).\] Select \(i_n\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{i\in\mathcal X}\operatorname{KG}_n(i)\), observe its response, and update the joint posterior. After the sampling budget is exhausted, recommend an alternative maximizing the terminal posterior mean.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Measure the alternative whose observation has the largest expected one-step increase in the best posterior mean.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) is finite and nonempty.
All displayed conditional expectations are finite.
The posterior models correlations among alternatives and specifies the observation law.

notation.meaning: One-step expected value of measuring alternative i.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Upper-Envelope Evaluation of Gaussian Discrete KG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact scalar integration after eliminating dominated affine pieces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a measured alternative \(i\), form lines \(a_j+b_jz\) with \(a_j=\mu_n(j)\) and \(b_j=b_j^{(i)}\). Remove duplicate-slope lines with smaller intercept and lines that never attain the upper envelope. If retained lines are active on \((c_{r-1},c_r]\), then \[\mathbb E\max_j(a_j+b_jZ)=\sum_r\left[a_r\{\Phi(c_r)-\Phi(c_{r-1})\}+b_r\{\phi(c_{r-1})-\phi(c_r)\}\right],\] where \(c_0=-\infty\) and \(c_R=\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gaussian finite-alternative KG is evaluated exactly by constructing the upper envelope of affine functions and integrating its active segments against the normal density.
assumptions_latex: The Gaussian affine-envelope representation applies.
Envelope breakpoints and active lines are computed exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed sum equals the expected posterior-best mean for the measured alternative.

notation.meaning: standard normal density and distribution function

knowledge_statements.title: Upper-Envelope Evaluation of Gaussian Discrete KG

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic complexity of evaluating all finite-alternative Gaussian KG scores through sorted upper envelopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each measured alternative \(i\), sorting the \(M\) slopes and constructing the upper envelope requires \(O(M\log M)\) comparisons and \(O(M)\) additional envelope work. Evaluating all \(M\) candidate measurements therefore requires \(O(M^2\log M)\) envelope work, excluding posterior-covariance construction and numerical optimization overhead.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sorted upper-envelope evaluation costs order M log M per measured alternative and order M squared log M for all alternatives.
assumptions_latex: Sorting-based exact upper-envelope construction is used.
Arithmetic operations and evaluations of \(\phi\) and \(\Phi\) have constant unit cost.
Posterior covariance coefficients are already available.
knowledge_statements.title: Gaussian Envelope-Evaluation Complexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic value-of-information property for finite alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If posterior means are integrable and satisfy \(\mathbb E_n[\mu_{n+1}(j)]=\mu_n(j)\) for every alternative, then \[\operatorname{KG}_n(i)=\mathbb E_n[\max_j\mu_{n+1}(j)]-\max_j\mu_n(j)\ge0.\] If measuring \(i\) leaves the entire posterior mean vector unchanged almost surely, then \(\operatorname{KG}_n(i)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discrete KG is nonnegative and vanishes for a measurement that cannot change any posterior mean.
assumptions_latex: All posterior means are integrable.
\(\mathbb E_n[\mu_{n+1}(j)]=\mu_n(j)\) for every alternative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{KG}_n(i)\ge0\), with zero value under posterior-mean invariance.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonnegativity and Zero-Information Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gaussian Affine-Envelope Representation of Discrete KG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar normal representation for a correlated Gaussian finite-alternative posterior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the latent alternative vector has posterior covariance \(\Sigma_n\), and measuring alternative \(i\) adds independent Gaussian noise of variance \(\lambda_i>0\). Define \[b_j^{(i)}=\frac{\Sigma_n(j,i)}{\sqrt{\Sigma_n(i,i)+\lambda_i}}.\] For \(Z\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), \[\mu_{n+1}(j)\overset d=\mu_n(j)+b_j^{(i)}Z,\qquad \operatorname{KG}_n(i)=\mathbb E\!\left[\max_j\{\mu_n(j)+b_j^{(i)}Z\}\right]-\max_j\mu_n(j).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A correlated Gaussian measurement makes every updated alternative mean affine in one common standard-normal innovation, reducing KG to an expected upper envelope of lines.
assumptions_latex: The alternative-value posterior is multivariate Gaussian.
Measurement noise is independent Gaussian with variance \(\lambda_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Discrete Gaussian KG is the expected upper envelope of \(\mu_n(j)+b_j^{(i)}Z\) minus the current largest mean.

notation.meaning: standardized effect of measuring i on mean j

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Offline knowledge gradient for discrete independent Gaussian alternatives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step value-of-information policy for discrete alternatives with independent Gaussian beliefs and noisy Gaussian measurements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A\) be a discrete action set containing at least two alternatives, with the displayed maxima attained. Conditional on \(S^n\), suppose \(\mu_a\sim\mathcal N(\theta_a^n,\bar\sigma_a^{2,n})\) independently across alternatives, and sampling \(a\) yields \(\widehat C_a^{n+1}=\mu_a+\varepsilon_a^{n+1}\), where the Gaussian measurement error has known precision \(\beta_a^W\). Writing \(\beta_a^n=1/\bar\sigma_a^{2,n}\), sampling \(a\) gives \(\theta_a^{n+1}=(\beta_a^n\theta_a^n+\beta_a^W\widehat C_a^{n+1})/(\beta_a^n+\beta_a^W)\) and \(\beta_a^{n+1}=\beta_a^n+\beta_a^W\), while beliefs for unobserved alternatives remain unchanged. With \(V^n(S^n)=\max_{a'\in\mathcal A}\theta_{a'}^n\), define \(v_a^{\mathrm{KG},n}=\mathbb E[V^{n+1}(S^{n+1})\mid S^n,\text{ sample }a]-V^n(S^n)\). Let \(\widetilde\sigma_a^{2,n}=\operatorname{Var}(\theta_a^{n+1}-\theta_a^n\mid S^n)=\bar\sigma_a^{2,n}-\bar\sigma_a^{2,n+1}\), \(\zeta_a^n=-\left|(\theta_a^n-\max_{a'\ne a}\theta_{a'}^n)/\widetilde\sigma_a^n\right|\), and \(f(z)=z\Phi(z)+\phi(z)\). Then \(v_a^{\mathrm{KG},n}=\widetilde\sigma_a^n f(\zeta_a^n)\), and the policy samples an alternative maximizing this index.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For discrete alternatives with independent Gaussian beliefs and Gaussian measurement noise, observing an alternative updates its posterior mean and precision by conjugate Bayesian updating. The offline knowledge gradient is the expected one-step increase in the largest posterior mean. Its closed form is the standard deviation of the posterior-mean change multiplied by z Phi(z) plus phi(z), evaluated at the normalized gap from the best competing alternative. The policy samples an alternative having the largest index.
assumptions_latex: |\mathcal A|\ge 2\text{, and all displayed maxima are attained.}
\mu_a\mid S^n\sim\mathcal N(\theta_a^n,\bar\sigma_a^{2,n})\text{ independently across alternatives.}
\widehat C_a^{n+1}=\mu_a+\varepsilon_a^{n+1}\text{, with conditionally Gaussian measurement error of known precision }\beta_a^W.

children.title: Continuous-Domain Knowledge Gradient
children.top_down_role: Knowledge-gradient policies requiring continuous posterior decision optimization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise nested Monte Carlo approximation of continuous-domain KG.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a candidate query \(x\), draw predictive fantasies \(Y_x^{(1)},\ldots,Y_x^{(K)}\) and define \[\widehat{\operatorname{KG}}_{n,K}(x)=\frac1K\sum_{k=1}^K\sup_{z\in\mathcal X}\mu_{n+1}(z;Y_x^{(k)})-\sup_{z\in\mathcal X}\mu_n(z).\] If every inner supremum is evaluated exactly and the summands are integrable, this is an unbiased pointwise estimator of \(\operatorname{KG}_n(x)\). Uncontrolled approximate inner maximization instead estimates a solver-dependent approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuous KG can be estimated with fantasy posterior updates and repeated continuous posterior-mean optimization; pointwise unbiasedness requires exact inner solves.
assumptions_latex: The fantasies are sampled from the current predictive law.
The optimized posterior-mean values are integrable.
Every displayed inner supremum is evaluated exactly for the unbiasedness claim.
knowledge_statements.title: Fantasy-Sample Continuous KG Approximation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step value-of-information property for a continuous posterior decision problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If posterior means obey \(\mathbb E_n[\mu_{n+1}(z)]=\mu_n(z)\) for every \(z\in\mathcal X\), and the random supremum is measurable and integrable, then \[\operatorname{KG}_n(x)=\mathbb E_n\!\left[\sup_{z\in\mathcal X}\mu_{n+1}(z)\right]-\sup_{z\in\mathcal X}\mu_n(z)\ge0.\] If observing at \(x\) leaves every posterior mean unchanged almost surely, then \(\operatorname{KG}_n(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact continuous-domain KG is nonnegative and vanishes for an observation that cannot change any posterior mean.
assumptions_latex: Posterior means satisfy conditional iterated expectation.
The random supremum is measurable and integrable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{KG}_n(x)\ge0\), with zero value for posterior-mean-invariant observations.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonnegativity of Exact Continuous KG

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample accuracy of the exact-inner-solve Monte Carlo KG estimator at one fixed query.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(x\) and write \(V_k(x)=\sup_{z\in\mathcal X}\mu_{n+1}(z;Y_x^{(k)})\). If the fantasies are conditionally i.i.d. and \(a\le V_k(x)\le b\) almost surely, then for every \(\epsilon>0\), \[\mathbb P_n\!\left(\left|\widehat{\operatorname{KG}}_{n,K}(x)-\operatorname{KG}_n(x)\right|\ge\epsilon\right)\le2\exp\!\left(-\frac{2K\epsilon^2}{(b-a)^2}\right).\] Consequently, conditional error at most \(\epsilon\) with probability at least \(1-\delta\) is ensured by \(K\ge (b-a)^2\log(2/\delta)/(2\epsilon^2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded optimized fantasy values give a Hoeffding pointwise error bound for the continuous-KG Monte Carlo estimator.
assumptions_latex: The query \(x\) is fixed independently of the fantasy sample.
Fantasy observations are conditionally i.i.d.
All inner posterior-mean suprema are exact and lie in \([a,b]\) almost surely.

notation.meaning: optimized posterior-mean value under the k-th fantasy

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nested-Solve Error Certificate for Fantasy KG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic propagation of certified inner and baseline optimization errors into a fantasy-sample continuous-KG estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fantasies \(Y_x^{(1)},\ldots,Y_x^{(K)}\), let \(V_k=\sup_{z\in\mathcal X}\mu_{n+1}(z;Y_x^{(k)})\) and \(V_0=\sup_{z\in\mathcal X}\mu_n(z)\). Suppose computed feasible values satisfy \(0\le V_k-\widetilde V_k\le\varepsilon_k\) and \(0\le V_0-\widetilde V_0\le\varepsilon_0\). With \(\widehat{\operatorname{KG}}_K=K^{-1}\sum_kV_k-V_0\) and \(\widetilde{\operatorname{KG}}_K=K^{-1}\sum_k\widetilde V_k-\widetilde V_0\), \[\left|\widetilde{\operatorname{KG}}_K-\widehat{\operatorname{KG}}_K\right|\le\varepsilon_0+\frac1K\sum_{k=1}^K\varepsilon_k.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified inner-solve and baseline gaps bound the numerical error in a fantasy-sample KG value.
assumptions_latex: Each computed inner value is feasible and has the stated certified global optimality gap.
The current posterior-mean baseline has the stated certified global optimality gap.

notation.meaning: Exact and computed optimized posterior-mean values for fantasy k.
Exact and computed current posterior-mean optima.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Incomplete Inner Search Can Erase the Correct KG Ranking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-fantasy posterior-decision example showing selection failure from incomplete inner search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the current posterior means of decisions \(a,b\) both equal \(1\). Query \(x\) has two equiprobable fantasy updates \((2,0)\) and \((0,2)\), so its exact KG is \(1\). Query \(x'\) has equiprobable updates \((3/2,1/2)\) and \((1/2,3/2)\), so its exact KG is \(1/2\). If an inner solver examines only decision \(a\), its computed optimized-value average is \(1\) for both queries. With exact baseline \(1\), both computed KG values are zero, and a tie rule may select \(x'\) although \(\operatorname{KG}(x)>\operatorname{KG}(x')\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Omitting possible posterior-mean maximizers can erase the correct continuous-KG ranking and select the inferior query.
assumptions_latex: The two displayed fantasy outcomes for each query are equiprobable.
The current baseline optimization is exact.
The incomplete inner solver evaluates only decision \(a\), and query ties may be resolved in favor of \(x'\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step posterior decision value over a continuous feasible domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be nonempty, let \(\mu_n(x)=\mathbb E[f(x)\mid D_n]\), and let \(D_{n+1}^{(x)}\) be the random data state after observing at \(x\). Define \[\operatorname{KG}_n(x)=\mathbb E_n\!\left[\sup_{z\in\mathcal X}\mu_{n+1}(z;D_{n+1}^{(x)})\right]-\sup_{z\in\mathcal X}\mu_n(z).\] Choose \(x_n\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X}\operatorname{KG}_n(x)\), obtain the observation, and update the posterior. Both the inner posterior-decision optimization and the outer acquisition optimization are continuous-domain problems; after the budget, recommend a maximizer of the terminal posterior mean.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the continuous location maximizing the expected one-step improvement in the optimally achievable posterior mean.
assumptions_latex: The displayed suprema and expectations are finite and measurable.
The outer argmax is attained.
The posterior and observation model are specified on \(\mathcal X\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Information Monotonicity of Batch Knowledge Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of a joint batch with a subbatch under the same posterior-mean terminal utility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq X\) and suppose \(\sigma(Y_S)\subseteq\sigma(Y_X)\) conditional on \(\mathcal D_n\). If the posterior decision values are measurable and integrable, then \(\operatorname{KG}_n(X)\ge\operatorname{KG}_n(S)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A joint batch cannot have lower expected posterior decision value than a contained subbatch when both use the same terminal utility.
assumptions_latex: \(\sigma(Y_S)\subseteq\sigma(Y_X)\) conditional on \(\mathcal D_n\).
The posterior decision values are measurable and integrable.
The batch and subbatch use the same terminal utility and baseline.

notation.meaning: A subbatch of the proposed batch.
Joint observation vector from batch X.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Batch Knowledge Gradient Is Not Additive
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Redundant-observation counterexample for an admissible repeated-location batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let action \(a\) have known value \(1\), and let action \(b\) have value \(\Theta\), where \(\mathbb P(\Theta=0)=\mathbb P(\Theta=2)=1/2\). Before sampling, the best posterior mean is \(1\). One exact observation of \(\Theta\) gives expected terminal value \(\mathbb E[\max\{1,\Theta\}]=3/2\), so its singleton KG is \(1/2\). If repeated locations are admissible, a synchronous batch containing two identical exact measurements of \(\Theta\) reveals no more than one measurement. Its batch KG is therefore \(1/2\), whereas the sum of the two singleton values is \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two perfectly redundant admissible measurements have positive singleton values, but their joint batch value is not their sum.
assumptions_latex: Repeated-location batches are admissible.
Both batch observations reveal the same latent variable \(\Theta\) exactly.
Terminal utility is the maximum posterior mean over \(a,b\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Fantasy Concentration for Synchronous qKG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional finite-sample accuracy of an exact-inner-solve fantasy estimator at one fixed admissible batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an admissible batch \(X\), draw conditionally i.i.d. joint fantasies \(Y_X^{(1)},\ldots,Y_X^{(K)}\), and let \(V_k(X)=\sup_z\mu_{n+q}(z;X,Y_X^{(k)})\). If \(a\le V_k(X)\le b\) almost surely and every inner supremum is exact, then \[\widehat{\operatorname{qKG}}_{n,K}(X)=\frac1K\sum_{k=1}^K V_k(X)-\sup_z\mu_n(z)\] is unbiased and \[\mathbb P_n\!\left(\left|\widehat{\operatorname{qKG}}_{n,K}(X)-\operatorname{qKG}_n(X)\right|\ge\epsilon\right)\le2\exp\!\left(-\frac{2K\epsilon^2}{(b-a)^2}\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded optimized joint-fantasy values give an unbiased fixed-batch qKG estimator with a Hoeffding error bound.
assumptions_latex: The candidate batch is fixed independently of the fantasy sample.
Joint fantasies are conditionally i.i.d. under the declared synchronous observation model.
Every inner posterior-mean optimization is exact and lies in \([a,b]\) almost surely.

notation.meaning: k-th joint fantasy observation for batch X.
Optimized posterior-mean value under the k-th joint fantasy.

Parallel Knowledge Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Batch value of information for simultaneously selected observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_n\) be the current data and let \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_q)\in\mathcal X^q\) be a batch whose joint future observation is \(Y_X\). If \(\mu_n(z)=\mathbb E[f(z)\mid D_n]\) and \(\mu_{n+q}(z;X,Y_X)\) is the posterior mean after observing the batch, define \[\operatorname{qKG}_n(X)=\mathbb E_n\!\left[\sup_{z\in\mathcal X}\mu_{n+q}(z;X,Y_X)\right]-\sup_{z\in\mathcal X}\mu_n(z).\] Select a maximizing batch, evaluate its points in parallel, update jointly when observations arrive, and recommend a maximizer of the terminal posterior mean after the fixed budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select the batch whose joint observations give the largest expected increase in the best posterior mean.
assumptions_latex: \(q\in\mathbb N\) and admissible batches form a nonempty subset of \(\mathcal X^q\).
The displayed expectations and suprema are finite and measurable.
A maximizing admissible batch exists.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero Value of a Target-Irrelevant Fidelity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for a fidelity observation carrying no posterior information about the target-fidelity function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Y_{x,\ell}\perp f(\cdot,\ell_\star)\mid\mathcal D_n\), then \(\mu_{n+1}(z,\ell_\star)=\mu_n(z,\ell_\star)\) almost surely for every \(z\), and consequently \(\operatorname{KG}_n(x,\ell)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fidelity conditionally uninformative about the target fidelity has zero multifidelity knowledge-gradient value.

Target posterior means and their supremum are measurable and integrable.

Multifidelity Knowledge Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost-aware value of information from correlated fidelity channels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x,\ell)\) be a jointly modeled response on \(\mathcal X\times\mathcal L\), let \(\ell_\star\) denote the target fidelity, and let \(c(x,\ell)>0\) be observation cost. With \(\mu_n(z,\ell_\star)=\mathbb E[f(z,\ell_\star)\mid D_n]\), define the target-value gain from sampling \((x,\ell)\) by \[\operatorname{KG}_n(x,\ell)=\mathbb E_n\!\left[\sup_{z\in\mathcal X}\mu_{n+1}(z,\ell_\star)\right]-\sup_{z\in\mathcal X}\mu_n(z,\ell_\star).\] Select \((x_n,\ell_n)\) maximizing \(\operatorname{KG}_n(x,\ell)/c(x,\ell)\) among affordable channels, observe it, update the joint posterior, and ultimately recommend a target-fidelity design.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the affordable location and fidelity giving the largest expected target-fidelity decision improvement per unit cost.
assumptions_latex: The joint posterior couples every sampled fidelity to the target fidelity.
\(c(x,\ell)>0\) and the affordable action set is nonempty.
The displayed expectations and optimization values are finite.

Cost of observing location x at fidelity l.

children.title: Derivative Knowledge Gradient

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Derivative Observation Is Not an Acquisition Derivative
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between derivative-channel KG and differentiating a KG acquisition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A derivative-KG query observes a random channel such as \(Y_{x,j}=\partial_j f(x)+\varepsilon\) and values the posterior decision change caused by that observation. This is distinct from \(\nabla_x\alpha_n(x)\), the derivative of an acquisition with respect to its query location. Existence or availability of either object does not imply existence or availability of the other.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Derivative knowledge gradient concerns observing an objective derivative, not computing the input gradient of a knowledge-gradient acquisition.
assumptions_latex: The derivative observation channel and acquisition input derivative are interpreted as separate mathematical objects.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y_{x,j}\) is observation data, whereas \(\nabla_x\alpha_n(x)\) is an acquisition-optimization quantity.
knowledge_statements.title: Derivative Observation Is Not an Acquisition Derivative

assumptions_latex: The latent objective is a differentiable random function \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\), and decisions maximize \(f\).
Conditional on \(\mathcal D_n\), the derivative observation \(Y_{x,j}=\partial_j f(x)+\varepsilon\) has a well-defined posterior predictive distribution.
The posterior mean after adjoining \((x,j,Y_{x,j})\) is \(\mu_{n+1}^{x,j,Y_{x,j}}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_n^{\mathrm{DKG}}(x,j)\) is the expected increase in the best posterior-mean objective value produced by observing derivative coordinate \(j\) at \(x\).

notation.meaning: Noisy derivative observation at location x in coordinate j.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step, risk-neutral derivative-channel knowledge gradient for maximization.

source_refs.locator: 7.4 The Knowledge Gradient Algorithm for Discrete Alternatives p. 262

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every admissible derivative query \((x,j)\), define
\[
\alpha_n^{\mathrm{DKG}}(x,j)=\mathbb E\!\left[\sup_{u\in\mathcal X}\mu_{n+1}^{x,j,Y_{x,j}}(u)\mid\mathcal D_n\right]-\sup_{u\in\mathcal X}\mu_n(u).
\]
When derivative-query costs \(c_j(x)>0\) differ, the cost-normalized policy selects any
\[
(x_{n+1},j_{n+1})\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{(x,j)}\frac{\alpha_n^{\mathrm{DKG}}(x,j)}{c_j(x)}.
\]
The expectation integrates over the current predictive law of \(Y_{x,j}\); it does not evaluate improvement in a realized objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Derivative knowledge gradient values a derivative query by its expected one-step increase in the maximum posterior mean, optionally divided by query cost.

children.top_down_role: Policies comparing information value across distinct observation types.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an admissible query \((x,c)\in\mathcal X\times\mathcal C\), define its knowledge gradient by
\[
\operatorname{KG}_n(x,c)=\mathbb E\!\left[\sup_{u\in\mathcal X}\mu_{n+1}^{x,c,Y_{x,c}}(u)\mid\mathcal D_n\right]-\sup_{u\in\mathcal X}\mu_n(u).
\]
The cost-sensitive heterogeneous-channel policy selects
\[
(x_{n+1},c_{n+1})\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{(x,c)}\frac{\operatorname{KG}_n(x,c)}{\kappa(x,c)}.
\]
Channels may represent objective values, derivatives, fidelities, or auxiliary responses, but their value is determined through their joint posterior dependence with the objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Heterogeneous-channel knowledge gradient compares correlated observation types by their expected increase in posterior decision value per unit cost.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounds and Nullity of Optimizer Information Gain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural properties of ideal optimizer-location mutual information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Whenever the information quantities are finite, \[0\le I(X^\star;Y_x\mid\mathcal D_n)\le H(X^\star\mid\mathcal D_n).\] Moreover, \(I(X^\star;Y_x\mid\mathcal D_n)=0\) if and only if \(X^\star\) and \(Y_x\) are conditionally independent given \(\mathcal D_n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimizer information gain is nonnegative, cannot exceed the remaining optimizer entropy, and vanishes exactly for a conditionally uninformative query.
assumptions_latex: The conditional mutual information and optimizer entropy are finite.
\(X^\star\) is defined by a specified tie rule when the optimizer is not unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le I(X^\star;Y_x\mid\mathcal D_n)\le H(X^\star\mid\mathcal D_n)\), with zero value exactly under conditional independence.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounds and Nullity of Optimizer Information Gain

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monte Carlo entropy reduction for a declared finite optimizer-location approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\{x_k^\star,w_k\}_{k=1}^K\) be a declared discrete approximation to \(p(X^\star\mid\mathcal D_n)\). For each candidate \(x\), draw conditionally iid fantasies \(Y_x^{(s)}\), update \(w_{k,s}'\propto w_kp(Y_x^{(s)}\mid X^\star=x_k^\star,\mathcal D_n)\), and compute \(\widehat\alpha_{K,S}(x)=H(w)-S^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^SH(w_s')\). For fixed \(K\), exact conditional likelihoods, and integrable entropy, this converges almost surely as \(S\to\infty\) to the information gain of the declared discrete approximation, not automatically to the continuous ideal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A practical approximation represents optimizer location by weighted particles and averages their entropy reduction over fantasy observations.
assumptions_latex: w_k\ge0,\quad\sum_kw_k=1.
Y_x^{(s)}\text{ are conditionally iid posterior-predictive fantasies}.
p(Y_x\mid X^\star=x_k^\star,\mathcal D_n)\text{ is defined for the declared approximation}.
H(w_s')\text{ is conditionally integrable}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mutual-information acquisition targeting the posterior optimizer location.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X^\star\) be a posterior-random optimizer selected by a declared measurable tie rule, and let \(Y_x\) be the prospective observation at \(x\). Optimizer-entropy search uses \(\alpha_n^{\mathrm{ES}}(x)=I(X^\star;Y_x\mid\mathcal D_n)\). Whenever the entropy representation is finite, \(\alpha_n^{\mathrm{ES}}(x)=H(X^\star\mid\mathcal D_n)-\mathbb E[H(X^\star\mid\mathcal D_n,Y_x)\mid\mathcal D_n]\). The next query maximizes this acquisition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimizer-entropy search chooses the observation with greatest expected information gain about optimizer location.
assumptions_latex: X^\star\text{ is defined by a declared measurable optimizer-selection rule}.
(X^\star,Y_x)\text{ has a joint posterior conditional on }\mathcal D_n.
The conditional mutual information is defined; the entropy-difference form additionally requires finite compatible entropies.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-target ambiguity when the posterior objective admits multiple optimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{u\in\mathcal X}f(u)\) is not almost surely a singleton, optimizer-location information is not uniquely specified until a measurable selection or a random-set-valued target is declared. Different tie rules can induce different laws for \(X^\star\) and hence different acquisitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiple optimizers require an explicit optimizer-selection convention; otherwise optimizer entropy is ambiguous.
assumptions_latex: The posterior may assign positive probability to nonunique optimizer sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pr(|\operatorname*{arg\,max}f|>1\mid\mathcal D_n)>0\implies X^\star\text{ requires an explicit target convention}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate invariance of mutual information despite coordinate dependence of differential entropy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any measurable bijection \(g\) on optimizer locations with measurable inverse, \(I(g(X^\star);Y_x\mid\mathcal D_n)=I(X^\star;Y_x\mid\mathcal D_n)\) whenever the mutual information is defined. Individual differential entropies can change under \(g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimizer mutual information is invariant under invertible reparameterization even though differential entropy alone is not.
assumptions_latex: g\text{ is a measurable bijection with measurable inverse}.
The displayed mutual informations are defined.
knowledge_statements.title: Reparameterization Invariance of Optimizer Information

assumptions_latex: Conditional on \(\mathcal D_n\), the random maximizer \(X^\star\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{u\in\mathcal X}f(u)\) has a specified tie-breaking rule.
A candidate query at \(x\) produces \(Y_x\) with a joint posterior distribution with \(X^\star\).
The displayed entropies or mutual information are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Maximizing \(\alpha_n^{\mathrm{ES}}(x)\) selects the observation expected to reduce uncertainty about the optimizer location most strongly.

notation.meaning: Random optimizer under the current posterior.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mutual-information formulation targeting the posterior optimizer location.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Optimizer-entropy search assigns to each query \(x\in\mathcal X\) the acquisition
\[
\alpha_n^{\mathrm{ES}}(x)=I(X^\star;Y_x\mid\mathcal D_n)
=H(X^\star\mid\mathcal D_n)-\mathbb E\!\left[H(X^\star\mid\mathcal D_n,Y_x)\mid\mathcal D_n\right].
\]
For discrete \(\mathcal X\), \(H\) is Shannon entropy. For continuous \(\mathcal X\), it is differential entropy relative to a fixed reference measure whenever finite. The next query is any \(x_{n+1}\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X}\alpha_n^{\mathrm{ES}}(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimizer-entropy search chooses the query with greatest mutual information about the posterior location of the objective maximizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimizer-Entropy Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ideal mutual-information formulation is mathematically coherent under the stated finiteness and tie-breaking assumptions, but no inspectable source is supplied for optimizer-entropy search.

children.title: Predictive Entropy Search
