knowledge_statements.statement_title: PES Is Not Marginal Predictive-Entropy Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating predictive entropy search from maximum-entropy design.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The ideal PES score has the form \[H(Y_x\mid\mathcal D_n)-\mathbb E_{X^\star\mid\mathcal D_n}H(Y_x\mid\mathcal D_n,X^\star).\] If the optimizer-conditioned entropy term is constant in \(x\), maximizing PES is equivalent to maximizing marginal predictive entropy. Without that condition the subtraction can change the ranking, so a point of greatest predictive entropy need not maximize information about \(X^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PES is not ordinary uncertainty sampling because optimizer-conditioned predictive entropy can change the ranking of query locations.
assumptions_latex: The displayed conditional entropies are finite.
knowledge_statements.title: PES Is Not Marginal Predictive-Entropy Sampling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic Monte Carlo architecture for approximate PES without selecting a particular conditioning engine.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Draw \(X_1^\star,\ldots,X_K^\star\) from the posterior optimizer law. For each draw construct an approximation \(q_k(y\mid x)\) to \(p(Y_x=y\mid\mathcal D_n,X^\star=X_k^\star)\), and set \[\widehat\alpha_{n,K}(x)=H[p(Y_x\mid\mathcal D_n)]-\frac1K\sum_{k=1}^K H[q_k(\cdot\mid x)].\] Maximizing \(\widehat\alpha_{n,K}\) implements approximate PES. Increasing \(K\) removes only Monte Carlo error; convergence to ideal PES additionally requires consistent optimizer sampling and conditional-law approximation together with sufficient entropy integrability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate PES samples possible optimizers and averages approximations to optimizer-conditioned predictive entropy; more Monte Carlo samples do not remove conditioning bias.
assumptions_latex: The optimizer samples and displayed entropies are well defined.
The marginal predictive entropy can be evaluated or consistently estimated.
Any convergence claim additionally assumes consistent conditional-law approximations and sufficient entropy integrability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\alpha_{n,K}(x)=H(Y_x\mid\mathcal D_n)-K^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^K H[q_k(\cdot\mid x)]\) is an approximate PES score.

notation.meaning: approximate predictive law conditioned on the k-th optimizer sample

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximum Predictive Entropy Can Disagree with PES
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite posterior-function model separating uncertainty sampling from optimizer information gain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let independent \(U,N\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) except that \(\mathbb P(N=1)=0.1\), and let \(Z\) be uniform on \(\{0,1,2,3\}\). On \(\mathcal X=\{a,b,c,d\}\), set \((f(a),f(b))=(10,9)\) when \(U=0\) and \((9,10)\) when \(U=1\), set \(f(c)=U\oplus N\), and set \(f(d)=Z\). With noiseless observations, the optimizer is \(a\) or \(b\) according to \(U\). In bits, \(H(Y_c)=1\), \(H(Y_d)=2\), \(I(Y_c;X^\star)=1-h_2(0.1)>0\), and \(I(Y_d;X^\star)=0\). Thus maximum predictive entropy uniquely selects \(d\), whereas PES uniquely selects \(c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A high-entropy objective observation can be independent of the optimizer, while a lower-entropy observation is informative about it.
assumptions_latex: The posterior function and noiseless observation model are exactly as specified.
Ties are absent because the optimizer is uniquely \(a\) or \(b\).
knowledge_statements.title: Maximum Predictive Entropy Can Disagree with PES

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete PES conditioning engine for a weighted finite posterior over functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let posterior particles \((f_j,w_j)_{j=1}^J\) satisfy \(w_j\ge0\), \(\sum_jw_j=1\), and let \(T(f_j)\) be their tie-broken optimizers. Under \(Y_x\mid f_j\sim N(f_j(x),\tau_x^2)\), define \[p(y\mid x)=\sum_jw_j\varphi_{\tau_x}(y-f_j(x)),\qquad p(y\mid x,X^\star=u)=\sum_{j:T(f_j)=u}\frac{w_j}{W_u}\varphi_{\tau_x}(y-f_j(x)),\] where \(W_u=\sum_{j:T(f_j)=u}w_j>0\). The score \[H[p(\cdot\mid x)]-\sum_uW_uH[p(\cdot\mid x,X^\star=u)]\] is exact for the discrete particle posterior and approximate for the target posterior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Group weighted function particles by optimizer and compare marginal with optimizer-conditioned predictive-mixture entropy.
assumptions_latex: w_j\ge0\text{ and }\sum_jw_j=1.
T\text{ is a fixed tie-broken optimizer map}.
\tau_x^2>0\text{ and all mixture entropies are finite}.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(x\). Let \(h_x(u)=H(Y_x\mid\mathcal D_n,X^\star=u)\in[0,B]\), and suppose \(\sup_u|\widetilde h_x(u)-h_x(u)|\le\eta\). For i.i.d. optimizer samples \(U_1,\ldots,U_K\), set \(\widehat c_K=K^{-1}\sum_k\widetilde h_x(U_k)\). With probability at least \(1-\delta\), \[|\widehat c_K-\mathbb Eh_x(X^\star)|\le\eta+B\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\delta)}{2K}}.\] Marginal-entropy numerical error adds separately, and increasing \(K\) cannot remove \(\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PES error separates into conditional-entropy approximation bias and optimizer-sampling error.
assumptions_latex: U_k\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\mathcal L(X^\star\mid\mathcal D_n).
0\le h_x(u)\le B.
\sup_u|\widetilde h_x(u)-h_x(u)|\le\eta.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X^\star\) be a measurable tie-broken posterior optimizer. Predictive entropy search uses \[\alpha_n^{\mathrm{PES}}(x)=I(Y_x;X^\star\mid\mathcal D_n)=H(Y_x\mid\mathcal D_n)-\mathbb E[H(Y_x\mid\mathcal D_n,X^\star)\mid\mathcal D_n].\] By mutual-information symmetry this also equals the expected reduction in \(H(X^\star\mid\mathcal D_n)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PES computes information about the optimizer through marginal predictive entropy minus optimizer-conditioned predictive entropy.

assumptions_latex: Conditional on \(\mathcal D_n\), \(X^\star\) is a tie-broken random maximizer of \(f\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ideal predictive-entropy representation before numerical approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Predictive entropy search represents optimizer information gain by
\[
\alpha_n^{\mathrm{PES}}(x)=I(Y_x;X^\star\mid\mathcal D_n)
=H(Y_x\mid\mathcal D_n)-\mathbb E_{X^\star\mid\mathcal D_n}\!\left[H(Y_x\mid\mathcal D_n,X^\star)\right].
\]
By symmetry of mutual information, this equals
\[
H(X^\star\mid\mathcal D_n)-\mathbb E_{Y_x\mid\mathcal D_n}\!\left[H(X^\star\mid\mathcal D_n,Y_x)\right].
\]
Thus the policy selects any maximizer of \(\alpha_n^{\mathrm{PES}}\) over the admissible query set; computational implementations may approximate the conditional predictive entropy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Predictive entropy search rewrites optimizer information gain as predictive entropy minus expected predictive entropy conditioned on the optimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Predictive Entropy Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The predictive-entropy representation is consistent with mutual-information symmetry, but the record has no source supporting its identification with Predictive Entropy Search.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Precomputation-and-reuse implementation of predictive entropy search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expectation-propagation implementation for evaluating predictive entropy search with a sufficiently differentiable Gaussian-process surrogate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Estimate the required maximum moments and draw Thompson samples \(\{x_i^*\}\). For each sampled optimizer \(x^*\), form the joint Gaussian law of the relevant function-value, gradient, and Hessian variables \(z^*\), and apply Gaussian expectation propagation to the optimizer factors. From the resulting site parameters, precompute
\[
V_*^{-1}=\left(\Sigma^*+\begin{bmatrix}\widetilde\Sigma&0\\0&0\end{bmatrix}\right)^{-1},\qquad
\alpha^*=V_*^{-1}\left(\begin{bmatrix}\widetilde\mu\\0\end{bmatrix}-\mu^*\right),
\]
which do not depend on the proposed observation location \(x\). For each \(x\) and sampled \(x^*\), compute the relevant joint Gaussian covariance \(\Sigma\) and cross-covariance \(K\), then update
\[
m=\mu+K\alpha^*,\qquad
S=\Sigma-KV_*^{-1}K^\top
 =\begin{bmatrix}\varsigma^2&\rho\\\rho&\varsigma_*^2\end{bmatrix}.
\]
After a final expectation-propagation update for the prediction constraint, the approximate conditional predictive variance is
\[
\sigma_*^2=\varsigma^2-\frac{(\varsigma^2-\rho)^2}{\gamma}.
\]
Use this variance to compute the acquisition contribution for the optimizer sample. For numerical stability, use a matrix factorization and linear solves rather than explicitly storing \(V_*^{-1}\). In Euclidean domains, the acquisition gradient can also be computed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each Thompson-sampled optimizer, precompute an expectation-propagation approximation involving the GP value, gradient, and Hessian conditions. Reuse those candidate-independent factors when evaluating each proposed observation, perform a final EP update for the prediction constraint, and use the resulting conditional predictive variance to obtain that sample's acquisition contribution. Stable implementations use factorizations rather than storing a matrix inverse. The acquisition can also be differentiated on Euclidean domains.
assumptions_latex: \text{The Gaussian-process surrogate admits the joint value-gradient-Hessian Gaussian distributions used by the construction.}
\{x_i^*\}\text{ are Thompson samples representing the posterior distribution of the optimizer.}
\text{Gaussian expectation propagation is used for the optimizer and prediction constraints.}
\text{The covariance systems admit stable linear solves.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sigma_*^2=\varsigma^2-(\varsigma^2-\rho)^2/\gamma,\qquad\text{and the optimizer-specific EP factors can be reused across candidate locations }x.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Predictive form of optimizer mutual information
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predictive-entropy representation underlying predictive entropy search for information about the global optimizer location.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x^*\) denote the random global-optimizer location under the posterior conditioned on \(\mathcal D\). The predictive entropy search acquisition is
\[
\alpha_{x^*}(x;\mathcal D)
=H[y\mid x,\mathcal D]
-\mathbb E_{x^*\mid\mathcal D}\!\left[H[y\mid x,x^*,\mathcal D]\right].
\]
Thus all entropy evaluations concern the one-dimensional prospective observation \(y\), although approximating its distribution conditional on \(x^*\) and integrating over the posterior distribution of \(x^*\) remain necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Predictive entropy search equals the predictive entropy of a prospective observation minus its expected predictive entropy conditional on the unknown global optimizer. The entropies are one-dimensional in the observation, but the conditional distribution and expectation over the optimizer still require approximation.

y\sim p(y\mid x,\mathcal D)
H[y\mid x,\mathcal D]\text{ and }H[y\mid x,x^*,\mathcal D]\text{ exist}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha_{x^*}(x;\mathcal D)=H[y\mid x,\mathcal D]-\mathbb E_{x^*\mid\mathcal D}[H[y\mid x,x^*,\mathcal D]].

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Truncated-normal conditional-entropy approximation for maximization with noiseless Gaussian prediction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(f(x)\mid\mathcal D_n\sim\mathcal N(\mu_n(x),\sigma_n^2(x))\), \(\sigma_n(x)>0\), and conditioning on \(F^\star=m\) is approximated by truncating \(f(x)\) above at \(m\). Let \(\gamma_m(x)=(m-\mu_n(x))/\sigma_n(x)\). The resulting entropy reduction is \[g(\gamma_m)=\frac{\gamma_m\phi(\gamma_m)}{2\Phi(\gamma_m)}-\log\Phi(\gamma_m).\] For posterior optimum-value samples \(m_1,\ldots,m_K\), \[\widehat\alpha_n^{\mathrm{MES}}(x)=\frac1K\sum_{k=1}^K g(\gamma_{m_k}(x)).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A standard noiseless Gaussian MES approximation averages a closed-form upper-truncated-normal entropy reduction over sampled optimum values.
assumptions_latex: The query observes the latent value without observation noise.
The conditional predictive law is approximated by an upper-truncated Gaussian.
The values \(m_k\) are posterior samples of a finite \(F^\star\), and \(\sigma_n(x)>0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Draw conditionally independent functions \(f^{(k)}\sim\mathcal L(f\mid\mathcal D_n)\) and compute \(M_k=\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}f^{(k)}(x)\). If each supremum is evaluated exactly and is measurable and finite, then \(M_1,\ldots,M_K\) are conditionally i.i.d. draws from \(\mathcal L(F^\star\mid\mathcal D_n)\). Replacing each supremum by a numerical maximum \(\widetilde M_k\) instead samples a solver-dependent approximation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Observation Noise Invalidates Direct Truncation of the Observation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the noiseless truncated-Gaussian MES approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_x=f(x)+\varepsilon_x\), with conditionally independent noise having unbounded upper support. Under a regular conditional law given \(F^\star=m\), one has \(f(x)\le m\) almost surely, but not necessarily \(Y_x\le m\). Whenever \(\mathbb P(f(x)>m-t\mid F^\star=m)>0\) and \(\mathbb P(\varepsilon_x>t)>0\), \(\mathbb P(Y_x>m\mid F^\star=m)>0\). Thus the noisy conditional predictive law is a convolution of a constrained latent law with the noise law and is not generally an observation Gaussian truncated at \(m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The optimum value truncates the latent response, not a noisy observation, so the noiseless MES truncation formula generally fails under observation noise.
assumptions_latex: A regular conditional law given \(F^\star=m\) exists.
\(Y_x=f(x)+\varepsilon_x\) with conditionally independent additive noise.
The stated latent and noise tail events have positive probability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(Y_x>m\mid F^\star=m)>0\) may hold although \(f(x)\le m\) conditionally almost surely.
knowledge_statements.title: Observation Noise Invalidates Direct Truncation of the Observation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Sample Error for Bounded Optimum-Value Averaging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monte Carlo error conditional on an exact optimum-value sampler and fixed entropy-reduction approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(x\). Let \(M_1,\ldots,M_K\) be conditionally i.i.d. posterior samples of \(F^\star\), and suppose \(0\le G_x(M)\le B\) almost surely. For \(\widehat\alpha_K(x)=K^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^KG_x(M_k)\), \[\mathbb P\left(|\widehat\alpha_K(x)-\mathbb E[G_x(F^\star)\mid\mathcal D_n]|\ge t\mid\mathcal D_n\right)\le2e^{-2Kt^2/B^2}.\] This controls only averaging error, not numerical maximization used to sample \(F^\star\) or conditional-entropy bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded per-sample MES contributions obey a fixed-candidate Hoeffding bound, excluding sampling and entropy-approximation bias.
assumptions_latex: M_k\mid\mathcal D_n\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\mathcal L(F^\star\mid\mathcal D_n).
0\le G_x(M_k)\le B\text{ almost surely}.
t>0\text{ and }0<\delta<1.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Sample Error for Bounded Optimum-Value Averaging

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ideal information criterion targeting the posterior optimal objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For maximization let \(F^\star=\sup_{u\in\mathcal X}f(u)\). Optimum-value entropy search uses \[\alpha_n^{\mathrm{MES}}(x)=I(Y_x;F^\star\mid\mathcal D_n)=H(Y_x\mid\mathcal D_n)-\mathbb E[H(Y_x\mid\mathcal D_n,F^\star)\mid\mathcal D_n].\] Equivalently it is the expected reduction in \(H(F^\star\mid\mathcal D_n)\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: MES Error Decomposition Under Approximate Optimum Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-query error bound conditional on supplied total-variation and uniform contribution-error bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(x\). Let \(P\) be the posterior law of \(F^\star\), let \(M_1,\ldots,M_K\overset{\mathrm{iid}}\sim Q\), and suppose \(0\le G_x,\widetilde G_x\le B\), \(\sup_m|\widetilde G_x(m)-G_x(m)|\le\eta\), and \(\|P-Q\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le\varepsilon\), where total variation is \(\sup_A|P(A)-Q(A)|\). Then, with probability at least \(1-\delta\),
\[
\left|\frac1K\sum_{k=1}^K\widetilde G_x(M_k)-\mathbb E_PG_x(F^\star)\right|
\le B\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\delta)}{2K}}+\eta+B\varepsilon.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a fixed query, MES error is bounded by Monte Carlo error plus assumed contribution and optimum-law approximation errors.
assumptions_latex: M_1,\ldots,M_K\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}Q.
0\le G_x(m),\widetilde G_x(m)\le B.
\sup_m|\widetilde G_x(m)-G_x(m)|\le\eta.
\|P-Q\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le\varepsilon under the stated convention.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact noisy-observation MES identity conditional on availability of the optimum-conditioned observation density; it is not by itself a conditioning algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Y_x=f(x)+\varepsilon_x\). If \(p_n(y\mid x)\), \(p_n(m)\), and \(p_n(y\mid x,m)\), with \(m=F^\star\), exist, then
\[
\alpha_n^{\mathrm{MES}}(x)=\int p_n(m)\int p_n(y\mid x,m)\log\frac{p_n(y\mid x,m)}{p_n(y\mid x)}\,dy\,dm.
\]
Thus noisy MES may be integrated once a valid engine for \(p_n(y\mid x,F^\star=m)\) has been supplied; the identity does not construct that conditional density.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noisy MES is an expectation of an optimum-conditioned observation log-density ratio, but this identity does not supply the difficult conditioning engine.
assumptions_latex: The displayed densities or suitable Radon–Nikodym derivatives exist.
The log-density ratio is integrable.
The conditional law includes the observation-noise convolution.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact optimum-conditioned observation density for a finite Gaussian candidate set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_r\}\), \(F=(f(x_1),\ldots,f(x_r))\mid\mathcal D_n\sim\mathcal N(\mu,K)\), \(M=\max_jF_j\), and \(Y_i=F_i+\varepsilon_i\) with independent \(\varepsilon_i\sim\mathcal N(0,\tau_i^2)\). Define \(G_i(m\mid y)=\Pr(M\le m\mid Y_i=y,\mathcal D_n)\) by conditioning \(F\) on \(Y_i=y\) and evaluating the resulting Gaussian probability of \(( -\infty,m]^r\). If \(g_i(m\mid y)=\partial_mG_i(m\mid y)\) and \(g_M(m)=\partial_m\Pr(M\le m\mid\mathcal D_n)\) exist and \(g_M(m)>0\), then Bayes' rule gives
\[
p_n(y\mid M=m)=p_n(y)\frac{g_i(m\mid y)}{g_M(m)}.
\]
Substitution in the MES density-ratio identity yields an exact finite-domain noisy-MES integral. Multivariate-normal probability evaluation, differentiation, and quadrature give numerical approximations whose errors must be controlled separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite Gaussian candidate set, derivatives of conditional maximum CDFs and Bayes' rule construct the exact noisy optimum-conditioned observation density.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) is finite and the latent evaluation vector is jointly Gaussian conditional on \(\mathcal D_n\).
Observation noise is independent Gaussian with \(\tau_i^2>0\).
The displayed maximum densities exist and are integrable, with \(g_M(m)>0\) on the relevant region.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ideal mutual-information criterion for the posterior optimum value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Optimum-value entropy search assigns to each admissible query \(x\) the mutual information
\[
\alpha_n^{\mathrm{MES}}(x)=I(Y_x;F^\star\mid\mathcal D_n)
=H(Y_x\mid\mathcal D_n)-\mathbb E_{F^\star\mid\mathcal D_n}\!\left[H(Y_x\mid\mathcal D_n,F^\star)\right].
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\alpha_n^{\mathrm{MES}}(x)=H(F^\star\mid\mathcal D_n)-\mathbb E_{Y_x\mid\mathcal D_n}\!\left[H(F^\star\mid\mathcal D_n,Y_x)\right].
\]
The policy chooses any \(x_{n+1}\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_x\alpha_n^{\mathrm{MES}}(x)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mutual information with the global maximum value
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimum-value information acquisition and its Gaussian entropy term in Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f^*\) denote the global maximum value. The predictive acquisition measuring the conditional mutual information between a prospective observation \(y\) at \(x\) and \(f^*\), given data \(\mathcal D\), is
\[
\alpha_{f^*}(x;\mathcal D)=H[y\mid x,\mathcal D]-\mathbb E\!\left[H[y\mid x,f^*,\mathcal D]\mid x,\mathcal D\right].
\]
When \(y\mid x,\mathcal D\) is Gaussian with variance \(s^2\),
\[
H[y\mid x,\mathcal D]=\frac12\log(2\pi e\,s^2).
\]
The full acquisition is generally not exactly computable because \(p(f^*\mid\mathcal D)\) is complex; MES and OPES provide approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The optimum-value information acquisition is the conditional mutual information between a prospective observation and the global maximum value. Under a Gaussian predictive distribution, its first entropy term is available in closed form. The remaining expected conditional entropy is generally intractable because the posterior distribution of the maximum value is complex, motivating MES and OPES approximations.
assumptions_latex: f^*\text{ is the global maximum value of }f
y\mid x,\mathcal D\sim\mathcal N(\mu,s^2)\text{ for the stated entropy formula}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha_{f^*}(x;\mathcal D)=H[y\mid x,\mathcal D]-\mathbb E\!\left[H[y\mid x,f^*,\mathcal D]\mid x,\mathcal D\right],\qquad H[y\mid x,\mathcal D]=\tfrac12\log(2\pi e\,s^2).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Information-Ratio Bayesian Regret Bound for Thompson Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-action Bayesian cumulative-regret guarantee under a declared information-ratio bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A^*\) be the tie-broken optimal action in a finite set, let Thompson sampling draw \(A_t\) from \(\mathcal L(A^*\mid\mathcal H_{t-1})\), and define \(\Delta_t=\mathbb E[f(A^*)-f(A_t)\mid\mathcal H_{t-1}]\) and \(g_t=I(A^*;(A_t,Y_t)\mid\mathcal H_{t-1})\). If \(\Delta_t^2\le\Gamma g_t\) almost surely for \(t\le T\), then \[\operatorname{BayesRegret}(T)\le\sqrt{\Gamma T H(A^*)}\le\sqrt{\Gamma T\log|\mathcal A|}.\] The result does not automatically extend to continuous domains, approximate posterior draws, or simple regret.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact posterior function-sampling policy for objective maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(\mathcal D_n\), Thompson sampling performs the update
\[
\widetilde f_n\sim\Pi_n,
\qquad
x_{n+1}=\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X}\widetilde f_n(x),
\qquad
Y_{n+1}\sim p(\,\cdot\mid f,x_{n+1}),
\]
and then sets \(\mathcal D_{n+1}=\mathcal D_n\cup\{(x_{n+1},Y_{n+1})\}\). The procedure repeats until a specified evaluation budget or stopping rule is reached. Its output may be the best observed feasible point or a maximizer of the terminal posterior mean, as fixed before execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Thompson sampling draws one objective function from the posterior, evaluates its maximizer, updates the posterior, and repeats until stopping.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Posterior-sampling decision rule for discrete alternatives having Gaussian marginal beliefs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration $n$, suppose each alternative $x$ has current belief
$$\mu_x\mid S^n\sim N(\bar\mu_x^n,\bar\sigma_x^{n,2}).$$
Draw a realization $\widehat\mu_x^n$ from the current belief for each alternative and select
$$X^{\mathrm{TS}}(S^n)\in\arg\max_x\widehat\mu_x^n.$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Thompson sampling draws a possible value for each alternative from its current Gaussian belief and selects an alternative attaining the largest sampled value. This randomization favors alternatives believed to be strong while retaining exploration through posterior uncertainty.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lazy posterior-function sampling that returns mutually consistent function values to an external optimizer implementing Thompson sampling.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic approximate function-posterior sampling for Thompson-style decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(n\), construct \(Q_n\approx\Pi_n\), draw
\[
\widetilde f_n\sim Q_n,
\qquad
x_{n+1}=T(\widetilde f_n),
\]
observe \(Y_{n+1}\) at \(x_{n+1}\), and update both \(\mathcal D_{n+1}\) and the approximation \(Q_{n+1}\). Continue until the prescribed budget or stopping condition is met. Conditional on \(\mathcal D_n\), the action distribution is
\[
\mathcal L(x_{n+1}\mid\mathcal D_n)=T_\#Q_n,
\]
which replaces the exact Thompson distribution \(T_\#\Pi_n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate posterior sampling replaces the exact function posterior by a tractable law and optimizes an independent draw from that approximation.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(W_n\mid\mathcal D_n\sim\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_n)\) and \(\widetilde f_{n,m}(x)=\mu_n(x)+\phi_m(x)^\top W_n\), then \(\widetilde f_{n,m}\mid\mathcal D_n\) is a Gaussian process with mean \(\mu_n\) and covariance \(k_{n,m}(x,x')=\phi_m(x)^\top\Sigma_n\phi_m(x')\). Every finite covariance matrix has rank at most \(m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Centered Gaussian feature coefficients define a Gaussian process with the posterior mean and a finite-rank feature covariance.
assumptions_latex: \(W_n\mid\mathcal D_n\sim\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_n)\) with \(\Sigma_n\succeq0\).
\(\phi_m(x)\in\mathbb R^m\) is deterministic conditional on \(\mathcal D_n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widetilde f_{n,m}\mid\mathcal D_n\sim\operatorname{GP}(\mu_n,k_{n,m})\), and its finite covariance matrices have rank at most \(m\).

notation.meaning: Conditional covariance of the feature coefficients.
Finite-rank covariance kernel induced by the features.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Rank Gaussian Function Law

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact coefficient-posterior sampling within a declared finite linear-feature model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\phi(x)^\top w\), \(w\sim\mathcal N(m_0,S_0)\), and observations satisfy \(y=\Phi w+\varepsilon\) with \(\varepsilon\sim\mathcal N(0,R)\). For \(S_0\succ0\) and \(R\succ0\), \[S_n=(S_0^{-1}+\Phi^\top R^{-1}\Phi)^{-1},\qquad m_n=S_n(S_0^{-1}m_0+\Phi^\top R^{-1}y).\] Draw \(w_n\sim\mathcal N(m_n,S_n)\), form \(\widetilde f_n(x)=\phi(x)^\top w_n\), and query its measurable tie-broken maximizer. This is exact Thompson sampling for the declared finite linear-feature model, but only approximate for a target process whose covariance is not represented by the feature span.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Condition a Gaussian linear-feature model, sample its coefficient posterior, and optimize the sampled finite expansion.
assumptions_latex: \(S_0\succ0\), \(R\succ0\), and \(\Phi\) is fixed conditional on the sampled locations.
The sampled feature function admits a measurable tie-broken maximizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Gaussian Linear-Feature Posterior Sampling

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Missed Feature Direction Can Collapse Sampled Optimizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-point witness showing optimizer bias from a deficient feature span.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathcal X=\{a,b\}\), let the target posterior have independent \(f(a),f(b)\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\). Its tie-broken optimizer selects each action with probability \(1/2\). Approximate it using the single constant feature \(\phi(a)=\phi(b)=1\) and a scalar Gaussian coefficient. Every approximate draw assigns equal values to \(a,b\); a fixed tie rule selecting \(a\) therefore produces action law \(\delta_a\). The omitted contrast direction \((1,-1)\) changes the optimizer law even though randomness remains in the retained constant direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feature span that omits the contrast between two actions can turn a nondegenerate optimizer distribution into a deterministic tie.
assumptions_latex: The target posterior and approximate feature law are as displayed.
Ties in the approximate draw are resolved in favor of \(a\).
knowledge_statements.title: A Missed Feature Direction Can Collapse Sampled Optimizers

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Landmark-eigensystem construction of a finite kernel feature model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose landmarks \(Z=(z_1,\ldots,z_m)\) and write \(K_{ZZ}=U\Lambda U^\top\) over retained positive eigenvalues. Define \[\phi_Z(x)=\Lambda^{-1/2}U^\top k(Z,x).\] Then \[k_Z(x,x')=\phi_Z(x)^\top\phi_Z(x')=k(x,Z)K_{ZZ}^{\dagger}k(Z,x')\] is positive semidefinite and finite rank. Gaussian linear-feature posterior sampling with \(\phi_Z\) gives exact draws for \(k_Z\), but only approximate draws for \(k\) unless the two kernels agree on the relevant domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nyström landmarks define a finite-rank kernel whose coefficient posterior can be sampled exactly.
assumptions_latex: K_{ZZ}\succeq0.
\Lambda\text{ contains the retained positive eigenvalues}.
The associated Gaussian linear-feature posterior is well posed.

notation.meaning: Pseudoinverse of the landmark Gram matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Nyström Feature Posterior Sampling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationary-kernel random features followed by Gaussian linear-model conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(k(x,x')=\sigma_k^2\mathbb E_{\omega\sim p}[\cos(\omega^\top(x-x'))]\). Draw \(\omega_r\overset{\mathrm{iid}}\sim p\), \(b_r\overset{\mathrm{iid}}\sim\mathrm{Unif}[0,2\pi]\), and define \[\phi_m(x)=\sqrt{\frac{2\sigma_k^2}{m}}(\cos(\omega_1^\top x+b_1),\ldots,\cos(\omega_m^\top x+b_m))^\top.\] Then \(\mathbb E[\phi_m(x)^\top\phi_m(x')]=k(x,x')\). Declare the finite model \(f_m(x)=\phi_m(x)^\top w\), assign a Gaussian prior to \(w\), condition that coefficient law on the observations, sample \(w_n\), and optimize \(\phi_m(x)^\top w_n\). This is exact for the sampled finite-feature model, not the original GP posterior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Random Fourier features approximate a stationary kernel, after which Gaussian coefficient conditioning yields finite-feature posterior draws.
assumptions_latex: k\text{ is continuous and stationary with the displayed normalized spectral law }p.
\omega_r\text{ and }b_r\text{ are independent as stated}.
The Gaussian finite-feature observation model is well posed.

notation.meaning: Normalized spectral distribution of the stationary kernel.

knowledge_statements.title: Random Fourier Feature Posterior Sampling

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Candidate Convergence of Feature Posterior Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional convergence of Gaussian feature-draw and optimizer laws when posterior moments are already known to converge on a finite candidate set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_r\}\). Suppose \(F_m\sim\mathcal N(\mu_m,K_m)\) and \(F\sim\mathcal N(\mu,K)\), with \(\mu_m\to\mu\) and \(K_m\to K\). Then \(F_m\Rightarrow F\). If \(P(F_i=F_j)=0\) for every \(i\ne j\), then the maximizing-index laws converge, so \(P(\operatorname*{argmax}_j(F_m)_j=i)\to P(\operatorname*{argmax}_jF_j=i)\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite candidate set, convergence of conditioned Gaussian moments implies convergence of feature-draw laws and, absent limiting ties, optimizer probabilities.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal X\text{ is finite}.
\mu_m\to\mu\text{ and }K_m\to K.
P(F_i=F_j)=0\text{ for all }i\ne j.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_m\Rightarrow F\quad\text{and}\quad P(\arg\max F_m=i)\to P(\arg\max F=i)\ \forall i.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Candidate Convergence of Feature Posterior Sampling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feature-count rate for random Fourier covariance and conditioned posterior approximation on fixed finite sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U=\{u_1,\ldots,u_r\}\) contain the training and candidate inputs and let \(\widehat k_m\) be the random Fourier kernel from the prior Random Fourier Feature Posterior Sampling record. With probability at least \(1-\delta\),
\[
\max_{i,j\le r}|\widehat k_m(u_i,u_j)-k(u_i,u_j)|\le \sigma_k^2\sqrt{\frac{8\log(2r^2/\delta)}{m}}=:e_m.
\]
Consequently the Gram-matrix operator error is at most \(re_m\). If the exact noisy training matrix \(A=K_{XX}+R\) satisfies \(\lambda_{\min}(A)\ge\lambda>0\) and its approximate perturbation has operator norm at most \(\lambda/2\), then
\[
\|\widehat A^{-1}-A^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le \frac{2\|\widehat A-A\|_{\mathrm{op}}}{\lambda^2}.
\]
For fixed data and bounded kernel blocks on \(U\), the conditioned posterior means and covariance entries therefore converge at order \(O(re_m)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On fixed training and candidate sets, random Fourier kernels concentrate at the inverse-square-root feature rate, and a positive conditioning margin transfers that rate to posterior moments.
assumptions_latex: The stationary kernel and random features satisfy the prior random Fourier construction.
The finite set \(U\) is fixed independently of the sampled features.
The exact noisy training covariance has smallest eigenvalue at least \(\lambda>0\).
The observed data and kernel blocks on \(U\) are fixed and finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_{i,j}|\widehat k_m(u_i,u_j)-k(u_i,u_j)|=O_{\Pr}(\sqrt{\log(r/\delta)/m}),\text{ with the same conditional rate up to finite-set and conditioning factors for posterior moments}.

notation.meaning: Fixed union of training and candidate inputs.
Conditioning margin of the exact noisy training covariance.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Set Random-Feature Posterior Concentration

assumptions_latex: The posterior mean is \(\mu_n:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\).
Features \(\phi_m:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R^m\) and a coefficient law \(W_n\sim Q_n\) satisfy \(\phi_m(x)^\top\operatorname{Cov}(W_n)\phi_m(x')\approx k_n(x,x')\).
The sampled finite-dimensional objective admits a measurable maximizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Sampling coefficients produces a coherent approximate posterior function draw whose covariance is the feature approximation to \(k_n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-feature representation of approximate posterior function draws.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A feature-based posterior draw is represented by
\[
\widetilde f_{n,m}(x)=\mu_n(x)+\phi_m(x)^\top W_n,
\qquad W_n\sim Q_n.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\mathbb E[\widetilde f_{n,m}(x)\mid\mathcal D_n]=\mu_n(x),
\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}(\widetilde f_{n,m}(x),\widetilde f_{n,m}(x')\mid\mathcal D_n)
=\phi_m(x)^\top\operatorname{Cov}(W_n)\phi_m(x').
\]
A Thompson-style query is any \(x_{n+1}\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X}\widetilde f_{n,m}(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feature-based sampling represents a posterior function draw by a random finite feature expansion and optimizes that sampled expansion.
knowledge_statements.title: Feature-Based Function Sampling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No direct source is supplied, and the claimed conditional mean equals the posterior mean only if the coefficient vector is conditionally centered; the current assumptions do not require this.

children.title: Ensemble-Based Sampling
children.top_down_role: Randomized acquisitions drawing candidate functions or decisions from surrogate ensembles.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Consistency of an Empirical Optimizer Distribution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-ensemble approximation of the action law induced by independent approximate-posterior function draws.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f^{(1)},f^{(2)},\ldots\) be conditionally independent and identically distributed with law \(Q_n\), and let \(T\) be a measurable tie-broken optimizer. On a separable metric action space, \(\widehat P_M=M^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^M\delta_{T(f^{(i)})}\) converges weakly almost surely to \(T_\#Q_n\). Moreover, \(\widehat P_M(A)\to(T_\#Q_n)(A)\) for every measurable continuity set \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimizers of independent ensemble function draws form an empirical action distribution converging to the intended approximate posterior-sampling action law.
assumptions_latex: Conditional on \(\mathcal D_n\), the ensemble functions are i.i.d. with law \(Q_n\).
The optimizer map \(T\) is measurable and single-valued.
The action space is a separable metric space.

notation.meaning: Optimizer distribution induced by the approximate function law.

knowledge_statements.title: Consistency of an Empirical Optimizer Distribution

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ensemble Collapse Produces an Incorrect Action Law
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite ensemble-collapse witness under a nondegenerate exact posterior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the exact posterior place probability \(1/2\) on each of two functions \(f_1,f_2\) over \(\{a,b\}\), with \((f_1(a),f_1(b))=(2,0)\) and \((f_2(a),f_2(b))=(0,2)\). Exact posterior sampling selects each action with probability \(1/2\). If every member of an ensemble equals \(f_1\), sampling any ensemble member selects \(a\) almost surely, so the ensemble action law is \(\delta_a\), at total-variation distance \(1/2\) from the exact action law.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identical ensemble members can collapse exploration even though the true posterior assigns positive probability to a different optimizer.
assumptions_latex: Optimization uses the unique maximizer of each displayed function.
All ensemble weights sum to one and every ensemble member equals \(f_1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Ensemble Collapse Produces an Incorrect Action Law

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted ensemble selection, likelihood updating, and optional resampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((f_i,w_i)_{i=1}^M\) approximate \(\mathcal L(f\mid\mathcal D_n)\), with nonnegative weights summing to one. Draw \(J\) with \(\mathbb P(J=i)=w_i\), query the fixed tie-broken optimizer \(T(f_J)\), and after observing \(y\) at \(x\) update \[w_i^+=\frac{w_i p(y\mid f_i,x)}{\sum_jw_jp(y\mid f_j,x)}.\] The induced action law before updating is \(\sum_iw_i\delta_{T(f_i)}\). Weight degeneracy may be monitored by \(\mathrm{ESS}=1/\sum_i(w_i^+)^2\); resampling can be followed by a posterior-invariant rejuvenation kernel. Resampling alone cannot create missing function support.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample a weighted function particle, optimize it, update particle weights by likelihood, and optionally resample and rejuvenate.
assumptions_latex: \sum_iw_i=1\text{ and }w_i\ge0.
\sum_iw_ip(y\mid f_i,x)>0.
T\text{ is a measurable single-valued optimizer map}.
Any rejuvenation kernel preserves the intended updated posterior.

notation.meaning: Tie-broken optimizer of particle function i.
Effective sample size of updated particle weights.

knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Weighted Function-Particle Ensemble

assumptions_latex: An ensemble \(\{f_n^{(1)},\ldots,f_n^{(M)}\}\) represents draws or weighted particles approximating the function posterior.
Weights \(w_1,\ldots,w_M\) are nonnegative and satisfy \(\sum_{i=1}^M w_i=1\).
Each ensemble function has a measurable tie-broken maximizer over \(\mathcal X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected action distribution is the weighted empirical mixture of the ensemble members' optimizing actions.

notation.meaning: Probability weight of ensemble member i.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted empirical posterior sampling over an ensemble of functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Draw an index \(J_n\) according to
\[
\mathbb P(J_n=i\mid\mathcal D_n)=w_i,
\]
then select
\[
x_{n+1}\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X}f_n^{(J_n)}(x).
\]
After observing the response at \(x_{n+1}\), update or refit the ensemble and its weights, and repeat until the evaluation budget is exhausted. If \(T(g)\) denotes the tie-broken maximizer of \(g\), then
\[
\mathcal L(x_{n+1}\mid\mathcal D_n)=\sum_{i=1}^M w_i\,\delta_{T(f_n^{(i)})}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ensemble sampling chooses a weighted random surrogate member and evaluates that member's optimizer, yielding an empirical approximation to posterior sampling.
knowledge_statements.title: Ensemble-Based Sampling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the ensemble approximation. The displayed mixture also requires selecting exactly the stated tie-broken optimizer T(f), whereas the algorithm only specifies membership in an argmax set.

children.title: Sampling-Fidelity Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Decision effects arising from imperfect posterior-draw fidelity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision-utility consequence of approximate Thompson action-law error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=T_\#\Pi_n\) and \(Q=T_\#Q_n\). If \(u:\mathcal X\to[-B,B]\) is measurable, then \(\lvert\mathbb E_Q[u]-\mathbb E_P[u]\rvert\le2B\,d_{\mathrm{TV}}(Q,P)\le2B\,d_{\mathrm{TV}}(Q_n,\Pi_n)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total-variation error in approximate posterior draws bounds distortion of every bounded utility of the selected action.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a measurable tie-broken optimizer map.
\(|u(x)|\le B<\infty\) for every \(x\).
\(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(P,Q)=\sup_A|P(A)-Q(A)|\).

notation.meaning: Exact and approximate Thompson action laws.
Bounded utility of the selected action.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Decision-Utility Distortion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimizer Pushforward Has No Converse Fidelity Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of inferring function-law fidelity from identical optimizer laws.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathcal X=\{a,b\}\), let \(g(a)=2,g(b)=0\) and \(h(a)=3,h(b)=1\). Set \(\Pi=\delta_g\) and \(Q=\delta_h\). The function laws are mutually singular, so \(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(\Pi,Q)=1\), but both functions have unique optimizer \(a\). Their optimizer pushforwards are therefore both \(\delta_a\) and have total-variation distance zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Completely different function laws can induce the same optimizer distribution, so accurate actions do not certify accurate function draws.
assumptions_latex: The optimizer map returns the unique maximizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimizer Pushforward Has No Converse Fidelity Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Small Total Variation Does Not Control Unbounded Utility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of bounded-utility distortion bounds without tail control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<\epsilon<1\), let \(P=\delta_0\) and \(Q_\epsilon=(1-\epsilon)\delta_0+\epsilon\delta_{\epsilon^{-2}}\) on \([0,\infty)\). Then \(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(P,Q_\epsilon)=\epsilon\to0\), but for \(u(x)=x\), \[\mathbb E_{Q_\epsilon}u-\mathbb E_Pu=\epsilon^{-1}\to\infty.\] Thus vanishing action-law total variation alone does not control unbounded decision utility; boundedness, uniform integrability, or quantitative tail conditions are necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vanishing probability placed on an increasingly extreme action makes total variation tend to zero while expected unbounded utility diverges.
assumptions_latex: Total variation is defined as \(\sup_A|P(A)-Q(A)|\).
knowledge_statements.title: Small Total Variation Does Not Control Unbounded Utility

assumptions_latex: The exact and approximate function-posterior laws are \(\Pi_n\) and \(Q_n\) on the same measurable function space.
The tie-broken optimization map \(T\) from functions to actions is measurable.
Total-variation distance \(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(Q_n,\Pi_n)\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Optimization cannot increase total-variation error: \(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(T_\#Q_n,T_\#\Pi_n)\le d_{\mathrm{TV}}(Q_n,\Pi_n)\).

notation.meaning: Exact and approximate posterior function laws.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision-distribution fidelity induced by approximate posterior sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every measurable action set \(A\),
\[
\left|(T_\#Q_n)(A)-(T_\#\Pi_n)(A)\right|
=\left|Q_n(T^{-1}(A))-\Pi_n(T^{-1}(A))\right|
\le d_{\mathrm{TV}}(Q_n,\Pi_n).
\]
Taking the supremum over \(A\) gives
\[
d_{\mathrm{TV}}(T_\#Q_n,T_\#\Pi_n)\le d_{\mathrm{TV}}(Q_n,\Pi_n).
\]
Thus improving function-posterior fidelity controls the induced Thompson-action error, although the inequality alone supplies no computational cost bound or converse guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total-variation error in approximate posterior functions upper-bounds the resulting error in Thompson action distributions, but does not quantify computational cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Sampling-Fidelity Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The total-variation contraction is standard, but it is uncited and presented with proof steps. It addresses sampling fidelity alone and does not itself express a computational fidelity tradeoff.

children.title: Global Learning Design Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies aimed primarily at global learning, uncertainty reduction, or level-set recovery.

children.title: Predictive-Variance Reduction
children.top_down_role: Local and integrated criteria for reducing surrogate uncertainty.

knowledge_statements.title: Predictive-Variance Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gaussian-process integrated posterior variance reduction under noisy point observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
After a prospective observation at \(x\), Gaussian conditioning gives
\[
s_{n+1,x}^2(u)=s_n^2(u)-\frac{k_n(u,x)^2}{s_n^2(x)+\tau^2(x)}.
\]
Hence the integrated predictive-variance reduction is
\[
\alpha_n^{\mathrm{IVR}}(x)=\int_{\mathcal X}\left(s_n^2(u)-s_{n+1,x}^2(u)\right)\nu(du)
=\int_{\mathcal X}\frac{k_n(u,x)^2}{s_n^2(x)+\tau^2(x)}\,\nu(du).
\]
A variance-reduction design selects any admissible maximizer of \(\alpha_n^{\mathrm{IVR}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integrated variance reduction selects the observation expected to remove the greatest weighted posterior variance across the design domain.
assumptions_latex: Conditional on \(\mathcal D_n\), \(f\) is a Gaussian process with covariance \(k_n\) and variance \(s_n^2(u)=k_n(u,u)\).
A query at \(x\) observes \(Y_x=f(x)+\varepsilon\), where \(\varepsilon\sim\mathcal N(0,\tau^2(x))\) is conditionally independent and \(s_n^2(x)+\tau^2(x)>0\).
The finite measure \(\nu\) satisfies \(\int_{\mathcal X}s_n^2(u)\,\nu(du)<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The integrated variance-reduction acquisition equals the integral of the squared posterior covariance divided by the positive predictive observation variance.

notation.meaning: Current posterior covariance and marginal variance.

source_refs.source_title: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences

source_witnesses.source_title: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Outcome Independence of Fixed-Model Variance Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preposterior determinism of Gaussian variance-reduction acquisitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With fixed Gaussian-process covariance and noise parameters, \(s_{n+1,x}^2(u)\), \(\Delta_n(u;x)\), and integrated variance reduction depend on the proposed location but not on the realized observation value. This property need not hold when covariance parameters, noise parameters, or model structure are updated as outcome-dependent random quantities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a fixed Gaussian covariance model, one-step variance reduction is known before observing the response.
assumptions_latex: Gaussian conditioning uses fixed covariance and noise parameters.
The proposed location is fixed before its response is observed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Var}(f(u)\mid D_n,x,Y_x)\text{ is constant as a function of }Y_x.
knowledge_statements.title: Outcome Independence of Fixed-Model Variance Reduction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local counterpart of integrated variance reduction at a designated prediction target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the Gaussian observation model, the posterior variance reduction at target \(u\) caused by observing at \(x\) is \[\Delta_n(u;x)=s_n^2(u)-s_{n+1,x}^2(u)=\frac{k_n(u,x)^2}{s_n^2(x)+\tau^2(x)}.\] It is nonnegative and vanishes exactly when \(k_n(u,x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local variance reduction is squared posterior covariance with the target divided by predictive observation variance.
assumptions_latex: Conditional on \(D_n\), \(f\) is a Gaussian process with covariance \(k_n\).
Observation noise is conditionally independent and \(s_n^2(x)+\tau^2(x)>0\).
A target \(u\) is fixed.

notation.meaning: Variance reduction at target u from sampling x.

knowledge_statements.title: Targeted Local Variance Reduction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint-observation extension of local and integrated variance reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proposed batch \(X\), let \(K_n(X,X)\) be its posterior latent covariance, \(T_X\) its observation-noise covariance, and \(k_n(u,X)\) the target-to-batch covariance row. If \(K_n(X,X)+T_X\) is positive definite, then \[s_{n+1,X}^2(u)=s_n^2(u)-k_n(u,X)[K_n(X,X)+T_X]^{-1}k_n(X,u).\] Integrating the final quadratic form against the target measure gives batch integrated variance reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Batch variance reduction is the Gaussian-conditioning quadratic form generated by the batch covariance matrix.
assumptions_latex: The joint posterior over the target and batch is Gaussian.
\(K_n(X,X)+T_X\) is positive definite.
The integrated quadratic form is finite when integration is used.
knowledge_statements.title: Batch Gaussian Variance Reduction

children.title: Maximum-Entropy Design
children.top_down_role: Design criteria valuing information about the latent response surface.

assumptions_latex: Conditional on \(\mathcal D_n\), the prospective scalar observation is \(Y_x=f(x)+\varepsilon\).
Its predictive law is Gaussian with variance \(s_n^2(x)+\tau^2(x)>0\).
Observation noise is conditionally independent of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For constant observation-noise variance, maximizing predictive entropy is equivalent to maximizing posterior predictive variance.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar Gaussian maximum-predictive-entropy sequential design.

source_refs.source_title: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The conditional differential entropy of the prospective observation is
\[
H(Y_x\mid\mathcal D_n)=\frac12\log\!\left(2\pi e\,[s_n^2(x)+\tau^2(x)]\right).
\]
Maximum-entropy design selects
\[
x_{n+1}\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X}H(Y_x\mid\mathcal D_n).
\]
Because the logarithm is strictly increasing, if \(\tau^2(x)=\tau^2\) is constant, this optimizer also maximizes \(s_n^2(x)\). When noise varies with \(x\), maximum observation entropy need not maximize latent-response uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gaussian maximum-entropy design maximizes predictive observation variance; with constant noise, this is exactly maximum latent posterior variance.
knowledge_statements.title: Maximum-Entropy Design

source_witnesses.source_title: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relationship between scalar maximum predictive entropy and information gained about the latent response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Y_x=f(x)+\varepsilon_x\), with conditionally independent \(f(x)\sim\mathcal N(\mu_n(x),s_n^2(x))\) and \(\varepsilon_x\sim\mathcal N(0,\tau^2(x))\), \[I(f(x);Y_x\mid D_n)=\frac12\log\!\left(1+\frac{s_n^2(x)}{\tau^2(x)}\right).\] If \(\tau^2(x)\) is constant, maximizing predictive observation entropy, latent variance, and this mutual information gives the same optimizer. Under heteroskedastic noise, entropy ranks \(s_n^2(x)+\tau^2(x)\), whereas information gain ranks \(s_n^2(x)/\tau^2(x)\), so their optimizers can differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constant Gaussian noise makes maximum entropy equivalent to maximum pointwise information gain; varying noise breaks the equivalence.
assumptions_latex: The latent response and observation noise are conditionally Gaussian and independent.
The relevant maximizers exist.

notation.meaning: Conditional mutual information between the latent value and observation.

knowledge_statements.title: Entropy–Information-Gain Equivalence Under Constant Noise

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximum-entropy design on a finite candidate set, including its Gaussian determinant representation and hyperparameter dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a density $p$ for which the integral exists, its differential entropy is $H(p)=-\int_{\mathcal X}p(x)\log p(x)\,dx$. Fix a design size $n$, a finite candidate set $\mathcal X$, and Gaussian-process hyperparameters. A maximum-entropy design chooses $X_n\subset\mathcal X$ to maximize the entropy of the latent or noisy response vector at $X_n$. If $Y_n\sim\mathcal N_n(0,\tau^2K_n)$ with $K_n^{ij}=C_\theta(x_i,x_j)+g\delta_{ij}$ and $K_n\succ0$, then maximizing this entropy is equivalent to maximizing $\log|K_n|$, hence also $|K_n|$. The resulting design generally depends on the chosen covariance hyperparameters, including $\theta$ and $g$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A maximum-entropy GP design of fixed size selects candidate points whose latent or noisy response vector has maximum entropy. For a nonsingular Gaussian covariance proportional to K_n, this is equivalent to maximizing det(K_n). The selected design depends on the covariance hyperparameters used during design.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal X\text{ is a fixed finite candidate set}
X_n\subset\mathcal X\text{ and }|X_n|=n
Y_n\sim\mathcal N_n(0,\tau^2K_n)
K_n^{ij}=C_\theta(x_i,x_j)+g\delta_{ij}
K_n\succ0
\theta,g,\tau^2\text{ are fixed while optimizing }X_n

children.title: Level-Set Estimation
children.top_down_role: Policies targeting recovery of regions above or below a specified level.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step Bayesian design criterion for integrated level-set classification loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[R_n=\int_{\mathcal X}\min\{c_{\mathrm{FN}}p_n(u),c_{\mathrm{FP}}[1-p_n(u)]\}\,\mu(du).\] For a prospective observation \(Y_x\), define \[\alpha_n^{\mathrm{SUR}}(x)=R_n-\mathbb E[R_{n+1}\mid D_n,x].\] A stepwise uncertainty-reduction policy selects an admissible maximizer of \(\alpha_n^{\mathrm{SUR}}\), equivalently a minimizer of expected next-step Bayes classification risk.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stepwise level-set design samples where the expected reduction in integrated posterior classification risk is greatest.
assumptions_latex: The posterior update after \((x,Y_x)\) is well defined.
The current and expected next-step risks are finite.
The relevant acquisition optimizer exists.

notation.meaning: Current integrated minimum posterior classification risk.
Expected one-step reduction in level-set classification risk.

knowledge_statements.title: Stepwise Expected Level-Set Risk Reduction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Bayes Optimality Is Not Joint Set Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between minimum integrated classification loss and credible coverage of an entire excursion set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pointwise Bayes level-set estimator minimizes integrated posterior misclassification loss but does not thereby satisfy \(\mathbb P(L_\tau(f)\subseteq\widehat L_n\mid D_n)\geq1-\delta\) or \(\mathbb P(\widehat L_n=L_\tau(f)\mid D_n)\geq1-\delta\). Such simultaneous guarantees require a joint posterior band or another calibrated set construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimal pointwise threshold classification does not automatically provide posterior coverage for the entire level set.
assumptions_latex: The estimator uses marginal posterior membership probabilities.
No simultaneous posterior band is assumed.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Bayes Optimality Is Not Joint Set Coverage

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost-sensitive extension of symmetric pointwise level-set estimation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_n(x)=\mathbb P(f(x)\geq\tau\mid D_n)\). If false inclusion costs \(c_{\mathrm{FP}}>0\) and false exclusion costs \(c_{\mathrm{FN}}>0\), then under integrated pointwise loss a Bayes estimator is \[\widehat L_n=\left\{x:p_n(x)\geq\frac{c_{\mathrm{FP}}}{c_{\mathrm{FP}}+c_{\mathrm{FN}}}\right\}.\] Its minimum posterior pointwise risk is \(\min\{c_{\mathrm{FN}}p_n(x),c_{\mathrm{FP}}[1-p_n(x)]\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unequal false-positive and false-negative costs shift the optimal posterior membership threshold away from one half.
assumptions_latex: \(c_{\mathrm{FP}},c_{\mathrm{FN}}>0\).
\(p_n\) is measurable.
The integrated loss is finite.
knowledge_statements.title: Asymmetric-Loss Bayes Level-Set Classifier

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed form for posterior level-set membership probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f(x)\mid D_n\sim\mathcal N(\mu_n(x),s_n^2(x))\) with \(s_n(x)>0\), then \[p_n(x)=\mathbb P(f(x)\geq\tau\mid D_n)=\Phi\!\left(\frac{\mu_n(x)-\tau}{s_n(x)}\right).\] Hence the asymmetric-loss estimator includes \(x\) exactly when \[\mu_n(x)-\tau\geq s_n(x)\Phi^{-1}\!\left(\frac{c_{\mathrm{FP}}}{c_{\mathrm{FP}}+c_{\mathrm{FN}}}\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gaussian level-set membership is a standardized posterior-mean threshold adjusted for uncertainty and error costs.
assumptions_latex: The marginal latent posterior at x is Gaussian.
The two error costs are positive.

notation.meaning: Posterior probability that x belongs to the upper level set.

knowledge_statements.title: Gaussian Exceedance-Probability Representation
Level-Set Estimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bayesian estimation of a threshold excursion set under pointwise misclassification loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) have posterior distribution \(\Pi_n\) after data \(\mathcal D_n\), and fix a threshold \(\tau\). The upper level set is \(L_\tau(f)=\{x\in\mathcal X:f(x)\geq\tau\}\). Under loss \(\ell(\widehat L,L)=\int_{\mathcal X}\mathbf 1\{\mathbf 1_{\widehat L}(x)\neq\mathbf 1_L(x)\}\,\mu(dx)\), its Bayes estimator is \(\widehat L_n=\{x:p_n(x)\geq 1/2\}\), where \(p_n(x)=\Pi_n(f(x)\geq\tau)\). A level-set design policy selects observations to reduce the posterior expected loss of \(\widehat L_n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Level-set estimation infers where an unknown function exceeds a threshold; under symmetric pointwise error, classify a location as inside whenever its posterior exceedance probability is at least one half.
assumptions_latex: \(\mu\) is a finite measure on \(\mathcal X\).
\(x\mapsto p_n(x)\) is \(\mu\)-measurable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat L_n=\{x\in\mathcal X:p_n(x)\geq 1/2\}\) minimizes posterior expected pointwise misclassification loss.

notation.meaning: upper excursion or level set at threshold tau
posterior probability that f(x) reaches the threshold

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical Bayesian excursion-set definition and pointwise Bayes classifier

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The level-set definition and symmetric-loss Bayes classifier are mathematically coherent and fit the leaf, but no cited source or inspectable locator supports the nontrivial estimator and design-policy claims.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Target region sought in active learning for level-set estimation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a response \(Y:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) and threshold \(T\in\mathbb R\), define \[\Gamma=\{x\in\mathbb R^m:Y(x)>T\}.\] Replacing \(Y(x)\) by \(Y(x)-T\) permits the threshold to be written as zero without changing the region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The upper level set consists of inputs whose response exceeds a threshold. Recentring the response converts the problem to a zero threshold.
assumptions_latex: Y:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R
T\in\mathbb R
