children.title: Contour Estimation
children.top_down_role: Policies concentrating evaluations near objective isocontours.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Contour Probability Is Not Joint Credibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correction to interpreting a pointwise tolerance-probability region as a credible contour set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A region \(B_{n,\varepsilon}=\{x:\mathbb P(|f(x)-\tau|\leq\varepsilon\mid D_n)\geq\gamma\}\) is defined by marginal probabilities. It does not by itself satisfy a joint posterior statement that the complete contour lies in \(B_{n,\varepsilon}\), nor that all points in the region are simultaneously within tolerance. Such credibility requires a joint posterior construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A thresholded pointwise contour-proximity map is not automatically a jointly credible contour band.
assumptions_latex: \(B_{n,\varepsilon}\) is constructed only from marginal posterior probabilities.
No joint posterior band is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Marginal contour-proximity thresholds do not imply simultaneous contour coverage.}

notation.meaning: Region selected by thresholding pointwise contour-proximity probabilities.

knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Contour Probability Is Not Joint Credibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition under which an equality contour equals an excursion-set boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For continuous \(f\) and \(L_\tau=\{x:f(x)\geq\tau\}\), \(\partial L_\tau\subseteq\{x:f(x)=\tau\}\), but equality need not hold. If \(f\equiv\tau\) on a nonempty open plateau, interior plateau points belong to the contour but not to \(\partial L_\tau\). Equality requires an additional local-crossing or no-level-plateau condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contour can contain flat interior regions, so it equals the excursion boundary only under a local crossing condition.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuous.
\(L_\tau=\{x:f(x)\geq\tau\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial L_\tau\subseteq\{f=\tau\},\quad \partial L_\tau=\{f=\tau\}\text{ only under an additional crossing condition.}

notation.meaning: Topological boundary of the upper excursion set.

knowledge_statements.title: Contour–Boundary Equivalence Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise posterior probability of lying within a response-scale tolerance of the contour.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f(x)\mid D_n\sim\mathcal N(\mu_n(x),s_n^2(x))\) with \(s_n(x)>0\), then \[\mathbb P(|f(x)-\tau|\leq\varepsilon\mid D_n)=\Phi\!\left(\frac{\tau+\varepsilon-\mu_n(x)}{s_n(x)}\right)-\Phi\!\left(\frac{\tau-\varepsilon-\mu_n(x)}{s_n(x)}\right).\] This quantity is a pointwise contour-proximity score, not a simultaneous credible contour set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gaussian contour proximity is the normal posterior mass in a tolerance interval around the target level.
assumptions_latex: The marginal latent posterior at x is Gaussian.
\(\varepsilon>0\).

notation.meaning: Response-scale tolerance around the contour level.

knowledge_statements.title: Gaussian Contour-Proximity Probability
Contour Estimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Posterior estimation of the equality contour associated with a fixed response level.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) and level \(\tau\), the contour is \(C_\tau(f)=\{x\in\mathcal X:f(x)=\tau\}\). Because an exact equality may have zero posterior probability at each fixed location, Bayesian contour estimation commonly identifies an uncertainty band \(B_{n,\varepsilon}=\{x:\Pi_n(|f(x)-\tau|\leq\varepsilon)\geq\gamma\}\), with tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\) and credibility \(\gamma\in(0,1)\). A sequential contour design chooses the next observation to reduce posterior uncertainty about \(C_\tau(f)\), equivalently about the boundary separating the upper and lower level sets when that boundary equals the contour.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Contour estimation locates points where the response equals a target level, usually through a credible tolerance band because exact equality has negligible pointwise posterior probability.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) and \(\tau\in\mathbb R\).
The relevant level-set boundary satisfies \(\partial\{f\geq\tau\}=C_\tau(f)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_\tau(f)=\{f=\tau\}\), while \(B_{n,\varepsilon}\) is a posterior-credible operational estimator of its neighborhood.

notation.meaning: contour of f at level tau
posterior credible tolerance band around the contour

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard contour and credible-band formulation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The contour definition is standard, but the pointwise probability band is called posterior-credible without a joint posterior coverage statement. A source is required to determine the intended band construction and justify that terminology.

children.title: Active Search
children.top_down_role: Policies seeking members of a target class or high-value region.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact nonmyopic policy for noiseless binary labels on a finite candidate set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For posterior information state \(D\), evaluated set \(S\), and \(b\) queries remaining, define \(V(D,S,0)=0\) and \[V(D,S,b)=\max_{x\notin S}\mathbb E\!\left[Z_x+V(D\cup\{(x,Z_x)\},S\cup\{x\},b-1)\mid D\right].\] Selecting any maximizing action at each state maximizes expected additional discoveries over the remaining budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact finite-horizon active search uses a Bellman recursion over posterior state, evaluated candidates, and remaining budget.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) is finite.
Labels are binary and revealed without error.
The posterior conditional label law is well defined.
\(0\leq b\leq |\mathcal X\setminus S|\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: V(D,S,b)\text{ equals the optimal expected number of additional discoveries in }b\text{ queries}.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Horizon Active-Search Bellman Policy

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case state growth for the finite noiseless binary-label Bellman recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(N\) initially unevaluated candidates and horizon \(T\), the Bellman recursion can encounter up to \[\sum_{j=0}^{T}\binom Nj2^j\] distinct evaluated-set and binary-label-history states. Enumerating all remaining actions therefore requires at most order \(N\sum_{j=0}^{T-1}\binom Nj2^j\) action backups, excluding posterior-update cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact nonmyopic active search has combinatorial state growth in the candidate count and horizon.
assumptions_latex: There are \(N\) initially unevaluated candidates.
Labels are binary and noiseless.
States with different evaluated sets or observed label assignments are distinguished.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Active-Search Planning State Growth

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain utility distinguishing active search from inferred region classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z_x=\mathbf 1\{f(x)\geq\tau\}\) and let \(S_T\) be the set evaluated by budget \(T\). Active-search discovery utility is \[U_T=\sum_{x\in S_T}Z_x.\] Unevaluated candidates do not contribute. With one noiseless-label query remaining, an optimal action maximizes \(\mathbb P(Z_x=1\mid D_n)\) over unevaluated candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active search rewards positive candidates actually evaluated; with one query left, choose the largest posterior positive probability.
assumptions_latex: The candidate set is finite.
Each candidate is evaluated at most once.
For the one-step rule, evaluation reveals the binary label without error.

notation.meaning: Set evaluated by the terminal budget.

knowledge_statements.title: Observed-Discovery Utility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating active search from whole-domain threshold classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Discovery utility \(U_T=\sum_{x\in S_T}Z_x\) is not equivalent to classification utility over all \(x\in\mathcal X\). A policy can discover many positives in a dense positive region while leaving the threshold boundary unresolved; a classification-oriented policy can instead spend queries near the boundary and discover fewer positives. Unevaluated posterior-positive candidates are not active-search discoveries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finding evaluated positives and accurately classifying the entire threshold region are different objectives.
assumptions_latex: Performance is evaluated at a finite budget.
Unevaluated candidates may receive posterior classifications.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U_T\text{ does not determine whole-domain threshold-classification loss.}
knowledge_statements.title: Discovery–Classification Objective Boundary
Active Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential Bayesian search maximizing the number of newly discovered threshold-exceeding locations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite candidate set \(\mathcal X\), threshold \(\tau\), budget \(T\), and posterior \(\Pi_0\), initialize \(S_0=\varnothing\). At stage \(n<T\), choose \(x_{n+1}\in\mathcal X\setminus S_n\) to maximize the conditional expected terminal utility \(\mathbb E_{\Pi_n}[\sum_{x\in S_n\cup\{x_{n+1},\ldots,x_T\}}\mathbf 1\{f(x)\geq\tau\}\mid\mathcal D_n]\), exactly or through an approximation. Observe \(y_{n+1}\), update \(\Pi_{n+1}\), and set \(S_{n+1}=S_n\cup\{x_{n+1}\}\). Stop after \(T\) evaluations and return the evaluated points whose observations or inferred labels are positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active search sequentially evaluates candidates to maximize the expected number of threshold-exceeding points discovered within a fixed budget.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) is finite and each candidate is evaluated at most once.
The observation model defines posterior updates \(\Pi_n\mapsto\Pi_{n+1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is the set of positive discoveries obtained by a policy optimizing or approximating expected terminal discovery count.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical finite-domain Bayesian active-search objective

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Active Search, but the displayed maximization contains unspecified future adaptive choices and conflates observed discoveries with inferred positive labels. An authoritative active-search formulation is needed before its objective and output can be fixed reliably.

children.title: Threshold-Region Classification
children.top_down_role: Design criteria emphasizing correct classification across a threshold boundary.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Posterior Bayes Risk of Threshold Classification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise and integrated loss for posterior threshold labels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_n(x)=\Pi_n(f(x)\geq\tau)\), with false-positive cost \(c_{10}>0\) and false-negative cost \(c_{01}>0\). The minimum posterior pointwise classification risk is \[r_n^*(x)=\min\{c_{01}p_n(x),c_{10}(1-p_n(x))\}.\] For a finite measure \(\nu\), the minimum integrated risk among measurable pointwise classifiers is \[R_n^*=\int_{\mathcal X}r_n^*(x)\,\nu(dx).\] Under equal costs \(c_{01}=c_{10}=c\), \(r_n^*(x)=c\min\{p_n(x),1-p_n(x)\}\), which is maximized at \(p_n(x)=1/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimum posterior classification loss is the smaller of the two error costs; under equal costs it is greatest at exceedance probability one half.
assumptions_latex: p_n\text{ is measurable}.
\nu(\mathcal X)<\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Posterior Bayes Risk of Threshold Classification

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bayes-Classifier Nonuniqueness at the Cost Cutoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tie behavior in cost-sensitive posterior threshold classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_n(x)=\Pi_n(f(x)\geq\tau)\), with false-positive cost \(c_{10}>0\) and false-negative cost \(c_{01}>0\). At any \(x\) satisfying \[p_n(x)=\frac{c_{10}}{c_{01}+c_{10}},\] the posterior risks of declaring either label are equal: \[c_{10}(1-p_n(x))=c_{01}p_n(x).\] Both labels, and every randomized mixture of them, are therefore Bayes-optimal at that location; a single-valued classifier requires an explicit tie convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the cost-sensitive cutoff both class labels have equal posterior risk, so a single-valued Bayes classifier needs a tie convention.
knowledge_statements.title: Bayes-Classifier Nonuniqueness at the Cost Cutoff

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Excess-Risk Identity for Threshold Classification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact posterior penalty for disagreeing with the cost-sensitive Bayes label away from the cutoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p=p_n(x)\), and let \(h^*(x)\) be any Bayes-optimal threshold label under false-positive cost \(c_{10}\) and false-negative cost \(c_{01}\). For a deterministic label \(h(x)\), its posterior excess risk is zero when \(h(x)\) is Bayes-optimal and otherwise equals \[\left|(c_{01}+c_{10})p-c_{10}\right|.\] Thus any classifier differing from the Bayes rule only on a measurable set \(A\) has integrated excess risk \[\int_A\left|(c_{01}+c_{10})p_n(x)-c_{10}\right|\nu(dx).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The cost of disagreeing with the posterior Bayes threshold label is exactly the distance, in risk units, from the cost-sensitive cutoff.
assumptions_latex: \(p_n\) and the classifiers are measurable.
The integrated expression is finite.

notation.meaning: Set of posterior-risk-minimizing labels at x.

knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Excess-Risk Identity for Threshold Classification

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robust threshold labeling from certified bounds on posterior exceedance probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\kappa=c_{10}/(c_{01}+c_{10})\), and suppose \(p_n(x)\in[\ell_n(x),u_n(x)]\). If \(\ell_n(x)>\kappa\), label one is uniquely Bayes-optimal for every compatible value of \(p_n(x)\); if \(u_n(x)<\kappa\), label zero is uniquely Bayes-optimal for every compatible value. If \(\kappa\in[\ell_n(x),u_n(x)]\), the interval alone cannot certify a unique Bayes label.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Probability bounds certify a unique threshold label only when their entire interval lies strictly on one side of the cost-sensitive cutoff.
assumptions_latex: \(0\le\ell_n(x)\le p_n(x)\le u_n(x)\le1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ell_n(x)>\kappa\Rightarrow h^*(x)=1;\quad u_n(x)<\kappa\Rightarrow h^*(x)=0;\quad \kappa\in[\ell_n(x),u_n(x)]\Rightarrow\text{no unique label is certified}.

notation.meaning: Certified interval for the posterior exceedance probability.

knowledge_statements.title: Posterior-Probability Interval Classification Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equal-Cost Cutoff Fails Under Asymmetric Misclassification Costs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of using posterior probability one half when false-positive and false-negative costs differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c_{10}=9\), \(c_{01}=1\), and \(p_n(x)=0.6\). The cost-sensitive cutoff is \(\kappa=9/10\). Declaring label one has posterior risk \(9(1-0.6)=3.6\), whereas declaring label zero has risk \(1\cdot0.6=0.6\). Thus the equal-cost rule \(\mathbf 1\{p_n(x)\ge 1/2\}\) selects the strictly suboptimal label.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-half probability cutoff can be strictly wrong when false positives and false negatives have unequal costs.
knowledge_statements.title: Equal-Cost Cutoff Fails Under Asymmetric Misclassification Costs

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gaussian Posterior Form of the Cost-Sensitive Threshold Classifier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form exceedance probability and decision boundary under a univariate Gaussian latent posterior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(f(x)\mid\mathcal D_n\sim N(\mu_n(x),s_n^2(x))\), let \(\kappa=c_{10}/(c_{01}+c_{10})\), and assume \(s_n(x)>0\). Then \[p_n(x)=\mathbb P(f(x)\ge\tau\mid\mathcal D_n)=\Phi\!\left(\frac{\mu_n(x)-\tau}{s_n(x)}\right).\] Consequently, declaring the above-threshold label is Bayes-optimal exactly when \[\mu_n(x)-\tau\ge s_n(x)\Phi^{-1}(\kappa),\] with both labels optimal at equality. If \(s_n(x)=0\), then \(p_n(x)=\mathbf 1\{\mu_n(x)\ge\tau\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a Gaussian latent posterior, the cost-sensitive threshold rule is an explicit standardized-mean inequality; zero posterior variance yields a deterministic label.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x)\mid\mathcal D_n\sim N(\mu_n(x),s_n^2(x))\).
The threshold label is \(\mathbf 1\{f(x)\ge\tau\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Gaussian Posterior Form of the Cost-Sensitive Threshold Classifier
Threshold-Region Classification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Posterior binary classification of an unknown response relative to a prescribed threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the latent threshold label be \(Z_\tau(x)=\mathbf 1\{f(x)\geq\tau\}\), and let \(p_n(x)=\Pi_n(Z_\tau(x)=1)\). With false-positive cost \(c_{10}>0\) and false-negative cost \(c_{01}>0\), a classifier \(h_n:\mathcal X\to\{0,1\}\) has posterior pointwise risk \(c_{10}(1-p_n(x))\) when declaring one and \(c_{01}p_n(x)\) when declaring zero. Hence the Bayes threshold-region classifier is \(h_n^*(x)=\mathbf 1\{p_n(x)\geq c_{10}/(c_{01}+c_{10})\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Threshold-region classification assigns each location above or below a response threshold using posterior exceedance probability and the relative costs of false-positive and false-negative decisions.
assumptions_latex: The posterior exceedance probability \(p_n(x)\) is defined for every classified location.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h_n^*(x)=\mathbf 1\{p_n(x)\geq c_{10}/(c_{01}+c_{10})\}\) minimizes posterior pointwise classification risk.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elementary cost-sensitive Bayes classification applied to posterior threshold labels

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cost-sensitive posterior classifier and threshold are internally correct and fit the leaf, but neither the classification result nor its threshold-region specialization has cited, inspectable support.

children.title: Acquisition Numerical Realization Pipeline
children.top_down_role: Numerical realization of acquisition policies, including approximation, differentiation, global search, and pending evaluations.

children.title: Acquisition Evaluation Methods
children.top_down_role: Analytic, numerical, and sampling-based evaluation of acquisition quantities.

children.title: Deterministic Acquisition Evaluation Family
children.top_down_role: Deterministic acquisition computation available in favorable surrogate and utility regimes.

children.title: Analytic Acquisition Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Closed-form acquisition computation available under favorable surrogate-utility combinations.

knowledge_statements.title: Analytic Acquisition Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form evaluation of a posterior expected acquisition without numerical integration or sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an acquisition has the posterior-expectation form \(\alpha_n(x)=\mathbb E_{\Pi_n}[u(x,F)]\). Its evaluation is analytic on a domain \(D\subseteq\mathcal X\) when there exists an explicitly computable function \(A\) such that \(\alpha_n(x)=A(\theta_n(x))\) for every \(x\in D\), where \(\theta_n(x)\) is a finite vector of posterior parameters, and computing \(A\) requires neither stochastic samples nor numerical quadrature. For example, if \(F(x)\sim N(m_n(x),s_n^2(x))\), many one-point piecewise-polynomial utilities reduce to expressions involving the standard normal distribution and density functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An acquisition is evaluated analytically when its posterior expectation reduces to an explicit function of finitely many posterior parameters, with no sampling or numerical integration.
assumptions_latex: \(u(x,F)\) is integrable under \(\Pi_n\).
The posterior law relevant to \(u\) is parameterized by finite-dimensional \(\theta_n(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_n(x)=A(\theta_n(x))\) is deterministically evaluable without quadrature or Monte Carlo sampling.

notation.meaning: random utility whose posterior expectation defines the acquisition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind and closed-form criterion fit the leaf. The broad claim about many Gaussian piecewise-polynomial utilities requires a specific source and scope; none is cited.

children.title: Semi-Analytic Acquisition Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Acquisition computation combining closed-form reductions with limited numerical work.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Error localization when the conditional inner expectation is evaluated exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(g_x(z)=\mathbb E[u(x,z,W)\mid Z=z]\) is evaluated exactly and \(\alpha_n(x)=\int g_x(z)P_Z(dz)\). For a deterministic residual-integration rule \(Q_mg_x=\sum_{i=1}^mw_i g_x(z_i)\), \[\alpha_n(x)-\widehat\alpha_{n,m}(x)=\int g_x(z)P_Z(dz)-Q_mg_x.\] Therefore every valid residual-integration bound \(|\int g_xdP_Z-Q_mg_x|\le\varepsilon_m(x)\) also bounds the complete semi-analytic evaluation error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the inner conditional expectation is exact, all semi-analytic evaluation error comes from the remaining numerical integral.
assumptions_latex: The conditional expectation \(g_x\) is computed without approximation.
The outer integral and deterministic residual rule are well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\alpha_n(x)-\widehat\alpha_{n,m}(x)|\le\varepsilon_m(x)\) whenever the residual-integration error is at most \(\varepsilon_m(x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Integration Error Identity
Semi-Analytic Acquisition Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Evaluation combining exact conditional expectation with low-dimensional deterministic integration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an acquisition be \(\alpha_n(x)=\mathbb E[u(x,Z,W)]\) under the posterior predictive law. If the conditional expectation \(g_x(z)=\mathbb E[u(x,z,W)\mid Z=z]\) is available analytically, then the tower property gives \(\alpha_n(x)=\int g_x(z)\,P_Z(dz)\). Semi-analytic evaluation computes \(g_x\) in closed form and evaluates only the remaining integral over \(Z\) numerically. For deterministic nodes \(z_i\) and weights \(w_i\), the resulting approximation is \(\widehat\alpha_{n,m}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i g_x(z_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Semi-analytic evaluation integrates part of the acquisition exactly after conditioning and applies deterministic numerical integration only to the remaining variables.
assumptions_latex: \(u(x,Z,W)\) is integrable.
A regular conditional law of \(W\) given \(Z\) exists.
\(g_x(z)\) is analytically computable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_n(x)=\int g_x(z)\,P_Z(dz)\) reduces the numerical integration dimension to that of \(Z\).

notation.meaning: random variable retained for numerical integration

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conditional-expectation decomposition underlying semi-analytic integration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional-expectation decomposition is coherent and the representation kind fits semi-analytic evaluation, but no source with a specific locator supports this terminology or acquisition-evaluation formulation.

children.title: Quadrature Acquisition Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Deterministic numerical integration for acquisition quantities lacking full analytic reduction.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic error bound for a Lipschitz acquisition integrand and a probability-weight quadrature measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_x\) be the predictive integration law and \(Q_{m,x}=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i\delta_{z_i}\) a probability measure. If \(z\mapsto u(x,z)\) is \(L_x\)-Lipschitz under metric \(d\) and both measures have finite first moments, then \[\left|\int u(x,z)P_x(dz)-\sum_{i=1}^m w_i u(x,z_i)\right|\le L_xW_1(P_x,Q_{m,x}).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a Lipschitz acquisition integrand, quadrature error is bounded by the Lipschitz constant times the Wasserstein distance between the predictive and weighted-node measures.
assumptions_latex: \(w_i\ge0\) and \(\sum_iw_i=1\).
\(u(x,\cdot)\) is \(L_x\)-Lipschitz.
\(P_x\) and \(Q_{m,x}\) have finite first moments.
knowledge_statements.title: Wasserstein Quadrature Error Certificate
Quadrature Acquisition Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic weighted-node approximation of an acquisition expectation or integral.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\alpha_n(x)=\int_{\mathcal Z}u(x,z)p_n(z\mid x)\,dz\), choose a deterministic quadrature rule \(\{(z_i,w_i)\}_{i=1}^m\) appropriate to the integration domain and weight density. For each candidate \(x\), evaluate the integrand at all nodes and return \(\widehat\alpha_{n,m}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i u(x,z_i)\), with weights incorporating \(p_n(\cdot\mid x)\) or after transforming a fixed reference rule. Increase \(m\) or refine the nodes until a prescribed deterministic error indicator is at most \(\varepsilon\), then output \(\widehat\alpha_{n,m}(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadrature evaluates an acquisition by a deterministic weighted sum of utility values at integration nodes, refined until a chosen numerical tolerance is met.
assumptions_latex: \(u(x,\cdot)p_n(\cdot\mid x)\) is integrable.
A quadrature rule and deterministic refinement or error indicator are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\alpha_{n,m}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i u(x,z_i)\) is the deterministic quadrature approximation returned at tolerance \(\varepsilon\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard deterministic quadrature construction applied to acquisition expectations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the displayed weighted sum is valid only after clearly specifying whether the density is absorbed into the weights or a reference transformation is used. A source is needed to establish the intended rule and refinement criterion.

children.title: Deterministic Evaluation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Surrogate, utility, or dimensional regimes limiting deterministic acquisition computation.

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Evaluation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimensional and regularity limits of closed-form and deterministic quadrature acquisition evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the Gaussian orthant acquisition \(\alpha(x)=\mathbb P(F_1(x)\geq\tau_1,\ldots,F_d(x)\geq\tau_d)\) for a correlated, nondegenerate Gaussian vector \(F(x)\). Except in special covariance structures or low dimensions, this probability lacks a simple univariate closed form. A tensor-product quadrature using \(m\) nodes per coordinate requires \(m^d\) integrand evaluations; thus its cost is exponential in \(d\). Moreover, the indicator integrand is discontinuous on threshold hyperplanes, weakening smooth-integrand quadrature guarantees. Consequently, deterministic evaluation becomes impractical as effective stochastic dimension grows unless exploitable structure or dimension reduction is present.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Correlated high-dimensional threshold acquisitions expose deterministic limits: closed forms generally disappear, tensor quadrature costs grow exponentially, and discontinuities degrade smoothness-based accuracy guarantees.
assumptions_latex: \(F(x)\) is a correlated nondegenerate Gaussian vector in \(\mathbb R^d\).
A tensor-product rule uses \(m\) nodes in each stochastic coordinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The deterministic work is \(m^d\), and discontinuous threshold utility prevents generic smooth-integrand convergence guarantees.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: tensor-product node count and discontinuous Gaussian orthant integrand give a concrete deterministic failure mechanism

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits exactly. The tensor count is clear, but the claims about absence of simple closed forms, degraded quadrature guarantees, and practical dimensional limits require authoritative, specifically located evidence.

children.title: Sampling-Based Acquisition Evaluation Family
children.top_down_role: Sampling-based acquisition computation for non-Gaussian, batch, and nested expectations.

children.title: Monte Carlo Acquisition Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Random-sampling evaluation of acquisition expectations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-candidate nonasymptotic acquisition-evaluation certificate for bounded utilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the independent utilities satisfy \(a\le U_i\le b\) almost surely, then for every \(\varepsilon>0\), \[\Pr\!\left(\left|\widehat\alpha_M(x)-\alpha(x)\right|\ge\varepsilon\right)\le 2\exp\!\left(-\frac{2M\varepsilon^2}{(b-a)^2}\right).\] Consequently, confidence level \(1-\delta\) is ensured by \(M\ge (b-a)^2\log(2/\delta)/(2\varepsilon^2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hoeffding's inequality gives a finite-sample fixed-candidate error certificate when acquisition utilities are bounded.
assumptions_latex: \(U_1,\ldots,U_M\) are independent.
\(a\le U_i\le b\) almost surely and \(\mathbb E[U_i]=\alpha(x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Utility Monte Carlo Error Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monte Carlo Variance and Central-Limit Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-candidate sampling error for independent acquisition-utility draws.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U_1,\ldots,U_M\) be i.i.d. with \(\mathbb E[U_i]=\alpha(x)\) and \(0<\operatorname{Var}(U_i)=\sigma^2(x)<\infty\). For \(\widehat\alpha_M(x)=M^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^M U_i\), \[\mathbb E[\widehat\alpha_M(x)]=\alpha(x),\qquad \operatorname{Var}(\widehat\alpha_M(x))=\frac{\sigma^2(x)}{M},\qquad \sqrt M\,\frac{\widehat\alpha_M(x)-\alpha(x)}{\sigma(x)}\Rightarrow N(0,1).\] Thus the root-mean-square sampling error is \(\sigma(x)/\sqrt M\), and reducing it by a factor \(r>1\) requires multiplying the sample count by \(r^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The independent-sample acquisition average is unbiased, has variance inversely proportional to sample count, and obeys the fixed-candidate central limit theorem.
assumptions_latex: \(U_1,\ldots,U_M\) are independent and identically distributed.
\(0<\operatorname{Var}(U_i)<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{RMSE}(\widehat\alpha_M)=\sigma/\sqrt M\) and the standardized error converges in distribution to \(N(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Monte Carlo Variance and Central-Limit Scaling
Monte Carlo Acquisition Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent posterior-sample estimation of an acquisition expectation with an empirical error assessment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\alpha_n(x)=\mathbb E[u(x,Z)]\), sample \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_M\) independently from the posterior predictive distribution and compute \(U_i=u(x,Z_i)\). Return \(\widehat\alpha_{n,M}(x)=M^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^M U_i\) and estimated standard error \(\widehat s_M(x)/\sqrt M\), where \(\widehat s_M^2(x)=(M-1)^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^M(U_i-\widehat\alpha_{n,M}(x))^2\). Continue sampling until a prescribed budget is exhausted or the estimated standard error is below tolerance. When \(u(x,Z)\) is integrable, \(\widehat\alpha_{n,M}(x)\) converges almost surely to \(\alpha_n(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Monte Carlo evaluation averages acquisition utilities over independent posterior samples and reports an empirical standard error, stopping at a budget or precision threshold.
assumptions_latex: \(Z_i\) are independent draws from the posterior predictive law.
\(\mathbb E[|u(x,Z)|]<\infty\); finite variance is additionally required for the stated standard error.

notation.meaning: utility evaluated on posterior sample i
sample standard deviation of simulated utilities

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sample-mean acquisition estimator and strong law of large numbers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Monte Carlo algorithm, variance qualification, and strong-law conclusion are mathematically consistent and fit the leaf, but no inspectable citation supports the estimator or convergence claim.

children.title: Quasi-Monte Carlo Acquisition Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Low-discrepancy evaluation of acquisition expectations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic low-discrepancy integration error for a transformed acquisition integrand.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_x(v)=u(x,T_x(v))\) on \([0,1]^s\), and let \(P_M=\{v_1,\ldots,v_M\}\). If \(f_x\) has finite Hardy–Krause variation \(V_{HK}(f_x)\), then \[\left|\frac1M\sum_{i=1}^M f_x(v_i)-\int_{[0,1]^s}f_x(v)\,dv\right|\le V_{HK}(f_x)D_M^*(P_M),\] where \(D_M^*(P_M)\) is the star discrepancy. Hence any point sequence with \(D_M^*(P_M)\to0\) is consistent for such integrands.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Koksma–Hlawka bounds deterministic QMC acquisition error by transformed-integrand variation times point-set discrepancy.
assumptions_latex: \(f_x\) has finite Hardy–Krause variation.
\(P_M\subset[0,1]^s\).

notation.meaning: star discrepancy of the QMC point set

knowledge_statements.title: Koksma–Hlawka Acquisition Error Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbiased randomized low-discrepancy acquisition estimates and replicate-based uncertainty assessment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a randomization maps each deterministic QMC point \(v_i\) to \(\widetilde v_i\) with marginal distribution \(\operatorname{Unif}([0,1]^s)\) while preserving the point set's low-discrepancy structure. For integrable \(f_x\), \[\widehat\alpha_M^{(r)}(x)=\frac1M\sum_{i=1}^M f_x(\widetilde v_i^{(r)})\quad\text{satisfies}\quad \mathbb E[\widehat\alpha_M^{(r)}(x)]=\alpha(x).\] If additionally \(f_x\in L^2([0,1]^s)\), then with \(R\ge2\) independent randomizations the replicate sample variance consistently estimates the randomized-replicate variance as \(R\to\infty\), and the grand mean has variance \(\operatorname{Var}(\widehat\alpha_M^{(1)})/R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Marginally uniform QMC randomization makes each replicate unbiased; square integrability and independent randomizations permit a conventional replicate standard error.
assumptions_latex: Each randomized point is marginally uniform.
The transformed integrand is integrable for unbiasedness and square-integrable for variance estimation.
Randomizations are independent across replicates.
knowledge_statements.title: Randomized QMC Replicate Estimation
Quasi-Monte Carlo Acquisition Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Low-discrepancy integration of a transformed posterior acquisition expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent the posterior draw as \(Z=T_x(U)\), where \(U\) is uniform on \([0,1]^s\), so \(\alpha_n(x)=\int_{[0,1]^s}u(x,T_x(v))\,dv\). Choose a low-discrepancy point set \(v_1,\ldots,v_M\), optionally apply independent randomizations for uncertainty assessment, and return \(\widehat\alpha^{\mathrm{QMC}}_{n,M}(x)=M^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^M u(x,T_x(v_i))\). For randomized replicates, stop when their empirical standard error meets tolerance or the point budget is exhausted. Deterministic consistency requires the transformed integrand to be Riemann integrable and the point sequence to be uniformly distributed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quasi-Monte Carlo replaces independent samples with low-discrepancy points transformed into posterior draws; randomized replicates can provide an empirical error estimate.
assumptions_latex: \(T_x\) pushes the uniform law on \([0,1]^s\) to the posterior predictive law.
The transformed integrand \(v\mapsto u(x,T_x(v))\) is Riemann integrable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For a uniformly distributed point sequence, \(\widehat\alpha^{\mathrm{QMC}}_{n,M}(x)\to\alpha_n(x)\) as \(M\to\infty\).

notation.meaning: transform from a uniform reference point to a posterior draw

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard transformed low-discrepancy integration construction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The QMC algorithm and stated consistency conditions are coherent and fit the leaf, but the transformed integration construction and convergence assertion lack a cited source and specific locator.

children.title: Nested Expectation Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Sampling-based computation for acquisitions containing multiple conditional expectation levels.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Smooth Nested-Estimator Bias and Budget Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-level mean-square rate under conditionally unbiased inner means and a smooth outer transformation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(\mathbb E[\widehat\mu_M(Z)-\mu(Z)\mid Z]=0\), \(\mathbb E[(\widehat\mu_M(Z)-\mu(Z))^2\mid Z]\le C/M\), \(|g(Z,y)|\le B\), and \(|\partial_{yy}g(Z,y)|\le L\) on the relevant range. Then \[\left|\mathbb E[g(Z,\widehat\mu_M(Z))]-\mathbb E[g(Z,\mu(Z))]\right|\le\frac{LC}{2M},\] and independent outer replications satisfy \[\mathbb E[(\widehat\alpha_{N,M}-\alpha)^2]\le \frac{B^2}{N}+\frac{L^2C^2}{4M^2}.\] Thus \(N=O(\varepsilon^{-2})\) and \(M=O(\varepsilon^{-1})\) suffice for root-mean-square error \(O(\varepsilon)\), using \(O(\varepsilon^{-3})\) inner samples in total.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a twice-differentiable outer map, inner plug-in bias is first order in the inverse inner count, yielding the standard sufficient cubic total-cost scaling for a target root-mean-square error.
assumptions_latex: The inner conditional-mean estimator is conditionally unbiased with conditional mean-square error at most \(C/M\).
The outer map is bounded by \(B\) and has second derivative bounded by \(L\) in its inner-mean argument.
Outer replications and their inner simulations are independent across outer indices.

notation.meaning: bound on the outer transformed payoff
bound on the second derivative of the outer transformation

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Nested-Estimator Bias and Budget Scaling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency and the fixed-inner-budget boundary for a two-level plug-in expectation estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mu(z)=\mathbb E[h(z,W)\mid Z=z]\), \(\widehat\mu_M(z)=M^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^M h(z,W_j)\), and \(\widehat\alpha_{N,M}=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N g(Z_i,\widehat\mu_{i,M})\). If \(h\) and \(g\) are bounded, \(g(z,\cdot)\) is continuous for almost every \(z\), outer draws are i.i.d., and inner draws are conditionally i.i.d., then for every sequence \(N_k\to\infty\), \(M_k\to\infty\), \[\widehat\alpha_{N_k,M_k}\xrightarrow{p}\alpha:=\mathbb E[g(Z,\mu(Z))].\] If \(M\) is fixed and only \(N\to\infty\), then \(\widehat\alpha_{N,M}\xrightarrow{p}\alpha_M:=\mathbb E[g(Z,\widehat\mu_M(Z))]\), which need not equal \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested Monte Carlo is consistent when both sample levels grow under boundedness and continuity, whereas increasing only the outer count can converge to a different finite-inner target.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) and \(g\) are bounded.
\(g(z,\cdot)\) is continuous for almost every outer state.
Outer samples are i.i.d. and inner samples are conditionally i.i.d.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N,M\to\infty\) yields convergence in probability to \(\alpha\); fixed \(M\) yields the possibly distinct limit \(\alpha_M\).
knowledge_statements.title: Nested Monte Carlo Double-Limit Consistency
Nested Expectation Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-level simulation for acquisitions containing a nonlinear function of a conditional expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\alpha(x)=\mathbb E_Z[g(x,Z,\mu(x,Z))]\), where \(\mu(x,z)=\mathbb E_W[h(x,z,W)\mid Z=z]\). Draw outer samples \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_N\). For each \(Z_i\), draw conditionally independent inner samples \(W_{i1},\ldots,W_{iM}\), form \(\widehat\mu_{i,M}=M^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^M h(x,Z_i,W_{ij})\), and return \(\widehat\alpha_{N,M}(x)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N g(x,Z_i,\widehat\mu_{i,M})\). Stop at prescribed \((N,M)\) or an error criterion. If \(g\) is nonlinear in its last argument, finite \(M\) generally makes this plug-in estimator biased.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested evaluation uses inner samples to estimate each conditional expectation and outer samples to average the resulting utility; nonlinear outer transformations generally create finite-inner-sample bias.
assumptions_latex: All displayed expectations are finite.
Inner samples are conditionally independent given each outer sample, and outer samples are independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\alpha_{N,M}(x)\) is the nested estimator, generally biased for finite \(M\) when \(g\) is nonlinear in \(\mu\).

notation.meaning: conditional expectation estimated by the inner loop

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical nested Monte Carlo plug-in estimator and nonlinear finite-inner-sample bias

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nested simulation algorithm fits the leaf. Nonlinearity commonly induces finite-inner-sample bias, but nonlinearity alone does not make bias universal; a source is needed to state sufficient conditions and exceptions precisely.

children.title: Batch Expectation Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Sampling-based computation for joint acquisition values over candidate batches.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Permutation Invariance of Symmetric Batch Expectations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural invariance of a batch expectation under reordering of an unordered candidate batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_q)\), let \(F_X\) have its joint posterior law, and let \(\pi\) be any permutation. If \(F_{\pi X}\overset d=\pi F_X\) and \(u(\pi X,\pi y)=u(X,y)\), then \[\alpha_n(\pi X)=\mathbb E[u(\pi X,F_{\pi X})]=\mathbb E[u(X,F_X)]=\alpha_n(X).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the predictive law is permutation-equivariant and the batch utility is symmetric, reordering the batch cannot change its expected acquisition value.
assumptions_latex: The joint predictive response vector is permutation-equivariant.
The batch utility is invariant under simultaneous permutation of sites and responses.

notation.meaning: Batch X with its coordinates permuted

knowledge_statements.title: Permutation Invariance of Symmetric Batch Expectations
Batch Expectation Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint posterior-sample evaluation of an acquisition for a batch of candidate locations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a batch \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_q)\in\mathcal X^q\), let \(F_X=(F(x_1),\ldots,F(x_q))\) have the joint posterior predictive law and define \(\alpha_n(X)=\mathbb E[u(X,F_X)]\). Draw joint samples \(F_X^{(1)},\ldots,F_X^{(M)}\), preserving posterior dependence among all batch components, and return \(\widehat\alpha_{n,M}(X)=M^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^M u(X,F_X^{(i)})\). Reuse common base random numbers when comparing batches, if desired, and stop at a sample budget or estimated-error tolerance. Sampling batch marginals independently is invalid unless their posterior predictive dependence is absent or the utility factorizes appropriately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Batch evaluation averages utility over joint posterior draws at all batch points; retaining cross-point dependence is essential for nonseparable batch acquisitions.
assumptions_latex: \(u(X,F_X)\) is integrable under the joint posterior predictive law.
Each \(F_X^{(i)}\) is a joint draw with the correct within-batch dependence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\alpha_{n,M}(X)\) consistently estimates \(\alpha_n(X)\); independent marginal sampling generally targets the wrong expectation.

notation.meaning: ordered batch of q candidate locations
joint posterior responses across the batch

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: posterior sample-average evaluation of a joint batch utility

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and joint-dependence emphasis fit batch evaluation, but consistency also requires independent joint draws or another explicitly consistent sampling scheme. A specific source is needed for the estimator and the claim about invalid independent marginal sampling.

children.title: Conditional-Posterior Lookahead Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Conditional posterior constructions for pending, batch, and multistep decisions.

children.title: Conditional Fantasy Models
children.top_down_role: Conditional surrogate constructions representing unresolved future observations.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Fantasy Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines posterior models conditioned on simulated future observations, without prescribing a particular surrogate family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given observed data \(\mathcal D\) and proposed fantasy sites \(X_F=(x_1^F,\ldots,x_q^F)\), draw fantasy outcomes \(Y_F\sim P(\cdot\mid\mathcal D,X_F)\). The conditional fantasy model associated with the realized fantasy outcomes is the surrogate posterior \[P(df\mid\mathcal D,X_F,Y_F):=P\bigl(df\mid\mathcal D\cup\{(X_F,Y_F)\}\bigr).\] Thus the conditional model depends on the simulated outcomes, whose uncertainty is described by their posterior predictive law.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conditional fantasy model is the surrogate posterior obtained by adjoining simulated outcomes at proposed sites; the simulated outcomes remain random under their posterior predictive distribution.
assumptions_latex: The surrogate posterior is a probability law \(P(df\mid\mathcal D)\) on functions over \(\mathcal X\).
The fantasy sites \(X_F=(x_1^F,\ldots,x_q^F)\) have a well-defined posterior predictive distribution.

notation.meaning: Observed data used to fit the surrogate
Locations and simulated outcomes of fantasy observations

source_refs.locator: 1.6.2 Policies based on lookahead approximations p. 20

source_witnesses.locator: 1.6.2 Policies based on lookahead approximations p. 20

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Off-Predictive Fantasy Mixing Can Break Coherence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of posterior-mixture coherence under an incorrect fantasy-outcome law.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in\{0,1\}\) have current posterior \(P(f=1\mid\mathcal D)=1/2\), and let the fantasy observation be noiseless, \(Y_F=f\). Correct predictive mixing gives \(\tfrac12\delta_0+\tfrac12\delta_1=P(df\mid\mathcal D)\). If instead fantasies are drawn from \(R=\delta_1\), every conditional fantasy posterior is \(\delta_1\), so the induced mixture is \(\delta_1\neq P(df\mid\mathcal D)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary noiseless example shows that an incorrect fantasy distribution can make the averaged fantasy posterior differ from the current posterior.
assumptions_latex: \(P(f=1\mid\mathcal D)=1/2\).
The fantasy observation satisfies \(Y_F=f\) almost surely.
The alternative fantasy law is \(R=\delta_1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Off-Predictive Fantasy Mixing Can Break Coherence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Predictive Averaging Consistency of Fantasy Posteriors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Marginal coherence of conditional fantasy posteriors averaged under the correct predictive fantasy law.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_F\sim P(\cdot\mid\mathcal D,X_F)\) and \(Q_y(df)=P(df\mid\mathcal D,X_F,Y_F=y)\). For every integrable measurable functional \(h\), \[\mathbb E\!\left[\int h(f)Q_{Y_F}(df)\mid\mathcal D,X_F\right]=\int h(f)P(df\mid\mathcal D).\] Equivalently, \(\int Q_y(df)P(dy\mid\mathcal D,X_F)=P(df\mid\mathcal D)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaging conditional fantasy posteriors over correctly distributed fantasy outcomes recovers the current posterior.
assumptions_latex: A regular conditional posterior \(Q_y\) exists.
\(h\) is integrable under the joint posterior law.

notation.meaning: Posterior conditioned on fantasy outcome y

knowledge_statements.title: Predictive Averaging Consistency of Fantasy Posteriors

children.title: Pending-Evaluation Fantasies
children.top_down_role: Fantasy constructions used when earlier evaluations remain incomplete.

assumptions_latex: The pending sites \(X_P\) are fixed and their outcomes have not yet been observed.
The acquisition \(a(x;\mathcal D')\) is integrable under the predictive law of pending outcomes.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Treats unresolved evaluations as fantasy observations when selecting an additional point.

source_refs.locator: 1.6.2 Policies based on lookahead approximations p. 20

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input observed data \(\mathcal D\), pending sites \(X_P\), a base acquisition \(a\), and a fantasy count \(M\). For each \(m=1,\ldots,M\), sample \(Y_P^{(m)}\sim P(\cdot\mid\mathcal D,X_P)\), form \(\mathcal D_P^{(m)}=\mathcal D\cup\{(X_P,Y_P^{(m)})\}\), and evaluate \(a(x;\mathcal D_P^{(m)})\). Return \[\widehat a_P(x)=\frac1M\sum_{m=1}^M a(x;\mathcal D_P^{(m)}),\] or its maximizer over the feasible domain. Its population target is \(a_P(x)=\mathbb E[a(x;\mathcal D\cup\{(X_P,Y_P)\})\mid\mathcal D,X_P]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample possible outcomes at pending locations, update the surrogate for each sample, and average the resulting acquisition values before selecting another point.
knowledge_statements.title: Pending-Evaluation Fantasies

source_witnesses.locator: 1.6.2 Policies based on lookahead approximations p. 20

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise unbiasedness, variance, and consistency of the immutable pending-fantasy estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(x\) and write \(Z=a(x;\mathcal D\cup\{(X_P,Y_P)\})\). If \(Y_P^{(1)},\ldots,Y_P^{(M)}\) are iid from \(P(\cdot\mid\mathcal D,X_P)\) and \(\mathbb E|Z|<\infty\), then \(\widehat a_P(x)\to a_P(x)\) almost surely. If additionally \(\operatorname{Var}(Z)<\infty\), then \(\mathbb E[\widehat a_P(x)]=a_P(x)\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(\widehat a_P(x))=\operatorname{Var}(Z)/M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a fixed candidate, iid joint predictive fantasies give an unbiased estimator with one-over-M variance and almost-sure consistency.
assumptions_latex: Fantasy replicates are iid from the joint predictive law of all pending outcomes.
The fantasized acquisition value is integrable.
The variance identity additionally requires a finite second moment.

notation.meaning: Acquisition value under one joint pending-outcome fantasy

knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Guarantees for Pending-Fantasy Averaging

children.title: Batch Fantasy Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Conditional acquisition computation for multiple proposed evaluations.

assumptions_latex: A candidate batch \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_q)\) has a joint posterior predictive distribution.
The batch utility \(u(X,Y;\mathcal D)\) is integrable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat A_q(X)=M^{-1}\sum_{m=1}^M u(X,Y^{(m)};\mathcal D)\) estimates \(A_q(X)=\mathbb E[u(X,Y;\mathcal D)\mid\mathcal D,X]\).

notation.meaning: Joint fantasy outcomes for the batch

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monte Carlo evaluation of a joint batch acquisition under correlated fantasy outcomes.

source_refs.locator: 1.6.2 Policies based on lookahead approximations p. 20

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input data \(\mathcal D\), a candidate batch \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_q)\), utility \(u\), and sample count \(M\). Draw joint fantasies \(Y^{(m)}\sim P(\cdot\mid\mathcal D,X)\) for \(m=1,\ldots,M\), preserving posterior dependence among batch outcomes. Compute \[\widehat A_q(X)=\frac1M\sum_{m=1}^M u(X,Y^{(m)};\mathcal D).\] Use common base random draws when comparing batches if desired, optimize \(\widehat A_q\) over feasible batches, and return a maximizing batch. The exact target is \(A_q(X)=\mathbb E[u(X,Y;\mathcal D)\mid\mathcal D,X]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Draw correlated outcomes for every point in a candidate batch, average the resulting batch utility, and optimize that Monte Carlo acquisition over feasible batches.
knowledge_statements.title: Batch Fantasy Evaluation

source_witnesses.locator: 1.6.2 Policies based on lookahead approximations p. 20

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform finite-sample error and acquisition-selection guarantee over finitely many candidate batches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_N\) be fixed candidate batches. Suppose each fantasy utility lies almost surely in \([a,b]\), and estimate every \(A_q(X_j)\) using \(M\) iid joint fantasies. Then, with probability at least \(1-\delta\), \[\max_{1\leq j\leq N}|\widehat A_q(X_j)-A_q(X_j)|\leq (b-a)\sqrt{\frac{\log(2N/\delta)}{2M}}=:\varepsilon_M.\] If \(\widehat j\in\arg\max_j\widehat A_q(X_j)\), then \[\max_jA_q(X_j)-A_q(X_{\widehat j})\leq2\varepsilon_M.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed finite batch family with bounded utilities, fantasy Monte Carlo has uniform error of order square root log N over M and incurs at most twice that error when selecting a batch.
assumptions_latex: The candidate batch family is fixed independently of the Monte Carlo samples used in the displayed guarantee.
For each batch, fantasy replicates are iid from its correct joint predictive law.
\(a\leq u(X_j,Y;\mathcal D)\leq b\) almost surely.

notation.meaning: Uniform fantasy Monte Carlo error bound

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Family Fantasy Monte Carlo Accuracy

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample showing that batch-outcome dependence cannot be discarded for nonlinear utility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q=2\), let the correct joint fantasy law satisfy \(Y_1=Y_2\) almost surely with each marginal uniform on \(\{-1,1\}\), and take \(u(Y_1,Y_2)=\mathbf1\{Y_1=Y_2\}\). Then \(\mathbb E_P[u]=1\). If the two correct marginals are instead sampled independently, \(\mathbb E_{P_1\otimes P_2}[u]=1/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sampling each batch outcome from the correct marginal while ignoring posterior correlation can bias a nonlinear batch-acquisition value.
assumptions_latex: The utility depends jointly and nonlinearly on batch outcomes.

notation.meaning: Incorrect product of the predictive marginals

knowledge_statements.title: Independent-Marginal Fantasy Bias

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fantasy Monte Carlo Unbiasedness and Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Statistical properties of the accepted joint-fantasy acquisition estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed batch \(X\), let \(U_m=u(X,Y^{(m)};\mathcal D)\) with iid joint fantasies \(Y^{(m)}\sim P(\cdot\mid\mathcal D,X)\). If \(\mathbb E|U_1|<\infty\), then \(\widehat A_q(X)=M^{-1}\sum_{m=1}^MU_m\to A_q(X)\) almost surely. If additionally \(\operatorname{Var}(U_1)<\infty\), then \[\mathbb E[\widehat A_q(X)\mid\mathcal D,X]=A_q(X),\qquad \operatorname{Var}(\widehat A_q(X)\mid\mathcal D,X)=\operatorname{Var}(U_1\mid\mathcal D,X)/M.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed batch, joint-fantasy Monte Carlo is unbiased, has variance decreasing as one over the fantasy count, and is strongly consistent.
assumptions_latex: Fantasy vectors are iid across Monte Carlo replicates and have the correct joint posterior predictive law.
The utility is integrable; the variance identity additionally requires finite variance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat A_q(X)\to A_q(X)\) almost surely and, under finite variance, \(\operatorname{Var}(\widehat A_q)=\operatorname{Var}(U_1)/M\).
knowledge_statements.title: Fantasy Monte Carlo Unbiasedness and Consistency

children.title: Multistep Lookahead Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Numerical valuation of acquisition decisions across several future stages.

assumptions_latex: The horizon \(H\) is finite and each action set \(\mathcal X_t(\mathcal D_t)\) is nonempty.
Stage rewards and the terminal value are integrable under every admissible policy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_t(\mathcal D_t)=\sup_{x_t\in\mathcal X_t(\mathcal D_t)}\mathbb E[r_t+V_{t+1}(\mathcal D_{t+1})\mid\mathcal D_t,x_t]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon posterior-state recursion evaluated through nested fantasy outcomes.

source_refs.locator: 1.6.2 Policies based on lookahead approximations p. 20
6. Control Optimization with Stochastic Dynamic Programming p. 123
source_refs.source_title: Simulation-Based Optimization: Parametric Optimization Techniques and Reinforcement Learning

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(V_H(\mathcal D_H)=g(\mathcal D_H)\). For \(t=H-1,\ldots,0\), evaluate candidate \(x_t\) by drawing \(Y_t\sim P(\cdot\mid\mathcal D_t,x_t)\), updating \(\mathcal D_{t+1}=\mathcal D_t\cup\{(x_t,Y_t)\}\), and applying \[V_t(\mathcal D_t)=\sup_{x_t\in\mathcal X_t(\mathcal D_t)}\mathbb E\!\left[r_t(\mathcal D_t,x_t,Y_t)+V_{t+1}(\mathcal D_{t+1})\mid\mathcal D_t,x_t\right].\] Nested quadrature or Monte Carlo fantasies approximate each expectation. Return a first-stage maximizer; later actions are reoptimized after their preceding fantasy outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate each first action by recursively averaging future rewards over fantasy observations while reoptimizing every later action, then return the best first action.
knowledge_statements.title: Multistep Lookahead Evaluation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform value-error certificate for an approximate finite-horizon Bellman evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_t\) be the exact Bellman operator and suppose \(\|\widehat T_tv-T_tv\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_t\) for every continuation value encountered. If \(\|\widehat V_H-V_H\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_H\) and \(\widehat V_t=\widehat T_t\widehat V_{t+1}\), then \[\|\widehat V_t-V_t\|_\infty\le\sum_{s=t}^{H}\varepsilon_s.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform stagewise numerical errors add across the finite lookahead horizon.
assumptions_latex: The exact Bellman operators are nonexpansive in the continuation value under the supremum norm.
Every stagewise operator-error bound holds uniformly on the continuation values used.
The terminal-value approximation has uniform error at most \(\varepsilon_H\).
knowledge_statements.title: Backward Evaluation-Error Accumulation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tree size for fixed-branching finite-horizon lookahead evaluation without branch reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every conditional expectation in an \(H\)-stage lookahead is represented by exactly \(m\ge1\) fantasy outcomes and no branches are merged or pruned, the full tree has \(m^H\) terminal scenarios and \(\sum_{t=0}^{H}m^t=(m^{H+1}-1)/(m-1)\) nodes for \(m\ne1\), or \(H+1\) nodes for \(m=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full H-stage lookahead with m fantasies per stage has m to the H terminal scenarios and geometrically many total nodes.
assumptions_latex: The lookahead contains \(H\) successive fantasy stages.
Every nonterminal node has exactly \(m\) children.
No branch reuse, merging, or pruning is performed.
knowledge_statements.title: Full Fantasy-Tree Growth

children.title: Analytic Acquisition Derivatives
children.top_down_role: Derivative calculations for differentiable surrogate and acquisition families.

assumptions_latex: The acquisition has the form \(a(x)=F(m(x),s(x))\) on an open subset of \(\mathbb R^d\).
The functions \(F\), \(m\), and \(s\) are differentiable at the relevant arguments.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chain-rule derivative for acquisitions expressed through differentiable posterior summaries.

source_refs.source_title: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(a(x)=F(m(x),s(x))\), where \(m\) and \(s\) are differentiable posterior mean and standard-deviation functions and \(F\) is differentiable on their range. Then the analytic acquisition derivative is \[
abla_xa(x)=F_m(m(x),s(x))

abla_	heta F(	heta(x))\). The formula applies only where all displayed derivatives exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a differentiable acquisition built from differentiable posterior summaries, its input gradient is obtained by chaining acquisition partial derivatives with surrogate-summary gradients.

The formulas use maximization, a fixed threshold \(\tau\), and \(\beta\ge0\).

children.top_down_role: Stochastic derivative estimators for Monte Carlo acquisition objectives.

children.title: Pathwise Gradient Estimators
children.top_down_role: Stochastic acquisition derivatives obtained through differentiable sample transformations.

assumptions_latex: There is a parameter-free random variable \(\varepsilon\sim Q\) and a differentiable sampler \(Z=T(x,\varepsilon)\).
The derivative of \(h(x,T(x,\varepsilon))\) is dominated locally by a \(Q\)-integrable random variable.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interchange-of-derivative form of the reparameterization gradient estimator.

source_refs.locator: 5. Parametric Optimization: Stochastic Gradients and Adaptive Search p. 71
source_refs.source_title: Simulation-Based Optimization: Parametric Optimization Techniques and Reinforcement Learning

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(A(x)=\mathbb E_Q[h(x,T(x,\varepsilon))]\), where the law \(Q\) of \(\varepsilon\) is independent of \(x\). If \(x\mapsto h(x,T(x,\varepsilon))\) is almost surely differentiable and its derivative admits a locally integrable dominating function, then \[
abla_xA(x)=\mathbb E_Q\!\left[
abla_x h(x,T(x,\varepsilon))ight].\] Hence independent draws \(\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_M\sim Q\) give the unbiased estimator \[\widehat g_{\mathrm{pw}}(x)= rac1M\sum_{m=1}^M
abla_xh(x,T(x,\varepsilon_m)).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Differentiate through a smooth reparameterized sampler and average sample derivatives; under domination, this gives an unbiased gradient of the expected acquisition.

children.title: Score-Function Gradient Estimators
children.top_down_role: Stochastic acquisition derivatives based on distributional log-sensitivity.

assumptions_latex: The law of \(Z\) has density \(p_x(z)\) on support independent of \(x\).
Differentiation may pass under the integral, and \(h(x,Z)\nabla_x\log p_x(Z)+\nabla_xh(x,Z)\) is integrable.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Likelihood-ratio gradient identity for parameter-dependent sampling distributions with fixed support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A(x)=\int h(x,z)p_x(z)\,dz\), with parameter-independent support. Under differentiation-under-the-integral conditions, \[
abla_xA(x)=\mathbb E_{p_x}\!\left[
abla_xh(x,Z)+h(x,Z)
abla_x\log p_x(Z)ight].\] Therefore samples \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_M\sim p_x\) yield \[\widehat g_{\mathrm{sf}}(x)= rac1M\sum_{m=1}^M\left[
abla_xh(x,Z_m)+h(x,Z_m)
abla_x\log p_x(Z_m)ight],\] an unbiased score-function estimator whenever the displayed terms are integrable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiply sample utility by the log-density score, add any direct utility derivative, and average to estimate the expected acquisition gradient unbiasedly.
knowledge_statements.title: Score-Function Gradient Estimators

children.title: Estimator Variance Control
children.top_down_role: Variance-reduction considerations for stochastic acquisition derivatives.

assumptions_latex: A square-integrable gradient estimator has the form \(G=H(Z)S(Z)\).
The score satisfies \(\mathbb E[S(Z)]=0\), and \(c\) is deterministic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_c=(H(Z)-c)S(Z)\) is unbiased, and its variance-minimizing scalar baseline is \(c^*=\mathbb E[H\lVert S\rVert^2]/\mathbb E[\lVert S\rVert^2]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar baseline control variate for a vector score-function gradient estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(G=H(Z)S(Z)\) with \(\mathbb E[S(Z)]=0\), define \(G_c=(H(Z)-c)S(Z)\). Then \(\mathbb E[G_c]=\mathbb E[G]\) for every deterministic scalar \(c\). If \(0<\mathbb E[\lVert S(Z)\rVert_2^2]<\infty\), the baseline minimizing \(\mathbb E[\lVert G_c-\mathbb E[G]\rVert_2^2]\) is \[c^*=\frac{\mathbb E[H(Z)\lVert S(Z)\rVert_2^2]}{\mathbb E[\lVert S(Z)\rVert_2^2]}.\] Replacing expectations by independent pilot estimates preserves the control-variate interpretation, though exact unbiasedness then depends on how the baseline is estimated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting a deterministic baseline from a score-weighted utility preserves its mean; a weighted least-squares baseline minimizes total estimator variance.
knowledge_statements.title: Estimator Variance Control

knowledge_statements.statement_title: General Linear Control Variate for Gradient Estimates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variance-minimizing linear adjustment using a known-mean auxiliary random vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\in\mathbb R^d\) be a square-integrable unbiased gradient estimator and \(C\in\mathbb R^k\) a square-integrable control with known mean \(\mu_C\). For any deterministic \(B\in\mathbb R^{d\times k}\), \[G_B=G-B(C-\mu_C)\] remains unbiased. If \(\Sigma_{CC}=\operatorname{Cov}(C,C)\) is nonsingular, the matrix minimizing \(\mathbb E\|G_B-\mathbb E G\|_2^2\) is \[B^*=\operatorname{Cov}(G,C)\Sigma_{CC}^{-1}.\] With \(M\) independent adjusted samples, the sample-mean covariance is \(\operatorname{Cov}(G_{B^*})/M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting a linear known-mean control preserves a stochastic gradient's expectation; covariance regression gives the minimum-total-variance coefficient, and independent averaging divides covariance by sample count.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) and \(C\) are square-integrable.
\(\mathbb E[C]=\mu_C\) is known.
\(\operatorname{Cov}(C,C)\) is nonsingular for the stated coefficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_B\) is unbiased and \(B^*=\operatorname{Cov}(G,C)\operatorname{Cov}(C,C)^{-1}\) minimizes total variance.
knowledge_statements.title: General Linear Control Variate for Gradient Estimates

children.title: Nondifferentiable Sampling Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Estimator limitations arising from discrete, discontinuous, or unstable sampling constructions.

assumptions_latex: The sampling law is uniform on \([0,x]\) for \(x>0\).
The sample payoff is \(h(z)=z\), so \(A(x)=\mathbb E[Z]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A'(x)=1/2\), but differentiating \(h(Z)\) while treating the sample as fixed gives \(0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete moving-support failure of naive differentiation that ignores sampling-boundary motion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x>0\) and \(Z\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,x]\). For the payoff \(h(z)=z\), \[A(x)=\mathbb E[Z]=\frac{x}{2},\qquad A'(x)=\frac12.\] A procedure that holds the realized \(Z\) fixed and differentiates only \(h(Z)\) reports \(\partial h(Z)/\partial x=0\), hence misses the derivative entirely. The failure occurs because the sampling support depends on \(x\). A valid reparameterization \(Z=xU\), with \(U\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\), restores the pathwise derivative \(\mathbb E[U]=1/2\); alternatively, a moving-boundary term must be included.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a sampling support moves with the decision, differentiating the payoff at a fixed sample can miss the entire gradient; uniform sampling gives a concrete example.
knowledge_statements.title: Nondifferentiable Sampling Boundaries

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-support counterexample showing that almost-everywhere sample derivatives need not differentiate an expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) and, for \(x\in(0,1)\), set \(h(x,U)=\mathbf 1\{U\le x\}\). Then \[A(x)=\mathbb E[h(x,U)]=x,\qquad A'(x)=1.\] For almost every realized \(U\), however, \(x\mapsto h(x,U)\) is locally constant at a fixed \(x\), so \(\partial_xh(x,U)=0\) almost surely and \(\mathbb E[\partial_xh(x,U)]=0\). Thus naive pathwise differentiation fails even though the sampling support is fixed; the missing derivative is carried by the moving discontinuity of the payoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An indicator payoff can have zero sample derivative almost surely while its expectation has derivative one, so fixed support alone does not validate pathwise differentiation.
assumptions_latex: \(U\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.title: Discontinuous-Payoff Pathwise Failure

children.title: Acquisition Inner Solvers
children.top_down_role: Optimization methods adapted to nonconvex acquisition landscapes and structured domains.

children.title: Multistart Local Optimization
children.top_down_role: Local acquisition solvers combined with diversified initialization.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(\mathcal X\) is nonempty and the acquisition \(a:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) can be evaluated.
A local solver returns a feasible stationary or locally optimal point from each supplied start.

notation.meaning: Local solver initialized at a specified point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diversified restarts followed by local acquisition optimization and incumbent selection.

source_refs.source_title: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an acquisition \(a\), feasible set \(\mathcal X\), restart count \(R\), initialization rule \(Q\), local solver \(L\), and local stopping tolerances. Generate diversified feasible starts \(x_r^{(0)}\sim Q\) or by a deterministic space-filling design. For \(r=1,\ldots,R\), compute \(x_r^*=L(a,\mathcal X,x_r^{(0)})\) until the local stopping rule holds. Evaluate all terminal points and return \[\widehat x\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{1\le r\le R}a(x_r^*).\] The method certifies only superiority among returned terminal points; without additional assumptions it does not certify global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run a local acquisition solver from diverse feasible starts and return the terminal point with the largest acquisition value; global optimality is not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.title: Multistart Local Optimization

source_witnesses.source_title: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computational cost of independent local acquisition runs and terminal-point reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If local run \(r\) has work \(W_r\) and span \(S_r\), then executing all \(R\) runs and comparing their terminal values requires total work \[\sum_{r=1}^R W_r+O(R).\] If the runs execute independently in parallel and terminal values are combined by a comparison tree, the span is \[\max_{1\le r\le R}S_r+O(\log R).\] Hence runs of work at most \(W\) have total work \(O(RW)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent local runs require the sum of their work; parallel execution has the span of the slowest run plus a logarithmic comparison reduction.
assumptions_latex: The \(R\) local runs can execute independently.
Run \(r\) has work \(W_r\) and span \(S_r\).
Terminal values can be combined using a comparison tree.

notation.meaning: Parallel span of local run r

knowledge_statements.title: Multistart Work and Parallel Span

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probability that multistart local acquisition optimization reaches a globally successful attraction basin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\subseteq\mathcal X\) be such that the deterministic local solver \(L\) returns a global maximizer whenever initialized in \(B\). If \(x_1^{(0)},\ldots,x_R^{(0)}\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}Q\), \(p=Q(B)\), terminal acquisition values are compared exactly, and the best terminal point is returned, then \[\Pr\!\left\{\widehat x\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}a(x)\right\}\ge 1-(1-p)^R.\] Thus the lower bound tends to one when \(p>0\); independent restarts alone give no such conclusion when all globally successful starts have \(Q\)-measure zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent restarts hit a globally successful basin of probability p with probability one minus (1-p) to the R; positive basin mass is essential for convergence in restart count.
assumptions_latex: \(x_1^{(0)},\ldots,x_R^{(0)}\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}Q\).
Every start in \(B\) is mapped by \(L\) to a global maximizer of \(a\).
Terminal acquisition values are evaluated exactly and the largest is returned.

notation.meaning: Set of starts leading to a global acquisition maximizer

knowledge_statements.title: Independent-Restart Basin Success Probability

children.title: Global Acquisition Search Family
children.top_down_role: Global and discrete methods for rugged or combinatorial acquisition domains.

children.title: Partition-Based Inner Search
children.top_down_role: Acquisition optimization through recursive subdivision of the candidate domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Partition-Based Inner Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-and-bound-style global acquisition search using valid cellwise upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a feasible domain \(\mathcal X\), acquisition \(a:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\), tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge 0\), and valid cellwise upper bounds \(U\). Initialize a finite active partition \(\mathcal P=\{\mathcal X\}\), evaluate a feasible representative, and maintain a feasible incumbent \(\widehat x\). Repeatedly select a cell \(C\in\mathcal P\) with maximal \(U(C)\), replace it by finitely many children whose union is \(C\), evaluate feasible representatives of the children, and update \(\widehat x\). Stop when \[\max_{C\in\mathcal P}U(C)-a(\widehat x)\le\varepsilon\] or when a resource limit is reached. Because the active cells continue to cover \(\mathcal X\), tolerance termination implies \[\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}a(x)-a(\widehat x)\le\varepsilon.\] Resource-limit termination alone provides no such certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain a covering partition of the feasible domain, split the cell with the largest valid acquisition upper bound, and update a feasible incumbent. A sufficiently small global bound gap certifies near-optimality; stopping only because resources are exhausted does not.
assumptions_latex: The feasible domain \(\mathcal X\) admits finite recursively refinable partitions whose active cells cover \(\mathcal X\).
For every active cell \(C\), the computable bound satisfies \(a(x)\le U(C)\) for all \(x\in C\).
The incumbent \(\widehat x\) is feasible, and the tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\mathcal X=\bigcup_{C\in\mathcal P}C\) and termination occurs with \(\max_{C\in\mathcal P}U(C)-a(\widehat x)\le\varepsilon\), then \(\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}a(x)-a(\widehat x)\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Finite active partition covering the feasible domain
Valid acquisition upper bound on cell C

children.title: Enumerative Inner Search
children.top_down_role: Acquisition optimization over finite or discretized candidate sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Enumerative Inner Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact acquisition maximization over an explicitly finite feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite feasible set \(\mathcal X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}\), where \(N\ge 1\), and an exactly evaluable acquisition \(a:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\). Evaluate \(a(x_1)\) and initialize \(\widehat x=x_1\). For \(i=2,\ldots,N\), evaluate \(a(x_i)\) and replace \(\widehat x\) whenever \(a(x_i)>a(\widehat x)\), using a fixed rule for ties. After all candidates have been examined, return \[\widehat x\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X}a(x).\] The procedure uses \(N\) acquisition evaluations and certifies global optimality over \(\mathcal X\), but not over a larger ambient domain from which \(\mathcal X\) may have been discretized.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate the acquisition exactly at every point of a nonempty finite feasible set and return the best under a fixed tie rule. This is globally exact for that enumerated set only.

children.title: Combinatorial Acquisition Search
