knowledge_statements.statement_title: Greedy Search for Cardinality-Constrained Submodular Acquisition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial acquisition maximization for a normalized monotone submodular set function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(a:2^V\to\mathbb R_+\) be normalized, monotone, and submodular, and let \(1\le k\le|V|\). Starting from \(S_0=\varnothing\), choose
\[v_t\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{v\in V\setminus S_{t-1}}\bigl(a(S_{t-1}\cup\{v\})-a(S_{t-1})\bigr),\qquad S_t=S_{t-1}\cup\{v_t\},\]
for \(t=1,\ldots,k\). Then
\[a(S_k)\ge\left(1-\left(1-\frac1k\right)^k\right)\max_{|S|\le k}a(S)\ge(1-e^{-1})\max_{|S|\le k}a(S).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Greedy marginal-gain search achieves the classical one-minus-one-over-e acquisition approximation under monotone submodularity and a cardinality constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite.
\(a(\varnothing)=0\), and \(a\) is nonnegative, monotone, and submodular.
Feasibility is \(|S|\le k\).
Marginal gains are evaluated exactly.

notation.meaning: greedy partial decision after t additions

knowledge_statements.title: Greedy Search for Cardinality-Constrained Submodular Acquisition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Greedy Combinatorial Search Has No Generic Approximation Guarantee
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of marginal-gain greedy without submodularity or comparable structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(M>1\), let \(V=\{u,v,w\}\), impose \(|S|\le2\), and define a nonnegative monotone set function by
\[a(\varnothing)=0,\quad a(\{u\})=1,\quad a(\{v\})=a(\{w\})=0,\]
\[a(\{u,v\})=a(\{u,w\})=1,\quad a(\{v,w\})=a(\{u,v,w\})=M.\]
Marginal-gain greedy first selects \(u\) and then returns a value-one pair, whereas the optimal feasible set \(\{v,w\}\) has value \(M\). Hence its approximation ratio is \(1/M\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without submodularity or comparable structure, greedy acquisition search can be arbitrarily worse than the optimal combinatorial decision.
assumptions_latex: Greedy selects an element of maximum current marginal gain.

notation.meaning: set returned by marginal-gain greedy search

knowledge_statements.title: Greedy Combinatorial Search Has No Generic Approximation Guarantee

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Loose Bounds Can Force Exponential Branch-and-Bound Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case node-complexity boundary for inclusion–exclusion search over a combinatorial acquisition domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) have \(d\) elements, let every subset be feasible, and let an inclusion–exclusion branch-and-bound tree represent all \(2^d\) subsets. Set \(a(S)=0\) for every \(S\subseteq V\), use the valid but loose bound \(U(N)=1\) at every nonterminal node, and choose \(0\le\varepsilon<1\). Then no nonterminal node satisfies the additive-gap pruning test \(U(N)\le a(\widehat S)+\varepsilon\). Consequently the method visits all \(2^d\) leaves and, for a full binary tree, \(2^{d+1}-1\) nodes. Valid bounds therefore ensure correctness but do not by themselves ensure subexponential search.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid but uninformative upper bound can prevent all early pruning, forcing branch-and-bound to enumerate exponentially many combinatorial decisions.
assumptions_latex: Every subset of \(V\) is feasible and the tree branches by inclusion or exclusion of each element.
\(a(S)=0\) for all feasible sets.
Every nonterminal node uses \(U(N)=1\), and \(0\le\varepsilon<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The search visits }2^d\text{ leaves and }2^{d+1}-1\text{ total nodes.}

notation.meaning: upper bound assigned to search node N

knowledge_statements.title: Loose Bounds Can Force Exponential Branch-and-Bound Search

assumptions_latex: The feasible family \(\mathcal F\subseteq 2^V\) over a finite ground set \(V\) is nonempty.
The acquisition value \(a(S)\) is evaluable for every \(S\in\mathcal F\).
A search oracle provides valid upper bounds \(U(N)\geq\max_{S\in\mathcal F(N)}a(S)\) for partial-decision nodes \(N\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified branch-and-bound realization for acquisition maximization over a finite combinatorial family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Create a root node representing \(\mathcal F\), obtain any incumbent \(\widehat S\in\mathcal F\), and maintain a queue of partial-decision nodes. At node \(N\), prune when \(U(N)\leq a(\widehat S)+\varepsilon\); otherwise branch into children whose feasible completions partition \(\mathcal F(N)\). Evaluate every complete feasible child and replace \(\widehat S\) whenever its acquisition value is larger. Stop when the queue is empty or its largest bound is at most \(a(\widehat S)+\varepsilon\). Output \(\widehat S\), which satisfies \(a(\widehat S)\geq\max_{S\in\mathcal F}a(S)-\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch-and-bound maximizes an acquisition over feasible discrete objects and certifies the incumbent within a chosen additive tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Combinatorial Acquisition Search

children.title: Hierarchical Acquisition Domains
children.top_down_role: Acquisition search over nested or tree-structured configuration spaces.

assumptions_latex: A finite rooted tree \(T\) has internal nodes representing choices and leaves representing terminal model configurations.
Each root-to-leaf path \(p\) carries a nonempty parameter domain \(X_p\).
The acquisition \(a(p,x)\) is defined for \(p\) a leaf path and \(x\in X_p\).

notation.meaning: Set of root-to-leaf paths of the hierarchy

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disjoint-union model of a finite hierarchy with path-dependent parameter domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The hierarchical acquisition domain induced by \(T\) is \(\mathcal X_T=\bigsqcup_{p\in\mathcal P(T)}(\{p\}\times X_p)\), where \(\mathcal P(T)\) denotes the root-to-leaf paths. A point \((p,x)\) is feasible exactly when all choices along \(p\) are mutually compatible and \(x\in X_p\). Coordinates attached to branches outside \(p\) are absent, rather than assigned arbitrary values. Acquisition optimization on this domain is therefore \(\sup_{(p,x)\in\mathcal X_T}a(p,x)=\max_{p\in\mathcal P(T)}\sup_{x\in X_p}a(p,x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hierarchical acquisition domain is a disjoint union of path-specific parameter spaces, with only coordinates on the selected path active.
knowledge_statements.title: Hierarchical Acquisition Domains

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition is the correct kind for this domain leaf, and the disjoint-union representation is internally coherent. It remains an uncited modeling choice: no source establishes that this is the intended hierarchical acquisition-domain definition.

children.title: Categorical Acquisition Search

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite categorical neighborhood optimum that is not globally acquisition-optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\{c_0,c_1,c_2\}\), with \(N(c_0)=\{c_1\}\), and let \(a(c_0)=1\), \(a(c_1)=0\), and \(a(c_2)=2\). Improving-neighbor search initialized at \(c_0\) stops immediately because \(a(c_0)>a(c_1)\), although \(c_2\) is the unique global maximizer. Thus exhaustive evaluation of \(N(\widehat c)\) certifies only neighborhood optimality when the neighborhood graph does not force access to every better assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A categorical search can stop at a neighborhood optimum while an unvisited, nonneighboring category assignment has a larger acquisition value.
assumptions_latex: The categorical domain and neighborhood map are finite.
The algorithm accepts only strictly improving neighbors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a(c_0)\ge a(c)\ \forall c\in N(c_0),\qquad a(c_0)<\max_{c\in C}a(c).

notation.meaning: Declared categorical neighborhood of assignment c

knowledge_statements.title: Categorical Neighborhood Trap

assumptions_latex: The categorical domain is the finite product \(C=\prod_{j=1}^m C_j\), with every \(C_j\) finite and nonempty.
The acquisition function \(a:C\to\mathbb R\) is evaluable at every categorical assignment.
A neighborhood map \(N:C\to 2^C\) is fixed, typically using one-coordinate category changes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a(\widehat c)\geq a(c)\) for every \(c\in N(\widehat c)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite neighborhood search with a local-optimality stopping certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(c_0\in C\). At iteration \(k\), evaluate \(a\) on every unevaluated point in \(N(c_k)\). If some neighbor has strictly larger acquisition, choose \(c_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{c\in N(c_k)}a(c)\); otherwise stop and output \(\widehat c=c_k\). Because \(C\) is finite and acquisition values increase strictly after every accepted move, the procedure terminates after finitely many moves. Its output satisfies \(a(\widehat c)\geq a(c)\) for every \(c\in N(\widehat c)\). Global optimality requires exhaustive coverage or an additional valid bounding mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly take an improving categorical neighbor; finite termination certifies neighborhood optimality, while global optimality needs enumeration or bounds.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the current posterior information, form the joint acquisition \(A_q(x_1,\ldots,x_q)\), including all dependence among the proposed evaluations. children.top_down_role: Greedy, conditional, believer, and penalization-based batch constructions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential construction using a fixed pseudo-response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\ell\). Starting with \(D_0=D\), recursively select \(x_j\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in X_j}a(x;D_{j-1})\) and set \(D_j=D_{j-1}\cup\{(x_j,\ell)\}\). Optimistic, pessimistic, and neutral choices of \(\ell\) are distinct policy variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constant liar repeatedly inserts the same artificial outcome while constructing a batch.
assumptions_latex: Pseudo-updating with \(\ell\) is well defined.
Each argmax is nonempty or explicitly approximated.
knowledge_statements.title: Constant-Liar Batch Construction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential construction using posterior-mean pseudo-observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from \(D_0=D\), for \(j=1,\ldots,q\), select \(x_j\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in X_j}a(x;D_{j-1})\), set \(\tilde y_j=\mathbb E[Y(x_j)\mid D_{j-1}]\), and update \(D_j=D_{j-1}\cup\{(x_j,\tilde y_j)\}\). Return \((x_1,\ldots,x_q)\) and discard pseudo-responses before assimilating actual outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Kriging believer temporarily treats selected batch points as observed at their posterior means.
assumptions_latex: Posterior means and acquisitions are defined after every pseudo-update.
Each argmax is nonempty or an explicit approximate maximizer is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_q=(x_1,\ldots,x_q)\text{ is constructed without new objective responses}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Kriging-Believer Batch Construction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Greedy Construction Has No General Joint Guarantee
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure without submodular structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M>0\), let \(F(\{a\})=1\), \(F(\{b\})=F(\{c\})=0\), \(F(\{a,b\})=F(\{a,c\})=1\), and \(F(\{b,c\})=M\). With batch size two, greedy first selects \(a\) and obtains value \(1\), whereas the optimal batch has value \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without submodularity-like structure, greedy batch construction can have an arbitrarily small approximation ratio.
assumptions_latex: The candidate set is \(\{a,b,c\}\) and batch size is two.
knowledge_statements.title: Greedy Construction Has No General Joint Guarantee

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Greedy Approximation for Monotone Submodular Batch Utility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Guarantee for exact marginal-gain batch construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:2^V\to\mathbb R_+\) be normalized, monotone, and submodular on finite \(V\). If \(S_0=\varnothing\) and each \(x_j\) maximizes \(F(S_{j-1}\cup\{x\})-F(S_{j-1})\) over \(V\setminus S_{j-1}\), then \(F(S_q)\ge[1-(1-1/q)^q]\max_{|S|\le q}F(S)\ge(1-e^{-1})\max_{|S|\le q}F(S)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact greedy marginal gains attain the standard one-minus-one-over-e guarantee for normalized monotone submodular batch utility.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite.
\(F\) is normalized, nonnegative, monotone, and submodular.
Every marginal-gain maximization is exact.
knowledge_statements.title: Greedy Approximation for Monotone Submodular Batch Utility

assumptions_latex: The design domain \(X\) is nonempty and the requested batch size is \(q\in\mathbb N\).
A one-step acquisition \(a(x\mid D,P)\) is available given observed data \(D\) and pending set \(P\).
A deterministic update rule \(G(P,x)\) represents conditioning, belief imputation, or local penalization after selecting \(x\).

notation.meaning: Temporary pending state after selecting batch elements

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy batch construction through deterministic temporary-state updates between selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(P_0=\varnothing\). For \(j=1,\ldots,q\), define the currently feasible set \(X_j\subseteq X\), choose \(x_j\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in X_j}a(x\mid D,P_{j-1})\), and update \(P_j=G(P_{j-1},x_j)\). The rule \(G\) may condition on the location alone, append a deterministic believed response, or penalize neighborhoods of previous selections. Stop after \(q\) choices and output \(B_q=(x_1,\ldots,x_q)\). No objective response from the new batch is required during construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build a batch greedily, updating a temporary pending-state model after each selected point without waiting for new observations.
knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Batch Construction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind is appropriate for sequential batch construction, and all symbols used in the selection recursion are introduced. A source is needed because the single update map is asserted to cover materially different constructions such as conditioning, believer imputation, and local penalization without specifying their distinct semantics.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential diversification without pseudo-responses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(a_0=a\). After selecting \(x_j\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x
e X_j}a_{j-1}(x)\), set \(a_j(x)=a(x)\prod_{i=1}^j\phi_i(x;x_i)\), where \(0\le\phi_i\le1\) downweights a declared neighborhood of \(x_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local penalization suppresses acquisition values near earlier batch members.
assumptions_latex: The base acquisition is nonnegative, or signed values are handled by a declared convention.
Each penalizer takes values in \([0,1]\).

notation.meaning: Local downweighting factor induced by selected point i.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Penalization Batch Construction

intermediate_metadata.reason: The complete local inventory comprises posterior-mean believer, constant-liar, and exact marginal-gain greedy constructions, together with the submodular approximation guarantee and arbitrary-gap failure family. The proposed local-penalization record is deferred because its displayed selection domain is malformed; that variant is not needed for core completeness. Joint optimization and real pending-feedback policies were excluded as sibling scopes.

children.title: Pending-Feedback Policy Family
children.top_down_role: Policy computation with incomplete evaluations and heterogeneous worker availability.

children.title: Asynchronous Acquisition Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies issuing new proposals whenever evaluation capacity becomes available.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ignoring Pending Eligibility Can Duplicate Dispatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure when a forbidden pending point remains eligible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(x^\star\) uniquely maximizes the completed-data acquisition, an evaluation at \(x^\star\) is pending, concurrent duplication is forbidden, and the dispatch rule neither removes pending locations nor changes its acquisition. The rule proposes the infeasible duplicate \(x^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ignoring pending eligibility can make an asynchronous policy propose a forbidden duplicate.
assumptions_latex: \(x^\star\) uniquely maximizes the completed-data acquisition.
\(x^\star\) is pending and concurrent duplication is forbidden.
knowledge_statements.title: Ignoring Pending Eligibility Can Duplicate Dispatch

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formal definition of asynchronous acquisition dispatch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F_t\) contain the completed observations, pending assignments, worker states, and declared exogenous information available at event time \(t\). An asynchronous acquisition policy takes an \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable dispatch action at each worker-availability stopping time; it cannot use unfinished responses or future events except through their conditional laws given \(\mathcal F_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An asynchronous policy dispatches at availability events using only currently available information.
assumptions_latex: Worker-availability times are stopping times for \((\mathcal F_t)\).
The feasible-action correspondence is measurable from the current state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_t\text{ is }\mathcal F_t\text{-measurable at each dispatch event }t\).

notation.meaning: Information available at event time t.
Dispatch action at event time t.

knowledge_statements.title: Event-Driven Nonanticipative Dispatch Policy

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absence of synchronization-induced idling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An asynchronous policy is work conserving when it dispatches whenever an eligible worker is idle, an admissible evaluation remains, and the stopping predicate is false. Under this definition, idling can arise from infeasibility, stopping, or policy-computation latency, but not solely from waiting for unrelated pending evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A work-conserving asynchronous policy does not idle an eligible worker merely to synchronize with other evaluations.
assumptions_latex: An eligible worker is idle.
A dispatch-feasible evaluation exists.
The stopping predicate is false.
knowledge_statements.title: Work-Conserving Asynchronous Dispatch

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work-conserving asynchronous dispatch with an additive inner-optimization tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At each worker-availability event \(t\), assimilate all newly completed observations into \(D_t\), update the pending set \(P_t\), and form the dispatch-feasible set \(X_t\). If stopping is false and \(X_t\ne\varnothing\), choose \(x_t\in X_t\) such that \[a_t(x_t\mid D_t,P_t)\ge\sup_{x\in X_t}a_t(x\mid D_t,P_t)-\varepsilon_t,\qquad \varepsilon_t\ge0,\] dispatch it immediately, and add its assignment to \(P_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Whenever capacity becomes available, update completed and pending state and immediately dispatch a feasible approximate acquisition maximizer.
assumptions_latex: The state and feasible-action correspondence are measurable at each availability event.
The pending-aware acquisition has a finite supremum on \(X_t\).
A feasible \(\varepsilon_t\)-maximizer with \(\varepsilon_t\ge0\) can be produced.

notation.meaning: Completed observations available at event t.

knowledge_statements.title: Event-Driven Approximate Acquisition Dispatch

assumptions_latex: At decision time \(t\), observed data are \(D_t\), pending evaluations are \(P_t\), and at least one worker is idle.
A pending-aware acquisition \(a_t(x\mid D_t,P_t)\) is defined on the dispatch-feasible set \(X_t\).
Dispatching a point adds it to \(P_t\), while completion moves its realized response into \(D_t\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Event-driven dispatch using completed and pending evaluations without synchronizing workers into batches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Whenever a worker becomes idle, assimilate every newly completed pair into \(D_t\), remove those evaluations from \(P_t\), and form \(a_t(\cdot\mid D_t,P_t)\). Choose \(x_t\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in X_t}a_t(x\mid D_t,P_t)\), dispatch \(x_t\), and immediately replace \(P_t\) by \(P_t\cup\{x_t\}\). Decisions occur at worker-availability events and do not wait for other pending evaluations. The policy terminates when the evaluation budget, time budget, or prescribed stopping predicate is met, returning the best completed feasible observation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each worker-availability event, update completed and pending sets, maximize a pending-aware acquisition, and dispatch immediately.
knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Acquisition Policies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the asynchronous-policy leaf and the event-driven description matches the title. No source supports the pending-aware dispatch policy, and the assumptions do not ensure that the displayed acquisition argmax exists.

children.title: Pending-Evaluation Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Acquisition computation that accounts for locations with unresolved outcomes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Plug-In Pending Outcomes Need Not Equal Marginalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of deterministic posterior-mean substitution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Y\in\{-1,1\}\) with equal conditional probabilities and \(g(y)=y^2\), then \(\mathbb E[g(Y)\mid D,P]=1\), whereas \(g(\mathbb E[Y\mid D,P])=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Substituting a posterior-mean pending response need not equal averaging over pending uncertainty.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb P(Y=-1\mid D,P)=\mathbb P(Y=1\mid D,P)=1/2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Plug-In Pending Outcomes Need Not Equal Marginalization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dependence Must Be Preserved Across Pending Outcomes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint-law requirement for several unresolved evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_P=(Y_{p_1},\ldots,Y_{p_m})\). Replacing \(\mathcal L(Y_P\mid D,P)\) by the product of its conditional marginals gives the same integral for every bounded measurable integrand \(g\) if and only if \(Y_{p_1},\ldots,Y_{p_m}\) are conditionally independent given \((D,P)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pending responses must be integrated jointly unless conditional independence justifies multiplying their marginal laws.
assumptions_latex: The pending-response vector has a conditional law given \((D,P)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\int g\,d\mathcal L(Y_P\mid D,P)=\int g(y)\prod_i d\mathcal L(Y_{p_i}\mid D,P)(y_i)\ \forall g\Longleftrightarrow Y_{p_i}\text{ are conditionally independent}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Dependence Must Be Preserved Across Pending Outcomes

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Continuity and Attainment After Pending Marginalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularity inherited by a properly defined pending-conditioned acquisition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be compact. If, for almost every pending outcome \(Y_P\), the map \(x\mapsto g(x,Y_P)\) is continuous and \(|g(x,Y_P)|\le M(Y_P)\) for every \(x\), where \(\mathbb E[M(Y_P)\mid D,P]<\infty\), then \(x\mapsto\mathbb E[g(x,Y_P)\mid D,P]\) is continuous and attains its maximum on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dominated samplewise continuity makes a pending-marginalized acquisition continuous and ensures attainment on a compact domain.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is compact.
\(g(\cdot,Y_P)\) is continuous almost surely.
An integrable envelope \(M(Y_P)\) dominates \(|g(x,Y_P)|\) uniformly in \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\mapsto\mathbb E[g(x,Y_P)\mid D,P]\text{ is continuous and }\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in X}\mathbb E[g(x,Y_P)\mid D,P]\ne\varnothing.

notation.meaning: Completed-data acquisition under a pending outcome.

knowledge_statements.title: Continuity and Attainment After Pending Marginalization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exactness of Mean Pending-Outcome Substitution for Affine Integrands
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limited case in which deterministic posterior-mean substitution agrees with pending-outcome marginalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_P\) be conditionally integrable given \((D,P)\), and suppose \(g(x,y)=a(x)+b(x)^{\top}y\). Then \[\mathbb E[g(x,Y_P)\mid D,P]=g\!\left(x,\mathbb E[Y_P\mid D,P]\right).\] Thus posterior-mean substitution is exact for affine dependence on pending outcomes but need not be exact for nonlinear dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Posterior-mean substitution is exact when the completed-data acquisition is affine in the pending outcomes, but not generally.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb E[\lVert Y_P\rVert\mid D,P]<\infty\).

notation.meaning: Completed-data acquisition at candidate x for pending outcome y.

knowledge_statements.title: Exactness of Mean Pending-Outcome Substitution for Affine Integrands

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tower-property decomposition when unresolved responses are partitioned into two groups.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the pending response vector as \(Y_P=(Y_A,Y_B)\). If \(g(x,Y_A,Y_B)\) is conditionally integrable and the required regular conditional laws exist, then \[\mathbb E[g(x,Y_A,Y_B)\mid D,P]=\mathbb E\!\left[\mathbb E[g(x,Y_A,Y_B)\mid D,P,Y_A]\mid D,P\right].\] Thus exact joint marginalization may be evaluated through nested conditioning without assuming conditional independence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pending outcomes may be integrated in stages by the tower property, provided their conditional dependence is retained.
assumptions_latex: \(Y_P=(Y_A,Y_B)\) admits the stated regular conditional distributions.
\(\mathbb E[|g(x,Y_A,Y_B)|\mid D,P]<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E[g\mid D,P]=\mathbb E[\mathbb E[g\mid D,P,Y_A]\mid D,P].
knowledge_statements.title: Iterated Marginalization of Pending Outcomes

assumptions_latex: Conditional on observed data \(D\), the surrogate induces a joint posterior law for \(f(x)\) and pending values \(Y_P\).
The pending locations form a finite tuple \(P=(p_1,\ldots,p_m)\).
For each realized pending vector \(y\), the completed-data acquisition is \(a(x;D\cup\{(P,y)\})\) and is integrable.

notation.meaning: Posterior random vector of pending responses

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact marginalization of an acquisition over unobserved responses at pending locations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The pending-conditioned acquisition at a candidate \(x\) is \(a_P(x)=\mathbb E[a(x;D\cup\{(P,Y_P)\})\mid D,P]\), where the expectation uses the joint posterior predictive law of \(Y_P\). Equivalently, when this law has density \(p(y\mid D,P)\), \(a_P(x)=\int a(x;D\cup\{(P,y)\})p(y\mid D,P)\,dy\). This construction averages the completed-data decision rule over all posterior-compatible pending outcomes; replacing \(Y_P\) by a single deterministic value is an approximation, not exact conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Average the completed-data acquisition over the joint posterior distribution of all unfinished responses at their pending locations.
knowledge_statements.title: Pending-Evaluation Conditioning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is an appropriate kind for this leaf, and the expectation and density forms are consistent when the stated integrability and density conditions hold. A source is essential because identifying this fantasy-outcome marginalization with exact pending-evaluation conditioning depends on the precise acquisition and posterior construction.

children.title: Heterogeneous-Worker Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Proposal policies for workers with differing speeds or capabilities.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conflict-free assignment when several heterogeneous workers are available.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite idle workers \(W_0\), finite candidate sets \(C_w\), and declared assignment scores \(s_{w,x}\), maximize \(\sum_{w,x}s_{w,x}z_{w,x}\) over binary \(z\), subject to \(\sum_{x\in C_w}z_{w,x}\le1\) for each worker and, when concurrent duplication is forbidden, \(\sum_{w:x\in C_w}z_{w,x}\le1\) for each design. Dispatch exactly the assignments with \(z_{w,x}=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assign several idle workers jointly while enforcing worker capability and nonduplication constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(W_0\) and each \(C_w\) are finite.
Assignment scores and capability constraints are fixed for the dispatch event.

notation.meaning: Indicator that design x is assigned to worker w.

knowledge_statements.title: Simultaneous Assignment of Idle Workers

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible action space for heterogeneous workers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For idle workers \(W\), worker-specific domains \(X_w\subseteq X\), and currently eligible designs \(U\subseteq X\), the feasible single-dispatch set is \(\mathcal F=\{(w,x):w\in W,\ x\in X_w\cap U\}\). Worker identity is decision relevant when capability, runtime, cost, fidelity, or observation law depends on \(w\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A heterogeneous scheduler selects a worker–design pair satisfying worker-specific capability and current eligibility.
assumptions_latex: \(W\) is the current set of idle workers.
Each \(X_w\) is the capability domain of worker \(w\).
knowledge_statements.title: Capability-Constrained Worker–Design Assignments

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Runtime Error Can Reverse Rate Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for utility-per-predicted-time scores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For assignments with utilities \(u_i>0\), predicted times \(\widehat T_i>0\), and true expected times \(T_i>0\), if \(u_1/\widehat T_1\ge u_2/\widehat T_2\) but \(u_1/T_1<u_2/T_2\), then predicted-time and true utility-rate rankings disagree. Guarantees based on true completion times therefore require a runtime-model error condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Misspecified runtimes can reverse a utility-per-time scheduling choice.
assumptions_latex: \(u_i,T_i,\widehat T_i>0\) for \(i=1,2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Runtime Error Can Reverse Rate Scheduling

assumptions_latex: Idle worker \(w\) has capability-feasible domain \(X_w\) and predictive completion time \(T_w(x)>0\) for \(x\in X_w\).
A pending-aware utility \(a(x\mid D,P)\geq0\) is available.
A positive scheduling score \(s_w(x)\) specifies the chosen utility-cost tradeoff.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint worker-design dispatch using capability constraints and predicted evaluation costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a dispatch event, form the feasible pair set \(\mathcal F=\{(w,x):w\in W_{\mathrm{idle}},\ x\in X_w\}\). For example, a rate-based policy uses \(s_w(x)=a(x\mid D,P)/T_w(x)\), while another declared score may encode deadlines or worker reliability. Select \((w^\star,x^\star)\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{(w,x)\in\mathcal F}s_w(x)\), dispatch \(x^\star\) to \(w^\star\), and add the assignment to the pending state. Repeat at completion or worker-arrival events until the stopping predicate holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a feasible worker-design pair by optimizing a declared score that balances pending-aware utility against worker-specific cost or capability.
knowledge_statements.title: Heterogeneous-Worker Scheduling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits worker scheduling, but the proposed score is a declared policy rather than a general heterogeneous-worker Bayesian-optimization rule. No source is supplied, the idle-worker set is not assumed nonempty, and positivity of the score does not ensure that the joint argmax is attained.

children.title: Stale-Decision Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Decision degradation caused by delayed results or outdated surrogate states.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hard failure boundary for stale dispatch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Even when \(a(\cdot;S_1)=a(\cdot;S_0)\), a proposal \(x_0\) is not dispatchable if \(x_0\notin X(S_1)\). Thus acquisition-value stability cannot replace current feasibility validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unchanged acquisition cannot make a newly infeasible stale proposal dispatchable.
assumptions_latex: \(x_0\in X(S_0)\) but \(x_0\notin X(S_1)\).
The acquisition is unchanged between states.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_0\notin X(S_1)\Rightarrow x_0\text{ is not dispatchable at }S_1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Changed Feasibility Overrides Value Stability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-based definition of an obsolete asynchronous proposal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v(S)\) increase whenever decision-relevant completed data, pending assignments, worker state, or feasibility information changes. A proposal computed from \(S_0\) is stale at dispatch state \(S_1\) when \(v(S_1)>v(S_0)\). Staleness alone does not imply infeasibility or current-state suboptimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proposal is stale when the decision state has advanced since it was computed.
assumptions_latex: State versions increase on every decision-relevant state change.
knowledge_statements.title: Stale Proposal and State Version

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Acquisition Drift Bounds Stale-Decision Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic stability bound for an old exact maximizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\ne\varnothing\) be the common feasible set, let \(x_0\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in X}a(x;S_0)\), and suppose \(\sup_{x\in X}|a(x;S_1)-a(x;S_0)|\le\varepsilon\). Then \(\sup_{x\in X}a(x;S_1)-a(x_0;S_1)\le2\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform acquisition drift of at most epsilon makes an old exact maximizer two-epsilon optimal under the new state.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set is nonempty and unchanged.
\(x_0\) maximizes the old-state acquisition.
Uniform acquisition drift is at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Acquisition Drift Bounds Stale-Decision Loss

assumptions_latex: A decision computed from snapshot state \(S_0=(D_0,P_0)\) proposes \(x_0\).
Before dispatch, the current state becomes \(S_1=(D_1,P_1)\), with acquisition \(a(\cdot;S_1)\).
A tolerance \(\delta\geq0\) and current feasible set \(X_1\) are prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_0\) is dispatchable only if \(x_0\in X_1\) and \(\sup_{x\in X_1}a(x;S_1)-a(x_0;S_1)\leq\delta\).

notation.meaning: State used to compute the proposed decision
Permitted acquisition loss caused by staleness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive acquisition-loss boundary for accepting a decision computed from an obsolete asynchronous state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the staleness loss of the precomputed proposal by \(L(x_0;S_1)=\sup_{x\in X_1}a(x;S_1)-a(x_0;S_1)\). The proposal is admissible for dispatch exactly when \(x_0\in X_1\) and \(L(x_0;S_1)\leq\delta\). If feasibility has changed or the loss exceeds \(\delta\), discard the proposal and recompute from \(S_1\). Thus the acceptance boundary certifies that dispatching the stale proposal sacrifices at most \(\delta\) acquisition units relative to a current-state maximizer; it does not by itself bound objective regret.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dispatch a stale proposal only when it remains feasible and its current acquisition loss is at most the declared tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Stale-Decision Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is the correct role for an acceptance boundary, and the statement properly distinguishes acquisition loss from objective regret. Nevertheless, this is an uncited, policy-defined safeguard rather than a universal stale-decision result; the assumptions also do not ensure that the current-state supremum is finite.

children.title: Guarantee Foundation Regime Pair
children.top_down_role: Representational and probabilistic foundations used to state Bayesian and worst-case guarantees.

children.title: Bayesian Sample-Path Regime
children.top_down_role: Prior-based analysis with the objective modeled as a Gaussian-process realization.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Infinite-Rank Gaussian Draws Lie Outside the Covariance RKHS
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating Bayesian Gaussian-process sample-path analysis from deterministic bounded-RKHS analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be a centered Gaussian random element admitting a Karhunen–Loève expansion \(f=\sum_{j\ge1}\sqrt{\lambda_j}Z_j e_j\), with infinitely many \(\lambda_j>0\), independent \(Z_j\sim N(0,1)\), and covariance Cameron–Martin space \(\mathcal H_k\). Then \[\Pr\{f\in\mathcal H_k\}=0.\] Consequently, an infinite-rank Bayesian GP sample-path guarantee cannot generally be reinterpreted as a guarantee uniform over a bounded ball of the covariance RKHS.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infinite-rank Gaussian-process draw lies outside its covariance RKHS almost surely, so Bayesian sample-path and bounded-RKHS regimes are not interchangeable.
assumptions_latex: The Gaussian process is realized as a Gaussian random element in a space for which the stated Karhunen–Loève expansion and Cameron–Martin space are defined.
The covariance operator has infinitely many strictly positive eigenvalues.
The coefficients \(Z_j\) are independent standard normal variables.

notation.meaning: Cameron–Martin space associated with the covariance kernel.

knowledge_statements.title: Infinite-Rank Gaussian Draws Lie Outside the Covariance RKHS

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) is a nonempty compact metric space.
\(f\sim\operatorname{GP}(m,k)\), and observations satisfy \(Y_t=f(X_t)+\varepsilon_t\) under the stated noise model.
Each \(X_t\) is measurable with respect to the history before \(Y_t\) is observed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Performance statements are interpreted under the joint law of the Gaussian-process sample path, observation noise, and any algorithmic randomization.

notation.meaning: Gaussian-process prior on the unknown objective
probability and expectation under the Bayesian joint model

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard Bayesian optimization sample-path formulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bayesian rather than RKHS worst-case interpretation of optimization guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Bayesian sample-path regime holds when the unknown objective is itself random with \(f\sim\operatorname{GP}(m,k)\), the sequential design satisfies \(X_t\in\mathcal X\) and \(X_t\) is \(\mathcal D_{t-1}\)-measurable, and observations obey \(Y_t=f(X_t)+\varepsilon_t\). Conditional predictions are computed from the posterior law \(\mathcal L(f\mid\mathcal D_t)\). A guarantee is Bayesian when its probability or expectation is taken over \(f\), the noise sequence, and algorithmic randomization; it may therefore hold for prior-almost-every sample path without holding uniformly over a deterministic function class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The objective is a Gaussian-process realization, and guarantees average or quantify probability over the prior, noise, and algorithmic randomness.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the Bayesian sample-path regime and is mathematically plausible, but no inspectable Bayesian-optimization source supports the stated joint-law and sample-path interpretation.

children.title: Kernel-Space Worst-Case Regime
children.top_down_role: Frequentist analysis over reproducing-kernel function classes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Pointwise Envelope of an RKHS Ball
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic evaluation and uniform-value bounds supplied by bounded RKHS norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(f\in\mathcal H_k\) and \(x\in\mathcal X\), \[f(x)=\langle f,k(x,\cdot)\rangle_{\mathcal H_k},\qquad |f(x)|\le \|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\sqrt{k(x,x)}.\] Therefore, if \(\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le B\) and \(\sup_x k(x,x)\le\kappa^2<\infty\), then \[\sup_x|f(x)|\le B\kappa.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded RKHS norm gives pointwise objective bounds, and a bounded kernel diagonal makes the bound uniform over the domain.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in\mathcal H_k\) and \(\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le B\).
For the uniform conclusion, \(\sup_x k(x,x)\le\kappa^2<\infty\).

notation.meaning: Kernel representer of evaluation at x.
Uniform upper bound on the square root of the kernel diagonal.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Pointwise Envelope of an RKHS Ball

assumptions_latex: \(k\) is a positive-definite kernel on \(\mathcal X\) with reproducing-kernel Hilbert space \(\mathcal H_k\).
The unknown objective is deterministic and satisfies \(\lVert f\rVert_{\mathcal H_k}\le B\).
Observation noise satisfies the specified frequentist tail condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting probability statements are uniform over the RKHS ball and take probability only over noise and algorithmic randomization.

notation.meaning: reproducing-kernel Hilbert space generated by k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard frequentist RKHS regime for Gaussian-process bandit analysis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic RKHS-ball formulation; no GP sample-path assumption is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The kernel-space worst-case regime fixes an unknown deterministic objective \(f\in\mathcal F_B:=\{g\in\mathcal H_k:\lVert g\rVert_{\mathcal H_k}\le B\}\). Sequential locations may depend measurably on past observations, but probability is taken only over observation noise and algorithmic randomization. Thus a confidence or regret assertion \(E_f\) at level \(1-\delta\) is uniform when \(\inf_{f\in\mathcal F_B}\mathbb P_f(E_f)\ge 1-\delta\). Membership in \(\mathcal F_B\), rather than positive prior probability under a Gaussian process, supplies the regularity assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The objective is an arbitrary deterministic member of a bounded RKHS ball, and guarantees hold uniformly over that class.
knowledge_statements.title: Kernel-Space Worst-Case Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition correctly distinguishes a deterministic RKHS-ball regime from a GP prior, but the uniform frequentist formulation has no cited source or locator.

children.title: Uniform Confidence Certificates
children.top_down_role: High-probability uncertainty-control families supporting optimistic search.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic consequence of a valid simultaneous band under exact upper-confidence maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If L_{t-1}(x)\le f(x)\le U_{t-1}(x) for all x\in\mathcal X, x^*\in\arg\max_x f(x), and x_t\in\arg\max_xU_{t-1}(x), then f(x^*)-f(x_t)\le U_{t-1}(x_t)-L_{t-1}(x_t). For U_{t-1}=\mu_{t-1}+\sqrt{\beta_t}\sigma_{t-1} and L_{t-1}=\mu_{t-1}-\sqrt{\beta_t}\sigma_{t-1}, this gives f(x^*)-f(x_t)\le2\sqrt{\beta_t}\sigma_{t-1}(x_t).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the simultaneous confidence event, exact upper-confidence search has instantaneous regret no greater than the selected point's confidence width.
assumptions_latex: L_{t-1}(x)\le f(x)\le U_{t-1}(x) for every x\in\mathcal X.
x_t globally maximizes U_{t-1}.
A global maximizer x^* exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Confidence-Width Instantaneous-Regret Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Coverage Does Not Imply Uniform Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating marginal confidence intervals from a simultaneous certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assertions \mathbb P(f(x)\in C_t(x))\ge1-\delta for each fixed (t,x) do not imply \mathbb P(\forall(t,x):f(x)\in C_t(x))\ge1-\delta. For m independent coverage events, each of probability 1-\delta, the intersection probability is (1-\delta)^m<1-\delta when m>1.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intervals valid separately at each point and time need not form one band valid everywhere and at every time.
assumptions_latex: At least two marginal coverage events are considered.
No simultaneous calibration or dependence argument is available.

notation.meaning: Confidence interval at point x and round t.

knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Coverage Does Not Imply Uniform Coverage

assumptions_latex: For every round \(t\), \(\mu_{t-1}\) and \(\sigma_{t-1}\) are the surrogate posterior mean and standard deviation.
A sequence \((\beta_t)_{t\ge1}\) and failure probability \(\delta\in(0,1)\) are fixed.
The probability law matches either the declared Bayesian or frequentist foundation regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On an event of probability at least \(1-\delta\), every round and every candidate point obey the displayed confidence inequalities simultaneously.

notation.meaning: lower and upper confidence functions at round t
surrogate posterior mean and standard deviation after t observations

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical simultaneous confidence-band certificate used by optimistic Bayesian optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract simultaneous band; calibration of \(\beta_t\) depends on the selected foundation regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(L_{t-1}(x)=\mu_{t-1}(x)-\sqrt{\beta_t}\,\sigma_{t-1}(x)\) and \(U_{t-1}(x)=\mu_{t-1}(x)+\sqrt{\beta_t}\,\sigma_{t-1}(x)\). These functions form a uniform confidence certificate at level \(1-\delta\) when
\[\mathbb P\!\left(\forall t\ge1,\ \forall x\in\mathcal X:\ L_{t-1}(x)\le f(x)\le U_{t-1}(x)\right)\ge1-\delta.\]
On this event, maximizing \(U_{t-1}\) is optimistic, and the pointwise uncertainty width is \(U_{t-1}(x)-L_{t-1}(x)=2\sqrt{\beta_t}\,\sigma_{t-1}(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single high-probability event simultaneously traps the objective between surrogate lower and upper bounds at every point and round.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Confidence Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind and simultaneous-band formulation fit the container, but a source is required to substantiate when a sequence beta_t yields the claimed all-round, all-point coverage in each foundation regime.

children.title: Optimization Performance Criteria
children.top_down_role: Distinct notions of optimization quality and consistency.

children.title: Final-Recommendation Error Criteria
children.top_down_role: Finite-budget quality of the reported solution.

children.title: Simple Regret
children.top_down_role: Finite-budget objective loss associated with the selected solution.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relation between terminal simple regret and regrets incurred at evaluated points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r_t:=f^*-f(X_t)\) and \(R_T:=\sum_{t=1}^T r_t\). If the terminal recommendation is a latent best evaluated point,
\[f(\widehat x_T)=\max_{1\le t\le T}f(X_t),\]
then
\[r_T^{\mathrm s}=\min_{1\le t\le T}r_t\le \frac{R_T}{T}\le R_T.\]
Consequently, \(R_T=o(T)\) implies \(r_T^{\mathrm s}\to0\) for this recommendation rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a latent best-evaluated recommendation, simple regret is the smallest query regret and is at most average cumulative regret.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) attains \(f^*\).
The recommendation has the largest latent objective value among \(X_1,\ldots,X_T\).
knowledge_statements.title: Best-Evaluated Recommendation Bound

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) attains its maximum \(f^*=\max_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)\).
After \(T\) evaluations, the algorithm outputs a recommendation \(\widehat x_T\in\mathcal X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The simple regret is nonnegative and equals zero exactly when the recommendation is globally optimal in objective value.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard maximization-form simple regret definition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximization convention with regret evaluated at the final recommendation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a maximization problem with \(f^*:=\max_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)\), the simple regret of the recommendation \(\widehat x_T\) after \(T\) evaluations is
\[r_T^{\mathrm s}:=f^*-f(\widehat x_T).\]
It measures only the quality of the final recommendation and does not charge for objective losses incurred at intermediate evaluation points. Consequently, \(r_T^{\mathrm s}\ge0\), and \(r_T^{\mathrm s}=0\) if and only if \(\widehat x_T\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simple regret is the gap between the global optimum value and the value at the algorithm's final recommendation.
knowledge_statements.title: Simple Regret

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a precise maximization-form definition of simple regret, but the record supplies no citation or inspectable locator.

children.title: Recommendation Error
children.top_down_role: Finite-budget discrepancy attributable to the reported recommendation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vanishing Value Error Need Not Localize on a Noncompact Domain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of simple-regret-to-location convergence without compactness or a suitable error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On \(\mathcal X=\mathbb R\), define
\[f(x):=-\frac{x^2}{1+x^4}.\]
Then \(X^*=\{0\}\) and \(f^*=0\). For \(x_n=n\),
\[f^*-f(x_n)=\frac{n^2}{1+n^4}\to0,\qquad d(x_n,X^*)=n\to\infty.\]
Hence arbitrarily small simple regret need not imply small recommendation error on a noncompact domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sequence can escape to infinity while its objective values approach the optimum, so value convergence alone need not localize recommendations.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X=\mathbb R\) with its usual metric.
knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Value Error Need Not Localize on a Noncompact Domain

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quantitative Conversion Between Value and Recommendation Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Error-bound and Lipschitz conversions between objective-value and localization errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Write \(r(x):=f^*-f(x)\) and \(e(x):=d(x,X^*)\). If, on a declared region, an error bound
\[r(x)\ge c\,e(x)^p\]
holds with \(c>0\) and \(p>0\), then
\[e(x)\le \bigl(r(x)/c\bigr)^{1/p}.\]
Conversely, if \(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz and \(X^*\ne\varnothing\), then
\[r(x)\le L e(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A growth condition converts simple regret into a distance bound, while Lipschitz continuity converts distance to the optimizer set into a value-gap bound.
assumptions_latex: \(X^*\ne\varnothing\).
For the first implication, \(f^*-f(x)\ge c\,d(x,X^*)^p\) with \(c,p>0\).
For the converse implication, \(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: e(x)\le(r(x)/c)^{1/p}\quad\text{and, under Lipschitz continuity,}\quad r(x)\le Le(x).

notation.meaning: objective-value or simple-regret error at x
distance from x to the optimizer set

knowledge_statements.title: Quantitative Conversion Between Value and Recommendation Error

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compact Equivalence of Value and Localization Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualitative equivalence between simple-regret convergence and optimizer-set localization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\mathcal X,d)\) be compact, let \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) be continuous, and let \(X^*:=\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)\). For every sequence \((x_n)\subset\mathcal X\),
\[f^*-f(x_n)\to0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad d(x_n,X^*)\to0.\]
Thus, under compactness and continuity, vanishing simple regret and vanishing recommendation error are equivalent even without a quantitative error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact domain with a continuous objective, objective values approach the optimum exactly when recommendations approach the optimizer set.
assumptions_latex: \((\mathcal X,d)\) is compact.
\(f\) is continuous on \(\mathcal X\).
\(X^*=\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: distance from x to the maximizer set

knowledge_statements.title: Compact Equivalence of Value and Localization Convergence

assumptions_latex: \((\mathcal X,d)\) is a metric space.
The optimizer set \(X^*:=\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)\) is nonempty.
The algorithm returns \(\widehat x_T\in\mathcal X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recommendation error vanishes exactly when the recommendation belongs to the optimizer set, provided the set is closed.

notation.meaning: distance from the recommendation to the optimizer set

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: parameter-space recommendation error distinguished from value-based simple regret
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision-space error, distinguished from the objective-value gap called simple regret.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X^*:=\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)\neq\varnothing\). The recommendation error after \(T\) evaluations is the distance from the reported decision to the optimizer set,
\[e_T:=d(\widehat x_T,X^*)=\inf_{x^*\in X^*}d(\widehat x_T,x^*).\]
This criterion measures localization rather than objective-value loss. If \(X^*\) is closed, then \(e_T=0\) if and only if \(\widehat x_T\in X^*\). Without an error bound connecting distance and objective gap, convergence of simple regret need not imply convergence of \(e_T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recommendation error measures how far the reported decision lies from the set of global optimizers, rather than its objective-value gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Recommendation Error

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The decision-space distance is well defined and distinct from simple regret, but the use of “recommendation error” for this quantity and the convergence comparison require a targeted source.

children.title: Incumbent Recommendation Rules
children.top_down_role: Alternative conventions for selecting the final reported solution from search evidence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Noisy Observed-Value Incumbent Can Select an Inferior Decision
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the largest-observation incumbent rule under additive noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let two evaluated decisions satisfy \(f(a)=1\) and \(f(b)=0\), with observations \(Y_a=f(a)+\varepsilon_a\) and \(Y_b=f(b)+\varepsilon_b\). Whenever \(\varepsilon_b-\varepsilon_a>1\), one has \(Y_b>Y_a\), so the observed-value incumbent recommends the objectively inferior decision \(b\). Thus \(\mathbb P(Y_b>Y_a)>0\) whenever \(\mathbb P(\varepsilon_b-\varepsilon_a>1)>0\), including nondegenerate Gaussian noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximizing noisy observations can recommend an inferior evaluated point because the winning observation may reflect extreme noise.
assumptions_latex: Both \(a\) and \(b\) are evaluated once.
\(\mathbb P(\varepsilon_b-\varepsilon_a>1)>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Noisy Observed-Value Incumbent Can Select an Inferior Decision

assumptions_latex: The evaluated locations and observations are \((X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^T\).
A score \(S_T\) is defined on the evaluated locations.
A deterministic measurable tie-breaking rule is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is an evaluated location maximizing the prescribed incumbent score.

notation.meaning: set of evaluated locations through round T

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: generic incumbent selection rule covering noisy and noiseless Bayesian optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic incumbent rule; the score selects observed-value or posterior-mean incumbents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input the history \(\mathcal D_T=\{(X_i,Y_i):1\le i\le T\}\), choose an incumbent score \(S_T:\mathcal X_T\to\mathbb R\), and return
\[\widehat x_T\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X_T}S_T(x),\]
using the fixed tie-breaking rule. In noiseless optimization one may set \(S_T(X_i)=Y_i=f(X_i)\). Under noisy observations, a posterior incumbent uses \(S_T(x)=\mu_T(x)\), thereby avoiding selection solely by an extreme noise realization. The algorithm stops at the prescribed budget \(T\) and outputs only \(\widehat x_T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the evaluation budget, return the sampled point with the largest chosen score, commonly its observed value or posterior mean.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Recommendation Rules

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the recommendation-rule container, but the generic score rule and its noisy posterior-mean specialization have no supporting source or locator.

children.title: Posterior Recommendation Risk
children.top_down_role: Uncertainty-sensitive assessment of the final recommendation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact posterior-risk representation for maximization simple regret.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M(f):=\max_{u\in\mathcal X}f(u)\) and \(\mu_T(x):=\mathbb E[f(x)\mid\mathcal D_T]\). If \(M(f)\) and \(f(x)\) are posterior-integrable, then
\[\rho_T(x)=\mathbb E[M(f)\mid\mathcal D_T]-\mu_T(x).\]
Consequently,
\[\inf_x\rho_T(x)=\mathbb E[M(f)\mid\mathcal D_T]-\sup_x\mu_T(x),\qquad \rho_T(x)-\inf_u\rho_T(u)=\sup_u\mu_T(u)-\mu_T(x).\]
Whenever the relevant extrema are attained, the Bayes recommendations for posterior expected simple regret are exactly the maximizers of \(\mu_T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Posterior expected simple regret is a decision-independent expected optimum minus posterior mean, so its Bayes rule maximizes posterior mean.
assumptions_latex: \(M(f)=\max_{u\in\mathcal X}f(u)\) exists posterior-almost surely.
\(M(f)\) and \(f(x)\) are posterior-integrable for every admissible recommendation \(x\).
knowledge_statements.title: Posterior Simple-Regret Risk Decomposition
Posterior Recommendation Risk
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bayesian decision-theoretic risk conditional on the observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonnegative posterior-integrable recommendation loss \(\ell(f,x)\), define the posterior recommendation risk by
\[\rho_T(x):=\mathbb E_{f\sim\Pi_T}[\ell(f,x)]=\int \ell(g,x)\,\Pi_T(dg).\]
A Bayes recommendation satisfies \(\widehat x_T^{\mathrm B}\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x\in\mathcal X}\rho_T(x)\), when the minimum is attained, and the posterior Bayes risk is \(\rho_T^*:=\inf_{x\in\mathcal X}\rho_T(x)\). For optimization loss, a canonical choice is \(\ell(f,x)=\max_{u\in\mathcal X}f(u)-f(x)\), making \(\rho_T(x)\) posterior expected simple regret.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Posterior recommendation risk is expected recommendation loss under the posterior; a Bayes recommendation minimizes that conditional expectation.
assumptions_latex: The posterior distribution \(\Pi_T=\mathcal L(f\mid\mathcal D_T)\) is well-defined.
The loss \(\ell(f,x)\) is nonnegative and posterior-integrable.
Recommendations are measurable with respect to \(\mathcal D_T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A Bayes recommendation minimizes posterior expected loss, and its minimum value is the posterior recommendation risk.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard Bayesian decision-theoretic posterior risk applied to optimization recommendations

children.title: Sequential Regret Criteria
children.top_down_role: Sequential performance accumulated across evaluations.

children.title: Cumulative Regret
children.top_down_role: Sequential objective loss accumulated across evaluations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Latent Regret Is Not Noisy Observed-Reward Regret
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes objective regret from a noise-contaminated observed-reward expression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under observations \(Y_t=f(X_t)+\varepsilon_t\), latent cumulative regret is
\[R_T=\sum_{t=1}^T(f^*-f(X_t)).\]
The observed-reward expression satisfies
\[\widetilde R_T:=\sum_{t=1}^T(f^*-Y_t)=R_T-\sum_{t=1}^T\varepsilon_t.\]
Thus \(\widetilde R_T\) need not be nonnegative and is not pathwise equal to cumulative objective regret. Equality of expectations follows if the noises are integrable and conditionally mean-zero, \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_t\mid\mathcal H_{t-1},X_t]=0\), but need not hold without such a condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing latent objective values by noisy observations changes cumulative regret by accumulated noise and can make the resulting quantity negative.
assumptions_latex: \(Y_t=f(X_t)+\varepsilon_t\).
The policy may choose \(X_t\) adaptively from the prior history.
knowledge_statements.title: Latent Regret Is Not Noisy Observed-Reward Regret

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) attains \(f^*=\max_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)\).
The sequential policy selects \(X_t\in\mathcal X\) for \(t=1,\ldots,T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Cumulative regret is the sum of instantaneous objective gaps and equals \(T\) times their average.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard maximization-form cumulative regret definition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pathwise pseudo-regret against the best fixed decision for a stationary objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each round \(t\), define the instantaneous regret \(r_t:=f^*-f(X_t)\), where \(f^*:=\max_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)\). The cumulative regret through horizon \(T\) is
\[R_T:=\sum_{t=1}^T r_t=Tf^*-\sum_{t=1}^T f(X_t).\]
It evaluates the entire sequence of queried decisions rather than only a terminal recommendation. The average regret is \(R_T/T\); hence the sublinear-regret condition \(R_T=o(T)\) is equivalent to average regret converging to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cumulative regret sums, over all rounds, the objective-value gap between each query and a global optimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Cumulative Regret

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cumulative-regret definition and sublinear-regret equivalence are precise, but no source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Bayesian Regret
children.top_down_role: Regret assessed under prior or posterior uncertainty over objective functions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bayesian Regret as a Mixture of Frequentist Risks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disintegration of Bayes regret over fixed-objective regret assessments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Pi\) be the prior on objectives and let \(\mathbb P_f\) denote a regular conditional law of observations and policy randomization given \(f\). If \(R_T(f)\) is jointly measurable and integrable, then
\[\operatorname{BR}_T=\mathbb E[R_T(f)]=\int_{\mathcal F}\mathbb E_f[R_T(f)]\,\Pi(df).\]
Therefore, any uniform frequentist bound \(\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb E_f[R_T(f)]\le B_T\) implies \(\operatorname{BR}_T\le B_T\) for every prior supported on \(\mathcal F\). The converse need not hold because a prior average does not control every fixed objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bayesian regret is the prior mixture of fixed-objective expected regrets; uniform frequentist bounds imply Bayes bounds, but prior-average bounds need not be uniform.
assumptions_latex: \(\Pi\) is a probability law supported on \(\mathcal F\).
A regular conditional law \(\mathbb P_f\) exists.
\(R_T(f)\) is jointly measurable and integrable.

notation.meaning: expectation conditional on fixed objective f

knowledge_statements.title: Bayesian Regret as a Mixture of Frequentist Risks

assumptions_latex: The objective \(f\) has a prior distribution and attains its maximum almost surely.
The policy and observation model induce a joint law under which \(R_T\) is integrable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Bayesian regret is the joint prior expectation of cumulative regret.

notation.meaning: joint expectation over objective, noise, and policy randomization

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard Bayes-regret definition for Bayesian bandit and optimization policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Prior-averaged cumulative regret under the Bayesian sample-path regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f^*:=\max_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)\) and \(R_T(f):=\sum_{t=1}^T(f^*-f(X_t))\). The Bayesian regret of a sequential policy at horizon \(T\) is
\[\operatorname{BR}_T:=\mathbb E[R_T(f)]=\mathbb E\!\left[\sum_{t=1}^T\bigl(\max_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)-f(X_t)\bigr)\right].\]
The expectation is taken jointly over the prior on \(f\), observation noise, and policy randomization. This differs from a frequentist assessment, which fixes \(f\) before taking an expectation or probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bayesian regret averages cumulative regret jointly over the prior objective, observation noise, and any randomization in the policy.
knowledge_statements.title: Bayesian Regret

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly averages cumulative regret over the Bayesian joint law and fits the container, but it lacks an inspectable source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bayesian regret, optimal regret, and attainment boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon Bayesian regret for finite-armed bandits, including its optimization interpretation, nonnegativity, epsilon-optimality, and possible nonattainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a $k$-armed bandit environment $\nu$ with arm means $\mu_i$ and $\mu^*=\max_{i\in[k]}\mu_i$, the regret of a policy $\pi$ over $n$ rounds is
\[
R_n(\pi,\nu)=n\mu^*-\mathbb E\!\left[\sum_{t=1}^nX_t\right].
\]
For a $k$-armed Bayesian bandit environment $(\mathcal E,\mathcal G,Q,P)$, define
\[
\mathrm{BR}_n(\pi,Q)=\int_{\mathcal E}R_n(\pi,\nu)\,dQ(\nu),
\qquad
\mathrm{BR}_n^*(Q)=\inf_\pi\mathrm{BR}_n(\pi,Q).
\]
If the infimum is attained, any minimizing policy $\pi^*$ is also a maximizer of prior-averaged expected cumulative reward:
\[
\pi^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_\pi\mathrm{BR}_n(\pi,Q)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\pi^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_\pi
\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{QP\pi}}\!\left[\sum_{t=1}^nX_t\right].
\]
A minimizer need not exist in general. Nevertheless, for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists a policy $\pi$ satisfying
\[
\mathrm{BR}_n(\pi,Q)\leq\mathrm{BR}_n^*(Q)+\varepsilon.
\]
Moreover, $\mathrm{BR}_n(\pi,Q)\geq0$, and even the regret of an attained Bayes-optimal policy can be strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-horizon regret compares a policy's expected cumulative reward with the reward corresponding to the best arm mean. Bayesian regret averages this quantity over the prior, and Bayesian optimal regret is its infimum over admissible policies. When a minimizer exists, minimizing Bayesian regret is equivalent to maximizing prior-averaged expected cumulative reward. A minimizer is not guaranteed to exist, although epsilon-optimal policies exist for every positive epsilon. Bayesian regret is nonnegative, and an attained optimal policy can still have strictly positive regret.

children.title: Frequentist Regret Assessment
children.top_down_role: Regret evaluation for fixed unknown objectives across observational randomness.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case optimal frequentist assessment over a deterministic objective class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an objective class \(\mathcal F\) and a declared class \(\mathfrak P\) of admissible nonanticipating policies, define the minimax expected regret at horizon \(T\) by
\[\mathfrak R_T(\mathcal F):=\inf_{\pi\in\mathfrak P}\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb E_f^{\pi}[R_T(f)].\]
If \(\mathfrak R_T(\mathcal F)\ge L_T\), then every \(\pi\in\mathfrak P\) satisfies \(\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb E_f^{\pi}[R_T(f)]\ge L_T\); without worst-case attainment, this means that for every \(\epsilon>0\) some \(f\in\mathcal F\) has \(\mathbb E_f^{\pi}[R_T(f)]\ge L_T-\epsilon\). An upper bound follows by exhibiting an admissible policy whose worst-case expected regret is at most the claimed value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimax frequentist regret is the infimum, over admissible policies, of worst-case expected regret over a fixed objective class.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F\) is a declared deterministic objective class.
\(\mathfrak P\) is a declared class of admissible nonanticipating policies.
\(R_T(f)\) is measurable and has a well-defined extended expectation for each \((f,\pi)\).

notation.meaning: expectation for fixed objective f under policy pi

review_flags: corrected_builder_overstatement: a worst-case objective need not attain the supremum, so the lower-bound interpretation is epsilon-approximate absent attainment
knowledge_statements.title: Minimax Frequentist Regret

assumptions_latex: The objective \(f\) is fixed in a deterministic class \(\mathcal F\).
For each \(f\), observation noise and policy randomization induce a probability law \(\mathbb P_f\).
The cumulative regret \(R_T(f)\) is measurable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Frequentist performance is stated pointwise or uniformly over fixed objectives, without averaging over a prior on \(f\).

notation.meaning: law conditional on fixed objective f

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-objective assessment, typically uniform over an RKHS ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A frequentist regret assessment treats \(f\in\mathcal F\) as fixed and evaluates randomness only from observations and the policy. An expected guarantee has the form
\[\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb E_f[R_T(f)]\le B_T,\]
while a uniform high-probability guarantee has the form
\[\inf_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb P_f\!\left(R_T(f)\le B_T(\delta)\right)\ge1-\delta.\]
Pointwise statements omit the supremum or infimum and hold for each declared \(f\). No prior averaging over objectives occurs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Frequentist regret fixes the objective and controls expected or high-probability regret, pointwise or uniformly over a deterministic function class.

children.title: Finite-Horizon Regret
children.top_down_role: Accumulated sequential loss over a prescribed evaluation budget.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Per-Horizon Bounds Are Not Simultaneous Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifier boundary between fixed-horizon and time-uniform regret guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose that for every fixed \(T\),
\[\mathbb P(R_T\le B_T(\delta))\ge1-\delta.\]
These statements may use different failure events and therefore do not imply
\[\mathbb P\!\left(\forall T\ge1:\ R_T\le B_T(\delta)\right)\ge1-\delta.\]
For a finite set of horizons \(\mathcal T\), a union bound gives simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\sum_{T\in\mathcal T}\delta_T\) when the bound at horizon \(T\) fails with probability at most \(\delta_T\). An infinite time-uniform claim requires a valid time-uniform argument, such as summable error allocation or a confidence sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A high-probability guarantee stated separately at each fixed horizon does not automatically hold for all horizons on one event.
assumptions_latex: Each fixed-horizon statement controls its own failure event.
No coupling or time-uniform construction is assumed.

notation.meaning: event that the regret bound holds at horizon T

knowledge_statements.title: Per-Horizon Bounds Are Not Simultaneous Bounds
Finite-Horizon Regret
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-budget, undiscounted regret over rounds 1 through T.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a prescribed integer horizon \(T\ge1\), finite-horizon regret is
\[R_T:=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\bigl(f^*-f(X_t)\bigr),\qquad f^*:=\max_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x).\]
The associated average regret is \(\overline r_T:=R_T/T\). A finite-horizon guarantee specifies a bound \(B(T,\delta)\) such that \(R_T\le B(T,\delta)\) on an event of probability at least \(1-\delta\), or specifies \(\mathbb E[R_T]\le B(T)\). The horizon and the probability convention must be declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a fixed evaluation budget, finite-horizon regret totals the opportunity loss incurred during exactly those rounds.
assumptions_latex: A positive integer horizon \(T\) is fixed before performance is assessed.
The policy selects \(X_t\) using information available before round \(t\).
The objective attains \(f^*=\max_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite-horizon regret is the total opportunity loss over exactly the first \(T\) sequential decisions.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard fixed-budget finite-horizon regret criterion

children.title: Global Optimization Consistency

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dense Evaluations Give Best-Observed Value Consistency

The evaluation sequence is dense.
Recommendations select a best observed point.

f is continuous.

knowledge_statements.title: Value Consistency Implies Optimizer-Set Consistency

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) attains its maximum \(f^*\).
The algorithm produces recommendations \((\widehat x_T)_{T\ge1}\).

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard value-consistency criterion for global optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value consistency of terminal recommendations; decision convergence requires additional identifiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An optimization procedure is globally consistent in value if its recommendations satisfy
\[r_T^{\mathrm s}:=f^*-f(\widehat x_T)\longrightarrow0\]
as \(T\to\infty\), in the declared mode: almost surely, in probability, or in expectation. Equivalently, \(f(\widehat x_T)\to f^*\) in that mode. If \(\mathcal X\) is compact, \(f\) is continuous, and the optimizer set \(X^*\) is nonempty, this criterion ensures asymptotically optimal values; convergence of \(\widehat x_T\) to a particular optimizer additionally requires uniqueness or an identifiability condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A globally consistent optimizer recommends points whose objective values converge to the global optimum under a stated probabilistic mode.
knowledge_statements.title: Global Optimization Consistency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property correctly expresses value consistency through vanishing simple regret and distinguishes it from convergence to a particular optimizer, but no source supports the terminology and mode-dependent formulation.

children.title: Sampling-Density Criteria
children.top_down_role: Coverage requirements imposed on evaluation locations over time.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Density Does Not Imply Positive Sampling Frequency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates topological coverage from allocation-frequency conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequence can be dense in X while some nonempty open sets have asymptotic sampling frequency zero. For example, enumerate a countable dense set (q_k) in [0,1] and insert between successive q_k blocks at 0 whose lengths dominate all preceding terms. The sequence is dense, but for every open interval U with 0\notin\overline U, T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbf1\{x_t\in U\}\to0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Topological density guarantees eventual proximity, not a positive long-run sampling fraction in every region.
assumptions_latex: Density is defined through the cumulative set of locations.
Inserted blocks at 0 grow fast enough to dominate the preceding sequence length.

notation.meaning: Number of visits to U through time T.

knowledge_statements.title: Density Does Not Imply Positive Sampling Frequency

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full-Support IID Sampling Is Almost Surely Dense
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probabilistic sufficient condition for the deterministic density criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let X be second-countable and x_1,x_2,\ldots be independent draws from a probability measure P with full support. Then almost surely every nonempty open set is visited infinitely often and \overline{\{x_t:t\ge1\}}=X. If X is also compact metric, the cumulative fill distance satisfies h_T\to0 almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent sampling from a full-support law is almost surely dense and has vanishing fill distance on compact metric spaces.
assumptions_latex: X has a countable topological base.
The samples are IID.
P has full topological support.
For fill-distance convergence, X is compact metric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \overline{\{x_t:t\ge1\}}=X\text{ a.s.},\qquad h_T\to0\text{ a.s. on compact metric }X.
knowledge_statements.title: Full-Support IID Sampling Is Almost Surely Dense

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a compact metric space with metric \(d\).
\((x_t)_{t\ge 1}\subset X\) is the sequence of evaluation sites.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h_T\to 0\), equivalently every nonempty open subset of \(X\) is sampled eventually.

notation.meaning: open ball of radius r centered at x

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses vanishing fill distance as the deterministic criterion for asymptotically dense Bayesian-optimization sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(T\ge 1\), define the fill distance by \[h_T:=\sup_{x\in X}\min_{1\le t\le T}d(x,x_t).\] The design satisfies the sampling-density criterion when \(h_T\to 0\) as \(T\to\infty\). On a compact metric space this is equivalent to requiring that, for every \(x\in X\) and every \(r>0\), there exists a finite \(T_{x,r}\) such that \(\{x_1,\ldots,x_{T_{x,r}}\}\cap B(x,r)\ne\varnothing\). Consequently, the closure of \(\{x_t:t\ge1\}\) equals \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sampling is asymptotically dense when its fill distance vanishes, equivalently when every neighborhood of every point eventually contains an evaluation.
knowledge_statements.title: Sampling-Density Criteria

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The compact-space fill-distance criterion and its density equivalence are mathematically sound and fit the condition container, but the record supplies no inspectable citation.
