Relevant-Region Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricts asymptotic coverage to a prescribed optimizer-containing or decision-relevant region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(T\ge1\), define \[h_T(R):=\sup_{x\in R}\min_{1\le t\le T}d(x,x_t).\] The design covers \(R\) when \(h_T(R)\to0\) as \(T\to\infty\). If \(R\) is compact, this is equivalent to requiring that, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exists \(T_\varepsilon<\infty\) such that \[R\subseteq\bigcup_{t=1}^{T_\varepsilon}B(x_t,\varepsilon).\] If \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) has a nonempty optimizer set \(X^*:=\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in X}f(x)\) satisfying \(X^*\subseteq R\), then every \(x^*\in X^*\) is approached arbitrarily closely by evaluation sites.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relevant region is covered when evaluations form increasingly fine nets over it. If it contains the nonempty optimizer set of the stated objective, every optimizer is approached arbitrarily closely by evaluations.

\((x_t)_{t\ge1}\subseteq X\) is the evaluation sequence.

children.title: Persistent-Exploration Conditions
children.top_down_role: Exploration behavior needed to avoid permanent exclusion of promising regions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete persistent-exploration condition on a finite action domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let X be finite. At round t, explore with conditional probability \varepsilon_t and, on exploration, draw from q with q(x)>0 for every x\in X. If exploration randomizations are conditionally independent of the past and \sum_{t=1}^\infty\varepsilon_t=\infty, then every action is sampled infinitely often almost surely, even if \varepsilon_t\to0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsummable vanishing exploration schedule with full-support exploratory draws visits every finite-domain action infinitely often.
assumptions_latex: X is finite.
q has full support.
The exploration randomizations satisfy the stated conditional independence.
\sum_t\varepsilon_t=\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Epsilon-Exploration Schedule

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary for independent epsilon-exploration schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If independent exploration indicators have probabilities \varepsilon_t with \sum_t\varepsilon_t<\infty, then only finitely many explorations occur almost surely. If additionally 0\le\varepsilon_t<1 for all t, then \prod_t(1-\varepsilon_t)>0, so no exploration ever occurs with positive probability. Thus \varepsilon_t\to0 alone does not ensure persistent exploration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exploration probabilities that decay too quickly yield only finitely many exploratory samples and may yield none.
assumptions_latex: Exploration indicators are independent.
\sum_t\varepsilon_t<\infty.

conditional probability of choosing U at round t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: States persistent exploration through divergent conditional sampling mass on every open set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each nonempty open set \(U\subseteq X\), let \(p_t(U):=\mathbb P(x_t\in U\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})\) and \(N_T(U):=\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbf 1\{x_t\in U\}\). A sufficient persistent-exploration condition is \[\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}p_t(U)=\infty\quad\text{almost surely for every nonempty open }U\subseteq X.\] Under the conditional Borel--Cantelli property for the sampling mechanism, this implies \(N_T(U)\to\infty\) almost surely for every such \(U\). Thus exploitation may dominate asymptotically, but no open region receives only finitely many evaluations.

children.title: GP-UCB Regret Theory
children.top_down_role: Guarantee families connecting optimism, confidence calibration, kernel geometry, and acquired information.

children.title: Maximum-Information-Gain Regret Mechanism
children.top_down_role: The bridge between posterior information accumulation and regret control.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-noise kernel information capacity used in GP-UCB regret bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a GP kernel matrix \(K_A\) on a design multiset \(A\) of size \(T\) and independent Gaussian noise variance \(\lambda^2>0\), define \[I_A:=I(y_A;f_A)=\frac12\log\det(I+\lambda^{-2}K_A),\qquad\gamma_T:=\sup_{|A|=T}I_A.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximum information gain is the largest mutual information between T noisy GP observations and their latent values over admissible designs.
assumptions_latex: The latent vector is Gaussian with covariance \(K_A\).
Observation errors are independent Gaussian with variance \(\lambda^2>0\).

notation.meaning: maximum information gain at horizon T

knowledge_statements.title: Maximum Information Gain

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bridge from posterior variances to maximum information gain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an ordered design \(A=(x_1,\ldots,x_T)\), \[I_A=\frac12\sum_{t=1}^T\log\!\left(1+\frac{\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)}{\lambda^2}\right).\] If \(k(x,x)\leq\kappa^2\), then \[\sum_{t=1}^T\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)\leq\frac{2\kappa^2}{\log(1+\kappa^2/\lambda^2)}I_A\leq\frac{2\kappa^2}{\log(1+\kappa^2/\lambda^2)}\gamma_T.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gaussian mutual information decomposes into sequential log-variance increments and controls selected posterior variances under a bounded kernel diagonal.
assumptions_latex: \(k(x,x)\leq\kappa^2<\infty\).
Posterior variances use the stated GP observation model.

notation.meaning: latent posterior variance before round t

knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Variance–Information Identity and Bound

assumptions_latex: A confidence event satisfies \(|f(x)-\mu_{t-1}(x)|\le b_t\sigma_{t-1}(x)\) for all selected rounds and points.
GP-UCB selects \(x_t\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in X}\mu_{t-1}(x)+b_t\sigma_{t-1}(x)\), with nondecreasing \(b_t\).
The posterior variances satisfy \(\sum_{t=1}^T\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)\le C\gamma_T\).

notation.meaning: maximum information gain from T observations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract confidence-width argument isolating the information-gain step in GP-UCB regret analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in X}f(x)\) and \(r_t:=f(x^*)-f(x_t)\). On the stated simultaneous confidence event, optimism and the GP-UCB selection rule give \(r_t\le2b_t\sigma_{t-1}(x_t)\). Hence, by monotonicity of \(b_t\), Cauchy--Schwarz, and the variance-information inequality, \[R_T:=\sum_{t=1}^Tr_t\le2b_T\sum_{t=1}^T\sigma_{t-1}(x_t)\le2b_T\sqrt{T\sum_{t=1}^T\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)}\le2b_T\sqrt{CT\gamma_T}.\] Thus sublinear regret follows whenever \(b_T^2\gamma_T=o(T)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simultaneous posterior confidence converts instantaneous regret into posterior width; cumulative variance is then controlled by maximum information gain.
knowledge_statements.title: Maximum-Information-Gain Regret Mechanism

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The confidence-width and information-gain mechanism is mathematically coherent and the principle kind fits this bridge container, but no primary GP-UCB source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Bayesian GP-UCB Guarantees

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-action Bayesian specialization of the prior-calibrated GP-UCB guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be finite with \(|X|=K\), and suppose the objective and observations follow the Gaussian-process model used by GP-UCB. For \(\delta\in(0,1)\), set \[\beta_t=2\log\!\left(\frac{K\pi^2t^2}{3\delta}\right),\qquad x_t\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in X}\{\mu_{t-1}(x)+\sqrt{\beta_t}\,\sigma_{t-1}(x)\}.\] Then, with probability at least \(1-\delta\), simultaneously for all \(t\ge1\) and \(x\in X\), \[|f(x)-\mu_{t-1}(x)|\le\sqrt{\beta_t}\sigma_{t-1}(x).\] If \(\sum_{t=1}^T\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)\le C\gamma_T\), then on this event \[R_T\le2\sqrt{CT\beta_T\gamma_T}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite action set, a two-sided Gaussian tail bound and summable union bound give an explicit time-uniform confidence schedule and cumulative-regret certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite with \(|X|=K\).
The objective is drawn from the Gaussian-process prior used for inference, and the Gaussian observation model is correctly specified.
\(\sum_{t=1}^T\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)\le C\gamma_T\) for every relevant horizon.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous-domain Bayesian specialization using Lipschitz sample paths and refining finite grids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be compact, let \(D_t\) be a finite \(t^{-2}\)-net, and suppose that with probability at least \(1-\delta_L\), \(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz. Set \[\beta_t=2\log\!\left(\frac{|D_t|\pi^2t^2}{3\delta_C}\right)\] and maximize \(\mu_{t-1}+\sqrt{\beta_t}\sigma_{t-1}\) over \(D_t\). Under the correctly specified GP model, gridwise confidence holds simultaneously with probability at least \(1-\delta_C\). If \(\sum_{t=1}^T\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)\leq C\gamma_T\), then with probability at least \(1-\delta_L-\delta_C\), \[R_T\leq2\sqrt{CT\beta_T\gamma_T}+L\sum_{t=1}^Tt^{-2}\leq2\sqrt{CT\beta_T\gamma_T}+\frac{L\pi^2}{6}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lipschitz sample paths and refining grids reduce compact-domain Bayesian GP-UCB to finite confidence unions with a summable discretization penalty.

Bayesian GP-UCB Guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bayesian guarantee conditional on a valid prior-calibrated simultaneous confidence schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\delta\in(0,1)\), let \(x^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in X}f(x)\), and suppose \((b_t)_{t\ge1}\) is nondecreasing and chosen so that, with probability at least \(1-\delta\) under the joint GP prior and observation law, \[|f(x)-\mu_{t-1}(x)|\le b_t\sigma_{t-1}(x)\quad\text{for every }t\ge1\text{ and }x\in X.\] If GP-UCB selects \[x_t\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in X}\bigl(\mu_{t-1}(x)+b_t\sigma_{t-1}(x)\bigr)\] and \(\sum_{t=1}^T\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)\le C\gamma_T\) for every \(T\ge1\), then, on the same event, \[R_T:=\sum_{t=1}^T\bigl(f(x^*)-f(x_t)\bigr)\le2b_T\sqrt{CT\gamma_T}.\] If additionally \(b_T^2\gamma_T=o(T)\), then \(R_T/T\to0\) on that event.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated GP prior, simultaneous posterior confidence band, and variance-information inequality, GP-UCB satisfies the cumulative-regret bound with probability at least one minus delta. The same event yields vanishing average regret under the stated growth condition.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is drawn from the Gaussian-process prior used by the algorithm, and observations follow the assumed conditionally Gaussian noise model.
\(\delta\in(0,1)\), and a simultaneous posterior confidence event over all \(t\ge1\) and \(x\in X\) has probability at least \(1-\delta\).
An optimizer \(x^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in X}f(x)\) exists.
The variance-information inequality \(\sum_{t=1}^T\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)\le C\gamma_T\) holds for every \(T\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With probability at least \(1-\delta\), \(R_T\le2b_T\sqrt{CT\gamma_T}\) for every \(T\ge1\); if \(b_T^2\gamma_T=o(T)\), then \(R_T/T\to0\) on that event.

children.title: Kernel-Space GP-UCB Guarantees
children.top_down_role: Worst-case performance certificates over bounded kernel function classes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A normalized confidence radius instantiating the fixed-kernel RKHS GP-UCB theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(k(x,x)\le1\), \(\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le B\), unit ridge regularization, and conditionally \(R\)-sub-Gaussian observation noise. Let \(\mu_{t-1}\) and \(\sigma_{t-1}\) be the associated kernel-ridge quantities and \(\gamma_{t-1}\) the matching maximum information gain. Then, with probability at least \(1-\delta\), simultaneously for all \(t\ge1\) and \(x\in X\), \[|f(x)-\mu_{t-1}(x)|\le\left[B+R\sqrt{2\left(\gamma_{t-1}+1+\log(1/\delta)\right)}\right]\sigma_{t-1}(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A kernel self-normalized inequality supplies a time-uniform confidence radius consisting of the RKHS radius plus a noise-and-information term.
assumptions_latex: \(k(x,x)\le1\) for every \(x\in X\).
\(f\in\mathcal H_k\) and \(\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le B\).
The noise is conditionally \(R\)-sub-Gaussian.
Posterior quantities use unit ridge regularization and the matching information-gain convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With probability at least \(1-\delta\), the displayed confidence inequality holds simultaneously for all \(t\ge1\) and \(x\in X\).

notation.meaning: maximum information gain under the stated normalization

knowledge_statements.title: Self-Normalized RKHS Confidence Radius
Kernel-Space GP-UCB Guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Frequentist RKHS-ball version, distinct from assuming the objective is a GP sample path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let kernel ridge regression with kernel \(k\) produce \(\mu_{t-1}\) and \(\sigma_{t-1}\). Choose a nondecreasing sequence \((b_t)_{t\ge1}\) so that the RKHS self-normalized concentration bound yields \[|f(x)-\mu_{t-1}(x)|\le b_t\sigma_{t-1}(x)\quad\text{for every }t\ge1\text{ and }x\in X\] with probability at least \(1-\delta\), for every fixed \(f\in\mathcal H_k\) satisfying \(\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le B\). If GP-UCB uses this radius and \(\sum_{t=1}^T\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)\le C\gamma_T\), then, on that event, \[R_T\le2b_T\sqrt{CT\gamma_T}.\] This is a worst-case function-class guarantee, and its probability is with respect to the observation noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every fixed objective in the bounded RKHS ball, self-normalized concentration gives a high-probability noise guarantee whose regret bound is uniform in the declared norm radius.
assumptions_latex: \(k\) is a positive-definite kernel with RKHS \(\mathcal H_k\), and the fixed objective satisfies \(\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le B\).
Observation noise is conditionally \(R\)-sub-Gaussian.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every fixed \(f\) with \(\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le B\), \(R_T\le2b_T\sqrt{CT\gamma_T}\) on an observation-noise event of probability at least \(1-\delta\).

children.title: Prior-Function Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility requirements linking Bayesian guarantees to assumed function behavior.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional boundary of infinite-dimensional Gaussian-measure nonmembership.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \[k(x,x')=\sum_{j=1}^{m}\lambda_j\phi_j(x)\phi_j(x'),\qquad \lambda_j>0,\quad m<\infty,\] and \(f\sim\operatorname{GP}(0,k)\). Then \(f=\sum_{j=1}^{m}\sqrt{\lambda_j}Z_j\phi_j\) with independent \(Z_j\sim N(0,1)\), and \[f\in\mathcal H_k,\qquad \|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}^2=\sum_{j=1}^{m}Z_j^2<\infty\quad\text{almost surely}.\] Nevertheless, no deterministic finite \(B\) contains every draw almost surely because this Gaussian norm has unbounded support.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-rank GP draw belongs to its covariance RKHS almost surely, although no fixed finite RKHS ball contains it almost surely.
assumptions_latex: The covariance kernel has exactly \(m<\infty\) positive modes.
\(f\) is drawn from the centered GP with covariance k.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(f\in\mathcal H_k)=1\), but \(\mathbb P(\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le B)<1\) for every finite \(B\).
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Rank Exception to GP–RKHS Nonmembership

assumptions_latex: \(f\sim\operatorname{GP}(0,k)\) on a domain where the covariance operator has infinitely many positive eigenvalues.
\(\mathcal H_k\) denotes the RKHS generated by \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(f\in\mathcal H_k)=0\), despite the algorithm using the same kernel \(k\).

notation.meaning: RKHS induced by the covariance kernel

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates covariance-kernel compatibility from membership in the corresponding RKHS.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compatibility has two distinct meanings. In the Bayesian regime, the data-generating objective is distributed according to the GP prior used for posterior inference. In the worst-case regime, the deterministic objective must satisfy \(f\in\mathcal H_k\) and usually \(\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le B\). These conditions are not interchangeable: if the covariance operator of \(k\) has infinitely many positive eigenvalues, then a draw \(f\sim\operatorname{GP}(0,k)\) satisfies \[\mathbb P\{f\in\mathcal H_k\}=0.\] Thus using the same kernel in both analyses does not make a Bayesian sample path satisfy the RKHS-ball hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matching the GP covariance kernel does not imply RKHS membership: in infinite dimension, a GP draw lies outside its covariance RKHS almost surely.
knowledge_statements.title: Prior-Function Compatibility

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated incompatibility is a genuine failure boundary and is standard under an appropriate infinite-rank Gaussian-measure setting, but that setting and the almost-sure nonmembership claim require an authoritative cited theorem.

children.title: Worst-Case Norm Dependence
children.top_down_role: Guarantee sensitivity to kernel-space size restrictions.

assumptions_latex: The deterministic objective satisfies \(\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le B\).
The kernel confidence radius has the form \(b_t=B+u_t(\delta,R,k)\), where \(u_t\) is independent of \(B\).
The GP-UCB information inequality holds with constant \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_T\le2(B+u_T)\sqrt{CT\gamma_T}\), displaying linear dependence on the norm bound.

notation.meaning: noise and confidence contribution to the radius

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records how the RKHS radius enters the standard confidence-width regret argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In an RKHS-uniform GP-UCB analysis, the deterministic interpolation bias contributes the term \(B\) to the confidence radius. If \(b_t=B+u_t(\delta,R,k)\), where \(u_t\) collects the noise, regularization, information-gain, and confidence terms, then the standard width argument gives \[R_T\le2\bigl(B+u_T(\delta,R,k)\bigr)\sqrt{CT\gamma_T}.\] Holding all other quantities fixed, this certificate is affine, and asymptotically linear, in the assumed worst-case norm radius \(B\). Therefore a uniform numerical guarantee requires a finite declared bound on \(\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The RKHS norm radius enters the confidence width additively, so the resulting worst-case regret certificate grows linearly with that radius.
knowledge_statements.title: Worst-Case Norm Dependence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional affine dependence on the RKHS radius follows from the assumed confidence-radius form and fits a property container, but no source establishes that form or its normalization and regularization conventions.

children.title: Exact-Observation Regret
children.top_down_role: GP-UCB performance in noiseless evaluation settings.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gap-dependent cumulative-regret bound from interpolation and optimism on a finite action set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be finite, evaluations exact, and the posterior interpolate sampled sites. On a simultaneous confidence event, exact GP-UCB never reselects a sampled strictly suboptimal point: its UCB equals its true value, while the global maximizer's UCB is at least \(f^*\). Hence each strictly suboptimal \(x\) is selected at most once and \[R_T\leq\sum_{x\in X:f(x)<f^*}(f^*-f(x))\quad\text{for every }T.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite domain with exact interpolation and valid confidence bands, GP-UCB incurs each suboptimal action’s gap at most once.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite and a maximizer exists.
Observations are exact and sampled sites have zero posterior variance.
The simultaneous confidence event is valid.
The UCB is maximized exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Domain Exact-Observation Regret Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of exact evaluations on posterior mean and latent variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a noiseless GP posterior with a nonsingular kernel matrix on distinct sampled sites, conditioning on \(y_i=f(x_i)\) gives \[\mu_t(x_i)=f(x_i),\qquad\sigma_t^2(x_i)=0.\] Under the fixed model, an immediate exact replicate supplies no additional latent-value information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A noiseless GP posterior interpolates sampled values and has zero latent variance at sampled sites.
assumptions_latex: Observations are exact.
The kernel matrix on distinct sampled sites is nonsingular.
The GP model and hyperparameters are fixed.
knowledge_statements.title: Noiseless Posterior Interpolation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic terminal simple-regret certificate from the noiseless kernel power function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k\) be a positive-definite kernel, let \(x_1,\ldots,x_t\) be distinct sites with nonsingular Gram matrix \(K_t\), and let \(\mu_t\) be the zero-mean noiseless kernel interpolant of \(f\in\mathcal H_k\). Define \[\sigma_t^2(x)=k(x,x)-k_t(x)^\top K_t^{-1}k_t(x).\] If \(\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le B\), then \(|f(x)-\mu_t(x)|\le B\sigma_t(x)\) for every \(x\). Consequently, if \(x^*\in\arg\max_X f\) and \(\widehat x_t\in\arg\max_X\mu_t\), then \[f(x^*)-f(\widehat x_t)\le B\bigl(\sigma_t(x^*)+\sigma_t(\widehat x_t)\bigr)\le2B\sup_{x\in X}\sigma_t(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For exact kernel interpolation, the power function deterministically bounds pointwise error and certifies the posterior-mean recommendation’s simple regret.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in\mathcal H_k\) with \(\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le B\).
Observations at distinct sites are exact and their Gram matrix is nonsingular.
The interpolant uses the zero-mean RKHS convention.
The objective and interpolant attain the displayed maxima.

notation.meaning: Kernel power function, equivalently noiseless posterior standard deviation.

knowledge_statements.title: Noiseless RKHS Interpolation Regret Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous-domain terminal consistency of exact kernel interpolation under dense sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a compact metric space, let \(k\) be a continuous positive-definite kernel, and let \(x_1,x_2,\ldots\) be distinct sites whose union is dense in \(X\), with every finite Gram matrix nonsingular. Let \(\mu_t\) and \(\sigma_t\) be the zero-mean noiseless kernel interpolant and power function. Then
\[
\sup_{x\in X}\sigma_t(x)\longrightarrow0.
\]
Consequently, for every \(f\in\mathcal H_k\) with \(\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le B\), if \(\widehat x_t\in\arg\max_X\mu_t\), then
\[
0\le \max_X f-f(\widehat x_t)\le2B\sup_X\sigma_t\longrightarrow0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense exact sampling with a continuous kernel drives the power function uniformly to zero and makes posterior-mean recommendations consistent for RKHS-bounded objectives.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is compact.
\(k\) is continuous and positive definite.
The distinct sampled sites are dense and their finite Gram matrices are nonsingular.
\(f\in\mathcal H_k\), \(\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le B\), and the displayed maxima are attained.

notation.meaning: kernel power function or noiseless posterior standard deviation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Singularity of the Positive-Noise Information Formula at Zero Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary preventing direct substitution of zero noise into the standard noisy-observation log-determinant information capacity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For one latent Gaussian value \(F\sim N(0,s^2)\), observed as \(Y_\lambda=F+\varepsilon_\lambda\) with independent \(\varepsilon_\lambda\sim N(0,\lambda^2)\) and \(s^2>0\), \[I(Y_\lambda;F)=\frac12\log\!\left(1+\frac{s^2}{\lambda^2}\right)\longrightarrow\infty\qquad(\lambda\downarrow0).\] At \(\lambda=0\), \(Y_0=F\), and the joint law of \((Y_0,F)\) is singular relative to the product of its continuous marginals, so \(I(Y_0;F)=\infty\). Therefore the positive-noise log-determinant capacity does not yield a finite noiseless complexity by setting \(\lambda=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact observation makes the mutual information between a nondegenerate continuous Gaussian value and itself infinite, so positive-noise information capacity cannot simply be evaluated at zero noise.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon_\lambda\sim N(0,\lambda^2)\) is independent of \(F\).
Mutual information is defined by relative entropy.
knowledge_statements.title: Singularity of the Positive-Noise Information Formula at Zero Noise

assumptions_latex: Observations are exact: \(y_t=f(x_t)\).
A valid simultaneous confidence bound \(|f(x)-\mu_{t-1}(x)|\le b_t\sigma_{t-1}(x)\) holds.
The noiseless posterior variances obey \(\sum_{t=1}^T\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)\le V_T\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noiseless width bound stated without importing a positive-noise mutual-information constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let GP-UCB select \(x_t\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in X}\mu_{t-1}(x)+b_t\sigma_{t-1}(x)\), with nondecreasing \(b_t\), using the posterior conditioned on exact evaluations. On the simultaneous confidence event, \(r_t:=f(x^*)-f(x_t)\le2b_t\sigma_{t-1}(x_t)\). Therefore \[R_T\le2b_T\sqrt{T\sum_{t=1}^T\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)}\le2b_T\sqrt{TV_T}.\] A noiseless regret rate follows only after bounding \(V_T\) for the kernel and design; the usual positive-noise log-determinant constant cannot be substituted unchanged at zero noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With exact evaluations, regret is controlled by cumulative noiseless posterior variance; positive-noise information-gain constants do not directly survive the zero-noise limit.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Observation Regret

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed conditional complexity bound is correct and appropriately separated from positive-noise information gain, but the noiseless confidence and variance-complexity claims lack an inspectable source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exponential regret convergence of partitioned GP-UCB under exact observations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A recursively partitioned GP-UCB policy for sufficiently regular Gaussian-process sample paths in the deterministic-observation setting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume exact observations and a Gaussian-process sample path having a unique global optimum and the required regular behavior near that optimum. A centered Gaussian process with Matérn covariance satisfies these stated requirements when \(v>2\). For the analyzed recursively subdividing GP-UCB policy, after localization to the neighborhood of the global optimum there exists a process-dependent constant \(c>0\), independent of \(\tau\), such that \[\mathbb E[\rho_\tau]=\mathcal O\!\left(\exp\!\left\{-\frac{c\tau}{(\log\tau)^{d/4}}\right\}\right).\] Since \(r_\tau\leq\rho_\tau\), the result also gives rapid simple-regret convergence and bounded cumulative regret after entry into the converged regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under exact observations, a unique global optimum, and suitable local sample-path behavior, the analyzed recursively partitioned GP-UCB policy has exponentially decreasing expected instantaneous regret after it localizes near the optimum. Centered Matérn Gaussian processes satisfy the stated requirements when v exceeds 2. The result also implies rapid simple-regret convergence and bounded cumulative regret after localization.

\text{the Gaussian-process sample path has a unique global optimum}

v>2\quad\text{for the stated centered Matérn sufficient condition}

\text{the algorithm has entered the localized convergence regime}

A simultaneous confidence event holds with nondecreasing multiplier \(b_t\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard homoscedastic sub-Gaussian observation regime with regularized information gain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let GP-UCB use posterior or kernel-ridge quantities computed with regularization \(\lambda>0\). On an event of probability at least \(1-\delta\), suppose \(|f(x)-\mu_{t-1}(x)|\le b_t\sigma_{t-1}(x)\) simultaneously. Then optimism gives \(r_t\le2b_t\sigma_{t-1}(x_t)\), and the variance-information inequality yields \[R_T\le2b_T\sqrt{T\sum_{t=1}^T\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)}\le2b_T\sqrt{C_\lambda T\gamma_T(\lambda)}.\] Hence average regret vanishes whenever \(b_T^2\gamma_T(\lambda)=o(T)\), with \(b_T\) accounting for the noise scale \(R\).

children.title: Heteroscedastic Regret
children.top_down_role: GP-UCB performance when observation uncertainty varies across the domain.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit conversion from heterogeneous information gain to cumulative posterior variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(k(x,x)\leq\kappa^2\) and \(0<v_t\leq v_{\max}<\infty\). Then \[\sum_{t=1}^T\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)\leq\frac{2\kappa^2}{\log(1+\kappa^2/v_{\max})}I(y_A;f_A).\] Thus, for matching heteroscedastic maximum information gain \(\gamma_T^{(v)}\), \[\sum_{t=1}^T\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)\leq C_v\gamma_T^{(v)},\qquad C_v=\frac{2\kappa^2}{\log(1+\kappa^2/v_{\max})}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded kernel variance and a finite upper noise bound give an explicit heteroscedastic variance-information constant.
assumptions_latex: \(k(x,x)\leq\kappa^2<\infty\).
\(0<v_t\leq v_{\max}<\infty\).
Information gain uses the matching diagonal noise covariance.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the standard heteroscedastic information conversion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Without a finite upper bound on \(v_t\), no design-independent \(C<\infty\) generally ensures \[\sum_t\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)\leq C\sum_t\log\!\left(1+\frac{\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)}{v_t}\right).\] For fixed \(s^2>0\) and \(v_t\to\infty\), \(\log(1+s^2/v_t)\to0\) while the unweighted variance contribution remains \(s^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arbitrarily large noise can make information increments vanish while latent posterior variances remain positive.
assumptions_latex: Observation variances may be arbitrarily large.
Positive latent posterior variance can persist at selected points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nexists C<\infty\text{ uniformly controlling unweighted posterior variance by heterogeneous information}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mutual-information decomposition for known positive observation variances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an ordered design \(A=(x_1,\ldots,x_T)\) with independent Gaussian variances \(v_t>0\), let \(V_A=\operatorname{diag}(v_1,\ldots,v_T)\). Then \[I(y_A;f_A)=\frac12\log\det(I+V_A^{-1/2}K_AV_A^{-1/2})=\frac12\sum_{t=1}^T\log\!\left(1+\frac{\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)}{v_t}\right).\]

assumptions_latex: Observation errors are independent Gaussian.
Each known variance \(v_t\) is strictly positive.
Posterior variances use the matching heteroscedastic model.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information control that remains valid without a uniform upper bound on heterogeneous noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For known positive observation variances \(v_t\), set \(u_t=\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)/v_t\). Then \[\sum_{t=1}^T\min\{u_t,1\}\leq\frac{1}{\log2}\sum_{t=1}^T\log(1+u_t)=\frac{2}{\log2}I(y_A;f_A).\] Thus heterogeneous information gain controls truncated noise-normalized posterior variances even when no finite constant controls \(\sum_t\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without bounded noise, information still controls truncated posterior signal-to-noise ratios, though not unweighted posterior variances.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With known varying noise levels, whitening defines a heteroscedastic information gain that controls GP-UCB regret through the corresponding posterior variances.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The result follows conditionally from the assumed heteroscedastic confidence and variance-information inequalities, but the whitening formula, admissible designs, and finiteness of the constant require sourced conditions such as positive noise levels and appropriate uniform bounds.

children.title: Unknown-Noise Regret Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Certificate limitations caused by unavailable or incorrectly calibrated noise information.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: No Uniform Calibration Without a Noise-Scale Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of finite scale-independent confidence calibration over an unbounded Gaussian noise-scale class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varepsilon\sim N(0,R^2)\), where \(R>0\) is unrestricted. For every finite radius \(c\) independent of \(R\), \[\inf_{R>0}\Pr_R\{|\varepsilon|\le c\}=0.\] Thus a confidence multiplier calibrated to a fixed finite noise proxy cannot provide uniform positive coverage, and hence cannot support a uniform GP-UCB regret certificate, over this unbounded-scale class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the admissible noise scale is unbounded, every finite scale-independent confidence radius has worst-case coverage zero.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon\sim N(0,R^2)\) for an unrestricted unknown \(R>0\).
The proposed radius \(c<\infty\) does not depend on \(R\).
knowledge_statements.title: No Uniform Calibration Without a Noise-Scale Bound

assumptions_latex: The learner receives \(y_t=f(x_t)+\varepsilon_t\) but imposes no bound, distributional restriction, or identifiability condition on \(\varepsilon_t\).
The decision space contains two points \(a\ne b\), and regret is measured against the maximizer of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_\pi\sup_{f,\varepsilon}R_T(\pi)\ge T/2\); sublinear worst-case regret is impossible.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifiability boundary when unknown observation noise is completely unrestricted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{a,b\}\) and consider \(f_0(a)=1,f_0(b)=0\) and \(f_1(a)=0,f_1(b)=1\). For either objective, an admissible unrestricted noise process can set \(\varepsilon_t=-f_i(x_t)\), making every observation equal to zero. Thus the complete observation history has the same law under \(f_0\) and \(f_1\). For any policy \(\pi\), one of these two objectives assigns unit regret to at least half of its expected selections, so \[\sup_{i\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E_i[R_T(\pi)]\ge T/2.\] Consequently, unknown noise requires quantitative restrictions or estimability; otherwise no sublinear worst-case regret guarantee is identifiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without any restriction on unknown noise, noise can erase all objective information; a two-point construction then forces linear worst-case regret.
knowledge_statements.title: Unknown-Noise Regret Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-point indistinguishability construction correctly demonstrates a failure boundary under completely unrestricted, objective-dependent noise, but the nontrivial minimax lower-bound claim has no evidence record or inspectable citation.

children.title: Spectral Information Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity regimes induced by kernel eigenvalue decay, smoothness, and dimension.

children.title: Kernel Eigenvalue Decay
children.top_down_role: Spectral regimes governing effective surrogate complexity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counting-function and effective-dimension rates implied by polynomial or exponential operator-spectrum decay.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonincreasing eigenvalues \(\lambda_j\ge0\), define \(N(\tau)=\#\{j:\lambda_j>\tau\}\) and \(d_{\mathrm{eff}}(\eta)=\sum_{j\ge1}\lambda_j/(\lambda_j+\eta)\). If \(\lambda_j\le Cj^{-p}\) with \(p>1\), then \[N(\tau)\le (C/\tau)^{1/p},\qquad d_{\mathrm{eff}}(\eta)=O(\eta^{-1/p}).\] If \(\lambda_j\le C e^{-cj^q}\) with \(C,c,q>0\), then \[N(\tau)=O\!\left((\log(C/\tau))^{1/q}\right),\qquad d_{\mathrm{eff}}(\eta)=O\!\left((\log(C/\eta))^{1/q}\right)\] as the thresholds decrease to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomial and exponential eigenvalue decay imply polynomial and polylogarithmic spectral counting and effective-dimension growth, respectively.
assumptions_latex: \((\lambda_j)_{j\ge1}\) is nonincreasing and nonnegative.
For the polynomial effective-dimension conclusion, \(p>1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Polynomial decay yields order \(\eta^{-1/p}\) effective dimension, while exponential decay yields order \((\log(C/\eta))^{1/q}\).

notation.meaning: Number of eigenvalues exceeding threshold tau.
Regularized effective dimension at scale eta.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Counting and Effective-Dimension Consequences
Kernel Eigenvalue Decay
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral decay of a compact kernel integral operator relative to a reference measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be compact, let \(\rho\) be a Borel probability measure on \(X\), and let \(k:X\times X\to\mathbb R\) be continuous, symmetric, and positive semidefinite. Define \((T_k g)(x)=\int_X k(x,x')g(x')\,d\rho(x')\) on \(L^2(\rho)\), with eigenvalues \(\lambda_1\geq\lambda_2\geq\cdots\geq0\). The kernel has polynomial eigenvalue decay of order \(p>0\) if \(\lambda_j\leq Cj^{-p}\) for every \(j\geq1\), and exponential decay of order \(q>0\) if \(\lambda_j\leq C\exp(-c j^q)\) for constants \(C,c>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Kernel eigenvalue decay quantifies how rapidly the ordered spectrum of the kernel integral operator decreases, using polynomial or exponential upper bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is compact and \(\rho\) is a Borel probability measure.
\(k\) is continuous, symmetric, and positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_j\leq Cj^{-p}\) or \(\lambda_j\leq C\exp(-cj^q)\), according to the selected decay class.

notation.meaning: Kernel integral operator on the reference-measure space.
Ordered eigenvalues of the kernel integral operator.
Reference probability measure on the input domain.

children.title: Maximum Information Gain
children.top_down_role: Information-complexity quantities controlling confidence-policy performance.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cardinality-constrained information maximization on a finite candidate set without repeated selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be finite and \(F(A)=\frac12\log\det(I+\sigma^{-2}K_A)\) for \(A\subseteq V\). The set function \(F\) is normalized, monotone, and submodular. Starting from \(A_0=\varnothing\), choose \[x_t\in\arg\max_{x\in V\setminus A_t}\bigl(F(A_t\cup\{x\})-F(A_t)\bigr),\qquad A_{t+1}=A_t\cup\{x_t\}.\] For every feasible budget \(T\), \[F(A_T)\ge(1-e^{-1})\max_{A\subseteq V,\ |A|\le T}F(A).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite candidate set, Gaussian information gain is monotone submodular, and greedy marginal-information selection attains the standard one-minus-one-over-e approximation.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite and selected sites are distinct.
\(K_A\) is generated by a positive-semidefinite kernel.

notation.meaning: Information gained from observing set A.
Set returned after T greedy additions.

knowledge_statements.title: Greedy Information-Gain Design

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sequential Variance Decomposition of Information Gain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chain-rule representation for noisy Gaussian-process observations along a fixed or adaptively generated design, conditional on its realized locations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For locations \(x_1,\ldots,x_T\) and independent Gaussian noise variance \(\sigma^2>0\), let \(s_{t-1}^2(x_t)\) be the posterior latent variance before observing \(y_t\). Conditional on the realized design, \[I(y_{1:T};f_{1:T}\mid x_{1:T})=\frac12\sum_{t=1}^T\log\!\left(1+\sigma^{-2}s_{t-1}^2(x_t)\right).\] For every admissible deterministic design, and pathwise for realized adaptive locations under the corresponding conditional interpretation, this quantity is at most \(\gamma_T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gaussian information gain is the sum of logarithmic signal-to-noise contributions from sequential posterior variances.
assumptions_latex: Conditional on the design locations, the latent evaluation vector is jointly Gaussian under \(k\).
Observation errors are independent \(N(0,\sigma^2)\), with \(\sigma^2>0\).

notation.meaning: Posterior latent variance immediately before observation t.

knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Variance Decomposition of Information Gain
Maximum Information Gain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-design information complexity for Gaussian-process observations with independent Gaussian noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\sim\mathcal{GP}(0,k)\), and observe \(y_x=f(x)+\varepsilon_x\), where the noises are independent \(N(0,\sigma^2)\). For a finite design \(A=(x_1,\ldots,x_T)\), let \(K_A=(k(x_i,x_j))_{i,j=1}^T\). The maximum information gain after \(T\) observations is
\[\gamma_T:=\sup_{A\in X^T} I(y_A;f_A)=\frac12\sup_{A\in X^T}\log\det(I_T+\sigma^{-2}K_A).\]
Repeated design points are permitted unless the design class explicitly excludes them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximum information gain is the largest mutual information obtainable from T noisy GP evaluations, equivalently a maximized log determinant of the kernel matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(f\sim\mathcal{GP}(0,k)\).
\(\varepsilon_x\sim N(0,\sigma^2)\) independently, with \(\sigma^2>0\).

notation.meaning: Kernel Gram matrix of design A.
Maximum information gain from T observations.
Latent values and noisy observations at design A.

children.title: Smoothness-Driven Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity behavior induced by kernel regularity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotonicity of the Classical Matérn Complexity Exponent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparative smoothness effect within the classical Matérn maximum-information-gain bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fixed input dimension \(d\ge1\), the exponent \[a_d(
u)= rac{d(d+1)}{2
u+d(d+1)}\] appearing in the classical Matérn bound \(\gamma_T=O(T^{a_d(
u)}\log T)\) is strictly decreasing in \(
u>0\) and satisfies \(a_d(
u)\downarrow0\) as \(
u	o\infty\). Thus, within the hypotheses of that bound and with other parameters fixed, increasing Matérn smoothness improves its polynomial information-growth exponent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Within the classical Matérn capacity bound, greater smoothness strictly decreases the polynomial information-growth exponent.
assumptions_latex: The classical Matérn information-gain theorem applies under its stated domain, kernel, and positive-noise hypotheses.
The input dimension \(d\ge1\) is fixed while \(\nu\) varies.

notation.meaning: Classical Matérn information-growth exponent at dimension d and smoothness nu.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity of the Classical Matérn Complexity Exponent
Smoothness-Driven Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical GP-UCB information-gain rate for Matérn kernels on compact Euclidean domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^d\) be compact, and let \(k\) be a Matérn kernel with smoothness parameter \(\nu>1\) and fixed positive length scale. Under independent Gaussian observation noise of fixed variance, the classical discretization-based information-gain estimate is
\[\gamma_T=O\!\left(T^{\frac{d(d+1)}{2\nu+d(d+1)}}\log T\right).\]
Consequently, any GP-UCB guarantee of the form \(R_T=O(\sqrt{T\beta_T\gamma_T})\) inherits a sublinear smoothness-dependent rate whenever \(\beta_T\) grows sufficiently slowly relative to the displayed exponent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For Matérn kernels, greater smoothness reduces the polynomial information-gain exponent and correspondingly improves the standard GP-UCB regret bound.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb R^d\) is compact.
\(k\) is Matérn with \(\nu>1\) and fixed positive length scale.
Observation noise is independent Gaussian with fixed positive variance.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits the leaf, but the precise classical Matérn exponent and required domain, kernel, and smoothness hypotheses need an authoritative theorem locator.

children.title: Dimension-Driven Complexity
children.top_down_role: Information growth attributable to ambient or effective dimension.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximum information gain controlled by finite feature dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(k(x,x')=\phi(x)^\top\phi(x')\), where \(\phi(x)\in\mathbb R^r\) and \(\sup_x\|\phi(x)\|_2\le L\). With independent Gaussian observation noise of variance \(\sigma^2>0\), every length-\(T\) design satisfies \[I(y_A;f_A)\le \frac r2\log\!\left(1+\frac{TL^2}{r\sigma^2}\right),\] and therefore \[\gamma_T\le \frac r2\log\!\left(1+\frac{TL^2}{r\sigma^2}\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a rank-r bounded-feature kernel, maximum information gain is at most linear in feature dimension and logarithmic in the evaluation count.
assumptions_latex: \(k(x,x')=\phi(x)^\top\phi(x')\) with \(\phi(x)\in\mathbb R^r\).
Observation noise is independent \(N(0,\sigma^2)\), with \(\sigma^2>0\).

notation.meaning: Feature-space dimension and an upper bound on kernel rank.
Maximum information gain from T observations.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Rank Dimension Bound
Dimension-Driven Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Squared-exponential GP-UCB complexity as a function of ambient Euclidean dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^d\) be compact, and let \(k(x,x')=s^2\exp(-\|x-x'\|_2^2/(2\ell^2))\) with fixed \(s,
\ell>0\). With independent Gaussian noise of fixed positive variance, the maximum information gain satisfies
\[\gamma_T=O((\log T)^{d+1}).\]
Thus a GP-UCB bound \(R_T=O(\sqrt{T\beta_T\gamma_T})\) becomes \(R_T=O(\sqrt{T\beta_T}(\log T)^{(d+1)/2})\). The exponent of the logarithmic factor exposes the dependence on ambient dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a squared-exponential kernel, information gain is polylogarithmic in evaluations but its logarithmic exponent grows with dimension.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb R^d\) is compact.
\(k\) is squared-exponential with fixed positive amplitude and length scale.
Observation noise is independent Gaussian with fixed positive variance.

notation.meaning: GP-UCB confidence multiplier at horizon T.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The squared-exponential information-gain and induced regret rates fit the dimension-driven complexity leaf, but their exact scope and hypotheses are unsupported by a cited theorem.

children.title: GP-UCB Model-Robustness Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Guarantee boundaries under learned hyperparameters, incorrect kernels, or invalid confidence calibration.

children.title: Adaptive-Hyperparameter GP-UCB
children.top_down_role: Guarantee behavior when surrogate hyperparameters are learned during search.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditional Regret Guarantee Under Predictable Kernel Adaptation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Width-based guarantee conditional on calibration and variance control along the adaptively selected kernel sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\theta_t\) be measurable with respect to \(H_{t-1}\), and let adaptive GP-UCB select \[x_t\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in X}\{\mu_{t-1}^{\theta_t}(x)+b_t s_{t-1}^{\theta_t}(x)\},\] where \(b_t\) is nondecreasing. Suppose that on one event \(E\), simultaneously for every \(t\le T\) and \(x\in X\), \[|f(x)-\mu_{t-1}^{\theta_t}(x)|\le b_t s_{t-1}^{\theta_t}(x),\] and suppose \[\sum_{t=1}^T(s_{t-1}^{\theta_t}(x_t))^2\le V_T.\] Then on \(E\), \[R_T\le2b_T\sqrt{TV_T}.\] Predictability of \(\theta_t\) alone establishes neither hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive kernel selection retains the usual width-based regret argument only when a simultaneous confidence event and cumulative variance bound remain valid along the data-dependent kernel sequence.
assumptions_latex: \(\theta_t\) is \(H_{t-1}\)-measurable.
An optimizer \(x^*\) exists.
The displayed confidence event holds for the adaptively selected kernels.
The selected adaptive deviations satisfy the stated quadratic bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Regret Guarantee Under Predictable Kernel Adaptation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Family Calibration for Adaptive Kernel Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient transfer theorem for history-dependent selection from finitely many calibrated kernel models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Theta=\{1,\ldots,M\}\). For each \(j\), suppose an event \(E_j\) of probability at least \(1-\delta/M\) satisfies \[|f(x)-\mu_{t-1}^j(x)|\leq b_{j,t}s_{t-1}^j(x)\quad\text{for all }t,x.\] Let \(\theta_t\) be history-measurable and maximize the selected model's UCB. If \[\sum_{t\leq T:\theta_t=j}(s_{t-1}^j(x_t))^2\leq V_{j,T},\] then, with probability at least \(1-\delta\), \[R_T\leq2\sqrt{T\sum_{j=1}^M b_{j,T}^2V_{j,T}}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive selection from a finite kernel family is valid when all candidate models are simultaneously calibrated and their selected-round variances are controlled.
assumptions_latex: \(|\Theta|=M<\infty\).
Each candidate model has a time-uniform confidence event with failure probability at most \(\delta/M\).
\(\theta_t\) is measurable with respect to past observations.
The displayed modelwise variance bounds hold and \(b_{j,t}\) is nondecreasing in \(t\).

notation.meaning: finite admissible kernel or hyperparameter family
selected-round variance bound for model j

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Family Calibration for Adaptive Kernel Selection
Adaptive-Hyperparameter GP-UCB
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predictable kernel adaptation with confidence calibration uniform over the admissible hyperparameter family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a domain \(X\), a kernel family \(\{k_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}\), a noise model, and confidence levels \(\beta_t\). Initialize with an admissible \(\theta_1\). At round \(t\), choose \(\theta_t\) using only the history \(H_{t-1}\); compute the corresponding posterior mean \(\mu_{t-1}^{\theta_t}\) and deviation \(s_{t-1}^{\theta_t}\); select
\[x_t\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in X}\left\{\mu_{t-1}^{\theta_t}(x)+\sqrt{\beta_t}\,s_{t-1}^{\theta_t}(x)\right\};\]
observe \(y_t\), update \(H_t\), and stop at the prescribed horizon, returning the sampled point with the largest specified recommendation score.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each round estimates kernel hyperparameters from past data, rebuilds the GP posterior, and maximizes a confidence bound calibrated uniformly over allowed adaptations.
assumptions_latex: \(\theta_t\) is measurable with respect to \(H_{t-1}\).
\(\beta_t\) is calibrated for all admissible adaptive choices of \(\theta_t\).

notation.meaning: Predictably selected kernel hyperparameter at round t.
Posterior standard deviation under the selected kernel.

children.title: Kernel Misspecification
children.top_down_role: Performance limits arising from incorrect covariance structure or smoothness assumptions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Continuous RKHS Embedding as a Compatibility Condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient transfer condition under which a different analysis kernel preserves an RKHS-ball guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k_0\) define the true function class and \(k\) be the kernel used by GP-UCB. If there exists \(L<\infty\) such that \[\mathcal H_{k_0}\subseteq\mathcal H_k\quad\text{and}\quad \|g\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le L\|g\|_{\mathcal H_{k_0}}\quad\text{for every }g\in\mathcal H_{k_0},\] then every objective satisfying \(\|f\|_{\mathcal H_{k_0}}\le B_0\) also satisfies \(\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le LB_0\). Consequently, a kernel-space GP-UCB theorem whose other assumptions hold for \(k\) applies with radius \(B=LB_0\). Without such inclusion, a bound on the \(k_0\)-norm alone does not establish the \(k\)-RKHS hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuous embedding of the true RKHS into the assumed RKHS transfers the function-class guarantee with an inflated norm radius.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H_{k_0}\) is continuously embedded in \(\mathcal H_k\) with constant L.
The remaining GP-UCB assumptions hold for k.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le LB_0\), so the assumed-kernel guarantee applies with radius \(LB_0\).

notation.meaning: kernel defining the true function class
kernel used by the algorithm and analysis

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous RKHS Embedding as a Compatibility Condition
Kernel Misspecification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A two-point example where an overcorrelated assumed kernel produces linear GP-UCB regret.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{a,b\}\), use noiseless observations, zero prior mean, and the assumed kernel \(k(x,x')=1\) for all \(x,x'\in X\). Let the true objective be \(f(a)=0\) and \(f(b)=1\), and break every acquisition tie in favor of \(a\). After observing \(a\), the assumed posterior has mean zero and variance zero at both points. GP-UCB therefore selects \(a\) at every subsequent round. Since \(b\) is optimal, the instantaneous regret is one and \(R_T=T\). The true objective is outside the assumed kernel's RKHS.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An assumed constant kernel makes two distinct points indistinguishable; deterministic tie-breaking can then prevent discovery of the optimum and cause linear regret.
assumptions_latex: \(X=\{a,b\}\) and observations are noiseless.
The assumed kernel is \(k(x,x')=1\).
Acquisition ties are resolved in favor of \(a\).

children.title: Confidence Miscalibration
children.top_down_role: Guarantee failures caused by invalid confidence widths.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Excessive Confidence Widths Can Cause Linear Regret
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Overwide uncertainty bonuses can destroy performance even when the reported bands contain the truth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{a,b\}\), \(f(a)=0\), and \(f(b)=1\). Suppose the reported surrogate quantities remain \[\mu_t(a)=0,\quad s_t(a)=1,\qquad \mu_t(b)=1,\quad s_t(b)=0.\] For every sequence satisfying \(\sqrt{\beta_t}>1\), both reported intervals contain the true values, but the UCB score of \(a\) is \(\sqrt{\beta_t}>1\), while that of \(b\) is \(1\). GP-UCB therefore selects \(a\) at every round and \(R_T=T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Confidence coverage alone is insufficient: permanently excessive width at a suboptimal point can force linear regret.
assumptions_latex: \(X=\{a,b\}\) with the stated objective and reported surrogate quantities.
\(\beta_t\) is finite, nonnegative, and satisfies \(\sqrt{\beta_t}>1\) at every round.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reported bands cover f, but \(R_T=T\).
knowledge_statements.title: Excessive Confidence Widths Can Cause Linear Regret
Confidence Miscalibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of optimism when the reported posterior uncertainty excludes the true optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(X=\{a,b\}\) with true values \(f(a)=0\) and \(f(b)=1\). Suppose a misspecified surrogate reports \(\mu_t(a)=0\), \(\mu_t(b)=-1\), and \(s_t(a)=s_t(b)=0\) at every round. For every finite multiplier \(\beta_t\), its upper-confidence scores are zero at \(a\) and minus one at \(b\); hence GP-UCB always chooses \(a\) and \(R_T=T\). The confidence condition \(f(b)\leq\mu_t(b)+\sqrt{\beta_t}s_t(b)\) fails, showing that a regret certificate cannot survive arbitrary underestimation of uncertainty at an optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If uncertainty is underestimated at the optimum, the UCB score may permanently exclude it, allowing linear regret regardless of the confidence multiplier.
assumptions_latex: The surrogate reports the stated fixed means and zero deviations.

children.title: Robustness to Model Error
children.top_down_role: Residual performance under bounded discrepancies between the surrogate class and objective.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Average-Regret Floor Under Uniform Model Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic consequence and limitation of the additive-error GP-UCB certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose that on one event, for every relevant horizon \(T\), \[R_T\le2\sqrt{CT\beta_T\gamma_T}+2\varepsilon_TT.\] Then \[\frac{R_T}{T}\le2\sqrt{\frac{C\beta_T\gamma_T}{T}}+2\varepsilon_T.\] Hence \(R_T/T\to0\) on that event if \(\beta_T\gamma_T=o(T)\) and \(\varepsilon_T\to0\). If instead \(\varepsilon_T\equiv\varepsilon>0\), the certificate yields only \[\limsup_{T\to\infty}\frac{R_T}{T}\le2\varepsilon\] when the information term vanishes; it does not certify no regret.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing average regret requires both a sublinear information term and vanishing uniform model error; fixed error leaves an order-epsilon floor in this certificate.
assumptions_latex: The additive-error regret bound holds for all relevant horizons on one event.
\(\beta_T\gamma_T=o(T)\) for the vanishing-information conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\varepsilon_T\to0\), then \(R_T/T\to0\); for fixed \(\varepsilon\), the certificate gives only \(\limsup_T R_T/T\le2\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.title: Average-Regret Floor Under Uniform Model Error
Robustness to Model Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive degradation of GP-UCB regret under a uniform surrogate approximation error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose that, simultaneously for every \(t\leq T\) and \(x\in X\),
\[|f(x)-\mu_{t-1}(x)|\leq\sqrt{\beta_t}\,s_{t-1}(x)+\varepsilon.\]
If \(x_t\) maximizes \(\mu_{t-1}(x)+\sqrt{\beta_t}s_{t-1}(x)\), then its instantaneous regret satisfies \(r_t\leq2\sqrt{\beta_t}s_{t-1}(x_t)+2\varepsilon\). Consequently, if \(\beta_t\leq\beta_T\) and \(\sum_{t=1}^T s_{t-1}^2(x_t)\leq C\gamma_T\), then
\[R_T\leq2\sqrt{C T\beta_T\gamma_T}+2\varepsilon T.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform model error adds at most twice that error per round to the usual uncertainty-driven GP-UCB regret certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(|f(x)-\mu_{t-1}(x)|\leq\sqrt{\beta_t}s_{t-1}(x)+\varepsilon\) uniformly.
\(x_t\) maximizes the stated upper-confidence score.
\(\sum_{t=1}^T s_{t-1}^2(x_t)\leq C\gamma_T\).

notation.meaning: Constant in the posterior-variance information bound.

children.title: Expected-Improvement Consistency
children.top_down_role: Convergence families for fixed, estimated, and noisy surrogate regimes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary of finite-domain EI enumeration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let X=\{a,b\}, with a observed at value 0, and let the surrogate assign unevaluated b conditional mean -1 and variance 0. Then EI(a)=EI(b)=0 although f(b)>f(a) is possible. A tie rule selecting a forever never evaluates the optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If an untested point can have zero posterior variance, EI may vanish there and fail to enumerate even a two-point domain.
assumptions_latex: An unevaluated point may have zero conditional variance.
Zero-EI ties may select an already evaluated point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: EI(b)=0\not\Rightarrow f(b)\le f(a),\text{ and EI consistency can fail}.
knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate-Variance Failure of Finite-Domain Enumeration

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Noisy EI Does Not Inherit the Enumeration Argument
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates noiseless finite-domain consistency from noisy EI variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With observation noise, a sampled point can retain positive posterior variance and positive expected improvement. Thus the noiseless assertions that EI vanishes at every sampled point and is positive at every unsampled point need not hold, so finite-domain enumeration does not follow without additional rules or assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Observation noise can keep expected improvement positive at sampled points, invalidating the noiseless enumeration argument.
assumptions_latex: Observations contain nonzero noise.
The EI distribution retains latent or predictive uncertainty at sampled points.
knowledge_statements.title: Noisy EI Does Not Inherit the Enumeration Argument

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctly indexed finite-domain, noiseless expected-improvement consistency theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let D_0\subseteq X be the points observed before sequential EI selection begins. If X is finite, observations are noiseless, each x\notin D_t has strictly positive conditional Gaussian variance, and each round globally maximizes expected improvement, then no evaluated point is repeated while an unevaluated point remains. Hence every point is evaluated after at most |X\setminus D_0| additional rounds, and a global maximizer is evaluated within that many rounds unless one already lies in D_0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite noiseless EI enumerates all points not already in the initial history, so it reaches an optimizer within the number of initially unobserved alternatives.
assumptions_latex: X is finite and D_0 is the initially evaluated subset.
Observations are noiseless.
Every unevaluated point has strictly positive conditional Gaussian variance.
Each round globally maximizes expected improvement.

notation.meaning: Set of points evaluated before sequential EI begins.
Number of additional rounds until an optimizer is evaluated.

knowledge_statements.title: Initial-History Finite-Domain EI Enumeration

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Plug-In Variance-Collapse Boundary for Expected Improvement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of EI exploration when estimated surrogate parameters collapse uncertainty away from sampled points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider plug-in expected improvement \(\operatorname{EI}_t(x)=\mathbb E_{\widehat\theta_t}[(F(x)-m_t)_+\mid H_t]\). If for some unevaluated \(x\), \(\widehat\sigma_t(x)=0\) and \(\widehat\mu_t(x)\le m_t\), then \(\operatorname{EI}_t(x)=0\). Thus an estimation rule permitting this collapse lacks the positive-EI premise needed for finite-domain enumeration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Plug-in hyperparameter estimation can destroy EI exploration by assigning zero variance and no predicted improvement to an untested point.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) has not been evaluated.
The acquisition uses fitted parameters without integrating parameter uncertainty.
\(\widehat\sigma_t(x)=0\) and \(\widehat\mu_t(x)\le m_t\).

notation.meaning: Plug-in posterior mean and standard deviation.

knowledge_statements.title: Plug-In Variance-Collapse Boundary for Expected Improvement

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The positivity mechanism underlying noiseless finite-domain expected-improvement enumeration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)\mid H_t\sim N(\mu_t(x),\sigma_t^2(x))\) and let \(m_t\) be the incumbent value for maximization. If \(\sigma_t(x)>0\), then
\[
\operatorname{EI}_t(x)=(\mu_t(x)-m_t)\Phi(z_t(x))+\sigma_t(x)\phi(z_t(x)),\qquad z_t(x)=\frac{\mu_t(x)-m_t}{\sigma_t(x)},
\]
and \(\operatorname{EI}_t(x)>0\). If \(\sigma_t(x)=0\), then \(\operatorname{EI}_t(x)=(\mu_t(x)-m_t)_+\). Hence EI vanishes exactly when the predictive law is degenerate at a value not exceeding the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gaussian expected improvement is strictly positive at every point with positive posterior variance and, at a zero-variance point, equals deterministic positive improvement.
assumptions_latex: The conditional latent value is Gaussian.
The acquisition is expected positive improvement over the maximization incumbent.

notation.meaning: standard normal distribution and density functions
best value observed before the prospective evaluation

knowledge_statements.title: Gaussian Expected-Improvement Positivity Characterization
Expected-Improvement Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain, noiseless consistency of expected improvement with a nondegenerate fixed GP surrogate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be finite and let evaluations of \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) be noiseless. Assume that, conditional on any proper subset of evaluated points, every unevaluated point has strictly positive GP posterior variance. Define expected improvement for maximization by \(\operatorname{EI}_t(x)=\mathbb E[(F(x)-m_t)_+\mid H_t]\), where \(m_t\) is the best observed value. If each round maximizes \(\operatorname{EI}_t\), then evaluated points have zero improvement while every unevaluated point has positive improvement. Thus no point is repeated before all points are sampled, and a global maximizer is evaluated within at most \(|X|\) rounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite noiseless domain with positive conditional variance at untested points, expected improvement samples every point and therefore finds a global optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite and observations are noiseless.
Every unevaluated point retains strictly positive conditional GP variance.
Each round globally maximizes expected improvement.

notation.meaning: Best objective value observed through round t.

children.title: Posterior-Sampling Regret
children.top_down_role: Bayesian and kernel-space performance families for Thompson-style policies.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bayes-Regret Bounds Are Not Uniform Fixed-Function Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates prior-averaged guarantees from frequentist kernel-class guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Bayes-regret inequality \mathbb E_{f\sim\Pi,\mathcal A,\varepsilon}[R_T(f)]\le B_T controls prior-averaged regret. It does not imply \sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb E_{\mathcal A,\varepsilon}[R_T(f)]\le B_T or a high-probability bound for every fixed f\in\mathcal F without an additional uniform theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A prior-averaged regret bound is not a worst-case RKHS or fixed-function guarantee.
assumptions_latex: The available bound averages over a prior on objectives.
No separate uniform fixed-function theorem is supplied.
knowledge_statements.title: Bayes-Regret Bounds Are Not Uniform Fixed-Function Bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional distributional identity underlying Thompson-style regret analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \theta be the latent environment, X^*=x^*(\theta) a measurably selected optimal action, and \widetilde\theta_t an independent draw from the posterior law of \theta given H_{t-1}. If X_t=x^*(\widetilde\theta_t), then for every measurable action set B, \mathbb P(X_t\in B\mid H_{t-1})=\mathbb P(X^*\in B\mid H_{t-1}).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimizing an independent posterior draw produces an action distributed like the posterior optimal action.
assumptions_latex: The optimal action admits a measurable selection.
The sampled environment has the exact posterior law conditional on history.

notation.meaning: Independent draw from the current posterior environment law.
Optimal action under the latent true environment.

knowledge_statements.title: Posterior Probability-Matching Identity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Prior-Support Exclusion Can Cause Linear Thompson-Sampling Regret
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-action posterior-sampling failure when the prior excludes the true optimal environment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X=\{a,b\}\) and suppose rewards are deterministic. The posterior model assigns probability one to \(f_0(a)=0,f_0(b)=-1\), whereas the true, prior-excluded objective is \(f_1(a)=0,f_1(b)=1\). Exact posterior sampling selects \(X_t=a\) at every round, observes the model-consistent value \(0\), and incurs \(R_T=\sum_{t=1}^T(f_1(b)-f_1(X_t))=T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the prior excludes the true environment, posterior sampling can repeatedly choose the wrong action and suffer linear regret.
assumptions_latex: The posterior-sampling policy draws from the stated degenerate prior.
Rewards are observed only at selected actions.
Regret is evaluated under the prior-excluded objective \(f_1\).

notation.meaning: Sole objective admitted by the prior.
True objective excluded from prior support.

knowledge_statements.title: Prior-Support Exclusion Can Cause Linear Thompson-Sampling Regret

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Prior-averaged cumulative-regret bound for exact posterior sampling with a discrete optimal action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X^*\) be a discrete prior-random optimal action and let exact posterior sampling satisfy \(\mathcal L(X_t\mid H_{t-1})=\mathcal L(X^*\mid H_{t-1})\). Define \(\Delta_t=\mathbb E[f(X^*)-f(X_t)\mid H_{t-1}]\) and \(g_t=I(X^*;(X_t,Y_t)\mid H_{t-1})\). If \(\Delta_t^2\leq\Gamma g_t\) almost surely for every \(t\), then \[\operatorname{BayesRegret}(T)\leq\sqrt{\Gamma T I(X^*;H_T)}\leq\sqrt{\Gamma T H(X^*)}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform information-ratio bound gives square-root Bayesian cumulative regret, with finite Shannon entropy of the discrete optimal action controlling total information.
assumptions_latex: \(X^*\) is discrete and \(H(X^*)<\infty\).
The policy uses exact posterior probability matching.
\(\Delta_t^2\leq\Gamma g_t\) almost surely at every round.

notation.meaning: Conditional information gained about the optimal action.

knowledge_statements.title: Information-Ratio Bayes-Regret Bound
Posterior-Sampling Regret
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-ratio Bayes-regret bound for Thompson-style posterior sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X^*\) be an optimal action under the prior and let \(H_{t-1}\) be the history. A posterior-sampling policy draws \(X_t\) from the conditional law of \(X^*\) given \(H_{t-1}\). Define \(\Delta_t=\mathbb E[f(X^*)-f(X_t)\mid H_{t-1}]\) and \(g_t=I(X^*;(X_t,Y_t)\mid H_{t-1})\). If \(\Delta_t^2\leq\Gamma g_t\) almost surely for every \(t\), then
\[\operatorname{BayesRegret}(T)\leq\sqrt{\Gamma T\,I(X^*;H_T)}\leq\sqrt{\Gamma T\,H(X^*)}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Posterior sampling has square-root Bayesian regret when its one-step squared regret is controlled by information gained about the optimal action.
assumptions_latex: \(X_t\mid H_{t-1}\) has the posterior distribution of \(X^*\).
\(\Delta_t^2\leq\Gamma g_t\) almost surely for every round.

notation.meaning: Conditional information gained about the optimal action.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The information-ratio complexity bound fits posterior-sampling regret, but the theorem requires an authoritative locator. The entropy inequality particularly requires a discrete optimal action with finite Shannon entropy, not merely an unspecified finite entropy condition.

children.title: Information-Policy Approximation Guarantees
children.top_down_role: Guarantees and approximation boundaries for entropy, mutual-information, and lookahead policies.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robust cardinality-constrained greedy submodular-information bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F:2^V\to\mathbb R_+ be normalized, monotone, and submodular. If at step t the selected element's marginal gain is within \varepsilon_t\ge0 of the largest available marginal, then the resulting size-T set A_T satisfies F(A_T)\ge(1-(1-1/T)^T)\max_{|A|\le T}F(A)-\sum_{t=1}^T\varepsilon_t\ge(1-e^{-1})\max_{|A|\le T}F(A)-\sum_{t=1}^T\varepsilon_t.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate greedy information maximization retains the standard approximation factor up to accumulated marginal-selection errors.
assumptions_latex: F is normalized, monotone, and submodular.
The constraint is a cardinality budget T.
The selected marginal is within \varepsilon_t of the best available marginal.

notation.meaning: Additive marginal-selection error at step t.
Best value among sets of cardinality at most T.

knowledge_statements.title: Additive-Error Greedy Information Guarantee

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additional structure required for observation-adaptive greedy policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonadaptive submodular set-function guarantee does not automatically apply when later queries depend on realized observations. An adaptive-greedy approximation requires the observation-conditioned utility to satisfy the relevant adaptive monotonicity and adaptive submodularity conditions; submodularity of the prior-averaged set function alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive information policies require adaptive-submodularity-type assumptions; ordinary set submodularity is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: Later query choices may depend on earlier observations.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive-Greedy Guarantee Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Information Approximation Does Not Certify Optimization Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between information-objective approximation and terminal optimization performance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A bound F(A_T)\ge c\max_{|A|\le T}F(A) for an information utility implies no bound on terminal simple regret or Bayes risk unless an additional comparison theorem links that utility to the declared terminal loss. High-entropy latent components can dominate F while leaving optimizer-relevant uncertainty unresolved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant-factor information guarantee is not by itself a terminal optimization-quality guarantee.
assumptions_latex: The approximation bound concerns an information utility.
No comparison inequality links that utility to terminal optimization loss.
knowledge_statements.title: Information Approximation Does Not Certify Optimization Loss
Information-Policy Approximation Guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy approximation for GP mutual-information design; not automatically applicable to optimizer entropy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V\) be a finite candidate set, let \(f_V\) be jointly Gaussian, and let \(y_x=f(x)+\varepsilon_x\) with independent Gaussian noises of positive variance. Then \(F(A)=I(y_A;f_V)\) is normalized, monotone, and submodular on subsets \(A\subseteq V\). If \(A_g\) is formed by greedily adding the point of largest conditional information gain until \(|A_g|=T\), then
\[F(A_g)\geq(1-e^{-1})\max_{A\subseteq V,\,|A|\leq T}F(A).\]
This guarantee does not follow merely by replacing \(f_V\) with the nonlinear optimizer variable \(X^*\), because the resulting objective need not be submodular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain:
Greedy GP information collection attains a 1
-
1/e approximation for latent-value information, but the guarantee need not extend to information about the optimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite and \(f_V\) is jointly Gaussian.
Observation noises are independent Gaussian variables with positive variance.
The policy greedily maximizes exact marginal information gain.

notation.meaning: Mutual information between selected observations and all latent values.
Random optimizer of the latent objective.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role fits the approximation-guarantee leaf. Both the greedy submodular-information guarantee and the claimed nonextension to optimizer information require specific sources; none are provided.
