children.title: Kernel-Dependent Regret Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Lower-bound regimes determined by kernel regularity and effective dimension.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degenerate kernel showing that no positive kernel-independent regret lower bound is universal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(k(x,x')=c>0\) on a nonempty domain, every function in \(\mathcal H_k\) is constant. Consequently every action is optimal and cumulative and simple regret are identically zero for every policy and horizon, irrespective of observation noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The constant kernel contains only constant objectives, so optimization regret is always zero.
assumptions_latex: \(k(x,x')=c>0\) for all \(x,x'\).
The objective belongs to \(\mathcal H_k\).
knowledge_statements.title: Constant-Kernel Zero-Regret Class

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm and information constraints required for a valid kernel lower-bound construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proposed hard packing with amplitude \(\Delta\) establishes an RKHS lower bound only if every hard function satisfies the declared radius and the induced observation laws meet the information-divergence condition used by the lower-bound argument. For a diagonal kernel this includes \(\sum_i g_i^2/\lambda_i\le B^2\). Omitting this constraint can place the bandit instance outside the asserted RKHS ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bandit-style hard family is valid only when its gaps fit the RKHS radius and its observation laws satisfy the required indistinguishability bound.
assumptions_latex: The minimax class is \(\{f:\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le B\}\).
The lower-bound argument uses a finite hard family and an information comparison.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists f\text{ in the packing with }\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}>B\Longrightarrow\text{the packing does not prove the stated RKHS bound}.
knowledge_statements.title: RKHS Hard-Instance Compatibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of a valid hard subclass into a minimax regret lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a common action and observation model and function classes \(\mathcal F_0\subseteq\mathcal F\), \[\inf_\pi\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb E_fR_T(\pi)\ge \inf_\pi\sup_{f\in\mathcal F_0}\mathbb E_fR_T(\pi).\] Therefore a finite hard family yields a lower bound for the full RKHS ball only after every hard function and its observation law have been embedded in that full problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid minimax lower bound on an embedded hard subclass lower-bounds the full kernel class.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F_0\subseteq\mathcal F\).
The policy space, action domain, observation law, and regret definition are inherited from the full problem.

notation.meaning: Hard subclass embedded in the full function class.

knowledge_statements.title: Hard-Subclass Restriction Principle

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact correspondence between a diagonal finite-domain kernel and a constrained stochastic bandit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the entire decision domain be \(\mathcal X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_M\}\) and suppose \(k(x_i,x_j)=\lambda_i\mathbf1\{i=j\}\) with \(\lambda_i>0\). A value vector \(g=(g_1,\ldots,g_M)\) then has RKHS norm \[\|g\|_{\mathcal H_k}^2=\sum_{i=1}^M\frac{g_i^2}{\lambda_i}.\] With independent Gaussian observation noise, optimization on this domain is exactly an \(M\)-armed Gaussian bandit subject to this ellipsoidal norm constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A diagonal kernel on the full finite decision domain is exactly a constrained multi-armed Gaussian bandit.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_M\}\).
\(k(x_i,x_j)=\lambda_i\mathbf1\{i=j\}\) with \(\lambda_i>0\).
The observation noise matches the stated Gaussian bandit model.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Domain Diagonal-Kernel Reduction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary showing that persistent rank-dependent lower bounds require noise or another information restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(k(x,x')=\phi(x)^\top\phi(x')\) has rank \(r<\infty\), every objective has form \(f_\theta(x)=\theta^\top\phi(x)\), and \(\phi(x_1),\ldots,\phi(x_r)\) are linearly independent. Exact evaluation at these \(r\) points uniquely identifies \(\theta\). Therefore a policy that evaluates this spanning design and can globally minimize the identified function has zero terminal simple regret from evaluation \(r\) onward. Kernel rank alone cannot imply a persistent noiseless simple-regret lower bound in this identifiable regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spanning set of r exact evaluations identifies a rank-r RKHS objective, so persistent rank-based simple-regret lower bounds need noise or another restriction.
assumptions_latex: The kernel has an exact rank-\(r\) feature map.
The objective lies in the associated finite-dimensional RKHS.
Observations are noiseless and a spanning evaluation design is used.
The identified objective can be globally minimized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\ge r\Longrightarrow r_T=0\text{ for the spanning-design identification policy}.
knowledge_statements.title: Noiseless Finite-Rank Identification Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain cumulative-regret lower-bound regime for the identity kernel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal X=\{1,\ldots,M\}\), \(k(i,j)=\mathbf1\{i=j\}\), and \(\mathcal F_B=\{f:\sum_{i=1}^Mf(i)^2\le B^2\}\). Under conditionally independent \(N(0,\sigma^2)\) observation noise, there is a universal constant \(c>0\) such that for \(T\ge M\ge2\),
\[
\inf_\pi\sup_{f\in\mathcal F_B}\mathbb E_fR_T(\pi)\ge c\min\{BT,\sigma\sqrt{MT}\}.
\]
Here \(R_T\) is cumulative maximization regret. The two regimes require hard-instance amplitudes bounded respectively by the RKHS radius and the Gaussian indistinguishability scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the rank-M identity kernel, minimax cumulative regret has a radius-limited linear regime and a noisy square-root rank regime.
assumptions_latex: \(T\ge M\ge2\).
The full decision domain is the M-point set and the kernel is the identity kernel.
Observations have independent Gaussian noise with variance \(\sigma^2>0\).
Regret is cumulative maximization regret.

notation.meaning: Kernel rank and number of independent arms.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Rank Independent-Arm Minimax Lower Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural criterion embedding one RKHS ball into another and transferring minimax regret lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k_1,k_2\) be kernels on the same domain and suppose \(k_2-k_1\) is positive semidefinite. Then \(\mathcal H_{k_1}\subseteq\mathcal H_{k_2}\) and \(\|f\|_{\mathcal H_{k_2}}\leq\|f\|_{\mathcal H_{k_1}}\) for every \(f\in\mathcal H_{k_1}\). Consequently, \(\{f:\|f\|_{\mathcal H_{k_1}}\leq B\}\subseteq\{f:\|f\|_{\mathcal H_{k_2}}\leq B\}\), so every valid minimax regret lower bound for the first ball transfers to the second under the same decision and observation model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive-semidefinite kernel domination embeds the first RKHS ball in the second, allowing valid lower bounds to transfer.
assumptions_latex: \(k_1\) and \(k_2\) are kernels on the same action domain.
\(k_2-k_1\) is positive semidefinite.
The compared problems have the same policy space, observation model, and regret definition.
knowledge_statements.title: Kernel-Domination Transfer of Lower Bounds
Kernel-Dependent Regret Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-rank kernel lower bound obtained from the independent-arm kernel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\{1,\ldots,M\}\), let \(k(i,j)=\mathbf 1\{i=j\}\), and consider objectives in the RKHS ball \(\{f:\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\leq B\}\). Observations are \(Y_t=f(X_t)+\varepsilon_t\) with independent \(N(0,\sigma^2)\) noise. There exists a universal constant \(c>0\) such that, in the nontrivial regime \(T\geq M\geq2\), every adaptive policy satisfies a minimax lower bound of the form
\[\sup_{\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\leq B}\mathbb E_f[R_T]\geq c\min\{BT,\sigma\sqrt{MT}\},\]
up to the compatibility of the hard-instance gap with the RKHS radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the rank-M independent-arm kernel, no adaptive policy can avoid the classical square-root dependence on kernel rank and horizon.
assumptions_latex: \(k(i,j)=\mathbf 1\{i=j\}\) on an M-point domain.
\(\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\leq B\) and noise is \(N(0,\sigma^2)\).
\(T\geq M\geq2\).

notation.meaning: Rank and number of independent kernel coordinates.
RKHS induced by the independent-arm kernel.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A complexity bound is appropriate for this lower-bound leaf, but the displayed minimax rate cannot be accepted without a precise lower-bound theorem. The phrase about compatibility of the hard-instance gap with the RKHS radius leaves essential parameter conditions unstated.

children.title: Regularity-Noise Complexity Limits
children.top_down_role: Deterioration of attainable performance with dimension, weak regularity, and observation noise.

children.title: Dimensionality Limits
children.top_down_role: Attainable-performance deterioration associated with increasing problem dimension.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructive noiseless upper bound for full-dimensional Lipschitz optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[0,1]^d\), let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) be \(L\)-Lipschitz, and let \(S_T\subset X\) have covering radius \(h_T:=\sup_{x\in X}\min_{s\in S_T}\|x-s\|_2\). If \(\widehat x_T\in\arg\min_{s\in S_T}f(s)\), then \[f(\widehat x_T)-\min_{x\in X}f(x)\le Lh_T.\] Regular grids with at most \(T\) points can achieve \(h_T\le C_dT^{-1/d}\), and therefore simple regret at most \(C_dLT^{-1/d}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluating a covering net gives Lipschitz simple regret proportional to its covering radius, yielding the ambient-dimensional rate T^{-1/d} on a cube.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz in Euclidean distance.
Every point in \(S_T\) is evaluated without noise.

notation.meaning: covering radius of the evaluated set

knowledge_statements.title: Covering-Net Upper Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Indistinguishable objective family behind the deterministic ambient-dimensional lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Run a deterministic \(T\)-query algorithm on the zero function over \([0,1]^d\), and let \(S\) contain its queried points and returned point. There are \(z\in[0,1]^d\) and \(r\ge c_d(T+1)^{-1/d}\) such that every point of \(S\) is at least \(r\) from \(z\). The function \[f_z(x)=-L\max\{0,r-\|x-z\|_2\}\] is \(L\)-Lipschitz and is zero on \(S\), but has minimum \(-Lr\) at \(z\). Hence the algorithm's simple regret is at least \(c_dL(T+1)^{-1/d}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unseen Lipschitz well can be placed away from all queried and returned points, yielding the dimensional lower rate.
assumptions_latex: The domain is \([0,1]^d\).
The algorithm is deterministic and observations are exact.
The objective class contains all \(L\)-Lipschitz functions.

notation.meaning: query points and returned point on the zero transcript
distance from an unsampled center to S

knowledge_statements.title: Unsampled-Ball Lipschitz Adversary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected simple-regret lower bound for randomized noiseless policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(d\ge1\), there is \(c_d>0\) such that every possibly randomized policy making at most \(T\) noiseless evaluations on \([0,1]^d\) and returning \(\widehat x_T\) satisfies
\[
\sup_{f:\operatorname{Lip}(f)\le L}\mathbb E\left[f(\widehat x_T)-\min_xf(x)\right]\ge c_dL(T+1)^{-1/d}.
\]
The expectation includes the policy's randomization. Thus randomization does not improve the minimax dimensional exponent for the unrestricted Lipschitz class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomized noiseless optimization of arbitrary Lipschitz functions retains the ambient-dimensional expected simple-regret rate.
assumptions_latex: The domain is \([0,1]^d\).
The objective class contains all real-valued \(L\)-Lipschitz functions.
The expectation includes algorithmic randomization.
Observations are noiseless.

notation.meaning: Positive packing constant depending only on dimension.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Lipschitz Dimensional Lower Bound
Dimensionality Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case noiseless global optimization over a full-dimensional Lipschitz domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d,T\geq 1\) and \(X=[0,1]^d\). For every deterministic algorithm that makes at most \(T\) adaptive, noiseless function evaluations and returns \(\widehat x_T\in X\), there exist a constant \(c_d>0\) and an \(L\)-Lipschitz function \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) such that its simple regret satisfies \[f(\widehat x_T)-\min_{x\in X}f(x)\geq c_d L(T+1)^{-1/d}.\] Thus uniform worst-case accuracy \(\varepsilon\) requires order at least \((L/\varepsilon)^d\) evaluations; the ambient dimension appears in the exponent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Worst-case Lipschitz optimization in dimension d needs exponentially many evaluations in d to attain fixed accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz in Euclidean distance.
The algorithm is deterministic and observations are noiseless.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and dimensional lower-bound role fit the leaf, but no source is supplied for the exact deterministic minimax statement, quantifiers, or dimension-dependent constant.

children.title: Smoothness Limits
children.top_down_role: Attainable-performance deterioration under weak objective regularity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructive noiseless optimization rate under Hölder regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[0,1]^d\) and suppose \(|f(x)-f(y)|\le L\|x-y\|_2^\alpha\) for \(0<\alpha\le1\). If \(S_T\) has covering radius \(h_T\) and \(\widehat x_T\) is its best evaluated point, then \[f(\widehat x_T)-\min_X f\le Lh_T^\alpha.\] A regular grid with at most \(T\) points can achieve \(h_T\le C_dT^{-1/d}\), and hence regret at most \(LC_d^\alpha T^{-\alpha/d}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A covering design for an alpha-Hölder objective attains simple regret of order T^{-alpha/d}.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\alpha\le1\).
\(f\) is \((L,\alpha)\)-Hölder and observations are noiseless.

notation.meaning: covering radius of the evaluated design

knowledge_statements.title: Hölder Covering Upper Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic optimization guarantee for a general shared modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,\rho)\) be compact and suppose \(|f(x)-f(y)|\le\omega(\rho(x,y))\), where \(\omega\) is nondecreasing and \(\omega(0)=0\). If \(S\) is an \(h\)-net and \(\widehat x\in\arg\min_{s\in S}f(s)\), then \[f(\widehat x)-\min_X f\le\omega(h).\] Consequently, any \(h\) satisfying \(\omega(h)\le\varepsilon\) yields accuracy \(\varepsilon\) after at most \(N(X,\rho,h)\) exact evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a shared modulus of continuity, simple regret is bounded by the modulus evaluated at the design's covering radius.
assumptions_latex: \((X,\rho)\) is compact.
\(\omega\) is a common nondecreasing modulus for the objective class.
Observations are exact.
knowledge_statements.title: Modulus-of-Continuity Covering Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: No Uniform Rate without a Shared Modulus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hidden-well boundary for continuous black-box optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a deterministic algorithm make finitely many exact evaluations on \([0,1]^d\) and return \(\widehat x\). On its zero-function transcript, choose an open ball containing none of the queried points or \(\widehat x\). For every \(M>0\), there exists a continuous bump supported in that ball, equal to zero at all queried points and at \(\widehat x\), and having minimum \(-M\). The transcript is unchanged while the simple regret is \(M\). Thus continuity without a common modulus or range bound gives no finite uniform simple-regret guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An arbitrarily deep continuous well can be hidden between finitely many samples, so continuity alone supplies no uniform optimization rate.
assumptions_latex: The domain has nonempty interior.
The algorithm is deterministic and uses finitely many exact evaluations.
The class imposes continuity but no common modulus or range bound.
knowledge_statements.title: No Uniform Rate without a Shared Modulus

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Randomized-policy extension of the hidden-well boundary for finite exact-evaluation optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a randomized algorithm make at most \(T<\infty\) exact evaluations on \(X=[0,1]^d\) and return \(\widehat x_T\). If the objective class is \(C(X)\), with neither a common modulus of continuity nor a range bound, then for every \(M>0\) there exists \(f\in C(X)\) such that \[\mathbb E\!\left[f(\widehat x_T)-\min_{x\in X}f(x)\right]\ge M.\] Hence randomization alone cannot provide a finite uniform expected simple-regret guarantee over this class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomized finite-query optimization still has unbounded worst-case expected regret over continuous functions lacking a shared modulus or range bound.
assumptions_latex: The algorithm uses at most \(T<\infty\) exact evaluations and may randomize adaptively.
The function class imposes continuity but no common modulus or range bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Randomized No-Shared-Modulus Impossibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone nesting of Hölder classes on a normalized bounded domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,\rho)\) have diameter at most one and let \(0<\alpha_1\leq\alpha_2\leq1\). If \(|f(x)-f(y)|\leq L\rho(x,y)^{\alpha_2}\) for all \(x,y\in X\), then \(|f(x)-f(y)|\leq L\rho(x,y)^{\alpha_1}\). Thus \(\mathcal H(L,\alpha_2)\subseteq\mathcal H(L,\alpha_1)\), and minimax simple-regret risk over the smoother class cannot exceed that over the rougher class under the same observation model and budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a unit-diameter domain, increasing the Hölder exponent shrinks the function class and cannot worsen minimax optimization risk.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{diam}_\rho(X)\le1\).
\(0<\alpha_1\le\alpha_2\le1\).
The compared minimax problems have the same observations, policies, budget, and regret mode.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal H(L,\alpha_2)\subseteq\mathcal H(L,\alpha_1)\Longrightarrow\mathfrak R_T(\mathcal H(L,\alpha_2))\le\mathfrak R_T(\mathcal H(L,\alpha_1)).

notation.meaning: Class of functions with Hölder constant L and exponent alpha.

knowledge_statements.title: Hölder-Class Ordering by Smoothness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Function-class definition underlying noiseless smoothness-limited optimization rates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((X,\rho)\) be a metric space, \(L\ge0\), and \(0<\alpha\le1\). Define
\[
\mathcal H_X(L,\alpha):=\left\{f:X\to\mathbb R:|f(x)-f(y)|\le L\rho(x,y)^\alpha\ \text{for all }x,y\in X\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, its members share the modulus \(\omega(r)=Lr^\alpha\). With \([f]_{C^{0,\alpha}}:=\sup_{x\ne y}|f(x)-f(y)|/\rho(x,y)^\alpha\), one has \(f\in\mathcal H_X(L,\alpha)\) exactly when \([f]_{C^{0,\alpha}}\le L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An alpha-Hölder class consists of functions sharing the modulus L times distance to the alpha power, equivalently functions whose Hölder seminorm is at most L.
assumptions_latex: \((X,\rho)\) is a metric space.
\(L\ge0\) and \(0<\alpha\le1\).

notation.meaning: Uniform alpha-Hölder function class with constant L.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Hölder Class

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected simple-regret lower bound matching the covering rate for noiseless Hölder optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(d\ge1\), \(0<\alpha\le1\), and \(L>0\). There is a constant \(c_{d,\alpha}>0\) such that every possibly randomized adaptive policy using at most \(T\ge1\) noiseless evaluations on \([0,1]^d\) satisfies
\[
\sup_{f\in\mathcal H_{[0,1]^d}(L,\alpha)}\mathbb E\!\left[f(\widehat x_T)-\min_{x\in[0,1]^d}f(x)\right]
\ge c_{d,\alpha}L(T+1)^{-\alpha/d}.
\]
Consequently, uniform expected accuracy \(\varepsilon\) requires order at least \((L/\varepsilon)^{d/\alpha}\) exact evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even randomized noiseless optimization over an alpha-Hölder ball has worst-case expected simple regret of order at least T to the minus alpha over d.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\alpha\le1\) and the objective belongs to \(\mathcal H_X(L,\alpha)\).
The policy uses at most \(T\) exact evaluations and may randomize adaptively.

notation.meaning: uniform alpha-Hölder ball with constant L

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Hölder Minimax Lower Bound
Smoothness Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hölder-regularity dependence of deterministic black-box optimization rates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(0<\alpha\leq1\), \(d,T\geq1\), and \(X=[0,1]^d\). For every deterministic algorithm using at most \(T\) noiseless evaluations, there exist \(c_{d,\alpha}>0\) and a function satisfying \(|f(x)-f(y)|\leq L\|x-y\|_2^\alpha\) for which \[f(\widehat x_T)-\min_{x\in X}f(x)\geq c_{d,\alpha}L(T+1)^{-\alpha/d}.\] Consequently, weaker Hölder smoothness decreases the attainable exponent, and accuracy \(\varepsilon\) requires order at least \((L/\varepsilon)^{d/\alpha}\) evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For alpha-Hölder objectives, worst-case simple regret cannot decrease faster than order T to the minus alpha over d.
assumptions_latex: \(|f(x)-f(y)|\leq L\|x-y\|_2^\alpha\).
Evaluations are noiseless and the algorithm is deterministic.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits, but the exact Hölder minimax rate and constant require an inspectable authoritative source.

children.title: Observation-Noise Limits
children.top_down_role: Attainable-performance deterioration caused by uncertain evaluations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-location observation complexity under independent sub-Gaussian noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Y_i=f(x)+\xi_i\), where \(\xi_i\) are independent, mean-zero, \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian errors, then for \(\bar Y_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nY_i\), \[\Pr\{|\bar Y_n-f(x)|>\varepsilon\}\le2\exp\!\left(-\frac{n\varepsilon^2}{2\sigma^2}\right).\] Hence \(n\ge2\sigma^2\varepsilon^{-2}\log(2/\delta)\) suffices for error at most \(\varepsilon\) with probability at least \(1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resolving even one latent objective value under sub-Gaussian observation noise requires inverse-square replication in the desired accuracy.
assumptions_latex: The errors are independent, mean zero, and \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian.
knowledge_statements.title: Replication Accuracy Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robust fixed-location estimation when sub-Gaussian tails are unavailable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\) be independent with common mean \(\mu\) and variance at most \(\sigma^2\). Partition them into \(k\) disjoint blocks of common size \(m\), compute the block means, and return their median \(\widehat\mu_{\mathrm{MOM}}\). If \(m\ge4\sigma^2/\varepsilon^2\) and \(k\ge8\log(1/\delta)\), then \[\Pr\{|\widehat\mu_{\mathrm{MOM}}-\mu|>\varepsilon\}\le\delta.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Median-of-means obtains logarithmic-confidence accuracy under independent finite-variance noise without sub-Gaussian tails.
assumptions_latex: Observations are independent with a common mean.
Each observation has variance at most \(\sigma^2\).
Blocks are disjoint and have equal integer size.

notation.meaning: block size and number of blocks

knowledge_statements.title: Median-of-Means Accuracy under Finite Variance

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Variance Does Not Give a Sub-Gaussian Sample-Mean Radius
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tail-assumption boundary of ordinary replication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p\in(0,1)\), let \(\xi\) equal \(a\) and \(-a\) with probability \(p/2\) each and zero otherwise, where \(a=\sigma/\sqrt p\). Then \(\mathbb E\xi=0\), \(\operatorname{Var}(\xi)=\sigma^2\), and \(\Pr(|\xi|=a)=p\). As \(p\downarrow0\), finite variance permits increasingly rare and large outliers; therefore a variance bound alone does not imply a sub-Gaussian tail bound with scale \(\sigma\), nor the corresponding uniform sub-Gaussian confidence radius for ordinary sample means.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-variance noise may have rare large outliers, so ordinary sample means do not receive sub-Gaussian confidence bounds without stronger assumptions.
assumptions_latex: Only zero mean and variance \(\sigma^2\) are imposed.
The noise law may be heavy-tailed.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Variance Does Not Give a Sub-Gaussian Sample-Mean Radius

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-location mean estimation under conditionally sub-Gaussian dependent noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Y_t=f(x)+\xi_t\) be repeated evaluations at a fixed point, adapted to \((\mathcal F_t)\), and suppose
\[
\mathbb E[e^{\lambda\xi_t}\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\le e^{\lambda^2\sigma^2/2}
\quad\text{almost surely for every }\lambda\in\mathbb R.
\]
Then
\[
\Pr\left(\left|n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^nY_t-f(x)\right|>\varepsilon\right)\le2e^{-n\varepsilon^2/(2\sigma^2)}.
\]
Thus independence may be replaced by the displayed conditional moment-generating-function condition; arbitrary dependence receives no such guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inverse-square replication rate survives dependent noise when increments are conditionally sub-Gaussian martingale differences.
assumptions_latex: The noise sequence is adapted.
The displayed conditional sub-Gaussian bound holds almost surely.
The latent value \(f(x)\) remains fixed during replication.
knowledge_statements.title: Martingale-Difference Replication Accuracy

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Adaptive Two-Hypothesis Gaussian Noise Lower Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-confidence inverse-square observation lower bound under adaptive sampling and stopping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider two actions and hypotheses \(H_1:(0,\Delta)\) and \(H_2:(\Delta,0)\) for minimization, with independent \(N(\mu,\sigma^2)\) observations. Let an adaptive procedure stop at \(N\) and recommend the better action with error probability at most \(\delta<1/2\) under both hypotheses. If \(P_i\) is the transcript law under \(H_i\), then
\[
D(P_1\|P_2)=\frac{\Delta^2}{2\sigma^2}\mathbb E_1N.
\]
Data processing through the recommendation gives
\[
\mathbb E_1N\ge\frac{2\sigma^2}{\Delta^2}\operatorname{kl}(1-\delta,\delta).
\]
The analogous inequality holds under \(H_2\), establishing the \(\sigma^2\Delta^{-2}\log(1/\delta)\) fixed-confidence scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even with adaptive allocation and stopping, reliably distinguishing two Gaussian objective values requires inverse-square sampling in their gap.
assumptions_latex: Observations are conditionally independent Gaussian with common known variance \(\sigma^2>0\).
The stopping time has finite expectation under both hypotheses.
The recommendation error is at most \(\delta<1/2\) under both hypotheses.

notation.meaning: Adaptive transcript law under hypothesis i.
Total number of observations before stopping.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Two-Hypothesis Gaussian Noise Lower Bound
Observation-Noise Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-point Gaussian testing lower bound underlying noisy optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two candidate points and two hypotheses with mean vectors \((0,\Delta)\) and \((\Delta,0)\), where each observation has independent variance \(\sigma^2\). If an adaptive procedure uses \(N\) total observations and selects the lower-mean point with error probability at most \(\delta<1/2\) under both hypotheses, then change of measure gives \[\frac{\Delta^2}{2\sigma^2}\max_i\mathbb E_i[N]\geq \operatorname{kl}(1-\delta,\delta).\] Hence resolving an objective gap \(\Delta\) at fixed confidence requires order \(\sigma^2\Delta^{-2}\) observations even before spatial search is considered.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gaussian noise alone forces inverse-square sampling in the objective gap needed to identify the better point reliably.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\mid x\sim\mathcal N(f(x),\sigma^2)\) independently conditional on chosen points.
The two hypotheses interchange means \(0\) and \(\Delta>0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-hypothesis noise lower bound fits the leaf, but the precise adaptive change-of-measure inequality and constant have no cited source.

children.title: Effective-Dimension Regimes
children.top_down_role: Performance limits governed by intrinsic rather than ambient dimensional structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization complexity governed by covering growth in an intrinsic metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,\rho)\) be compact, let \(f\) be \(L\)-Lipschitz in \(\rho\), and suppose \(N(X,\rho,\varepsilon)\le C\varepsilon^{-k}\) for \(0<\varepsilon\le1\). Evaluating an \(\varepsilon\)-net and returning its best point uses at most \(C\varepsilon^{-k}\) evaluations and has simple regret at most \(L\varepsilon\). Thus the constructive exponent is governed by \(k\), rather than an ambient coordinate count.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomial covering growth with exponent k yields a covering-design complexity governed by k instead of ambient dimension.
assumptions_latex: \((X,\rho)\) is compact.
\(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz in \(\rho\).
\(N(X,\rho,\varepsilon)\le C\varepsilon^{-k}\) for \(0<\varepsilon\le1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\ge C\varepsilon^{-k}\implies f(\widehat x_T)-\min_X f\le L\varepsilon.
knowledge_statements.title: Metric-Entropy Effective Dimension

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundary for projection-based effective dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^k\) have nontrivial nullspace, and suppose the domain contains distinct points \(x,x'\) with \(Px=Px'\). There exists an objective varying along a discarded direction for which \(f(x)\ne f(x')\); such an objective cannot be represented as \(\bar f\circ P\). Consequently, a projection-only policy that selects the inferior representative of this fiber can incur the positive gap \(|f(x)-f(x')|\), which cannot be removed using projected coordinates alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the objective varies in a discarded direction, points with identical projected coordinates can have different values, invalidating projection-only optimization.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) has rank less than \(d\).
The domain contains two distinct points in one projection fiber.
The objective class permits variation along a nullspace direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Discarded-Direction Optimization Failure

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Packing Lower Bound under Intrinsic Metric Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matching noiseless lower exponent when the metric space contains polynomially many separated regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((X,\rho)\) contain, for all sufficiently small \(\varepsilon\), at least \(c\varepsilon^{-k}\) points with pairwise distance greater than \(2\varepsilon\). For the class of all \(L\)-Lipschitz functions and noiseless evaluation, there is \(c'>0\) such that every possibly randomized \(T\)-query policy satisfies
\[
\sup_f\mathbb E r_T\ge c'LT^{-1/k}.
\]
Together with the prior Metric-Entropy Effective Dimension upper bound, polynomial covering and packing growth with exponent \(k\) gives matching intrinsic-dimensional simple-regret exponents.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomial metric packing growth forces the same intrinsic-dimensional exponent achieved by an epsilon-net design.
assumptions_latex: The metric packing lower bound holds uniformly at sufficiently small scales.
The objective class contains all \(L\)-Lipschitz functions in \(\rho\).
Observations are noiseless.
knowledge_statements.title: Packing Lower Bound under Intrinsic Metric Growth

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularized dimension determined by kernel-eigenvalue mass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a positive-semidefinite kernel matrix or covariance operator with eigenvalues \(\lambda_j\ge0\) and regularization level \(\eta>0\), define
\[
d_{\mathrm{eff}}(\eta)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(K(K+\eta I)^{-1}\bigr)=\sum_j\frac{\lambda_j}{\lambda_j+\eta}.
\]
When the trace is finite, \(d_{\mathrm{eff}}(\eta)\) lies between zero and the algebraic rank and measures directions whose eigenvalues are large relative to \(\eta\). It is scale dependent and need not equal projection rank, ambient dimension, or a metric-entropy exponent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Spectral effective dimension is the regularized sum of kernel eigenvalue leverage factors and depends on resolution scale.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is positive semidefinite and the displayed trace is finite.

notation.meaning: Spectral effective dimension at regularization scale eta.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Effective Dimension

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact posterior and pointwise-acquisition reduction under a known linear projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^k\) have rank \(k<d\). Suppose \(m(x)=\bar m(Px)\), \(K(x,x')=\bar K(Px,Px')\), and the likelihood at input \(x\) depends on the input only through \(Px\). Then the posterior marginal law of \(f(x)\) is identical for points in the same fiber \(P^{-1}\{z\}\). Hence every pointwise acquisition that is a fixed functional of this posterior marginal factors as \(a_n(x)=\bar a_n(Px)\), and
\[
\sup_{x\in X}a_n(x)=\sup_{z\in P(X)}\bar a_n(z).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A correctly projected GP and likelihood make posterior marginals and pointwise acquisitions constant along projection fibers.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is fixed and known.
The prior mean, covariance, and likelihood factor through \(P\).
The acquisition depends only on posterior marginal quantities that factor through \(P\).
knowledge_statements.title: Projected-GP Fiber Invariance

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scale Monotonicity of Spectral Effective Dimension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resolution dependence of regularized kernel effective dimension for a finite positive-semidefinite matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\succeq0\) be a finite matrix with eigenvalues \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n\), and let \(d_{\mathrm{eff}}(\eta)=\sum_{j=1}^n\lambda_j/(\lambda_j+\eta)\) for \(\eta>0\). Then \(d_{\mathrm{eff}}\) is nonincreasing and
\[
\frac{d}{d\eta}d_{\mathrm{eff}}(\eta)=-\sum_{j=1}^n\frac{\lambda_j}{(\lambda_j+\eta)^2}\le0.
\]
Moreover, \(\lim_{\eta\downarrow0}d_{\mathrm{eff}}(\eta)=\operatorname{rank}(K)\) and \(\lim_{\eta\to\infty}d_{\mathrm{eff}}(\eta)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Spectral effective dimension decreases as regularization increases, interpolating between algebraic rank and zero.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a finite positive-semidefinite matrix.

notation.meaning: spectral effective dimension at regularization scale eta

knowledge_statements.title: Scale Monotonicity of Spectral Effective Dimension
Effective-Dimension Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected Gaussian-process models whose acquisition search has lower intrinsic dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^k\) be linear with rank \(k<d\). Suppose a Gaussian-process prior has mean \(m(x)=\bar m(Px)\) and kernel \(K(x,x')=\bar K(Px,Px')\), and observations depend on inputs only through \(Px\). Then the posterior mean and variance are constant on every fiber \(\{x:Px=z\}\). Any pointwise acquisition depending only on these posterior quantities factors as \(a_t(x)=\bar a_t(Px)\), so maximizing it over \(X\) is equivalent to maximizing \(\bar a_t(z)\) over \(P(X)\subseteq\mathbb R^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projected GP model makes posterior quantities and pointwise acquisitions depend on intrinsic dimension k rather than ambient dimension d.
assumptions_latex: \(P\in\mathbb R^{k\times d}\) has rank \(k<d\).
\(m(x)=\bar m(Px)\) and \(K(x,x')=\bar K(Px,Px')\).
The likelihood depends on \(x\) only through \(Px\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_t=\bar a_t\circ P\) and \(\sup_{x\in X}a_t(x)=\sup_{z\in P(X)}\bar a_t(z)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits an effective-dimension regime and is mathematically plausible, but no source supports the posterior fiber-invariance and acquisition-factorization claim.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed information-capacity bound controlled by algebraic kernel rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_A\succeq0\) be the kernel matrix of a size-\(T\) design, with \(\operatorname{rank}(K_A)\le r\), \(k(x,x)\le\kappa^2\), and Gaussian noise variance \(\eta>0\). Then \[\frac12\log\det(I+\eta^{-1}K_A)\leq\frac r2\log\!\left(1+\frac{T\kappa^2}{r\eta}\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-rank kernel has information gain bounded in terms of its rank.
assumptions_latex: \(K_A\succeq0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(K_A)\le r\).
\(k(x,x)\le\kappa^2\).
Gaussian observation-noise variance is \(\eta>0\).

notation.meaning: Uniform algebraic rank bound for design kernel matrices.
Maximum information gain from T noisy observations.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Rank Information-Gain Bound

intermediate_metadata.reason: The local inventory covers projection, metric-entropy, and scale-dependent spectral notions of effective dimension, matching metric upper/lower exponents, and projection failure. The proposed finite-rank information-gain inequality is mathematically sound but deferred as canonically owned by Spectral Information Complexity. Ambient-dimensional, smoothness, and observation-noise limits were excluded as sibling scopes.

children.title: Statistical-Computational Performance Gaps
children.top_down_role: Loss of theoretical performance caused by surrogate approximation or inexact acquisition optimization.

children.title: Surrogate Approximation Gaps
children.top_down_role: Performance loss attributable to approximate surrogate representations or inference.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Surrogate Consistency Is Insufficient for Recommendation Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of minimizer selection under pointwise surrogate convergence without uniform or variational control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There exist functions \(f,\widetilde f_n:[0,1]\to\mathbb R\) such that \(\widetilde f_n(x)\to f(x)\) for every fixed \(x\), while for choices \(\widehat x_n\in\arg\min_x\widetilde f_n(x)\), \[\limsup_{n\to\infty}\left(f(\widehat x_n)-\min_xf(x)\right)>0.\] Hence pointwise surrogate convergence alone does not imply objective-value consistency of surrogate recommendations; suitable uniform or epigraphical control can restore such conclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A surrogate may converge at every fixed point while moving approximation artifacts keep its minimizers truly suboptimal.
assumptions_latex: Only pointwise convergence \(\widetilde f_n(x)\to f(x)\) is assumed.
Each recommendation globally minimizes its approximate surrogate.

notation.meaning: global minimizer of the approximate surrogate

knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Surrogate Consistency Is Insufficient for Recommendation Consistency

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recommendation-gap control from unequal lower and upper surrogate errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \[-\eta_-\leq f(x)-\widetilde f(x)\leq\eta_+\quad(x\in X).\] If \(\widetilde f(\widehat x)\leq\inf_X\widetilde f+\delta\), then \[f(\widehat x)-\inf_Xf\leq\eta_++\eta_-+\delta.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Upper and lower surrogate-envelope errors contribute separately to the true recommendation gap.
assumptions_latex: \(X\neq\varnothing\).
\(\eta_+,\eta_-,\delta\geq0\).
The displayed envelopes hold globally.

notation.meaning: upper true-objective error relative to the surrogate
lower true-objective error relative to the surrogate

knowledge_statements.title: Asymmetric Surrogate-Envelope Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Argmin Consistency with Vanishing Optimization Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive consistency counterpart to failure under pointwise convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\|\widetilde f_n-f\|_\infty\to0\) and \(\widetilde f_n(\widehat x_n)\leq\inf_X\widetilde f_n+\delta_n\), where \(\delta_n\to0\). Then \[f(\widehat x_n)-\inf_Xf\to0.\] If additionally \(X\) is compact, \(f\) is continuous, and its minimizer \(x^*\) is unique, then \(\widehat x_n\to x^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform surrogate convergence and vanishing optimization error imply value consistency; compactness and uniqueness yield decision consistency.
assumptions_latex: \(X\neq\varnothing\).
\(\|\widetilde f_n-f\|_\infty\to0\).

Surrogate Approximation Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform surrogate error converted into a recommendation-error certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be nonempty and let \(f,\widetilde f:X\to\mathbb R\) satisfy \(\sup_{x\in X}|f(x)-\widetilde f(x)|\leq\eta\). If \(\widehat x\in X\) obeys \(\widetilde f(\widehat x)\leq\inf_{x\in X}\widetilde f(x)+\delta\), then \[f(\widehat x)-\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\leq2\eta+\delta.\] Thus a certified uniform surrogate error and a certified surrogate-optimization tolerance jointly provide a directly checkable bound on true simple regret.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform surrogate error eta and surrogate optimization tolerance delta certify true recommendation error at most twice eta plus delta.

children.title: Acquisition Evaluation Gaps
children.top_down_role: Performance loss attributable to inaccurate acquisition-value computation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Unbiasedness Does Not Control the Acquisition Maximizer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of optimizer-level guarantees under merely pointwise-unbiased acquisition evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(M>0\), there exist a two-point domain \(X=\{u,v\}\), an exact acquisition \(a\), and pointwise-unbiased random estimates \(\widetilde a(x)\) such that a maximizer \(\widehat x\in\arg\max_X\widetilde a\) satisfies \[\mathbb E\!\left[\sup_{x\in X}a(x)-a(\widehat x)\right]\ge M.\] Thus pointwise unbiasedness alone supplies neither a uniform acquisition-error bound nor an optimizer-level gap certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unbiased acquisition estimates at each fixed point need not make the maximizer of the noisy estimates nearly optimal.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) has two points.
\(\mathbb E[\widetilde a(x)]=a(x)\) for each fixed \(x\).
\(\widehat x\) maximizes the realized approximate acquisition under a fixed tie rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_{a,\widetilde a}\mathbb E[\sup_Xa-a(\widehat x)]=+\infty\ \text{under pointwise unbiasedness alone}.

notation.meaning: maximizer of the realized approximate acquisition

knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Unbiasedness Does Not Control the Acquisition Maximizer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous acquisition-evaluation accuracy and induced selection loss on a finite candidate set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be finite with \(|X|=m\). For each \(x\in X\), let \(\widetilde a_N(x)\) average \(N\) unbiased acquisition estimates whose centered errors are independent and \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian across replications; dependence between candidates within a replication is allowed. Then \[\Pr\!\left(\max_{x\in X}|\widetilde a_N(x)-a(x)|>\eta\right)\le2m\exp\!\left(-\frac{N\eta^2}{2\sigma^2}\right).\] If \(N\ge2\sigma^2\eta^{-2}\log(2m/\alpha)\) and \(\widehat x\in\arg\max_X\widetilde a_N\), then with probability at least \(1-\alpha\), \(\max_Xa-a(\widehat x)\le2\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite candidate set, sub-Gaussian Monte Carlo estimates need logarithmically many samples in the candidate count to control the selected point's exact acquisition gap.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite with cardinality \(m\).
For each candidate, replication errors are independent across replications, unbiased, and \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian.
The computed acquisition is maximized exactly over \(X\).
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Candidate Monte Carlo Acquisition Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acquisition-evaluation concentration on a compact metric domain, with the distinct mesh contribution shown explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,\rho)\) be compact, let \(a:X\to\mathbb R\) be \(L\)-Lipschitz, and let \(S_h\) be a finite \(h\)-net with \(|S_h|=m\). At each \(s\in S_h\), let \(\widetilde a_N(s)\) average \(N\) unbiased estimates whose centered errors are independent and \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian across replications; candidates may be dependent within a replication. If \(\widehat x\in\arg\max_{s\in S_h}\widetilde a_N(s)\), then with probability at least \(1-\alpha\), \[\sup_{x\in X}a(x)-a(\widehat x)\le Lh+2\sigma\sqrt{\frac{2\log(2m/\alpha)}{N}}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a metric net, a Lipschitz acquisition has a certified selection loss equal to a mesh term plus twice the simultaneous Monte Carlo evaluation error.
assumptions_latex: \((X,\rho)\) is compact and \(a\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz.
\(S_h\) is a finite \(h\)-net with \(|S_h|=m\).
At each net point, errors are unbiased, independent across replications, and \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian; cross-candidate dependence within a replication is allowed.
The computed acquisition is maximized exactly over \(S_h\).

notation.meaning: finite h-net of the acquisition domain

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss certificate for uniformly approximate acquisition evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a,\widetilde a:X\to\mathbb R\) be exact and computed acquisition functions with \(\sup_{x\in X}|a(x)-\widetilde a(x)|\leq\eta\). If the returned point satisfies \(\widetilde a(\widehat x)\geq\sup_{x\in X}\widetilde a(x)-\delta\), then \[\sup_{x\in X}a(x)-a(\widehat x)\leq2\eta+\delta.\] The bound separates acquisition-evaluation error \(\eta\) from the optimization tolerance \(\delta\), and both quantities are sufficient to certify the loss relative to the exact acquisition maximizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate acquisition values with uniform error eta and maximization tolerance delta lose at most twice eta plus delta.
assumptions_latex: \(X\neq\varnothing\).
\(\sup_{x\in X}|a(x)-\widetilde a(x)|\leq\eta\).

children.title: Inner-Optimization Gaps
children.top_down_role: Performance loss caused by failure to optimize the acquisition objective adequately.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stationarity Does Not Certify the Global Acquisition Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of local first- and second-order stopping conditions for nonconcave acquisition maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There exist twice continuously differentiable acquisitions \(a:[0,1]\to\mathbb R\) and points \(x\in(0,1)\) with \(a'(x)=0\) and \(a''(x)<0\) such that \[\sup_{z\in[0,1]}a(z)-a(x)>0.\] Hence even strict local maximality does not certify a small global inner-optimization gap without additional global structure or a valid global upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strict local acquisition maximum can remain arbitrarily worse than the global maximum, so local solver convergence is not a global-gap certificate.
assumptions_latex: The acquisition is not assumed concave.

notation.meaning: strict local maximizer returned by a local method

knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity Does Not Certify the Global Acquisition Gap

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global Upper-Bound Certificate for Acquisition Maximization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certification of a feasible acquisition incumbent using a valid global upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a:X\to\mathbb R\), \(x\in X\), and \(U\geq\sup_{z\in X}a(z)\). Then \[0\leq\sup_{z\in X}a(z)-a(x)\leq U-a(x).\] Hence \(U-a(x)\leq\varepsilon\) certifies global \(\varepsilon\)-optimality. A merely local or invalid upper bound provides no such certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible incumbent’s difference from a valid global acquisition upper bound certifies its global acquisition gap.
assumptions_latex: \(X\neq\varnothing\), \(x\in X\), and \(a(x),U\) are finite.
\(U\geq\sup_{z\in X}a(z)\).

notation.meaning: valid global upper bound on the acquisition supremum

knowledge_statements.title: Global Upper-Bound Certificate for Acquisition Maximization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: GP-UCB Regret with Inexact Acquisition Maximization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Propagation of certified GP-UCB inner-solver gaps into cumulative regret.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q_t(x)=\mu_{t-1}(x)+b_t\sigma_{t-1}(x)\), with nondecreasing \(b_t\), and suppose \(|f(x)-\mu_{t-1}(x)|\leq b_t\sigma_{t-1}(x)\) simultaneously. If \(q_t(x_t)\geq\sup_xq_t(x)-\varepsilon_t\), then \[f(x^*)-f(x_t)\leq2b_t\sigma_{t-1}(x_t)+\varepsilon_t.\] If \(\sum_{t=1}^T\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)\leq C\gamma_T\), then \[R_T\leq2b_T\sqrt{CT\gamma_T}+\sum_{t=1}^T\varepsilon_t.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified GP-UCB maximization errors add to the usual confidence-width cumulative-regret bound.
assumptions_latex: A maximizer \(x^*\) exists.
The simultaneous confidence event holds.
\(\varepsilon_t\geq0\) and \(q_t(x_t)\geq\sup_xq_t(x)-\varepsilon_t\).
\(\sum_{t=1}^T\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)\leq C\gamma_T\).
knowledge_statements.title: GP-UCB Regret with Inexact Acquisition Maximization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global value-gap certificate for differentiable concave acquisition maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be nonempty and convex, and let \(a:X\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable and concave. A point \(x\in X\) globally maximizes \(a\) if and only if \(\langle\nabla a(x),z-x\rangle\leq0\) for every \(z\in X\). More generally, \[\sup_{z\in X}\langle\nabla a(x),z-x\rangle\leq\varepsilon\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\sup_{z\in X}a(z)-a(x)\leq\varepsilon.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a differentiable concave acquisition on a convex domain, the first-order residual certifies its global value gap.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty and convex.
\(a\) is differentiable and concave on \(X\).
The linear-optimization residual is validly bounded.

notation.meaning: First-order global residual for concave acquisition maximization.

knowledge_statements.title: Concave Acquisition First-Order Certificate
Inner-Optimization Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-round condition quantifying imperfect maximization of an acquisition function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an acquisition function \(a_t:X\to\mathbb R\), a selected point \(x_t\in X\) is an \(\varepsilon_t\)-accurate inner solution precisely when \[a_t(x_t)\geq\sup_{x\in X}a_t(x)-\varepsilon_t.\] Equivalently, its inner-optimization gap \(g_t:=\sup_Xa_t-a_t(x_t)\) satisfies \(0\leq g_t\leq\varepsilon_t\). Over \(T\) rounds, any analysis charging acquisition suboptimality additively incurs at most \(\sum_{t=1}^T\varepsilon_t\); vanishing average charge requires \(T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\varepsilon_t\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inner solver is epsilon-accurate when its acquisition value lies within epsilon of the global acquisition supremum.
assumptions_latex: \(X\neq\varnothing\) and \(\sup_Xa_t<\infty\).
\(\varepsilon_t\geq0\).

children.title: Statistical-Computational Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Interactions between numerical effort, approximation fidelity, and sample efficiency.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Marginal Balance for Continuous Resource Allocation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary interior condition for allocating a fixed resource budget between sampling and computation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E(n,B)=2\eta(n)+\delta(B)\), where \(\eta\) and \(\delta\) are differentiable and nonincreasing, subject to \(c_{\rm obs}n+B=C\). If an interior allocation \((n^*,B^*)\) locally minimizes \(E\), then \[-\frac{2\eta'(n^*)}{c_{\rm obs}}=-\delta'(B^*).\] Thus an interior optimum equalizes marginal certified error reduction per resource unit; an optimum not satisfying interiority may occur at a boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An interior budget optimum equalizes marginal certified error reduction per unit cost between observations and computation.
assumptions_latex: \(\eta\) and \(\delta\) are differentiable and nonincreasing.
\(c_{\rm obs}n+B=C\), with \(c_{\rm obs}>0\).
\((n^*,B^*)\) is an interior local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Marginal Balance for Continuous Resource Allocation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex KKT Certificate for Resource Allocation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global optimality conditions for a convex statistical-computational allocation model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\eta,\delta\) be proper closed convex nonincreasing functions. Minimize \(E(n,B)=\eta(n)+\delta(B)\) over \(n,B\geq0\), \(cn+B\leq C\), where \(c,C>0\), under a convex constraint qualification. A feasible \((n^*,B^*)\) is globally optimal iff some \(\lambda\geq0\) satisfies \[0\in\partial\eta(n^*)+c\lambda+N_{\mathbb R_+}(n^*),\quad0\in\partial\delta(B^*)+\lambda+N_{\mathbb R_+}(B^*),\] \[\lambda(cn^*+B^*-C)=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For convex decreasing error curves, feasibility, complementary slackness, and subgradient balance characterize globally optimal allocations.
assumptions_latex: \(\eta\) and \(\delta\) are proper, closed, convex, and nonincreasing.
A convex constraint qualification holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed KKT conditions are necessary and sufficient for global optimality.

notation.meaning: normal cone to the nonnegative half-line

knowledge_statements.title: Convex KKT Certificate for Resource Allocation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form continuous allocation for equal power-law error decay.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E(n,B)=An^{-r}+DB^{-r}\), where \(A,D,r,c,C>0\), subject to \(cn+B=C\) and \(n,B>0\). With \(\rho=(Dc/A)^{1/(r+1)}\), the unique minimizer is \[n^*=\frac{C}{c+\rho},\qquad B^*=\frac{\rho C}{c+\rho},\] and \[E(n^*,B^*)=(c+\rho)^r(A+D\rho^{-r})C^{-r}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equal power-law exponents yield constant optimal resource shares and combined error of order \(C^{-r}\).
assumptions_latex: \(n,B\) are positive continuous allocations.
knowledge_statements.title: Equal-Exponent Statistical-Computational Allocation Rate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Marginal Balance Need Not Be Globally Sufficient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonconvex decreasing-error allocation where marginal balance holds at a nonglobal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(0<\epsilon<1\), impose \(n+B=1\), and set \[\eta(n)=1-n+\frac{\epsilon}{4\pi}\sin(4\pi n),\qquad\delta(B)=1-B.\] Both functions are strictly decreasing. At \((n,B)=(1/8,7/8)\), marginal reductions are equal, but \(\eta(n)+\delta(1-n)=1+\frac{\epsilon}{4\pi}\sin(4\pi n)\) has a strict local maximum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonconvex decreasing error curves can satisfy marginal balance at a strict local maximum of total error.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\epsilon<1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Marginal Balance Need Not Be Globally Sufficient

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotically optimal continuous resource split when statistical and computational errors have different power-law exponents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E(n,B)=An^{-p}+DB^{-q}\), where \(A,D,p,q,c>0\), under \(cn+B=C\) with \(n,B>0\), and suppose \(p\ne q\). If \(p<q\), then the unique minimizer satisfies \[n^*=C/c-o(C),\qquad B^*\sim\left(\frac{Dqc}{Ap}\right)^{1/(q+1)}(C/c)^{(p+1)/(q+1)},\] and \(E(n^*,B^*)\sim Ac^pC^{-p}\). If \(p>q\), then \[B^*=C-o(C),\qquad n^*\sim\left(\frac{Ap}{cDq}\right)^{1/(p+1)}C^{(q+1)/(p+1)},\] and \(E(n^*,B^*)\sim DC^{-q}\). Thus the slower-decaying error receives an asymptotically linear budget share, while the faster-decaying component receives a sublinear but diverging allocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With unequal power-law error exponents, the slower-decaying component receives almost all resources and the optimized error decays with the smaller exponent.
assumptions_latex: \(A,D,p,q,c>0\) and \(p\ne q\).
Allocations are positive and continuous.
The full budget is used: \(cn+B=C\).
knowledge_statements.title: Unequal-Exponent Statistical–Computational Allocation
Statistical-Computational Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budget allocation between information acquisition and numerical surrogate optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(n\) expensive observations yield a surrogate \(\widetilde f_n\) with certified uniform statistical error \(\eta(n)\), while \(B\) computational work units produce \(\widehat x_{n,B}\) satisfying \(\widetilde f_n(\widehat x_{n,B})\leq\inf_X\widetilde f_n+\delta(B)\). Then \[f(\widehat x_{n,B})-\inf_Xf\leq2\eta(n)+\delta(B).\] Under the resource constraint \(c_{m obs}n+B\leq C\), the certified allocation problem is therefore to minimize \(2\eta(n)+\delta(B)\) over feasible \((n,B)\), explicitly trading statistical accuracy against computation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed budget should balance declining statistical error from observations against declining numerical error from additional computation.
assumptions_latex: \(\|f-\widetilde f_n\|_\infty\leq\eta(n)\).
\(\widetilde f_n(\widehat x_{n,B})-\inf_X\widetilde f_n\leq\delta(B)\).
\(c_{\rm obs}n+B\leq C\).
