children.title: Explicit-Constraint Search Regimes
children.top_down_role: Search over explicit feasible regions with expensive objectives.

children.title: Known Feasible Regions
children.top_down_role: Optimization domains restricted by explicit feasibility information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent extended-real representation of acquisition maximization over a known feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq X\) be nonempty and known, and let \(a:X\to\mathbb R\). Define \[\widetilde a(x)=\begin{cases}a(x),&x\in F,\\-\infty,&x\notin F.\end{cases}\] Whenever \(a\) attains its maximum on \(F\), \[\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in X}\widetilde a(x)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in F}a(x).\] A finite-valued mask \(b\) is exact only if its best infeasible value is strictly below \(\max_{x\in F}a(x)\); otherwise an infeasible point may remain or become a maximizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A known feasible region can be enforced exactly by assigning minus infinity outside it; a finite penalty needs a verified separation from the best feasible value.
assumptions_latex: \(F\neq\varnothing\).
Membership in \(F\) is known before objective evaluation.
The acquisition attains a maximum on \(F\) when argmax equality is asserted.
knowledge_statements.title: Indicator-Masked Acquisition
Known Feasible Regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acquisition maximization when all constraints are known before objective evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a design domain \(X\), known constraints \(c_j:X\to\mathbb R\), and acquisition functions \(a_t\), form \(F:=\{x\in X:c_j(x)\leq0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\). Initialize with any \(x_1\in F\). At round \(t\), select \[x_t\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in F}a_t(x),\] evaluate the expensive objective only at \(x_t\), and update the surrogate. Stop at a prescribed budget \(T\) and return the best observed feasible point. Every expensive evaluation is feasible because membership in \(F\) is checked before evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When constraints are known, maximize each acquisition directly over the feasible set so every expensive objective evaluation is feasible.
assumptions_latex: \(F=\{x\in X:c_j(x)\leq0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\neq\varnothing\).
Each constraint \(c_j\) is known and evaluable before the objective.
A maximizer of \(a_t\) over \(F\) is available at each round.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits known feasible regions, but a feasible-directions section is not a claim-specific source for this Bayesian-optimization procedure and guarantee.

children.title: Cheap Constraint Screening
children.top_down_role: Candidate filtering using constraints inexpensive relative to objective evaluation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consequences of false-negative and false-positive screening errors before expensive objective evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq X\) be the true feasible set and \(\widehat F=\{x:\widehat s(x)=1\}\) the set accepted by a cheap screen. Restricting acquisition maximization to \(\widehat F\) prevents infeasible expensive queries exactly when \(\widehat F\subseteq F\), and it preserves every feasible candidate exactly when \(F\subseteq\widehat F\). Thus both protections hold exactly when \(\widehat F=F\). A rejected feasible maximizer demonstrates false-negative loss; an accepted infeasible point demonstrates that screening alone does not certify feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: False negatives can remove the best feasible candidate, while false positives can spend expensive evaluations on infeasible candidates; exact screening provides both protections.
assumptions_latex: \(F\neq\varnothing\).
Candidates failing the screen are not evaluated.
Acquisition search is restricted to \(\widehat F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat F\subseteq F\text{ prevents infeasible queries},\quad F\subseteq\widehat F\text{ prevents exclusion of feasible candidates};\quad \widehat F=F\text{ gives both}.

notation.meaning: set accepted by the cheap screen

knowledge_statements.title: Errors in Cheap Feasibility Screens
Cheap Constraint Screening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage screening that avoids expensive objectives at cheaply detected infeasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s:X\to\{0,1\}\) be a cheap, exact feasibility screen, with \(s(x)=1\) exactly for feasible points. At round \(t\), generate candidates in \(X\), discard every candidate with \(s(x)=0\), and choose \[x_t\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in X:\,s(x)=1}a_t(x).\] Evaluate the expensive objective only at \(x_t\), update its surrogate, and stop after \(T\) expensive evaluations. If screening cost is excluded from that budget, no expensive evaluation is spent on a point certified infeasible by \(s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply a cheap exact feasibility test first, then spend expensive objective evaluations only on candidates that pass.
assumptions_latex: \(s(x)=1\) if and only if \(x\) is feasible.
Evaluating \(s\) is cheap relative to evaluating the objective.
\(\{x\in X:s(x)=1\}\neq\varnothing\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits cheap constraint screening, but the cited introductory stochastic-optimization section does not specifically support the exact-screening Bayesian-optimization procedure.

children.title: Geometry-Aware Feasible Search
children.top_down_role: Acquisition optimization that directly respects explicit feasible-region geometry.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility-preserving local acquisition search over a closed convex feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(a\) be differentiable, and fix \(\eta>0\). At \(x_t\in F\), set \(y_t=P_F(x_t+\eta\nabla a(x_t))\) and \(d_t=y_t-x_t\). Choose \(\alpha_t\in[0,1]\) satisfying an ascent line-search condition and set \(x_{t+1}=x_t+\alpha_td_t\). Convexity gives \(x_{t+1}\in F\). Moreover, \(d_t=0\) exactly when \(\nabla a(x_t)^\top(z-x_t)\le0\) for every \(z\in F\), a first-order stationarity certificate that does not imply global optimality for a nonconcave acquisition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project an acquisition-gradient step onto a closed convex feasible set and move along the feasible segment; a projection fixed point certifies first-order stationarity only.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(a\) is differentiable at each iterate.
\(x_0\in F\) and \(\alpha_t\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_t\in F\ \forall t,\qquad P_F(x_t+\eta\nabla a(x_t))=x_t\iff \nabla a(x_t)^\top(z-x_t)\le0\ \forall z\in F.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the feasible region

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Acquisition-Ascent Search
Geometry-Aware Feasible Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasible-set parameterization for acquisition optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq X\) be a nonempty feasible set and let \(\phi:Z\to F\) be surjective. For every acquisition function \(a:X\to\mathbb R\), \[\sup_{x\in F}a(x)=\sup_{z\in Z}a(\phi(z)).\] Hence acquisition search may be performed in coordinates \(z\), with every generated design \(\phi(z)\) feasible. Moreover, if \(\widehat z\) satisfies \(a(\phi(\widehat z))\geq\sup_{z\in Z}a(\phi(z))-\varepsilon\), then \(\widehat x=\phi(\widehat z)\) is feasible and has acquisition gap at most \(\varepsilon\) over \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A surjective parameterization of the feasible set converts constrained acquisition search into an equivalent unconstrained coordinate search.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq X\) is nonempty.
\(\phi:Z\to F\) is surjective.
\(\sup_{x\in F}a(x)<\infty\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits geometry-aware search and is mathematically coherent, but the feasible-directions locator does not specifically support the surjective-parameterization equivalence and gap transfer.

children.title: Disconnected Feasible Domains
children.top_down_role: Search complications caused by fragmented explicit feasible regions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global acquisition optimization over finitely many disconnected feasible components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\bigsqcup_{k=1}^K F_k\) be the union of finitely many nonempty path-connected components. For every acquisition function \(a:F\to\mathbb R\), \[\sup_{x\in F}a(x)=\max_{1\le k\le K}\sup_{x\in F_k}a(x).\] If each component supremum is attained at \(x_k\in F_k\), comparing \(a(x_k)\) yields a global maximizer. Searching fewer than all components has no global guarantee unless valid upper bounds certify that every omitted component cannot improve the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global search over finitely many disconnected components requires solving each relevant component and comparing their best acquisition values.
assumptions_latex: \(1\le K<\infty\).
The nonempty sets \(F_k\) are the path-connected components of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.title: Componentwise Acquisition Decomposition
Disconnected Feasible Domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reachability failure of path-preserving local search on disconnected feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the feasible region be the disjoint union \(F=F_1\cup F_2\), where \(F_1\) and \(F_2\) are distinct path-connected components. Any feasible local method whose iterates admit continuous paths in \(F\) from \(x_t\) to \(x_{t+1}\) remains forever in the component containing its initialization. Therefore, if \(x_0\in F_1\) while every global acquisition maximizer lies in \(F_2\), the method cannot attain a global maximizer. Global coverage requires restarts, component enumeration, or proposals capable of jumping between components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible path-preserving local optimizer cannot leave its initial connected component, so it may miss the global acquisition maximizer.
assumptions_latex: \(F=F_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}F_2\) has distinct path-connected components.
Each update is connected to the preceding iterate by a continuous path contained in \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_t\in F_1\) for all \(t\), even when \(\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in F}a(x)\subseteq F_2\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits disconnected feasible domains, but the cited feasible-directions section does not specifically support the path-component reachability statement or prescribed remedies.

children.title: Modeled Black-Box Constraints
children.top_down_role: Joint objective and feasibility learning when constraints are expensive.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dependence Failure of Marginal Feasibility Products
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of multiplying marginal constraint-satisfaction probabilities when constraint posteriors are dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a fixed candidate, let posterior feasibility events be \(E_1=\{U=0\}\) and \(E_2=\{U=1\}\), where \(U\mid\mathcal D_t\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\). Then \(\Pr(E_1\mid\mathcal D_t)=\Pr(E_2\mid\mathcal D_t)=1/2\), but \(E_1\cap E_2=\varnothing\), so \[\Pr(E_1\cap E_2\mid\mathcal D_t)=0\ne\tfrac14=\Pr(E_1\mid\mathcal D_t)\Pr(E_2\mid\mathcal D_t).\] Multiplying marginal feasibility probabilities can therefore assign positive weight to a candidate having zero joint feasibility probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dependent constraints can each appear feasible marginally while simultaneous feasibility is impossible, so marginal probabilities cannot be multiplied without independence.
assumptions_latex: The two posterior feasibility events depend on the same Bernoulli latent variable.
The product of marginal probabilities is used as a surrogate for joint feasibility.

notation.meaning: posterior event that constraint j is satisfied

knowledge_statements.title: Dependence Failure of Marginal Feasibility Products
Modeled Black-Box Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constrained Bayesian optimization with probabilistic surrogates for both objective and expensive feasibility functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X\) be the design space, with unknown objective \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) and constraints \(c_j:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\), \(j=1,\ldots,m\). The optimization problem is \[\min_{x\in\mathcal X} f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad c_j(x)\le 0\ \text{for all }j.\] After data \(\mathcal D_t\), surrogate posteriors define the feasibility probability \[p_t^{\mathrm{feas}}(x)=\Pr\!\left(c_j(x)\le0\ \forall j\mid\mathcal D_t\right).\] A feasibility-weighted acquisition has the form \(a_t(x)=a_t^{f}(x)p_t^{\mathrm{feas}}(x)\); under conditionally independent constraint posteriors, \(p_t^{\mathrm{feas}}(x)=\prod_{j=1}^m\Pr(c_j(x)\le0\mid\mathcal D_t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective and expensive constraints receive posterior models; an acquisition can weight objective utility by the posterior probability that every constraint is satisfied.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\neq\varnothing\) and all unknown responses are measurable.
Observations admit posterior distributions conditional on \(\mathcal D_t\).
The product formula additionally assumes conditional independence of the constraint values at each candidate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the container and is mathematically coherent, including the conditional-independence qualification. No cited source supports the feasibility-weighted acquisition or product formula, so source verification is required.

children.title: Decoupled Evaluation-Source Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies selecting which objective or constraint information source to evaluate.

children.title: Decoupled Objective Evaluations
children.top_down_role: Policies for acquiring objective information independently of constraint observations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-only observation channel, distinct from the policy selecting that channel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For h(x)=(f(x),c_1(x),\ldots,c_m(x)), a decoupled objective action (x,0) returns Y_0=f(x)+\varepsilon_0 without directly observing any c_j(x). Its likelihood depends on the latent response vector only through f(x), and it may have source cost \lambda_0(x)>0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decoupled objective action observes the objective without requiring any constraint observation.
assumptions_latex: The objective observation-noise law is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Y_0=f(x)+\varepsilon_0\text{ with no direct constraint observation}.
knowledge_statements.title: Decoupled Objective Evaluation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Posterior effect of an objective-only action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An objective-only action directly observes only f(x). If f is posterior-independent of the constraint vector c before the action, conditioning on Y_0 leaves the constraint posterior unchanged; a correlated multi-output surrogate may propagate the update to constraints without making them directly observed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective-only evaluation may indirectly update correlated constraints but directly observes only the objective.
assumptions_latex: The joint posterior and observation likelihood are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\perp c\mid\mathcal D\Longrightarrow p(c\mid\mathcal D,Y_0)=p(c\mid\mathcal D).
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Only Posterior Effect
Decoupled Objective Evaluations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Evaluation actions that observe the objective without simultaneously observing expensive constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For response vector \(h(x)=(f(x),c_1(x),\ldots,c_m(x))\), a decoupled objective evaluation at \(x\in\mathcal X\) is an action \((x,0)\) returning \[Y_0=f(x)+\varepsilon_0\] and no direct observation of any \(c_j(x)\). Its likelihood depends on the latent responses only through \(f(x)\). If the objective and constraint processes are posterior-independent before the action, conditioning on \(Y_0\) updates the posterior of \(f\) while leaving every constraint posterior unchanged. The action may have its own positive cost \(\lambda_0(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decoupled objective action observes only the noisy objective at a design, incurs its own cost, and need not evaluate any constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(f,c_1,\ldots,c_m\) are latent responses on a common nonempty design space \(\mathcal X\).
\(\varepsilon_0\) has a specified observation-noise law.
Posterior invariance of constraints requires posterior independence from \(f\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits decoupled objective evaluation and correctly qualifies posterior invariance by independence. No inspectable citation supports this formalization.

children.title: Decoupled Constraint Evaluations
children.top_down_role: Policies for acquiring constraint information independently of objective observations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-only observation channel, distinct from the policy selecting that channel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For h(x)=(f(x),c_1(x),\ldots,c_m(x)), a decoupled constraint action (x,j), j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}, returns Y_j=c_j(x)+\varepsilon_j without directly observing f(x) or c_k(x) for k\ne j. Its likelihood depends on the latent response vector only through c_j(x), and it may have source cost \lambda_j(x)>0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decoupled constraint action observes one selected constraint without requiring an objective or other-constraint observation.
assumptions_latex: m\ge1.
The selected source and its observation-noise law are known.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Y_j=c_j(x)+\varepsilon_j\text{ is the sole direct response}.

notation.meaning: Evaluation of constraint source j at x.

knowledge_statements.title: Decoupled Constraint Evaluation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Posterior effect of a constraint-only action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A constraint-only action directly observes only c_j(x). If c_j is posterior-independent of f and of c_k for k\ne j before the action, conditioning on Y_j leaves their posteriors unchanged; a correlated multi-output surrogate may instead propagate the update without converting those responses into direct observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint-only evaluation can update correlated outputs indirectly, but directly observes only the selected constraint.
assumptions_latex: The joint posterior and observation likelihood are specified.
knowledge_statements.title: Direct Observation versus Posterior Propagation
Decoupled Constraint Evaluations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Evaluation actions that observe selected constraints without necessarily observing the objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For response vector \(h(x)=(f(x),c_1(x),\ldots,c_m(x))\), a decoupled constraint evaluation is an action \((x,j)\), where \(j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), returning \[Y_j=c_j(x)+\varepsilon_j\] without directly observing \(f(x)\) or any \(c_k(x)\) with \(k\ne j\). Its likelihood depends on the latent responses only through \(c_j(x)\), and the action has cost \(\lambda_j(x)>0\). Under posterior independence, conditioning on \(Y_j\) updates only the posterior for constraint \(j\); correlated multi-output models may propagate the update to other responses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decoupled constraint action evaluates one selected noisy constraint at a design, without requiring an objective or other-constraint evaluation.
assumptions_latex: \(m\ge1\) and all constraint responses share the design space \(\mathcal X\).
Each \(\varepsilon_j\) has a specified observation-noise law.
The evaluation-source index \(j\) is observable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y_j=c_j(x)+\varepsilon_j\) is the sole direct response from action \((x,j)\).

notation.meaning: evaluation of constraint source j at x
cost of evaluating constraint j at x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches the leaf and distinguishes direct observation from correlated posterior propagation. An authoritative source with a specific locator is absent.

children.title: Evaluation-Source Selection
children.top_down_role: Choice among independently available objective or constraint information sources.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic repeated selection of a design and independently available response source.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration t, compute a declared action score A_t(x,s) from the current joint posterior and source cost, choose an admissible maximizer or specified approximation over \mathcal X\times\mathcal S, observe only source s_t at x_t, update the joint posterior, and stop before exceeding the declared cost or evaluation budget. Terminal recommendation and feasibility rule must be declared separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Score design-source pairs, observe only the selected source, update the joint posterior, and respect the declared budget.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal S\text{ is the set of selectable sources}.
Source costs are positive and the budget accounting rule is specified.
The action score, approximation tolerance, and terminal recommendation are specified.
knowledge_statements.title: Cost-Aware Evaluation-Source Selection

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ratio and Net-Value Rules Can Disagree
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample to equivalence of two cost-aware source scores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For two actions with (U,\lambda)=(4,1) and (10,4), the utility-per-cost scores are 4 and 2.5, while the net utilities are 3 and 6. Thus the ratio rule selects the first action and the net-value rule selects the second.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Utility per cost and utility minus cost can rank evaluation sources oppositely.
assumptions_latex: U\ge0.
\lambda>0.
knowledge_statements.title: Ratio and Net-Value Rules Can Disagree

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Policy-neutral value assigned to a design-source action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let V(b) be finite terminal decision value at belief b. If action (x,s) yields predictive observation Y and posterior b^{x,s,Y}, define \operatorname{VOI}_b(x,s)=\mathbb E_b[V(b^{x,s,Y})]-V(b). With cost \lambda_s(x)>0, maximizing \operatorname{VOI}-\lambda is a myopic net-value rule, whereas maximizing \operatorname{VOI}/\lambda is a distinct efficiency heuristic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A source's one-step value is its expected improvement in terminal decision value; net-value and value-per-cost policies differ.
assumptions_latex: V(b)\text{ and the predictive expectation are finite}.
\lambda_s(x)>0.
knowledge_statements.title: One-Step Evaluation-Source Value of Information

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step source-elimination certificate under information dominance and cost ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a fixed design and belief, if source s_1 Blackwell-dominates s_2, then every finite Bayesian terminal decision problem satisfies \operatorname{VOI}(x,s_1)\ge\operatorname{VOI}(x,s_2). If also \lambda_{s_1}(x)\le\lambda_{s_2}(x), then s_2 is weakly dominated for one-step net-value selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A no-more-expensive source that is more informative in the Blackwell sense weakly dominates the other source for myopic net value.
assumptions_latex: The sources are compared at the same design and current belief.
Terminal expected utility is finite.
knowledge_statements.title: Blackwell-Dominated Source Elimination
Evaluation-Source Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost-aware joint selection of a design and a decoupled response source.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal S=\{0,1,\ldots,m\}\) index the objective and constraint sources. Given posterior data \(\mathcal D_t\), positive costs \(\lambda_s(x)\), and a nonnegative one-step utility \(U_t(x,s)\), choose \[(x_t,s_t)\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{(x,s)\in\mathcal X\times\mathcal S}\frac{U_t(x,s)}{\lambda_s(x)}.\] Observe only \(Y_{s_t}\) at \(x_t\), update the joint posterior to \(\mathcal D_{t+1}\), and repeat until the budget or stopping rule is reached. Return a posterior-recommended feasible design, such as the feasible point with smallest posterior objective mean.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, select the design-source pair with greatest modeled utility per unit cost, observe that source, update the posterior, and continue within budget.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal S\) is finite and \(\lambda_s(x)>0\) for every admissible action.
The maximization admits a selected maximizer or a specified numerical approximation.
\(U_t(x,s)\) is measurable and determined by the current posterior.

notation.meaning: set of independently selectable evaluation sources
posterior utility of an evaluation action

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits evaluation-source selection, but utility-per-cost maximization and the terminal recommendation are policy-dependent choices rather than a universal decoupled-BO algorithm. A specific source is needed to establish the intended version.

children.title: Safe Recoverability Policy Family
children.top_down_role: Policies maintaining safety or recoverability throughout the evaluation sequence.

children.title: Safe-Set Maintenance Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies preserving admissible evaluations throughout sequential search.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of a uniform confidence event into an all-queries safety guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[E=\{\ell_{j,t}(x)\le g_j(x)\text{ for every relevant }j,t,x\}\] satisfy \(\Pr(E)\ge1-\delta\). Suppose \(S_0\) is truly safe, every maintained set is formed only through valid lower-bound and regularity certificates, and each query satisfies \(x_t\in S_t\). Then \[\Pr\bigl(g_j(x_t)\ge0\ \forall j,t\bigr)\ge1-\delta.\] Separate marginal coverage statements for individual \((j,t,x)\) do not imply this pathwise guarantee without simultaneous calibration or a valid allocation of failure probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A confidence event covering all constraints, points, and times transfers to an all-query safety guarantee; separate unadjusted marginal bounds do not.
assumptions_latex: \(\Pr(E)\ge1-\delta\).
\(S_0\) is truly safe.
Every query belongs to the recursively certified set.
knowledge_statements.title: Simultaneous-Confidence Safety Certificate
Safe-Set Maintenance Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive certification of designs using conservative constraint bounds and known regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let safety mean \(g_j(x)\ge0\) for \(j=1,\ldots,m\), and let each \(g_j\) be \(L_j\)-Lipschitz under metric \(d\). Initialize with a certified nonempty set \(S_0\). At stage \(t\), let \(\ell_{j,t}(x)\) be a simultaneous lower confidence bound and define \(\bar\ell_{j,t}(x)=\max_{0\le r\le t}\ell_{j,r}(x)\). Maintain \[S_t=S_{t-1}\cup\left\{x\in\mathcal X:\exists z\in S_{t-1},\ \bar\ell_{j,t}(z)-L_jd(x,z)\ge0\ \forall j\right\}.\] Permit evaluation only at points in \(S_t\). On the event that all confidence bounds are valid, every maintained point satisfies every safety constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from certified designs, retain prior safe points and add only points certified by lower confidence bounds and Lipschitz propagation.
assumptions_latex: \((\mathcal X,d)\) is a metric space and \(S_0\neq\varnothing\) is certified safe.
Each \(g_j\) is \(L_j\)-Lipschitz.
Simultaneously, \(\ell_{j,t}(x)\le g_j(x)\) for all relevant indices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_{t-1}\subseteq S_t\subseteq\{x:g_j(x)\ge0\ \forall j\}\) on the confidence event.

notation.meaning: certified safe set at stage t
lower confidence bound for safety function j
Lipschitz constant of safety function j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recursive safe-set algorithm fits the container and its safety conclusion is properly restricted to the simultaneous confidence event. No source supports this particular cumulative-bound and Lipschitz update.

children.title: Safe-Set Expansion Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies enlarging the region certified for subsequent evaluation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Points that lower-bound Lipschitz expansion cannot certify from the initial safe seed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the true safety functions \(g_j\) be \(L_j\)-Lipschitz and define \[\mathcal E(A)=A\cup\{x:\exists z\in A,\ g_j(z)-L_jd(x,z)\ge0\ \forall j\}.\] Starting with \(A_0=S_0\), set \(A_{n+1}=\mathcal E(A_n)\) and \(A_\infty=\bigcup_{n\ge0}A_n\). Any policy that admits points only through valid lower bounds \(\ell_{j,t}(z)\le g_j(z)\) and certificates \(\ell_{j,t}(z)-L_jd(x,z)\ge0\) satisfies \(S_t\subseteq A_\infty\). Hence this expansion rule cannot certify a point outside \(A_\infty\), even when that point is truly safe.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lower-bound Lipschitz expansion cannot move beyond the ideal safely reachable closure of its initial seed.
assumptions_latex: \(S_0\) is the initial certified safe set.
Each \(g_j\) is \(L_j\)-Lipschitz.
Every lower bound used for admission is valid on the stated confidence event.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S_t\subseteq A_\infty\ \forall t;\qquad x\notin A_\infty\Rightarrow x\text{ cannot be certified by this rule}.

notation.meaning: ideal safely reachable closure of the initial seed

knowledge_statements.title: Lipschitz-Reachability Limit of Safe Expansion
Safe-Set Expansion Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe sampling aimed at certifying currently uncertain designs outside the maintained safe set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a maintained safe set \(S_t\), lower and upper confidence bounds \(\ell_{j,t},u_{j,t}\), and Lipschitz constants \(L_j\), define the potential expanders \[G_t=\left\{z\in S_t:\exists x\notin S_t,\ u_{j,t}(z)-L_jd(x,z)\ge0\ \forall j\right\}.\] If \(G_t\neq\varnothing\), evaluate a point \(z_t\in G_t\) maximizing a specified uncertainty score, for example \(\max_j(u_{j,t}(z)-\ell_{j,t}(z))\). Update the confidence bounds and recompute the safe set. The policy never evaluates the uncertified exterior point directly; expansion occurs only after observations certify it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample uncertain points already known safe when optimistic constraint values there could certify new nearby designs; add exterior designs only after conservative certification.
assumptions_latex: The current set \(S_t\) is certified safe.
Each safety function is Lipschitz with known constant \(L_j\).
The displayed confidence bounds are jointly valid on the intended confidence event.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_t\in G_t\subseteq S_t\), and newly admitted points require lower-bound certification.

notation.meaning: set of safe points capable of potential expansion
upper confidence bound for safety function j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm has the correct safe-expansion role and keeps evaluations within the certified set. The precise potential-expander test and uncertainty policy require an authoritative citation.

children.title: Recoverability Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies retaining access to acceptable states after adverse outcomes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic-programming representation of finite-horizon return to an invariant backup set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For dynamics \(x^+=F(x,a)\), safe admissible actions \(a\in\mathcal A(x)\), and safety inequalities \(g_j(x,a)\ge0\), define \[\operatorname{Pre}(B)=\{x:\exists a\in\mathcal A(x),\ g_j(x,a)\ge0\ \forall j,\ F(x,a)\in B\}.\] Given an invariant backup set \(S\), set \(R_0=S\) and \(R_{h+1}=R_h\cup\operatorname{Pre}(R_h)\). Then \(R_h\) is exactly the set of states from which a safe admissible trajectory reaches \(S\) in at most \(h\) steps, and \(R_h\subseteq R_{h+1}\). After an exploratory transition, membership of its successor in \(R_H\) certifies retention of an \(H\)-step recovery plan.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-horizon recoverability is represented by repeatedly adding safe predecessors of the current backward-reachable set.
assumptions_latex: The transition map and safe admissible-action correspondence are specified.
\(S\) is controlled invariant under a certified backup policy.
The recovery horizon is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_h=\{x:x\text{ reaches }S\text{ safely in at most }h\text{ steps}\},\qquad R_h\subseteq R_{h+1}.

notation.meaning: safe one-step predecessor of set B

knowledge_statements.title: Backward-Reachable Recoverable Sets
Recoverability Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon return-to-safety condition for dynamical evaluation policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider dynamics \(x_{k+1}=F(x_k,a_k)\), a certified invariant backup set \(S\), admissible actions \(A(x)\), and safety predicates \(g_j(x,a)\ge0\). For horizon \(H\in\mathbb N\), a state \(x\) is recoverable when there exist \(h\le H\) and actions \(a_0,\ldots,a_{h-1}\) such that \[a_k\in A(x_k),\quad g_j(x_k,a_k)\ge0\ \forall j,k,\quad x_h\in S.\] A recoverability policy permits an exploratory action only if its predicted successor remains in this recoverable set; upon loss of exploration eligibility, it follows a certified backup policy into \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A state is recoverable when an admissible, constraint-satisfying action sequence can return it to an invariant safe set within a fixed horizon.
assumptions_latex: The transition map \(F\) and admissible-action correspondence \(A\) are specified.
The backup set \(S\) is controlled invariant under a certified policy.
The horizon \(H\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is recoverable exactly when a safe admissible trajectory reaches \(S\) within \(H\) steps.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-horizon condition is internally coherent and relevant to recoverability policies, but recoverability has domain-specific variants. No source establishes that this dynamical definition is the intended safe-BO variant.

children.title: Cost-Fidelity Bayesian Optimization Coupling
children.top_down_role: Policies jointly selecting locations, information sources, fidelity, and resource expenditure.

children.title: Discrete Information-Source Fidelity Family
children.top_down_role: Optimization across a finite collection of simulators, approximations, or data sources.

children.title: Discrete Fidelity Levels
children.top_down_role: Optimization over a finite ordered collection of approximation fidelities.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ordered Labels Do Not Imply Monotone Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary between an ordered fidelity index and an approximation-error guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X=\{x_0\}\), let the target be \(F_3(x_0)=0\), and define \(F_1(x_0)=1\), \(F_2(x_0)=2\). Although \(z_1<z_2<z_3\), \[|F_2(x_0)-F_3(x_0)|=2>1=|F_1(x_0)-F_3(x_0)|.\] Therefore an ordering of fidelity labels alone does not imply monotone approximation error, increasing cost, or increasing informativeness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A higher-labelled fidelity can be less accurate than a lower-labelled one, so accuracy, cost, and informativeness monotonicity require separate assumptions.
assumptions_latex: Only the labels \(z_1<z_2<z_3\) are assumed ordered.
No monotone discrepancy condition is imposed.

notation.meaning: response at discrete fidelity level k

knowledge_statements.title: Ordered Labels Do Not Imply Monotone Accuracy
Discrete Fidelity Levels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite ordered approximations to a distinguished target-fidelity objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal Z=\{z_1,\ldots,z_K\}\) be an ordered finite fidelity set with target level \(z_K\). A discrete-fidelity response is a function \(F:\mathcal X\times\mathcal Z\to\mathbb R\) whose target objective is \(f(x)=F(x,z_K)\). Each level has evaluation cost \(\lambda_k(x)>0\) and may have a known discrepancy bound \[|F(x,z_k)-f(x)|\le\epsilon_k\quad\text{for all }x\in\mathcal X,\] where \(\epsilon_K=0\). Lower levels are informative approximations rather than interchangeable observations of \(f\); their costs, biases, and correlations must be represented by the surrogate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite ordered set of fidelity levels supplies approximations of differing cost and discrepancy, with one distinguished level defining the target objective.
assumptions_latex: \(K\ge2\) and \(\mathcal X\neq\varnothing\).
The target response \(F(\cdot,z_K)\) is well defined.
Any asserted discrepancy bounds \(\epsilon_k\) hold uniformly on \(\mathcal X\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits discrete fidelity levels and clearly distinguishes the target fidelity. The optional uniform discrepancy model is a substantive modeling variant requiring a cited source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rejected from this definition leaf because its primary home is Cross-Source Dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_1\) be a Gaussian process and, for \(k=2,\ldots,K\), define \[F_k(x)=\rho_{k-1}F_{k-1}(x)+\delta_k(x),\] where \(\delta_2,\ldots,\delta_K\) are mutually independent Gaussian processes and are independent of \(F_1\). Then \((F_1,\ldots,F_K)\) is a joint multi-output Gaussian process with the corresponding recursive cross-covariances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ordered fidelity hierarchy can be coupled by scaling the preceding level and adding an independent discrepancy process.
assumptions_latex: \(F_1\) and all \(\delta_k\) are Gaussian processes.
The discrepancy processes are mutually independent and independent of \(F_1\).
\(\rho_{k-1}\in\mathbb R\) are fixed or conditioned-upon coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_k=\rho_{k-1}F_{k-1}+\delta_k\) defines a joint Gaussian fidelity hierarchy.

notation.meaning: linear linkage coefficient from fidelity k-1 to k

knowledge_statements.title: Autoregressive Discrete-Fidelity Representation

children.title: Discrete Information Sources
children.top_down_role: Optimization using a finite collection of simulators, datasets, or experimental channels.

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Information Sources
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite selectable evaluators that need not possess a total fidelity ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal S=\{1,\ldots,K\}\) index a finite collection of information sources. Source \(s\) queried at \(x\in\mathcal X\) returns \[Y_s(x)=F_s(x)+\varepsilon_s(x)\] at cost \(\lambda_s(x)>0\). One distinguished source \(s_\star\), or a separately modeled latent response, defines the target objective \(f\). Unlike ordered fidelity levels, the sources need not admit a total accuracy ordering: different sources may have location-dependent bias, noise, cost, and relevance to \(f\). A source-selection policy therefore chooses pairs in \(\mathcal X\times\mathcal S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discrete information sources are finitely many selectable evaluators with source-dependent response, noise, cost, and possibly no global accuracy ordering.
assumptions_latex: \(K\ge2\) and every source has a specified observation model.
\(\lambda_s(x)>0\) for every admissible source-design pair.
A target response is distinguished from auxiliary information.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly allows discrete sources without a total accuracy ordering and fits the terminal container. No inspectable source supports the formal response and source-selection model.

children.title: Cross-Source Dependence
children.top_down_role: Surrogate relationships linking observations from distinct fidelities or sources.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact posterior update induced in one source by observing another source.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Condition on current data \(D\), and suppose \((F_r(x'),Y_s(x))\) is jointly Gaussian with means \(m_r(x')\), \(m_{Y_s}(x)\), covariance \(c_{rs}(x',x)\), and \(v_s(x)=\operatorname{Var}(Y_s(x)\mid D)>0\). After observing \(Y_s(x)=y\), \[\mathbb E[F_r(x')\mid D,y]=m_r(x')+\frac{c_{rs}(x',x)}{v_s(x)}\bigl(y-m_{Y_s}(x)\bigr),\] and \[\operatorname{Cov}(F_r(x'),F_r(x'')\mid D,y)=c_{rr}(x',x'')-\frac{c_{rs}(x',x)c_{sr}(x,x'')}{v_s(x)}.\] Thus transfer is governed by posterior cross-covariance; if it vanishes for all target locations, the observation produces no target-source update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a joint Gaussian model, observing one source updates another by a cross-covariance-weighted residual and reduces its covariance by a rank-one cross-source term.
assumptions_latex: The relevant latent response and prospective observation are jointly Gaussian conditional on \(D\).
The displayed conditional covariances are finite.

notation.meaning: posterior cross-covariance between source r and the source-s observation
posterior predictive variance of the source-s observation

knowledge_statements.title: Gaussian Cross-Source Posterior Transfer
Cross-Source Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multi-output Gaussian-process coupling across discrete information sources.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A separable cross-source Gaussian-process model places a joint prior on \(F_s(x)\) with mean \(m_s(x)\) and covariance \[\operatorname{Cov}(F_s(x),F_r(x'))=B_{sr}k(x,x'),\] where \(k\) is a positive-semidefinite kernel on \(\mathcal X\) and \(B\in\mathbb R^{K\times K}\) is positive semidefinite. Nonzero \(B_{sr}\) transfers information between sources: conditioning on a noisy observation from source \(s\) can change predictions for source \(r\). If \(B_{sr}=0\) for every \(s\ne r\), the latent source processes are mutually independent under the joint Gaussian prior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-semidefinite source covariance matrix couples source outputs, allowing an observation from one source to update predictions for another.
assumptions_latex: \(k\) is a positive-semidefinite kernel on \(\mathcal X\).
\(B\) is a positive-semidefinite matrix.
The source responses have a jointly Gaussian prior.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The separable multi-output Gaussian-process representation is mathematically coherent, and the independence statement is valid under the stated joint Gaussian prior. A specific source is nevertheless required.

children.title: Source-Specific Bias
children.top_down_role: Systematic discrepancies that limit transfer across information sources.

knowledge_statements.title: Source-Specific Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive discrepancy representation relative to a target response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) be the target response. Information source \(s\) is represented by \[Y_s(x)=f(x)+b_s(x)+\varepsilon_s(x),\] where \(b_s:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) is its systematic discrepancy and \(\varepsilon_s(x)\) is zero-mean observation noise. A target source \(s_\star\) may be anchored by \(b_{s_\star}(x)=0\) for all \(x\). Without an anchor or equivalent identifying restrictions, \(f\) and the biases are not separately identifiable, since adding a common function to \(f\) and subtracting it from every \(b_s\) leaves all source responses unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each source equals the target plus a systematic source-dependent discrepancy and noise; an anchor or equivalent restriction is needed to identify target and biases separately.
assumptions_latex: The additive response decomposition is appropriate for every modeled source.
\(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_s(x)]=0\).
Separate identification uses an anchor or other explicit constraint on the bias functions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive bias representation fits the container, and the stated nonidentifiability without anchoring is correct. No citation supports this source-discrepancy model.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without target observations or restrictions coupling discrepancy across fidelity, different target objectives explain exactly the same lower-fidelity responses.

knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Fidelity-Only Nonidentifiability without Cross-Fidelity Restrictions
Continuous Fidelity Controls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bayesian optimization with a continuously selectable accuracy or resource coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal Z\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) be a continuous fidelity domain with distinguished target \(z_\star\). A continuous-fidelity response is \(F:\mathcal X\times\mathcal Z\to\mathbb R\), with target objective \(f(x)=F(x,z_\star)\). Querying \((x,z)\) returns \[Y(x,z)=F(x,z)+\varepsilon(x,z)\] at cost \(\lambda(x,z)>0\). Fidelity controls are meaningful when their effect is modeled, for example through a discrepancy envelope \(|F(x,z)-f(x)|\le\epsilon(z)\) with \(\epsilon(z_\star)=0\), and through a joint surrogate over \(\mathcal X\times\mathcal Z\). The acquisition selects both design and fidelity subject to budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous fidelity variable jointly controls evaluation accuracy and cost; the target objective is the response at a distinguished terminal fidelity.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\neq\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal Z\) contains the target \(z_\star\).
\(\lambda(x,z)>0\) for admissible queries.
Any stated discrepancy envelope holds throughout \(\mathcal X\times\mathcal Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)=F(x,z_\star)\) and queries are selected from \(\mathcal X\times\mathcal Z\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches continuous fidelity controls and introduces the design, fidelity, target, observation, and cost objects consistently. The discrepancy-envelope formulation and joint acquisition claim require an authoritative source.

children.title: Uncertain Evaluation-Cost Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cost-aware policies when duration or resource demand must also be modeled.

children.title: Unknown Evaluation Costs
children.top_down_role: Policies operating when resource demand must be inferred from observations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pathwise Budget Boundary for Unrevealed Costs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hard-budget limitation when an evaluation charge is unknown until execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_n\) be the remaining hard budget and let \(C(x_{n+1})\) be unrevealed before execution. The condition \(\mathbb E[C(x_{n+1})\mid\mathcal D_n]\le B_n\) does not imply \(C(x_{n+1})\le B_n\) almost surely. A pathwise guarantee therefore requires a valid pre-execution almost-sure upper bound \(\bar c_n(x_{n+1})\le B_n\), reservation of such a bound, or an enforceable mechanism that caps or cancels execution before the budget is exceeded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected affordability does not ensure pathwise affordability; a hard budget requires a valid upper bound, reservation, or enforceable execution cap.
assumptions_latex: \(C(x_{n+1})\) is not observed before execution begins.
\(B_n\) is a hard remaining budget.
knowledge_statements.title: Pathwise Budget Boundary for Unrevealed Costs

assumptions_latex: The design space \(\mathcal X\) is nonempty, and evaluating \(x\in\mathcal X\) reveals both an objective observation and a positive realized cost.
Conditional posterior distributions for the objective \(f\) and cost \(C\) are available from the current data \(\mathcal D_n\).

notation.meaning: Positive random evaluation cost at a design
Nonnegative utility delivered by evaluating a design

review_flags: Exact Bayesian-optimization source for the expected utility-per-random-cost policy is missing.
Alternative risk-sensitive treatments of unknown cost require separate statements.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step cost-aware selection when cost is latent until the evaluation completes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input the current data \(\mathcal D_n\), a joint posterior for objective \(f\) and positive cost \(C\), and a nonnegative one-step utility \(U_n\). Initialize these posteriors from prior data. At iteration \(n\), select any maximizer of \(\mathbb E[U_n(x,f)/C(x)\mid\mathcal D_n]\), evaluate it, observe the objective and realized cost, and condition both models on the new observation. Stop when the cumulative realized cost reaches the prescribed budget, and output the incumbent design according to the objective posterior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Model an unknown evaluation cost jointly with objective utility, choose the design maximizing posterior expected utility per realized cost, update both models, and stop at the cost budget.
knowledge_statements.title: Unknown Evaluation Costs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports using posterior expected utility divided by random realized cost. Positivity alone does not ensure a finite expectation or an attained maximizer; the precise policy and required conditions need an authoritative source.

children.title: Variable Evaluation Costs
children.top_down_role: Policies for evaluation costs that vary across locations, sources, or episodes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Myopic Ratio Rule Is Not Budget-Optimal
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-budget counterexample to global optimality of one-step utility-per-cost selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a deterministic allocation problem with budget \(B=4\) and repeatable actions \(A,B\) having \((c_A,u_A)=(3,5)\) and \((c_B,u_B)=(2,3)\). The utility-per-cost rule chooses \(A\) because \(5/3>3/2\), obtains utility \(5\), and leaves no affordable action. Choosing \(B\) twice is feasible and obtains utility \(6\). Thus maximizing one-step utility per cost is not generally optimal for total finite-budget utility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A higher one-step utility-to-cost ratio can strand budget and yield less total utility than a lower-ratio allocation, so ratio selection is only myopic.
assumptions_latex: Utilities are additive and action \(B\) may be selected twice.
knowledge_statements.title: Myopic Ratio Rule Is Not Budget-Optimal

assumptions_latex: Every admissible evaluation has a known deterministic cost \(c(x)>0\) before selection.
The remaining budget is \(B_n\ge 0\), and \(U_n(x)\ge 0\) is a posterior one-step utility.
review_flags: Exact source for this variable-cost Bayesian-optimization policy is missing.
Utility-per-cost is a myopic policy, not a universal optimality claim.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Known heterogeneous costs handled by a feasible utility-per-cost acquisition rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a design space \(\mathcal X\), current data, known costs \(c(x)>0\), remaining budget \(B_n\), and posterior utility \(U_n(x)\). Initialize \(B_0\) to the total budget. At iteration \(n\), restrict candidates to \(\{x:c(x)\le B_n\}\), maximize \(U_n(x)/c(x)\), evaluate the selected point, update the objective posterior, and set \(B_{n+1}=B_n-c(x_{n+1})\). Stop when no candidate is affordable, and output the incumbent design.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among affordable designs with known heterogeneous costs, select the largest posterior utility per cost, deduct the incurred cost, and stop when no evaluation remains affordable.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable Evaluation Costs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the policy leaf, but no citation supports this particular myopic utility-per-cost rule for known heterogeneous evaluation costs. It must not be presented as generally optimal.

children.title: Cost-Prediction Uncertainty
children.top_down_role: Decision effects of uncertainty in predicted duration or resource consumption.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consequence of propagating positive cost uncertainty instead of substituting posterior mean cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Conditionally on \(\mathcal D_n\), suppose \(U_n(x)\ge 0\), \(C(x)>0\) almost surely, \(U_n(x)\perp C(x)\mid\mathcal D_n\), and the displayed expectations are finite. Then \[\mathbb E\!\left[\frac{U_n(x)}{C(x)}\,\middle|\,\mathcal D_n\right]=\mathbb E[U_n(x)\mid\mathcal D_n]\,\mathbb E[C(x)^{-1}\mid\mathcal D_n]\ge \frac{\mathbb E[U_n(x)\mid\mathcal D_n]}{\mathbb E[C(x)\mid\mathcal D_n]}.\] If \(\mathbb E[U_n(x)\mid\mathcal D_n]>0\), equality holds exactly when \(C(x)\) is conditionally almost surely constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under conditional independence, integrating utility divided by cost uses expected reciprocal cost and dominates the mean-cost plug-in ratio; the inequality is strict for nondegenerate cost and positive expected utility.
assumptions_latex: \(U_n(x)\ge 0\) and \(C(x)>0\) almost surely conditional on \(\mathcal D_n\).
\(U_n(x)\perp C(x)\mid\mathcal D_n\).
\(\mathbb E[U_n(x)\mid\mathcal D_n]\), \(\mathbb E[C(x)\mid\mathcal D_n]\), and \(\mathbb E[C(x)^{-1}\mid\mathcal D_n]\) are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E[U_n(x)/C(x)\mid\mathcal D_n]\ge \mathbb E[U_n(x)\mid\mathcal D_n]/\mathbb E[C(x)\mid\mathcal D_n].
knowledge_statements.title: Reciprocal-Cost Jensen Effect

assumptions_latex: The posterior cost satisfies \(C(x)>0\) almost surely for every candidate design.
The conditional expectation defining the acquisition is finite.

notation.meaning: Random posterior utility from evaluating a design

review_flags: Exact source for integrating cost-prediction uncertainty inside the acquisition is missing.
Replacing random cost by its posterior mean is generally a different acquisition.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Posterior integration of uncertain cost rather than plug-in use of a point prediction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given data \(\mathcal D_n\), let both objective-dependent utility \(U_n(x,f)\) and positive evaluation cost \(C(x)\) be posterior random variables. The uncertainty-aware utility-per-cost acquisition is the posterior expectation of their ratio, not in general the ratio of their posterior expectations. Thus \(a_n^{\mathrm{PUC}}(x)=\mathbb E[U_n(x,f)/C(x)\mid\mathcal D_n]\), with dependence between objective and cost retained in the joint expectation, and the next evaluation maximizes this acquisition over \(\mathcal X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cost-prediction uncertainty is propagated by averaging the utility-to-cost ratio under the joint posterior, retaining dependence and avoiding a generally inequivalent plug-in ratio.
knowledge_statements.title: Cost-Prediction Uncertainty

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation matches the leaf, but no source supports integrating the random reciprocal cost inside the joint posterior expectation. The distinction from a plug-in ratio is mathematically material and requires sourcing.

children.title: Cost-Aware Selection Bias
children.top_down_role: Search distortions caused by systematically favoring inexpensive evaluations.

assumptions_latex: The acquisition has the form \(a_n(x)=u_n(x)/c(x)\) with \(u_n(x)>0\) and \(c(x)>0\).
Two candidates \(x_1,x_2\) are compared at the same iteration.

notation.meaning: Positive cost used by the policy

review_flags: The algebraic ordering property is standard, but a source addressing its Bayesian-optimization selection consequences is missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordering distortion induced specifically by utility-per-cost normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the utility-per-cost rule \(a_n(x)=u_n(x)/c(x)\), candidate \(x_1\) is preferred to \(x_2\) exactly when its relative utility exceeds its relative cost. Consequently, whenever \(u_n(x_1)>u_n(x_2)\) but \(u_n(x_1)/u_n(x_2)<c(x_1)/c(x_2)\), the cost-aware rule reverses the ranking of the unadjusted utility and selects \(x_2\). This is the policy's cost-aware selection bias toward sufficiently cheaper evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dividing utility by cost reverses an unadjusted ranking exactly when the utility ratio is smaller than the corresponding cost ratio, favoring the cheaper candidate.
knowledge_statements.title: Cost-Aware Selection Bias

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed ordering equivalence is correct under the stated positivity assumptions, but no citation supports interpreting this algebraic ranking effect as cost-aware selection bias in Bayesian optimization.

children.title: Multiobjective Bayesian Optimization
children.top_down_role: Surrogate-guided learning of trade-off sets and preference-dependent recommendations.

children.title: Scalarization-Based Policies
children.top_down_role: Reduction through fixed, adaptive, or randomized preferences.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Randomized scalarization for distributing evaluations across preferences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(n\), draw \(\Lambda_n\sim\pi_n(\cdot\mid\mathcal D_n)\), construct an acquisition \(a_n(x;\Lambda_n)\) for \(s_{\Lambda_n}(F(x))\), select a measurable maximizer, evaluate the full objective vector, and update the surrogate. A preference set receiving zero probability eventually receives no direct future targeting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample a preference, optimize its scalar acquisition, and update using the full vector response.
assumptions_latex: \(\pi_n\) is a specified probability kernel.
The scalarization orientation and acquisition are specified.
A measurable maximizer-selection rule exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Random-Preference Scalarized Bayesian Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted-Sum Reach and Unsupported Pareto Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Guarantee and limitation of positive weighted sums in minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(w\in\mathbb R_{++}^m\) and \(x_w\in\arg\min_x w^\top f(x)\), then \(x_w\) is Pareto optimal. Weighted sums recover supported efficient objective vectors, but a nonconvex upper image may contain Pareto vectors that minimize no nonzero nonnegative weighted sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive weighted sums return Pareto optima, but unsupported points on nonconvex fronts can be unreachable.
assumptions_latex: All objectives are minimized.
A scalarized minimizer exists.
Weights are strictly positive for the strong Pareto conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w\in\mathbb R_{++}^m,\ x_w\in\arg\min_x w^\top f(x)\Rightarrow x_w\text{ is Pareto optimal}.
review_flags: The Builder's ambiguous converse was removed; the supported-solution formulation is retained.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted-Sum Reach and Unsupported Pareto Points

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strictly increasing nonlinear scalarization capable of targeting nonsupported regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(w_i>0\), \(\rho>0\), and reference vector \(z\), define \(s_{w,z}(y)=\max_i w_i(y_i-z_i)+\rho\sum_iw_i(y_i-z_i)\). This scalarization is strictly increasing in the componentwise order, so every global minimizer of \(s_{w,z}(f(x))\) is Pareto optimal. Its max term can target nonsupported portions of a nonconvex front.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Augmented Chebyshev scalarization combines worst weighted deviation with a positive weighted sum and can reach regions missed by weighted sums.
assumptions_latex: \(w_i>0\) for every objective.
A global scalarized minimizer exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Augmented Chebyshev Scalarization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed, Adaptive, Sampled, and Preference-Averaged Scalarization Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Umbrella separation of four noninterchangeable scalarization-selection rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given scalar acquisitions \(a_n(x;\lambda)\): (i) a fixed-preference policy uses a prescribed \(\lambda_0\) and maximizes \(a_n(x;\lambda_0)\); (ii) a history-adaptive policy sets \(\lambda_n=\phi_n(\mathcal D_n)\) before maximizing \(a_n(x;\lambda_n)\); (iii) a sampled-preference policy draws \(\Lambda_n\sim\pi_n(\cdot\mid\mathcal D_n)\) and then maximizes \(a_n(x;\Lambda_n)\); and (iv) a preference-averaged policy maximizes \(\bar a_n(x)=\int a_n(x;\lambda)\pi_n(d\lambda\mid\mathcal D_n)\). Maximizing the averaged acquisition is generally not equivalent to sampling a preference and maximizing conditionally.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed, history-adaptive, freshly sampled, and preference-averaged scalarization policies use distinct selection rules.
assumptions_latex: The scalarization orientation and each induced acquisition are specified.
\(\phi_n\) is measurable and \(\pi_n\) is a probability kernel.
Required maximizers or measurable approximate-selection rules exist.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed, Adaptive, Sampled, and Preference-Averaged Scalarization Policies

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Preference Averaging Is Not Random Preference Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-action counterexample separating averaged and sampled scalarized acquisitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let actions be \(x_1,x_2\), preferences \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2\) be equiprobable, and acquisitions satisfy \(a(x_1;\lambda_1)=2\), \(a(x_2;\lambda_1)=0\), \(a(x_1;\lambda_2)=0\), and \(a(x_2;\lambda_2)=1\). The averaged acquisition uniquely selects \(x_1\), whereas sampled-preference maximization selects \(x_1\) and \(x_2\) with equal probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximizing expected acquisition over preferences can differ from sampling one preference and optimizing it.
assumptions_latex: Conditional acquisition maximizations have no ties.
knowledge_statements.title: Preference Averaging Is Not Random Preference Selection

assumptions_latex: The objective map is \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R^m\), with minimization in every component.
The scalarization \(s_\lambda:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) and preference parameter \(\lambda\) are fixed or sampled before selecting the evaluation.

notation.meaning: Scalarization indexed by a preference parameter
Single-objective acquisition induced by the scalarized posterior

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports scalarization-based multiobjective Bayesian optimization.
Different scalarizations recover different subsets of the Pareto front.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction of multiobjective Bayesian optimization through fixed, adaptive, or randomized scalar preferences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input posterior data \(\mathcal D_n\), a family of scalarizations \(s_\lambda\), a preference rule for \(\lambda\), and a scalar Bayesian-optimization acquisition. Initialize the vector-objective surrogate. At iteration \(n\), fix or sample \(\lambda\), form the posterior scalar objective \(s_\lambda(f(x))\), compute its acquisition \(a_n^{(\lambda)}(x)\), and maximize either that acquisition or its expectation over randomized preferences. Evaluate the vector objective, update the surrogate, and return the nondominated evaluated set at termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convert vector outcomes to scalar utilities using fixed, adaptive, or sampled preferences, optimize the induced acquisition, and return the nondominated evaluated designs.
knowledge_statements.title: Scalarization-Based Policies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the scalarization-based multiobjective Bayesian-optimization procedure. The statement also combines fixed, sampled, and expected-over-preferences policies without specifying when each selection formula applies.

children.title: Hypervolume-Based Policies
children.top_down_role: Acquisitions valuing expansion of the dominated objective-space region.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-space utility underlying hypervolume policies for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) and a reference point \(r\) weakly worse than every relevant vector, let \(D(P;r)=\bigcup_{y\in P}\prod_{i=1}^m[y_i,r_i]\) and \(\operatorname{HV}(P;r)=\lambda_m(D(P;r))\). For \(y\leq r\), \(\operatorname{HVI}(y;P,r)=\operatorname{HV}(P\cup\{y\};r)-\operatorname{HV}(P;r)=\lambda_m(\prod_i[y_i,r_i]\setminus D(P;r))\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hypervolume measures the reference-bounded region dominated by a set; improvement is the additional measure contributed by a candidate.
assumptions_latex: All objectives are minimized.
\(P\) is finite and relevant vectors weakly dominate \(r\).
\(\lambda_m\) is Lebesgue measure.
knowledge_statements.title: Dominated Hypervolume and Hypervolume Improvement

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural properties of dominated hypervolume.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(r\), \(D(A;r)\supseteq D(B;r)\) implies \(\operatorname{HV}(A;r)\geq\operatorname{HV}(B;r)\). Changing \(r\), however, changes box side lengths and can reverse the hypervolume ordering of mutually nondominating approximation sets; therefore the reference point is part of the policy specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hypervolume is monotone under dominated-region inclusion for a fixed reference point, but rankings can depend on the reference point.
assumptions_latex: A common minimization convention and fixed valid reference point are used for monotonicity.
knowledge_statements.title: Reference-Point Dependence and Dominated-Region Monotonicity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint batch variant accounting for overlap among candidates' dominated regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a batch \(X_q=(x_1,\ldots,x_q)\), define \(q\operatorname{EHVI}_n(X_q)=\mathbb E[\operatorname{HV}(P_n\cup\{F(x_j):1\le j\le q\};r)-\operatorname{HV}(P_n;r)\mid\mathcal D_n]\). A joint batch policy maximizes this quantity over admissible batches. Generally \(q\operatorname{EHVI}_n(X_q)\neq\sum_{j=1}^q\operatorname{EHVI}_n(x_j)\), because dominated increments can overlap and predictions can be dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Batch EHVI values the union of the batch members' improvements and is generally not the sum of individual EHVI values.
assumptions_latex: The joint posterior of all batch objective vectors is specified.
The reference point and minimization convention are fixed.
Expected batch improvement is finite.

notation.meaning: Joint expected hypervolume improvement of a size-q batch.

knowledge_statements.title: Batch Expected Hypervolume Improvement

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical sequential EHVI under a fixed minimization convention and reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For current finite nondominated evaluated objective set \(P_n\), fixed reference point \(r\), and posterior random objective vector \(F(x)\), define \(\operatorname{EHVI}_n(x)=\mathbb E[\operatorname{HVI}(F(x);P_n,r)\mid\mathcal D_n]\). Select a measurable global maximizer \(x_{n+1}\in\arg\max_{x\in\mathcal X}\operatorname{EHVI}_n(x)\), observe every objective component, and update the joint posterior and \(P_n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequential EHVI chooses the design with greatest posterior expected increase in dominated hypervolume.
assumptions_latex: All objectives are minimized.
\(P_n\) is finite and \(r\) is fixed and componentwise no better than every objective vector included in the reference-bounded calculation.
Expected hypervolume improvement is finite and a measurable maximizer is selected.
knowledge_statements.title: One-Step Expected Hypervolume Improvement Policy

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Noisy Observations Require a Latent-Front Convention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating noiseless EHVI from noisy hypervolume policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With noisy objective observations, the observed nondominated set need not equal the nondominated set of latent objective values. Consequently, an expression using a deterministic observed \(P_n\) does not uniquely define noisy EHVI. A noisy policy must declare whether it integrates over latent values at evaluated designs, conditions on a represented latent front, or uses a plug-in front; these choices generally yield different acquisitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noisy EHVI is not uniquely specified until the treatment of uncertainty in the latent incumbent front is declared.
assumptions_latex: At least one objective is observed with nonzero noise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_n^{\rm obs}\neq P_n^{\rm latent}\ \text{in general, so noiseless EHVI has no unique noisy extension}.
knowledge_statements.title: Noisy Observations Require a Latent-Front Convention

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fully Bayesian Noisy Expected Hypervolume Improvement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential noisy EHVI integrating uncertainty in latent objective values at previously evaluated designs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_n=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), let \(F_n=(F(x_1),\ldots,F(x_n))\) be the posterior-random latent objective vectors, and let \(P(F_n)=\operatorname{ND}\{F(x_i):1\le i\le n\}\). Under minimization, define hypervolume through the reference-bounded dominated region \(\{z:\exists y\in P,\ y\le z\le r\}\), so outcomes not dominating \(r\) contribute no invalid box. Then \[\operatorname{NEHVI}_n(x)=\mathbb E\!\left[\operatorname{HV}\bigl(P(F_n)\cup\{F(x)\};r\bigr)-\operatorname{HV}\bigl(P(F_n);r\bigr)\mid\mathcal D_n\right].\] A fully Bayesian noisy-EHVI policy selects a measurable global maximizer. The expectation is joint over latent values at previous designs and the candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noisy EHVI averages hypervolume improvement jointly over the uncertain latent front and the candidate's latent objectives.
assumptions_latex: All objectives are minimized and a fixed finite reference point is used with the reference-bounded dominated-region convention.
The joint posterior of latent objective vectors at old and candidate designs is specified.
The expectation is finite and a measurable maximizer exists.

notation.meaning: Posterior-random nondominated latent front at evaluated designs.
Fully Bayesian noisy expected hypervolume improvement.

knowledge_statements.title: Fully Bayesian Noisy Expected Hypervolume Improvement

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Biobjective Hypervolume by a Nondominated Sweep
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact low-dimensional computation underlying biobjective hypervolume policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite minimization set \(P\subset\mathbb R^2\), remove points outside the reference box, dominated points, and duplicates. Sort the remaining points so that \(y^{(1)}_1<\cdots<y^{(k)}_1\), hence \(y^{(1)}_2>\cdots>y^{(k)}_2\). With \(y^{(0)}_2=r_2\), \[\operatorname{HV}(P;r)=\sum_{j=1}^k(r_1-y^{(j)}_1)(y^{(j-1)}_2-y^{(j)}_2).\] Comparison sorting gives \(O(n\log n)\) time and \(O(n)\) storage for \(n=|P|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In two objectives, sorting the nondominated staircase and summing disjoint rectangles computes exact hypervolume in O(n log n) time.
assumptions_latex: All objectives are minimized.
Only points weakly dominating the finite reference point contribute.
Coordinate comparisons and arithmetic take constant time.

notation.meaning: The j-th nondominated point in increasing first-coordinate order.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Biobjective Hypervolume by a Nondominated Sweep

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case computational boundary when objective dimension is part of the input.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For rational point coordinates and reference point, exact dominated-hypervolume computation is \(\#P\)-hard when the objective dimension is part of the input. Exact deterministic hypervolume improvement, and hence exact EHVI for posterior families admitting degenerate predictive laws, contains exact hypervolume computation as a special case and has no general polynomial-time algorithm unless the corresponding counting-complexity collapse occurs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact hypervolume is counting-hard in variable dimension; exact EHVI inherits this worst-case obstruction through deterministic predictive instances.
assumptions_latex: The number of objectives is variable rather than fixed.
Coordinates have finite rational encodings.
Exact rather than approximate evaluation is required.
review_flags: hardness claim uses the finite rational encoding model
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Dimension Exact Hypervolume Hardness

assumptions_latex: All objectives are minimized, and the reference point \(r\in\mathbb R^m\) is dominated by every objective vector of interest.
The current nondominated objective set \(P_n\) is finite.

notation.meaning: Current nondominated set in objective space

Reference-point and minimization conventions require source confirmation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step expected hypervolume improvement for finite nondominated objective sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input the current nondominated objective set \(P_n\), posterior vector outcome \(F(x)\), and reference point \(r\). For each candidate \(x\), compute the posterior expected increment in dominated hypervolume, \(\mathbb E[\operatorname{HV}(P_n\cup\{F(x)\};r)-\operatorname{HV}(P_n;r)\mid\mathcal D_n]\). Select a maximizer, evaluate all objective components there, update the surrogate and \(P_n\), and repeat until the evaluation budget is exhausted. Output the final nondominated evaluated set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the design with greatest posterior expected expansion of the dominated region relative to a fixed reference point, then update the nondominated set.
knowledge_statements.title: Hypervolume-Based Policies

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed computational boundary for exact hypervolume and EHVI.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed objective dimension, exact hypervolume admits algorithms polynomial in the number of points, whereas variable objective dimension produces worst-case intractability; exact EHVI consequently inherits dimension-sensitive decomposition or integration costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact hypervolume is tractable in fixed low dimension but can become intractable as the number of objectives varies.
assumptions_latex: Coordinates have a finite encoding.
Objective dimension is variable in the hardness claim.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Exact hypervolume complexity depends critically on objective dimension.}
