children.title: Information-Based Pareto Learning
children.top_down_role: Policies targeting uncertainty about Pareto sets, fronts, or preference-optimal solutions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Representation Dependence of Pareto-Object Differential Entropy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on entropy formulations for coordinate encodings of random fronts and sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a continuous coordinate encoding \(Z\) is reparameterized by a differentiable bijection \(W=\phi(Z)\), then \(h(W\mid\mathcal D)=h(Z\mid\mathcal D)+\mathbb E[\log|\det J_\phi(Z)|\mid\mathcal D]\). Raw differential entropy is therefore encoding-dependent, whereas \(I(Y_x;Z\mid\mathcal D)\) is invariant under measurable bijections of \(Z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Differential entropy depends on the chosen coordinates for a Pareto object, while mutual information is invariant under bijective reparameterization.
assumptions_latex: The encoding has a density.
\(\phi\) is a differentiable bijection with nonzero Jacobian determinant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: h(\phi(Z)\mid\mathcal D)-h(Z\mid\mathcal D)=\mathbb E[\log|\det J_\phi(Z)|\mid\mathcal D].
knowledge_statements.title: Representation Dependence of Pareto-Object Differential Entropy

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Predictive-Entropy Form of Pareto Information Gain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mutual-information representation avoiding direct entropy evaluation of a random Pareto object.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a measurable Pareto target \(Z\) and prospective observation \(Y_x\), finite conditional mutual information satisfies \(I(Y_x;Z\mid\mathcal D)=H(Y_x\mid\mathcal D)-\mathbb E[H(Y_x\mid Z,\mathcal D)\mid\mathcal D]\), whenever the displayed entropies are defined. Equivalently, mutual information may always be defined through conditional relative entropy under its usual absolute-continuity conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Information about a Pareto target can be computed as reduction in predictive observation entropy, avoiding direct entropy of the target representation.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) and \(Y_x\) are measurable random elements.
Conditional mutual information is finite; displayed entropies exist when that form is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: I(Y_x;Z\mid\mathcal D)=H(Y_x\mid\mathcal D)-\mathbb E[H(Y_x\mid Z,\mathcal D)\mid\mathcal D].
knowledge_statements.title: Predictive-Entropy Form of Pareto Information Gain

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step information policy for a specified measurable Pareto target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z=\psi(F)\) be a declared measurable target of the posterior objective function, such as a finite-domain Pareto set, a measurably encoded front, or a preference-optimal solution. For a prospective vector observation \(Y_x\), define \(a_n(x)=I(Y_x;Z\mid\mathcal D_n)\). If this quantity is finite and admits a measurable maximizer, select \(x_{n+1}\in\arg\max_x a_n(x)\), observe \(Y_{x_{n+1}}\), and update the joint posterior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the observation carrying the most conditional mutual information about a precisely represented Pareto target.
assumptions_latex: \(Z=\psi(F)\) is a measurable random element on a declared measurable space.
The observation kernel and joint posterior are specified.
Conditional mutual information is finite and a measurable maximizer exists.

notation.meaning: Measurable map from the latent objective function to the selected Pareto target.

knowledge_statements.title: Pareto-Target Mutual-Information Policy

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinct information targets that must not be interchanged implicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For latent vector objective \(F\), three distinct targets are \(Z_X=\operatorname{ParetoSet}(F)\subseteq\mathcal X\), \(Z_Y=F(Z_X)\subseteq\mathbb R^m\), and \(Z_\lambda\in\arg\min_x s_\lambda(F(x))\) under a declared measurable tie rule. Generally \(I(Y_x;Z_X\mid\mathcal D)\), \(I(Y_x;Z_Y\mid\mathcal D)\), and \(I(Y_x;Z_\lambda\mid\mathcal D)\) differ, so the target is part of the policy specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Learning the Pareto set, objective-space front, and a preference-optimal solution are different information objectives.
assumptions_latex: Each target has a specified measurable representation.
The preference scalarization and tie rule defining \(Z_\lambda\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Z_X\not\equiv Z_Y\not\equiv Z_\lambda\quad\text{as information targets in general}.

notation.meaning: Design-space Pareto set, objective-space front, and preference-optimal target.

knowledge_statements.title: Pareto-Set, Pareto-Front, and Preference-Optimum Targets

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information targets based on ideal or preference-indexed optimum values rather than optimizer locations or an entire Pareto object.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=(F_1,\ldots,F_m)\) be a latent minimization objective. The ideal-value target is \(V^{\mathrm{id}}=(\inf_xF_1(x),\ldots,\inf_xF_m(x))\); for a fixed scalarization \(s_\lambda\), the preference-value target is \(V_\lambda=\inf_x s_\lambda(F(x))\). Whenever the selected target \(V\) is measurable and \(I(Y_x;V\mid\mathcal D_n)<\infty\), an optimum-value information policy uses \(a_n(x)=I(Y_x;V\mid\mathcal D_n)\). These value targets differ from the Pareto set, Pareto front, and preference-optimal design and generally induce different acquisitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Information policies may learn ideal or scalarized optimum values, which are distinct targets from Pareto sets, fronts, and optimizer locations.
assumptions_latex: The infima define measurable random elements, or measurable finite-domain minima are used.
The scalarization and preference parameter are fixed when \(V_\lambda\) is targeted.
Conditional mutual information is finite.

notation.meaning: Vector of componentwise latent optimum values.
Latent optimum value of a fixed scalarization.

knowledge_statements.title: Pareto-Related Optimum-Value Information Targets

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional data-processing relation between fine and coarse measurable representations of a Pareto target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\) be a measurable Pareto target, let \(Z'=\phi(Z)\) be a measurable coarsening, and let \(Y_x\) be a prospective observation. Whenever the conditional mutual informations are defined, \[I(Y_x;Z'\mid\mathcal D_n)\le I(Y_x;Z\mid\mathcal D_n).\] Thus a summary cannot increase the information attributed to an observation, although it can change the acquisition maximizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A measurable summary of a Pareto target cannot carry more information from an observation than the original target.
assumptions_latex: \(Z'=\phi(Z)\) for a measurable map \(\phi\).
The relevant regular conditional laws and conditional mutual informations exist.

notation.meaning: Measurable coarsening of the original Pareto target.

knowledge_statements.title: Information Loss Under Pareto-Target Coarsening

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Determined estimator for finitely encoded Pareto targets and observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((Y^{(s)},Z^{(s)})_{s=1}^S\) be conditionally iid draws from the posterior joint law of finite-alphabet variables \((Y_x,Z)\). For empirical frequencies \(\widehat p_S\), define \[\widehat I_S(Y_x;Z)=\sum_{y,z:\widehat p_S(y,z)>0}\widehat p_S(y,z)\log\frac{\widehat p_S(y,z)}{\widehat p_S(y)\widehat p_S(z)}.\] Candidate designs may be ranked using this estimate, provided their target and observation encodings remain fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For fixed finite encodings, estimate Pareto information gain from the empirical joint-frequency table.
assumptions_latex: \(Y_x\) and \(Z\) have fixed finite alphabets.
The paired samples are conditionally iid under the current posterior.
The encodings are declared before estimation.

notation.meaning: Empirical posterior joint frequency of the encoded observation and target.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Alphabet Plug-In Pareto-Information Estimator

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Consistency of Finite-Alphabet Pareto Information Estimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency boundary for the finite-alphabet plug-in estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under conditionally iid sampling from a fixed joint law on finite alphabets, with \(0\log0=0\), \[\widehat I_S(Y_x;Z)\xrightarrow[S\to\infty]{\mathrm{a.s.}}I(Y_x;Z\mid\mathcal D_n).\] The conclusion does not directly cover continuous observations, changing discretizations, or unencoded random sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The empirical mutual-information estimate is strongly consistent for fixed finite encodings only.
assumptions_latex: Samples are conditionally iid given \(\mathcal D_n\).
Both alphabets are finite and fixed as \(S\) grows.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong Consistency of Finite-Alphabet Pareto Information Estimation

assumptions_latex: The posterior induces a random Pareto object \(Z\), such as a Pareto set, front, or preference-optimal solution.
The mutual information \(I(Y_x;Z\mid\mathcal D_n)\) is finite for every candidate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_{n+1}\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X}I(Y_x;Z\mid\mathcal D_n)=\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X}\bigl[H(Z\mid\mathcal D_n)-\mathbb E[H(Z\mid\mathcal D_n,Y_x)\mid\mathcal D_n]\bigr].\]

notation.meaning: Posterior random Pareto object of interest
Prospective observation at a candidate design

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mutual-information acquisition targeting a specified random Pareto object.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\) denote the posterior random Pareto set, Pareto front, or preference-optimal solution, and let \(Y_x\) be the observation obtained at \(x\). The information acquisition equals \(I(Y_x;Z\mid\mathcal D_n)\), equivalently the current conditional entropy of \(Z\) minus its expected conditional entropy after observing \(Y_x\). An information-based Pareto policy selects a design maximizing this quantity, observes the vector response, conditions the posterior, and repeats until its budget is exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select evaluations that maximize expected information about a designated Pareto set, front, or preference-optimal solution, measured by posterior entropy reduction.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Posterior utility for learning an unknown Pareto frontier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given data \(\mathcal D=(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\), let \(q_{\mathcal D}(x)=\Pr(x\text{ is not dominated by any sampled point}\mid\mathcal D)\). When this function is integrable, \(U(\mathcal D)=-\int_{\mathcal X}q_{\mathcal D}(x)\,dx\) is a utility for posterior Pareto-frontier learning. Because \(q_{\mathcal D}(x)\ge0\), \(U(\mathcal D)\le0\). If the integrated nondomination uncertainty tends to zero as the frontier is learned, then \(U(\mathcal D)\to0\), its maximal value. Observations can be selected through one-step lookahead in this utility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integrating the posterior probability that candidates remain nondominated by sampled points measures uncertainty about the Pareto frontier. Negating the integral gives a utility bounded above by zero; it approaches zero if the integrated uncertainty vanishes and can support one-step lookahead selection.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal D=(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)
q_{\mathcal D}\text{ is measurable and integrable over }\mathcal X
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U(\mathcal D)=-\int_{\mathcal X}q_{\mathcal D}(x)\,dx\le0,\qquad \int_{\mathcal X}q_{\mathcal D}(x)\,dx\to0\implies U(\mathcal D)\to0.

children.title: Random-Environment Optimization
children.top_down_role: Policies integrating performance over environmental uncertainty.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic BO policy for a known-law mean environmental objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration n, update a surrogate for f(x,w), integrate its posterior under P_W to represent g, select an admissible evaluation using an acquisition defined for g, observe the response at the realized or validly selected environment, and update the surrogate. Return a declared posterior recommendation for minimizing g.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integrate the surrogate over the known environmental law, acquire observations for mean performance, and return a recommended design.
assumptions_latex: The acquisition and recommendation are defined for g.
The observation mechanism preserves identification of the P_W expectation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat x_N\in\mathcal X\text{ is recommended for minimizing }g.
knowledge_statements.title: Environment-Integrated Bayesian-Optimization Loop

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identification boundary when environments are selected rather than naturally realized.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If uncontrolled environments satisfy W_i\sim P_W, observations directly target the declared law. If instead w_i is selected from q_i(\cdot\mid x_i)\ne P_W, naive unweighted averaging need not estimate g. Valid correction requires an explicit joint model or valid weighting; importance weighting additionally requires P_W\ll q_i(\cdot\mid x) on the relevant support.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selected environments require modeling or valid reweighting; otherwise the learned expectation may target the wrong law.
assumptions_latex: g(x)\text{ is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q_i\ne P_W\Longrightarrow\text{uncorrected averages need not estimate }g.
knowledge_statements.title: Environmental Sampling-Law Compatibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mean performance under a fixed known environmental distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an uncontrollable environment W\sim P_W and integrable response f(x,W), define g(x)=\mathbb E_{P_W}[f(x,W)]. Random-environment Bayesian optimization learns f or g through costly observations and seeks a minimizer of g.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Random-environment BO minimizes mean performance under a known environmental law.
assumptions_latex: P_W\text{ is fixed and known}.
f(x,W)\text{ is }P_W\text{-integrable for every }x.
knowledge_statements.title: Known-Law Random-Environment Objective

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Posterior representation of the mean environmental objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If f\mid\mathcal D_n is Gaussian with mean m_n and covariance k_n and the integrals exist, then g\mid\mathcal D_n is Gaussian with \mu_n^g(x)=\int m_n(x,w)P_W(dw) and k_n^g(x,x')=\iint k_n((x,w),(x',w'))P_W(dw)P_W(dw').
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integrating a joint GP over the known environmental law yields a GP for mean performance.
assumptions_latex: The displayed mean and covariance integrals are finite.

notation.meaning: Posterior mean of the joint response.
Posterior covariance of the joint response.

knowledge_statements.title: Environment-Integrated Gaussian-Process Posterior

assumptions_latex: The environment \(W\) has a known probability law \(P_W\), and \(f(x,W)\) is integrable for every \(x\in\mathcal X\).
A posterior surrogate for the joint input \((x,w)\) is available from \(\mathcal D_n\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bayesian optimization of mean performance under a known environmental distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a design space \(\mathcal X\), environmental law \(P_W\), joint surrogate for \(f(x,w)\), and an evaluation budget. Initialize the surrogate from \(\mathcal D_0\). At iteration \(n\), integrate the posterior over \(W\sim P_W\) to induce a posterior for \(g(x)=\mathbb E_W[f(x,W)]\), maximize an acquisition defined for minimizing \(g\), observe performance at the selected design and realized or chosen environment, and update the joint surrogate. Output a posterior-recommended minimizer of \(g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integrate the joint surrogate over the known environmental law, optimize an acquisition for expected performance, update with each environment-dependent observation, and return the recommended design.

children.title: Risk-Sensitive Bayesian Optimization
children.top_down_role: Optimization of tail, quantile, reliability, or downside-sensitive performance.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic loop for one fixed, explicitly declared risk functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a risk functional \rho and a joint surrogate for L_x=f(x,W). At iteration n, propagate the posterior and environmental law through \rho, choose an admissible observation using an acquisition defined for uncertainty about \rho(L_x), update the surrogate, and at termination return a declared posterior recommendation for minimizing \rho(L_x).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagate surrogate uncertainty through one declared risk functional and acquire evaluations for that risk objective.
assumptions_latex: \rho(L_x)\text{ is finite on the modeled losses.
The acquisition is calibrated to the chosen \rho rather than a different risk functional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat x_N\in\mathcal X\text{ is recommended for minimizing }\rho(L_x).
knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Functional Bayesian-Optimization Loop

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantile-loss specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For L_x=f(x,W) and \alpha\in(0,1), \operatorname{VaR}_\alpha(L_x)=\inf\{z:\Pr(L_x\le z)\ge\alpha\}. Quantile-risk Bayesian optimization seeks to minimize this functional over x.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quantile-risk BO minimizes a declared upper loss quantile.
assumptions_latex: L_x\text{ has a probability distribution for every }x.
knowledge_statements.title: Value-at-Risk Environmental Objective

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probability-of-failure specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For failure threshold \tau, define r_\tau(x)=\Pr(f(x,W)>\tau). Reliability-oriented Bayesian optimization minimizes r_\tau(x), equivalently maximizing \Pr(f(x,W)\le\tau).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reliability BO minimizes failure probability or maximizes threshold satisfaction probability.
assumptions_latex: \{f(x,W)>\tau\}\text{ is measurable for every }x.
knowledge_statements.title: Reliability Objective

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating quantile, tail-mean, and reliability policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Equal \operatorname{VaR}_\alpha values do not imply equal \operatorname{CVaR}_\alpha values or equal failure probabilities at a fixed threshold. Atoms can also make the set of quantile minimizers unstable under small distributional changes. Therefore an acquisition calibrated for one of these functionals is not generally valid for the others.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quantile, tail-mean, and reliability objectives are not interchangeable.
assumptions_latex: The compared risk quantities are finite where required.
knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Functional Noninterchangeability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tail-mean objective and auxiliary-threshold formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For integrable loss L_x and \alpha\in(0,1), \operatorname{CVaR}_\alpha(L_x)=\inf_{z\in\mathbb R}\left[z+\frac{1}{1-\alpha}\mathbb E(L_x-z)_+\right]. Consequently, minimizing CVaR over x is equivalent at the level of infima to joint minimization over (x,z) of the displayed objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: CVaR is a threshold plus scaled expected excess loss, giving an auxiliary-variable tail-risk formulation.
assumptions_latex: \mathbb E|L_x|<\infty\text{ for every }x.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Value-at-Risk Representation

assumptions_latex: For every design \(x\), the environmental loss \(L_x=f(x,W)\) is integrable.
A risk functional \(\rho\) is fixed and finite on the posterior-supported losses.

notation.meaning: Environmental loss induced by a design
Chosen risk functional, such as a quantile or conditional tail expectation

Initialize the surrogate from \(\mathcal D_0\). children.title: Distributionally Robust Bayesian Optimization
children.top_down_role: Surrogate-guided optimization under ambiguity about environmental distributions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mechanism-neutral loop separating the BO policy from ambiguity-set subproblem solvers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration n, condition a surrogate for f on \mathcal D_n, propagate its posterior through Q\mapsto\mathbb E_Q[f(x,W)] and the supremum over Q\in\mathcal P, select an admissible design-environment evaluation by a declared acquisition, and update the surrogate. At termination return a declared posterior recommendation for minimizing R.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a surrogate to learn the worst-case expectation, acquire informative evaluations, and return a robust recommendation.
assumptions_latex: The ambiguity set and environmental sampling mechanism are specified.
The posterior robust functional and acquisition are finite on candidate actions.
The inner worst-case problem is solved or approximated with declared accuracy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat x_N\in\mathcal X\text{ is selected using the posterior robust objective}.
knowledge_statements.title: Surrogate-Guided Distributionally Robust Evaluation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case mean performance over a fixed ambiguity set of environmental laws.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty ambiguity set \mathcal P of laws on W, define R(x)=\sup_{Q\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_Q[f(x,W)]. Distributionally robust Bayesian optimization seeks a design minimizing R while learning f through costly evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distributionally robust BO learns and minimizes worst-case expected performance over an ambiguity set.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal P\ne\varnothing.
R(x)\text{ is well-defined in the extended reals for each }x.
knowledge_statements.title: Distributionally Robust Environmental Objective

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finiteness boundary for acquisition and recommendation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If for every x there is Q_x\in\mathcal P with \mathbb E_{Q_x}[f(x,W)]=+\infty, then R(x)=+\infty for all x. The objective cannot rank designs, and finite-value improvement acquisitions are undefined until \mathcal P or the growth of f is restricted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every design admits infinite worst-case expected loss, the robust objective cannot guide optimization.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal P\ne\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Everywhere-Infinite Robust Objective

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reduction to known-distribution random-environment optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \mathcal P=\{P_W\}, then R(x)=\mathbb E_{P_W}[f(x,W)] for every x.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singleton ambiguity set recovers the ordinary known-distribution expectation objective.
assumptions_latex: f(x,W)\text{ is }P_W\text{-integrable for every }x.
knowledge_statements.title: Singleton-Ambiguity Reduction

assumptions_latex: The ambiguity set \(\mathcal P\) is nonempty and contains probability laws on the environmental space.
For every \(x\in\mathcal X\), the worst-case expectation is finite.

notation.meaning: Ambiguity set of environmental probability laws

review_flags: The cited robust-optimization section provisionally supports the worst-case formulation, not its Bayesian-optimization acquisition.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case expected performance over a fixed ambiguity set of environmental laws.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an ambiguity set \(\mathcal P\), a surrogate for \(f(x,w)\), and an evaluation budget. Initialize the surrogate from observed design-environment responses. At iteration \(n\), use its posterior to represent \(R(x)=\sup_{Q\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_Q[f(x,W)]\), compute an acquisition for minimizing or learning \(R\), and evaluate a maximizing candidate under an admissible environmental sampling mechanism. Update the surrogate and ambiguity information when permitted. At termination, output a posterior-recommended minimizer of the worst-case expected objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use the surrogate to learn worst-case expected performance over an ambiguity set of environmental laws, acquire informative designs, and return the robust recommendation.
knowledge_statements.title: Distributionally Robust Bayesian Optimization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited robust-optimization section may support the worst-case expectation objective, but not the surrogate-guided Bayesian-optimization procedure. The acquisition and environmental sampling mechanism are left unspecified and need a directly relevant source.

children.title: Cross-Task Transfer Bayesian Optimization Family
children.top_down_role: Policies sharing information across contexts, tasks, systems, or optimization episodes.

children.title: Contextual Bayesian Optimization
children.top_down_role: Optimization policies conditioned on observed but uncontrolled context.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Population objective for a policy mapping observed exogenous contexts to controllable actions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\sim q\) be an exogenous context observed before action selection and let \(f(x,z)\) be an integrable loss. A contextual policy is a measurable map \(\pi:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal X\), with population risk \[R_q(\pi)=\mathbb E_{Z\sim q}[f(\pi(Z),Z)].\] If the pointwise argmin correspondence admits a measurable selection, every \(\pi^\star\) satisfying \(\pi^\star(z)\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x,z)\) for \(q\)-almost every \(z\) minimizes \(R_q\) over measurable policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Contextual optimization seeks a measurable action rule; a measurable pointwise minimizer minimizes expected loss over the deployment context distribution.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\sim q\) is uncontrolled and observed before choosing the action.
\(f(\pi(Z),Z)\) is integrable for every admissible policy.
The pointwise argmin correspondence admits a measurable selection for the final conclusion.
knowledge_statements.title: Contextual Policy Objective

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-pattern boundary separating contextual optimization from joint-input optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For round \(n\), a variable \(z_n\) can index the current contextual action only if it is uncontrolled and available to the policy before \(x_n\) is selected. If the optimizer chooses \(z_n\), then \((x_n,z_n)\) is a joint design variable. If \(z_n\) is revealed only after selection of \(x_n\), a current-round rule \(x_n=\pi(z_n)\) is not implementable under that information pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contextual action requires an uncontrolled context available before acting; controllable contexts are design variables, while later-revealed contexts cannot condition the current action.
assumptions_latex: \(x_n\) must be measurable with respect to the information available when the round-\(n\) action is chosen.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_n=\pi(z_n)\ \text{is implementable only if }z_n\text{ is available before }x_n\text{ is chosen}.
knowledge_statements.title: Observed-Before-Action Context Boundary

assumptions_latex: At round \(n\), an uncontrolled context \(z_n\in\mathcal Z\) is observed before choosing a controllable action \(x_n\in\mathcal X\).
The posterior models the response function \(f:\mathcal X\times\mathcal Z\to\mathbb R\).

notation.meaning: Recommended action policy after n observations

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports contextual Bayesian optimization.
The displayed recommendation uses minimization while the acquisition is written in maximization form.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential action selection after observing an exogenous context.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a joint surrogate for \(f(x,z)\), an action space \(\mathcal X\), and sequentially revealed contexts. Initialize from \(\mathcal D_0\). At round \(n\), observe the uncontrolled context \(z_n\), form the conditioned acquisition \(a_{n-1}(x;z_n)\), choose a maximizing action \(x_n\), observe its response, and append \((x_n,z_n,y_n)\) to the data. After the stopping rule, output the context-indexed posterior policy \(\pi_n\) that recommends an action for each context.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Observe the exogenous context first, maximize a context-conditioned acquisition over controllable actions, update the joint surrogate, and return a context-indexed action policy.
knowledge_statements.title: Contextual Bayesian Optimization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports the contextual Bayesian-optimization policy. The displayed recommendation also equates a single-valued policy with an argmin set; it must use membership, define a tie-breaking selection, or explicitly be set-valued.

children.title: Multitask Bayesian Optimization
children.top_down_role: Joint optimization across correlated tasks with task-aware evaluations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic multitask BO policy with declared target-task utility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: From data \mathcal D_n=\{(x_i,t_i,y_i)\}_{i=1}^n, update the joint posterior, choose (x_{n+1},t_{n+1}) by an acquisition whose terminal utility is defined on \mathcal T_\star, observe that task, and update \mathcal D_{n+1}. At termination return one declared posterior recommendation for every target task.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose design-task pairs using a joint posterior and a utility tied to the declared target tasks.
assumptions_latex: The acquisition and terminal recommendation specify \mathcal T_\star.
Every selected task is evaluable and its observation model is specified.
knowledge_statements.title: Task-Aware Sequential Evaluation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Jointly modeled task-indexed responses with explicit target and auxiliary tasks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:\mathcal X\times\mathcal T\to\mathbb R and let \varnothing\ne\mathcal T_\star\subseteq\mathcal T denote tasks requiring recommendations. Multitask Bayesian optimization may evaluate any (x,t)\in\mathcal X\times\mathcal T under a joint surrogate and returns \widehat x(t) for each t\in\mathcal T_\star; tasks outside \mathcal T_\star are auxiliary information sources.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multitask BO shares information through a joint task model while distinguishing recommendation targets from auxiliary tasks.
assumptions_latex: The evaluated task is observed.
\mathcal T_\star\ne\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Multitask Bayesian-Optimization Problem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact independence boundary for auxiliary-task transfer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If p(f\mid\mathcal D)=\prod_{t\in\mathcal T}p(f_t\mid\mathcal D_t), then for s\ne t, p(f_t\mid\mathcal D,Y_s)=p(f_t\mid\mathcal D). Thus an auxiliary observation has zero information value for a terminal utility depending only on the target posterior, absent another coupled state variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Posterior-independent tasks cannot transfer Bayesian information to one another.
assumptions_latex: s\ne t.
Terminal utility has no direct dependence on Y_s or another coupled state.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero Cross-Task Information Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard coregionalized representation of cross-task information sharing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A separable multitask Gaussian process has k((x,t),(x',t'))=k_X(x,x')B_{tt'}, with k_X positive semidefinite and B\succeq0. On finite grids its covariance is B\otimes K_X; posterior transfer between distinct tasks requires nonzero conditional cross-covariance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separable multitask GP factors design similarity and task covariance; cross-task updates require cross-covariance.
assumptions_latex: k_X\text{ is positive semidefinite}.
B\succeq0.
knowledge_statements.title: Separable Multitask Gaussian-Process Surrogate

assumptions_latex: Tasks belong to an index set \(\mathcal T\), and observations have the form \((x,t,y)\).
A joint surrogate supplies cross-task posterior dependence for \(f:\mathcal X\times\mathcal T\to\mathbb R\).
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports multitask Bayesian optimization.
The task-selection rule may require costs or a designated target task in specialized variants.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint design and task selection under an explicitly correlated multitask surrogate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input design space \(\mathcal X\), task set \(\mathcal T\), a joint cross-task surrogate, and an evaluation budget. Initialize the posterior from observations \((x_i,t_i,y_i)\). At iteration \(n\), compute a task-aware acquisition \(a_n(x,t)\) using the joint posterior, select a maximizing design-task pair, observe its response, and condition the surrogate. Stop at the budget and output, for each target task, a posterior-recommended minimizer; cross-task covariance permits an observation on one task to update predictions on another.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Jointly choose a design and task using a correlated surrogate, update all tasks through posterior dependence, and return a recommended design for each target task.
knowledge_statements.title: Multitask Bayesian Optimization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports joint design-task acquisition under a correlated surrogate. The policy does not specify whether all tasks are optimization targets or some are auxiliary information sources, a distinction that changes the acquisition and recommendation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multitask optimization and cross-task information transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A general problem-setting definition used as foundational context for multitask Bayesian optimization; it does not itself specify a Bayesian surrogate or acquisition rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given related task objectives \(\{f_i:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\}_{i\in I}\), multitask optimization addresses their sequential or simultaneous optimization. If task performances are correlated as functions of the input, information obtained from one task may be transferred to help optimize other tasks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multitask optimization addresses the sequential or simultaneous optimization of objectives representing related tasks. When performance is correlated across tasks as a function of the input, observations from one task may help optimize other tasks.
assumptions_latex: \(f_i:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) for each \(i\in I\)
The objectives represent related tasks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{If task performances are correlated over }\mathcal X,\text{ cross-task information transfer may accelerate optimization.}

children.title: Cross-Episode Bayesian Optimization Transfer
children.top_down_role: Transfer of surrogate structure or policy knowledge across optimization episodes.

children.title: Warm-Start Bayesian Optimization
children.top_down_role: Initialization using designs, observations, or surrogate state from earlier episodes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic target-episode loop after transferred initialization, with an unambiguous new-evaluation budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize S_0=T(H,D_0). For t=0,\ldots,N-1, form the target posterior from (S_0,D_t), select x_{t+1} by the prescribed acquisition rule, observe y_{t+1}, and set D_{t+1}=D_t\cup\{(x_{t+1},y_{t+1})\}. If D_N\ne\varnothing, return a prescribed incumbent or posterior recommendation based on D_N.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transfer an initial state, perform exactly N new target evaluations, update after each observation, and return the declared recommendation.
assumptions_latex: N\in\mathbb N_0 counts new target evaluations after D_0.
The transfer map and posterior updates are well-defined.
The acquisition rule supplies an admissible query.
A returned evaluated-point incumbent requires D_N\ne\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |D_N\setminus D_0|=N\text{ counting evaluation records with multiplicity}.
knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Started Bayesian-Optimization Loop

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Historical information used before the first new target-episode evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given source-episode information H and initial target data D_0, a target run is warm-started when its initial belief or policy state is S_0=T(H,D_0) and T depends nontrivially on H. It reduces to a cold start when T(H,D_0)=T(\varnothing,D_0).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Bayesian-optimization run is warm-started when past episodes affect its initial target belief or policy state.
assumptions_latex: T(H,D_0) is a valid state for the target policy.

notation.meaning: Target data available before new evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Bayesian Optimization

children.title: Meta-Bayesian Optimization
children.top_down_role: Optimization policies adapted from a population of related episodes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical integrated and plug-in treatments of shared meta-parameters for a new episode.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given historical-task data \(H\), target-task data \(D_t\), and shared parameter \(\theta\), the full-Bayes meta-predictive is \[p_{\mathrm{FB}}(f_\star\mid H,D_t)=\int p(f_\star\mid D_t,\theta)\,p(\theta\mid H,D_t)\,d\theta.\] An empirical-Bayes variant estimates \(\widehat\theta(H)\) and uses \[p_{\mathrm{EB}}(f_\star\mid H,D_t)=p(f_\star\mid D_t,\widehat\theta(H)).\] The two predictives coincide when \(p(\theta\mid H,D_t)=\delta_{\widehat\theta(H)}\), but need not coincide otherwise; acquisitions are evaluated under the predictive selected by the method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Meta-BO may integrate shared-parameter uncertainty or plug in an estimated meta-parameter; these agree for a degenerate matching meta-posterior but generally differ.
assumptions_latex: The conditional target-task predictive exists for admissible \(\theta\).
The full-Bayes integral exists.
\(\widehat\theta(H)\) is a defined meta-parameter estimator.

notation.meaning: meta-parameter estimate learned from historical tasks

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Bayes and Empirical-Bayes Meta Predictives
Meta-Bayesian Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hierarchical Bayesian transfer across a population of related optimization tasks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let tasks be indexed by \(j\), with latent task functions \(f_j:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\). Meta-Bayesian optimization specifies a shared hyperparameter \(\theta\sim p(\theta)\), task functions \(f_j\mid\theta\sim p(f\mid\theta)\), and observations \(y_{ji}\mid f_j,x_{ji}\sim p(y\mid f_j(x_{ji}))\). Historical data \(H\) induce the meta-posterior \(p(\theta\mid H)\). For a new task with data \(D_t\), its predictive distribution is \(p(f_\star\mid D_t,H)=\int p(f_\star\mid D_t,\theta)p(\theta\mid H)\,d\theta\), and acquisitions are evaluated under this predictive distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Meta-Bayesian optimization learns a posterior over shared task structure and integrates it into the predictive model and acquisition rule for each new task.
assumptions_latex: All task functions share the domain \(\mathcal X\).
Historical and target tasks are conditionally exchangeable given \(\theta\).
The displayed posterior and predictive integrals exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Historical tasks affect new-task decisions through the meta-posterior \(p(\theta\mid H)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: hierarchical Bayesian formulation of cross-task meta-learning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role and hierarchical formulation fit the meta-Bayesian-optimization leaf, but the task-index domain and composition of H are not explicit, and no source supports this particular formulation. An authoritative meta-BO or hierarchical transfer-BO reference with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Cross-Episode Surrogate Transfer
children.top_down_role: Reuse of surrogate structure across related optimization runs.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional-variance effect of source observations in a fixed Gaussian cross-episode surrogate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=f_\star(x)\), and let \(Y_t\) and \(Y_s\) be target- and source-episode observation vectors. If \((F,Y_t,Y_s)\) is jointly Gaussian and \(\operatorname{Var}(Y_s\mid Y_t)\) is nonsingular, then \[\operatorname{Var}(F\mid Y_t,Y_s)=\operatorname{Var}(F\mid Y_t)-\operatorname{Cov}(F,Y_s\mid Y_t)\operatorname{Var}(Y_s\mid Y_t)^{-1}\operatorname{Cov}(Y_s,F\mid Y_t).\] Hence source observations cannot increase conditional posterior variance under the fixed joint model, and they leave it unchanged exactly when \(\operatorname{Cov}(F,Y_s\mid Y_t)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a fixed joint Gaussian surrogate, conditioning on source observations subtracts a positive-semidefinite variance term; there is no variance effect exactly at zero conditional cross-covariance.
assumptions_latex: \((F,Y_t,Y_s)\) is jointly Gaussian.
\(\operatorname{Var}(Y_s\mid Y_t)\) is nonsingular.

notation.meaning: target latent response at the prediction point

knowledge_statements.title: Gaussian Transfer Variance Reduction
Cross-Episode Surrogate Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Posterior prediction for a target episode under a shared latent multi-episode surrogate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_1,\ldots,f_m,f_\star\) be source and target latent functions with joint prior \(p(f_1,\ldots,f_m,f_\star\mid\theta)\), and let \(H\) and \(D_t\) denote source and target observations. Cross-episode surrogate transfer uses the target predictive law \[p(f_\star\mid H,D_t)=\int p(f_\star\mid H,D_t,\theta)\,p(\theta\mid H,D_t)\,d\theta.\] Under a Gaussian multi-task surrogate, prediction at \(x\in\mathcal X\) is obtained by conditioning the joint Gaussian vector of source observations, target observations, and \(f_\star(x)\); nonzero cross-episode covariance is the channel through which \(H\) changes target predictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A joint multi-episode surrogate transfers information by conditioning target predictions on source data through shared parameters or nonzero cross-episode covariance.
assumptions_latex: All modeled episodes possess a well-defined joint prior.
The observation likelihood is specified for every episode.
Required conditional distributions exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(f_\star\) is conditionally independent of \(H\) given \(D_t\), then \(p(f_\star\mid H,D_t)=p(f_\star\mid D_t)\), so no surrogate transfer occurs.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: posterior conditioning in hierarchical or multi-task surrogate models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is an appropriate kind for a transferred predictive law, but no source is supplied. The no-transfer conclusion also needs the conditioning scope made explicit, particularly whether theta or other shared latent variables have been marginalized. A specific multi-task or cross-episode surrogate reference is required.

children.title: Negative Transfer Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Episode mismatch that makes transferred structure or policy knowledge harmful.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Transferred Greedy Prior Can Cause Negative Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-design example explicitly linking transferred beliefs, policy behavior, and target regret.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X=\{a,b\}\), with exact target objective \(f(a)=1\) and \(f(b)=0\) to be minimized. With one target evaluation, let \(A_T\) have transferred posterior means \(m_T(a)=0<m_T(b)=2\), query the posterior-mean minimizer \(a\), and recommend its queried point. Let matched baseline \(A_0\) query and recommend \(b\). Then \(R_1(A_T,f)=1\) and \(R_1(A_0,f)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Misleading transferred beliefs make a greedy policy choose the wrong design while a matched target-only baseline achieves zero regret.
assumptions_latex: Target evaluations are exact.
Both policies receive one evaluation and recommend their queried design.
The transfer policy greedily minimizes its transferred posterior mean without independent exploration.
knowledge_statements.title: Transferred Greedy Prior Can Cause Negative Transfer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matched-protocol comparison of transfer and target-only performance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_T\) be a transfer policy and \(A_0\) a target-only baseline using the same target domain, target-evaluation budget, observation protocol, and recommendation convention. For simple regret \(R_N(A,f)=f(\widehat x_N^A)-\inf_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)\), transfer is negative on target \(f\) at budget \(N\) when \(R_N(A_T,f)>R_N(A_0,f)\). In a stochastic comparison, the guarantee mode must be matched, for example \(\mathbb E[R_N(A_T,f)]>\mathbb E[R_N(A_0,f)]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative transfer means that a transfer policy performs strictly worse than a matched target-only baseline under the same budget, protocol, recommendation rule, and guarantee mode.
assumptions_latex: The policies share the target domain, budget, observation protocol, and recommendation convention.
Regret is finite, or integrable when expectations are compared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_N(A_T,f)>R_N(A_0,f)\text{, or the corresponding strict inequality in the declared matched guarantee mode}.

notation.meaning: Target simple regret after N target evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Operational Negative Transfer
Negative Transfer Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary at which transferred information worsens target-episode Bayesian-optimization decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_N(A,f)=f(\widehat x_N^A)-\inf_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)\) be the simple regret of policy \(A\) after \(N\) target evaluations. For a transfer policy \(A_T\) and an otherwise identical target-only policy \(A_0\), negative transfer on target \(f\) occurs when \(R_N(A_T,f)>R_N(A_0,f)\), or in a stochastic setting when \(\mathbb E[R_N(A_T,f)]>\mathbb E[R_N(A_0,f)]\). A concrete failure mechanism arises when a transferred prior assigns zero probability to every neighborhood of the true minimizer while the target-only prior assigns positive probability there; posterior updating cannot recover excluded minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transfer is negative when it yields larger target regret than a target-only baseline; support-excluding transferred priors provide a sharp failure mechanism.
assumptions_latex: Both policies use the same target domain, budget, and observation protocol.
The regret expectations exist when the stochastic comparison is used.
The transferred posterior remains absolutely continuous with respect to its support-restricted prior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Prior support exclusion can make \(A_T\) permanently unable to select neighborhoods containing a true minimizer, whereas \(A_0\) need not share this failure.

notation.meaning: Simple regret after N target evaluations.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: regret comparison and Bayesian support-exclusion failure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, and the regret comparison is a reasonable operational definition. However, prior support exclusion alone does not imply that a Bayesian-optimization policy can never query neighborhoods of the minimizer; that requires additional assumptions linking posterior support to the acquisition rule and its exploration behavior. A sharp negative-transfer source is needed before the stated mechanism or conclusion can be retained.

children.title: Localized Trust-Region Bayesian Optimization
children.top_down_role: Localized surrogate and acquisition strategies for high-dimensional or locally structured objectives.

children.title: Local Surrogate Regions
children.top_down_role: Localized modeling around incumbents or promising regions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by discarding informative observations outside a nominal region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(x\in\mathcal R\) and an excluded observation \(Y_z\) satisfies \(\operatorname{Cov}(f(x),Y_z\mid\mathcal D_{\mathcal R})\neq0\) in a nondegenerate jointly Gaussian posterior, then conditioning on \(Y_z\) changes the conditional mean or variance of \(f(x)\). A local-data posterior can therefore differ from the restricted global posterior and induce different acquisition rankings within \(\mathcal R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discarding an outside observation that remains conditionally informative can change predictions and local acquisition rankings.
assumptions_latex: The relevant conditional joint law is nondegenerate Gaussian.
\(\operatorname{Cov}(f(x),Y_z\mid\mathcal D_{\mathcal R})\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p(f(x)\mid\mathcal D_{\mathcal R},Y_z)\neq p(f(x)\mid\mathcal D_{\mathcal R}).

notation.meaning: Excluded observation outside the local region.

review_flags: The Gaussian assumption makes the covariance criterion sufficient; the Builder's unrestricted version was too broad.
knowledge_statements.title: Information Loss Under Local-Only Conditioning

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinct ways to obtain predictions on a local search region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mathcal R\subseteq\mathcal X\), a global-posterior restriction uses \(p(f_{\mathcal R}\mid\mathcal D)\), whereas local-data fitting uses \(p(f_{\mathcal R}\mid\mathcal D_{\mathcal R})\) for a declared \(\mathcal D_{\mathcal R}\subseteq\mathcal D\). Conditional independence \(f_{\mathcal R}\perp\!\!\!\perp(\mathcal D\setminus\mathcal D_{\mathcal R})\mid\mathcal D_{\mathcal R}\) is sufficient, and at the level of conditional kernels equivalent, to equality of these two posterior laws.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting a global posterior to a region differs from discarding outside data; the two agree under the corresponding conditional-independence condition.
assumptions_latex: The relevant regular conditional distributions exist.
The local data-selection rule is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_{\mathcal R}\perp\!\!\!\perp(\mathcal D\setminus\mathcal D_{\mathcal R})\mid\mathcal D_{\mathcal R}\Rightarrow p(f_{\mathcal R}\mid\mathcal D)=p(f_{\mathcal R}\mid\mathcal D_{\mathcal R}).

notation.meaning: Latent function restricted to the region.
Data retained by the local selection rule.

review_flags: Equality for one realized dataset alone must not be interpreted as conditional independence.
knowledge_statements.title: Global-Posterior and Local-Data Restrictions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scaled Local Region with Declared Data Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric region and observation-selection components of a local surrogate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c_t\in\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), \(\Delta_t>0\), and nonsingular \(L_t\). Define \(\mathcal R_t=\mathcal X\cap\{x:\|L_t^{-1}(x-c_t)\|_\infty\le\Delta_t\}\). A local-data rule is a declared history-dependent map \(S_t(H_t,\mathcal R_t)\subseteq\{1,\ldots,t\}\), producing \(\mathcal D_t^{\rm loc}=\{(x_i,y_i):i\in S_t(H_t,\mathcal R_t)\}\). A local surrogate either conditions on \(\mathcal D_t^{\rm loc}\) or restricts the global posterior to \(\mathcal R_t\); these constructions must be distinguished.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local surrogate specifies both a scaled search neighborhood and an explicit retained-data rule, or instead declares that it restricts the global posterior.
assumptions_latex: \(L_t\) is nonsingular and \(\Delta_t>0\).
The data-selection map is measurable and completely specified.
The required posterior exists.

notation.meaning: History- and region-dependent observation-index selection rule.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Local Region with Declared Data Selection
Local Surrogate Regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Surrogate restriction to a neighborhood of the current incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), let \(c_t\in\mathcal X\) be the incumbent, and let \(\Delta_t>0\). A local surrogate region is \(\mathcal R_t=\mathcal X\cap\{x:\lVert L_t^{-1}(x-c_t)\rVert_\infty\leq\Delta_t\}\), where \(L_t\) is nonsingular and controls coordinate scaling. A local surrogate is fitted or conditioned using the observations selected for \(\mathcal R_t\), and the next query satisfies \(x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal R_t}a_t(x)\). The region is local because both surrogate use and acquisition optimization are restricted relative to \(c_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local surrogate region is a scaled neighborhood of the incumbent within which the surrogate is used and the acquisition function is optimized.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is nonempty.
\(L_t\) is nonsingular and \(\Delta_t>0\).
The restricted acquisition problem has a prescribed exact or approximate solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every generated query lies in \(\mathcal R_t\), hence within scaled distance \(\Delta_t\) of \(c_t\).

children.title: Adaptive Trust-Region Policies
children.top_down_role: Acquisition policies coupled to evolving local search regions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restart variant after a local region reaches its minimum scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a prescribed failure condition holds at \(\Delta_t=\Delta_{\min}\), terminate the local run, draw a new center from a declared restart distribution, reset \(\Delta_{t+1}=\Delta_0>\Delta_{\min}\) and all streak counters, and resume localized acquisition optimization. If infinitely many independent restarts occur and every nonempty open \(U\subseteq\mathcal X\) has restart probability \(p(U)>0\), then every such \(U\) is visited by a restart center almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After collapse, restart from a globally supported center and reset the radius and counters; infinitely many independent restarts eventually visit every open region with positive restart probability.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\Delta_{\min}<\Delta_0\).
Collapse and counter-reset rules are fixed.
Restarts are independent, occur infinitely often, and have full topological support.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pr(c_k\in U\ \text{for some restart }k)=1\quad\text{for every nonempty open }U\subseteq\mathcal X.
review_flags: The almost-sure coverage conclusion requires infinitely many independent restarts.
knowledge_statements.title: Independent Restart After Trust-Region Collapse

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Permanent Confinement to a Suboptimal Basin
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global-search failure of purely local adaptation without restart or independent exploration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let all evaluated designs belong to \(B\subseteq\mathcal X\), let \(x^\star\notin\overline B\) be globally optimal, and suppose \(\inf_{x\in B}f(x)>f(x^\star)\). Any recommendation restricted to evaluated designs then has simple regret at least \(\inf_{x\in B}f(x)-f(x^\star)>0\), regardless of how regions are adapted within \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A policy whose entire evaluation history remains in a strictly suboptimal basin cannot converge globally.
assumptions_latex: Every evaluated design lies in \(B\).
Recommendations are restricted to evaluated designs.
\(\inf_{x\in B}f(x)>f(x^\star)\).
review_flags: The Builder version was revised because confinement only after time T does not exclude a superior earlier evaluation.
knowledge_statements.title: Permanent Confinement to a Suboptimal Basin

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fully Specified Success-Failure Trust-Region State Machine
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic adaptive trust-region policy with explicit streak resets and radius-boundary behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain \((c_t,\Delta_t,u_t,v_t)\), where \(u_t,v_t\) count consecutive successes and failures. Select \(x_{t+1}\in\arg\max_{x\in\mathcal R(c_t,\Delta_t)}a_t(x)\). On success set \((u',v')=(u_t+1,0)\); if \(u'=s\), set \(\Delta_{t+1}=\min\{\gamma_+\Delta_t,\Delta_{\max}\}\) and reset both counters, otherwise retain \(\Delta_t\) and set \((u_{t+1},v_{t+1})=(u',0)\). On failure set \((u',v')=(0,v_t+1)\); if \(v'=q\), set \(\Delta_{t+1}=\max\{\gamma_-\Delta_t,\Delta_{\min}\}\) and reset both counters, otherwise retain the radius and set \((u_{t+1},v_{t+1})=(0,v')\). Recenter at the declared incumbent. A threshold event resets the counters even when clipping leaves the radius unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Success and failure streaks reset each other; reaching a threshold expands or contracts the clipped radius and resets both counters, including at radius bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(s,q\in\mathbb N_{>0}\).
\(0<\gamma_-<1<\gamma_+\) and \(0<\Delta_{\min}\le\Delta_{\max}\).
Success, incumbent, region, tie-breaking, and acquisition-solution rules are declared.
knowledge_statements.title: Fully Specified Success-Failure Trust-Region State Machine
Adaptive Trust-Region Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Success-driven adaptation of a local Bayesian-optimization search region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a center \(c_0\), radius \(\Delta_0\in[\Delta_{\min},\Delta_{\max}]\), and success and failure counters at zero. At iteration \(t\), maximize the acquisition over \(\mathcal R_t\), evaluate the selected point, and declare success if the incumbent improves by at least \(\eta\geq0\). After \(s\) consecutive successes set \(\Delta_{t+1}=\min\{\gamma_+\Delta_t,\Delta_{\max}\}\); after \(q\) consecutive failures set \(\Delta_{t+1}=\max\{\gamma_-\Delta_t,\Delta_{\min}\}\); otherwise retain \(\Delta_t\). Recenter at the incumbent and stop at the evaluation budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The policy searches inside a local region, expands it after sustained improvement, contracts it after sustained failure, and recenters it on the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\gamma_-<1<\gamma_+\) and \(0<\Delta_{\min}\leq\Delta_{\max}\).
\(s,q\) are positive integers.
Each restricted acquisition subproblem has a prescribed exact or approximate solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every iteration, \(\Delta_t\in[\Delta_{\min},\Delta_{\max}]\), and every proposed point belongs to the current region \(\mathcal R_t\).

children.title: Bayesian Optimization Assessment Interface

children.title: Predictive Calibration Validation System
children.top_down_role: Out-of-sample, sequential, and calibration checks for surrogate predictions.

children.title: Out-of-Sample Predictive Validation
children.top_down_role: Assessment of surrogate predictions on observations excluded from model fitting.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Out-of-sample scoring with all response-dependent pipeline steps repeated within training folds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) into folds \(V_1,\ldots,V_K\). For each \(k\), fit the entire surrogate pipeline using only \(D\setminus V_k\), issue \(P_i^{(-k)}\) for \(i\in V_k\), and report \[\widehat R_{\mathrm{CF}}=\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{i\in V_k}S(P_i^{(-k)},y_i).\] Preprocessing, hyperparameter tuning, and model selection that use responses are repeated within each training fold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cross-fitting gives every observation a prediction from a pipeline trained without its fold, preventing response leakage from tuning or preprocessing.
assumptions_latex: \(V_1,\ldots,V_K\) are disjoint and cover all observation indices.
No response in \(V_k\) influences the pipeline producing \(P_i^{(-k)}\).
\(S\) is a declared predictive loss or proper score.

notation.meaning: Predictive distribution fitted without fold k.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Fitted Predictive Validation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies the population risk represented by an honest validation sample.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_D\) be fitted from training data \(D\). If, conditionally on \(D\), validation pairs \((X_i,Y_i)\) have common law \(Q\), do not affect \(P_D\), and the score is integrable, then \[\mathbb E\!\left[\frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m S(P_D(\cdot\mid X_i),Y_i)\middle|D\right]=R_Q(P_D),\quad R_Q(P_D)=\mathbb E_Q[S(P_D(\cdot\mid X),Y)\mid D].\] Independence among validation pairs is unnecessary for this expectation identity, although it matters for usual variance and concentration formulas.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An honest held-out average targets risk under the validation law, not automatically under a different deployment or adaptive-query law.
assumptions_latex: \((X_i,Y_i)\mid D\) has marginal law \(Q\) for every \(i\).
The fitted predictor does not use validation responses.
\(\mathbb E_Q|S(P_D(\cdot\mid X),Y)|<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.title: Validation-Distribution Risk Identity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of fresh-sample interpretation after validation responses influence the reported procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If validation responses determine preprocessing, hyperparameters, model choice, stopping, or any other component of the reported predictor, the validation score generally is not an unbiased estimate of the fresh-sample risk of that complete selection procedure. A separate untouched test sample or properly nested resampling is then required for an honest final assessment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reusing validation responses to construct or select the reported model invalidates their automatic interpretation as fresh out-of-sample evidence.
assumptions_latex: The same validation responses are used both to choose the reported procedure and to score it.
knowledge_statements.title: Validation Leakage Boundary
Out-of-Sample Predictive Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Held-out evaluation of a fitted surrogate predictive distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition observations into training data \(D_{\mathrm{tr}}\) and validation data \(D_{\mathrm{va}}=\{(x_i,y_i)\}_{i=1}^m\), with validation responses unused during fitting. Fit the surrogate on \(D_{\mathrm{tr}}\), obtain predictive distributions \(P_i(\cdot)=P(Y\in\cdot\mid x_i,D_{\mathrm{tr}})\), and report a proper-score estimate \(m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m S(P_i,y_i)\). For predictive intervals \(I_i(1-\alpha)\), also report empirical coverage \(m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m\mathbf 1\{y_i\in I_i(1-\alpha)\}\). The output is the score and coverage indexed by the chosen holdout rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fit the surrogate without held-out responses, then evaluate its predictive distributions using proper scores and empirical interval coverage on those responses.
assumptions_latex: Validation responses are not used in model fitting or hyperparameter selection.
\(S(P,y)\) is a specified proper scoring rule.
The fitted surrogate supplies predictive distributions and intervals at validation inputs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reported quantities estimate predictive performance under the sampling mechanism that generated \(D_{\mathrm{va}}\), not necessarily under future adaptive acquisition designs.

children.title: Sequential Predictive Validation
children.top_down_role: Assessment of predictive performance across the evolving evaluation sequence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Anytime-valid sequential calibration check along an adaptive evaluation path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_t\) be an event-valued rule fixed using \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\), let \(p_t=P_t(A_t)\), and define \(Z_t=\mathbf1\{Y_t\in A_t\}-p_t\). If \(P_t\) is the true conditional law of \(Y_t\) given \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\), then \(\mathbb E[Z_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]=0\) and \(|Z_t|\le1\). Any confidence sequence valid for this bounded martingale-difference process therefore gives an anytime-valid test of the declared event probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under correct sequential event probabilities, forecast residuals are bounded martingale differences and can be monitored with an anytime-valid confidence sequence.
assumptions_latex: The event rule \(A_t\) and probability \(p_t\) are fixed before observing \(Y_t\).
\(p_t=\Pr(Y_t\in A_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})\) under the asserted model.
The implemented confidence sequence is valid for bounded martingale differences.
knowledge_statements.title: Predictable-Event Martingale Diagnostic

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Retrospective Refit Is Not Prequential Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonanticipation boundary for sequential predictive assessment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A prediction for time \(t\) recomputed after incorporating \(Y_t\) or a later response is not the \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable forecast issued before \(Y_t\). Its score is an in-sample or retrospective smoothing diagnostic and cannot replace the one-step-ahead prequential loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A retrospectively recomputed prediction cannot substitute for the forecast available before the response arrived.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\) is the information available before response \(Y_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_t\notin\mathcal F_{t-1}\Longrightarrow S(P_t,Y_t)\text{ is not a one-step-ahead prequential score}.
knowledge_statements.title: Retrospective Refit Is Not Prequential Validation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Prequential Risk Targets the Evaluation Policy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpretation of one-step-ahead losses at adaptively selected locations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_t\) and predictive law \(P_t\) be \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable, and put \(L_t=S(P_t,Y_t)\). If \(L_t\) is integrable, then \[\mathbb E[L_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]=r_t(X_t),\] where \(r_t(X_t)\) is the conditional predictive risk at the location chosen by the policy. Thus \(T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T L_t\) assesses predictions along the policy-induced trajectory, not risk under an unvisited exogenous input distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prequential scores evaluate predictions at the adaptive locations actually selected by the policy.
assumptions_latex: \(X_t\) and \(P_t\) are \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable.
\(\mathbb E|S(P_t,Y_t)|<\infty\).

notation.meaning: Conditional predictive risk at the selected location.

knowledge_statements.title: Prequential Risk Targets the Evaluation Policy
Sequential Predictive Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Prequential validation using predictions issued before each adaptive observation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For adaptively collected data \(D_t=\{(x_i,y_i)\}_{i=1}^t\), let \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\) contain all information available before choosing \(x_t\). At each \(t\), record the predictive law \(P_t(\cdot)=P(Y_t\in\cdot\mid x_t,\mathcal F_{t-1})\) before observing \(y_t\), then record the loss \(S(P_t,y_t)\). For horizon \(T\), output \(T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T S(P_t,y_t)\) and, for intervals \(I_t(1-\alpha)\), the coverage sequence \(\{\mathbf 1\{y_t\in I_t(1-\alpha)\}\}_{t=1}^T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each adaptive query, save the pre-observation predictive distribution and score it after the response arrives, producing time-indexed predictive diagnostics.
assumptions_latex: \(x_t\) is measurable with respect to \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\).
Each \(P_t\) is recorded before \(y_t\) is observed.
\(S(P,y)\) is a specified proper scoring rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every validation loss is genuinely one-step-ahead: \(P_t\) cannot depend on the realized value \(y_t\).

notation.meaning: Information available before the t-th response.
