children.title: Uncertainty Calibration
children.top_down_role: Assessment of whether predictive uncertainty matches observed error behavior.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional calibration formulation valid for predictive distributions with atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_x(y^-)=\lim_{z\uparrow y}F_x(z)\), let \(V\sim\operatorname{Unif}(0,1)\) be independent of \((X,Y)\), and define \[U=F_X(Y^-)+V\bigl(F_X(Y)-F_X(Y^-)\bigr).\] If \(F_X\) is the true conditional CDF of \(Y\) given \(X\), then \(U\mid X\sim\operatorname{Unif}(0,1)\). The unrandomized transform \(F_X(Y)\) generally is not uniform when the predictive law has atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomization within CDF jumps gives the proper PIT diagnostic for discrete and mixed predictive distributions.
assumptions_latex: \(V\perp(X,Y)\) and \(V\sim\operatorname{Unif}(0,1)\).
\(F_x\) is the asserted conditional predictive CDF.

notation.meaning: Left limit of the predictive CDF.
Independent randomizer within a CDF jump.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Probability Integral Transform

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Marginal Calibration Does Not Imply Conditional Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cancellation of opposite conditional calibration errors across input strata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\{0,1\}\) be equiprobable. Suppose \(U\mid X=0\) has density \(2u\) and \(U\mid X=1\) has density \(2(1-u)\) on \((0,1)\). Then \(U\sim\operatorname{Unif}(0,1)\) marginally, while neither conditional distribution is uniform.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Opposite subgroup errors can cancel and produce a perfectly uniform pooled PIT despite conditional miscalibration in every subgroup.
knowledge_statements.title: Marginal Calibration Does Not Imply Conditional Calibration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantile-coverage representation of marginal predictive calibration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For generalized predictive quantiles \(q_X(u)=F_X^{-1}(u)\), define \(C(u)=\Pr\{Y\le q_X(u)\}\). At continuity levels, marginal quantile calibration is \(C(u)=u\). If the two interval endpoints have no boundary mass, the coverage of \([q_X(\alpha/2),q_X(1-\alpha/2)]\) is \(C(1-\alpha/2)-C(\alpha/2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The calibration curve maps nominal quantile levels to observed marginal coverage; the identity curve represents marginal calibration.
assumptions_latex: Generalized predictive quantiles are used.
The displayed central-interval identity excludes boundary atoms at its endpoints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C(u)=u\text{ at all relevant levels}\Longleftrightarrow\text{marginal quantile calibration}.
knowledge_statements.title: Marginal Calibration Curve
Uncertainty Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional coverage criterion for surrogate predictive uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_x\) be a surrogate predictive distribution for response \(Y\) at input \(x\), and let \(F_x\) be its continuous cumulative distribution function. The predictive uncertainty is calibrated on an input distribution \(Q\) when \[\Pr\{Y\leq F_X^{-1}(u)\mid X\}=u\quad\text{for every }u\in(0,1),\quad Q\text{-almost surely}.\] Equivalently, the probability integral transform \(U=F_X(Y)\) is conditionally uniform given \(X\). Marginal calibration replaces the conditional equality by \(\Pr\{U\leq u\}=u\) and is strictly weaker.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Predictive uncertainty is conditionally calibrated when every stated predictive quantile has its nominal conditional coverage; marginally uniform probability transforms give a weaker criterion.
assumptions_latex: \((X,Y)\) has a specified evaluation distribution.
Each \(F_x\) is continuous and strictly increasing on its effective support.
Predictive distributions are fixed before their corresponding responses are observed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Conditional calibration implies \(\Pr\{Y\in I_X(1-\alpha)\mid X\}=1-\alpha\) for every central predictive interval \(I_X(1-\alpha)\).

notation.meaning: Predictive cumulative distribution at input x.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is the correct role for a calibration criterion, and the conditional quantile statement is plausible under the stated continuity assumptions. No authoritative source is cited, and the record should explicitly state that F_x is the CDF of P_x. A probabilistic calibration reference with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Calibration Drift
children.top_down_role: Changes in uncertainty reliability as sampled regions or operating conditions evolve.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Marginal Coverage Can Hide Conditional Calibration Drift
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cancellation boundary for aggregate calibration monitoring.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_t\in\{0,1\}\) have equal group probabilities in two periods, and let \(p\in(\eta,1-\eta)\). In period 1, suppose coverage conditional on \(G_t=0\) and \(G_t=1\) is respectively \(p+\eta\) and \(p-\eta\); in period 2 interchange the two values. Marginal coverage equals \(p\) in both periods, while each group's conditional coverage changes by \(2\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Opposite groupwise calibration changes can cancel and leave aggregate coverage unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \Pr(G_t=0)=\Pr(G_t=1)=1/2\text{ in both periods}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pr(Y_t\in I_t)=p\text{ in both periods, although groupwise coverage changes by }2\eta.
knowledge_statements.title: Marginal Coverage Can Hide Conditional Calibration Drift

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Detector-independent temporal change in calibration of predictions issued before observing their responses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each time \(t\) and level \(u\in U\subset(0,1)\), let \(q_t(u)\) be a predictive \(u\)-quantile issued before \(Y_t\) is observed. Define the time-indexed prequential calibration error \[c_t(u)=\Pr\{Y_t\le q_t(u)\}-u.\] Calibration is stable on an index set \(I\) when \(c_t(u)\) is invariant in \(t\in I\) for every \(u\in U\); calibration drift occurs when there exist \(s,t\in I\) and \(u\in U\) with \(c_s(u)\ne c_t(u)\). Conditional drift is defined analogously after fixing declared strata or conditioning events. This population definition does not specify a detector or significance threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Calibration drift is temporal change in pre-observation predictive calibration error at one or more fixed probability levels or declared strata.
assumptions_latex: Each q_t(u)\text{ is issued before observing }Y_t.
U\subset(0,1)\text{ is fixed for the comparison}.
The displayed probabilities exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists s,t\in I,\ u\in U:\ c_s(u)\ne c_t(u)\text{ characterizes marginal prequential calibration drift.}

notation.meaning: predictive u-quantile issued at time t

knowledge_statements.title: Prequential Calibration Drift
Calibration Drift
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Time variation in predictive calibration under sequential Bayesian optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nominal level \(1-\alpha\), define the windowed coverage error at time \(t\) by \[E_t(\alpha)=\frac{1}{w}\sum_{s=t-w+1}^{t}\mathbf 1\{y_s\in I_s(1-\alpha)\}-(1-\alpha),\] where each interval \(I_s(1-\alpha)\) is issued before observing \(y_s\). Calibration drift over two windows ending at \(t_1<t_2\) is present when \(|E_{t_2}(\alpha)-E_{t_1}(\alpha)|>\delta\) for a prespecified tolerance \(\delta>0\). Multiple levels may be monitored by taking the supremum over a fixed set \(\mathcal A\subset(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Calibration drift occurs when pre-observation predictive coverage changes across sequential windows by more than a prespecified tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(w\) is a positive window length and \(t_1,t_2\geq w\).
Intervals are recorded before their responses are observed.
\(\delta>0\) and monitored levels \(\mathcal A\) are fixed before evaluation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The condition \(\sup_{\alpha\in\mathcal A}|E_{t_2}(\alpha)-E_{t_1}(\alpha)|>\delta\) certifies drift relative to the chosen windows, levels, and tolerance.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure boundary is suitable for this leaf, but the proposed window difference and tolerance define one operational detector rather than a canonical boundary. No source justifies this detector, its threshold, or simultaneous monitoring over multiple levels. A specific calibration-drift or sequential-monitoring reference is required.

children.title: Surrogate Specification Sensitivity Analysis
children.top_down_role: Robustness checks across surrogate specifications and inference treatments.

children.title: Surrogate-Model Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Robustness of decisions across alternative surrogate families.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Controlled comparison of distinct surrogate families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Prespecify surrogate families \(\mathcal M\), a baseline, and comparison outputs. Fit every \(M\in\mathcal M\) to the same observations under declared family-appropriate computational budgets; evaluate predictive laws and acquisitions on common validation and candidate sets; and report paired predictive-score, calibration, acquisition, and decision differences. Replicate or couple stochastic fitting sufficiently to distinguish computational variation from family variation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare surrogate families on common data and evaluation objects while reporting predictive and decision effects separately.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M\), the baseline, and outputs are prespecified.
All families receive the same observed information.
Family-specific fitting budgets and randomness protocols are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{(P_M,a_M,\operatorname*{argmax}a_M):M\in\mathcal M\}\text{ is compared on common evaluation objects}.
knowledge_statements.title: Paired Surrogate-Family Sensitivity Analysis

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tie-invariant comparison of acquisition maximizer sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty compact maximizer sets \(A_M=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}a_M(x)\) in a metric space \((\mathcal X,\rho)\), define \[d_H(A_M,A_{M_0})=\max\!\left\{\sup_{x\in A_M}\inf_{z\in A_{M_0}}\rho(x,z),\sup_{z\in A_{M_0}}\inf_{x\in A_M}\rho(x,z)\right\}.\] This Hausdorff comparison is tie-invariant and equals zero exactly when the compact maximizer sets coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hausdorff distance compares entire acquisition-maximizer sets and cannot report zero merely because two distinct sets intersect.
assumptions_latex: \(A_M\) and \(A_{M_0}\) are nonempty compact subsets of \(\mathcal X\).
\(\rho\) is a metric.
knowledge_statements.title: Set-Valued Decision Sensitivity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Model and Fitting Sensitivity Are Confounded Without Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attribution boundary for surrogate-family comparisons.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If surrogate families are fitted with unequal information, tuning objectives, optimization effort, or stochastic accuracy, observed output differences do not uniquely identify a family effect. Attribution requires controlled fitting protocols or a factorial comparison that varies family and fitting factors separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unequal fitting procedures can masquerade as surrogate-family sensitivity.
assumptions_latex: At least one fitting factor changes jointly with surrogate family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Joint family and fitting changes}\Longrightarrow\text{family effect not separately identified}.
knowledge_statements.title: Model and Fitting Sensitivity Are Confounded Without Control
Surrogate-Model Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Change in predictions or decisions induced by varying the surrogate specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M\) be a prescribed family of surrogate specifications and let \(P_M(\cdot\mid D)\) and \(a_M(\cdot;D)\) denote the predictive law and acquisition under \(M\in\mathcal M\). For metrics \(d_P\) on predictive laws and \(d_X\) on decisions, predictive and policy sensitivities relative to a baseline \(M_0\) are \[S_P(D)=\sup_{M\in\mathcal M}d_P(P_M(\cdot\mid D),P_{M_0}(\cdot\mid D)),\qquad S_X(D)=\sup_{M\in\mathcal M}d_X(x_M,x_{M_0}),\] where \(x_M\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}a_M(x;D)\) follows a fixed tie-breaking rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Surrogate sensitivity measures the largest predictive or acquisition-decision change over a prespecified family of model specifications relative to a baseline.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M\), \(d_P\), \(d_X\), and baseline \(M_0\) are fixed before comparison.
Every specification is fitted to the same data \(D\).
Acquisition maximizers use a common deterministic tie-breaking rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_P(D)=S_X(D)=0\) exactly when all compared specifications match the baseline in the measured predictions and selected decisions.

children.title: Kernel Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Robustness of predictions or proposals across covariance specifications.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kernel-only sensitivity analysis under a declared common fitting and decision protocol.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose the candidate kernels and comparison outputs before fitting. Use common data, mean and likelihood conventions, hyperparameter-fitting criterion, optimization budget and randomness protocol, evaluation set, acquisition construction, and tie rule. Refit each kernel under this protocol and report predictive and decision discrepancies separately. Jointly changing nonkernel components measures composite pipeline sensitivity rather than kernel-only sensitivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A kernel comparison is attributable to kernels only when fitting, likelihood, evaluation, and decision conventions are controlled.
assumptions_latex: All compared fits use the same observations and evaluation domain.
Candidate kernels and reported discrepancies are prespecified.
knowledge_statements.title: Controlled Kernel Comparison Protocol

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Predictive Stability Does Not Ensure Decision Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acquisition argmax instability near ties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Even when \(\|a_1-a_2\|_\infty\le\varepsilon\), selected maximizers can be arbitrarily far apart if the baseline acquisition has separated candidates whose values differ by at most \(2\varepsilon\). Stable decisions require an argmax margin, a stable tie rule, or a set-valued comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tiny kernel-induced acquisition perturbation can switch between distant nearly tied maximizers.
assumptions_latex: The acquisition domain contains separated candidate locations.
The acquisition gap between competing locations is at most \(2\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.title: Predictive Stability Does Not Ensure Decision Stability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-data posterior comparison for two covariance kernels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For common training data \((X,y)\), mean vector \(m\), and noise covariance \(\Sigma\), kernel \(k_j\) gives \[\mu_j(x)=m(x)+k_{j,x}^{\top}(K_j+\Sigma)^{-1}(y-m),\qquad v_j(x)=k_j(x,x)-k_{j,x}^{\top}(K_j+\Sigma)^{-1}k_{j,x}.\] Kernel-induced posterior sensitivity at \(x\) is the difference of these quantities when every nonkernel component is held fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With data, mean, noise, and kernel parameters fixed, kernel sensitivity follows directly by comparing the GP conditioning formulas.
assumptions_latex: \(K_j+\Sigma\succ0\) for each compared kernel.
Data, mean, noise covariance, and fitting convention are common.
Kernel parameters are fixed at the declared fitted or prespecified values.

notation.meaning: Training covariance matrix under kernel j.
Training-to-test covariance vector under kernel j.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Protocol GP Kernel Comparison
Kernel Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Surrogate and acquisition variation across Gaussian-process covariance kernels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal K\) be a prescribed set of positive-semidefinite kernels on \(\mathcal X\), fitted to common data \(D\) under a common mean and noise convention. For each \(k\in\mathcal K\), let \((\mu_k(x),\sigma_k^2(x))\) be the Gaussian-process posterior moments and let \(x_k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}a_k(x)\). Relative to \(k_0\in\mathcal K\), kernel sensitivity is summarized by \[S_\mu=\sup_{k\in\mathcal K,x\in\mathcal X}|\mu_k(x)-\mu_{k_0}(x)|,\quad S_\sigma=\sup_{k\in\mathcal K,x\in\mathcal X}|\sigma_k(x)-\sigma_{k_0}(x)|,\] together with the decision distances \(d_X(x_k,x_{k_0})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Kernel sensitivity compares posterior means, posterior uncertainties, and acquisition maximizers across a fixed family of covariance kernels fitted under common conventions.
assumptions_latex: Every \(k\in\mathcal K\) is positive semidefinite on \(\mathcal X\).
All kernels use the same data, mean convention, likelihood, and hyperparameter-fitting protocol.
The displayed suprema are finite and acquisition ties are resolved consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Zero values of \(S_\mu\) and \(S_\sigma\) mean that all compared kernels yield the baseline posterior moments throughout \(\mathcal X\), though acquisition equality also depends on the acquisition rule.

children.title: Noise-Model Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Robustness across alternative treatments of observation noise.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Controlled comparison across plausible observation-noise specifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix the observations, latent surrogate family, prior, computational protocol, evaluation set, and acquisition rule. For each prespecified noise model \(\eta\in H\), refit all likelihood-dependent quantities and report predictive location, latent variance, observation variance, tail probabilities, acquisition values, and maximizer sets. Incommensurate discrepancies are reported separately unless dimensionless normalizations and weights were declared in advance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refit the same latent surrogate under declared noise assumptions and report inferential and decision changes componentwise.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is specified before inspecting sensitivity results.
All nonnoise conventions and computational budgets are common.
Comparisons use the same evaluation and decision rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{(P_\eta,a_\eta,\operatorname*{argmax}a_\eta):\eta\in H\}\text{ is the controlled stress-test output}.
knowledge_statements.title: Noise-Model Stress-Test Grid

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Latent and Noise Variation Need Not Be Identified
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attribution boundary without replication or structural restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite Gaussian observation vector whose covariance is \(K_\theta+\Sigma_\eta\), distinct pairs \((\theta_1,\eta_1)\ne(\theta_2,\eta_2)\) satisfying \(K_{\theta_1}+\Sigma_{\eta_1}=K_{\theta_2}+\Sigma_{\eta_2}\) are observationally equivalent. Without replication, restrictions, or other identifying information, noise-only attribution is therefore protocol-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Latent covariance and observation noise can explain the same observed covariance, preventing unique noise attribution without extra structure.
assumptions_latex: Inference uses a finite observation vector.
Distinct latent/noise parameter pairs yield the same total covariance.
knowledge_statements.title: Latent and Noise Variation Need Not Be Identified

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gaussian Nugget Sensitivity of Latent Variance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic effect of assumed homoskedastic noise with fixed kernel parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(K\succeq0\), test covariance vector \(k_x\), and \(\tau^2>0\), \[v_\tau(x)=k(x,x)-k_x^\top(K+\tau^2I)^{-1}k_x,\qquad \frac{\partial v_\tau(x)}{\partial\tau^2}=k_x^\top(K+\tau^2I)^{-2}k_x\ge0.\] Thus increasing only the assumed nugget weakly increases latent posterior variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With the kernel fixed, increasing the assumed Gaussian nugget weakly increases GP latent posterior uncertainty.
assumptions_latex: \(K\succeq0\) and \(\tau^2>0\).
Kernel parameters, data, and all other model components are fixed.
knowledge_statements.title: Gaussian Nugget Sensitivity of Latent Variance
Noise-Model Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic sensitivity of a Bayesian-optimization policy to its observation-noise specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_t=\{(x_i,y_i)\}_{i=1}^t\) be fixed data, let \(\eta\in H\) index candidate observation-noise models, and let \(a_t(x;\eta)\) be the resulting acquisition function on \(X\). For a metric \(d\) on probability measures and a decision metric \(\rho\) on \(X\), define posterior and policy noise sensitivities relative to \(\eta_0\) by \[S_{\mathrm{post}}(\eta;\eta_0)=d\!\left(\Pi_\eta(\cdot\mid D_t),\Pi_{\eta_0}(\cdot\mid D_t)\right),\qquad S_{\mathrm{dec}}(\eta;\eta_0)=\inf_{u\in M_\eta,\,v\in M_{\eta_0}}\rho(u,v),\] where \(M_\eta=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in X}a_t(x;\eta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noise-model sensitivity compares posterior distributions and acquisition maximizers obtained from the same data under alternative observation-noise specifications.
assumptions_latex: \(D_t\) and all surrogate components other than the noise model are held fixed.
Each acquisition maximizer set \(M_\eta\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_{\mathrm{post}}\) and \(S_{\mathrm{dec}}\) quantify inferential and decision sensitivity to the noise model.

notation.meaning: surrogate posterior under noise specification eta

children.title: Prior Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Dependence of surrogate beliefs or proposals on prior specification.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Controlled prior perturbation with separately reported posterior and policy effects.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix data, likelihood, surrogate family, inference tolerance, evaluation set, and acquisition construction. For every prior \(P\) in a prespecified class \(\mathcal P\), compute posterior predictive summaries and the induced acquisition on common evaluation objects. Report discrepancies and decision changes separately, or combine them only using prespecified dimensionless normalizations and weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vary only the prior and compare posterior and acquisition effects on declared common scales.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P\) is prespecified.
Every \(P\in\mathcal P\) yields a proper posterior.
Likelihood, data, model family, and computational tolerances are fixed.
knowledge_statements.title: Componentwise Prior Sensitivity Analysis

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of conclusions drawn from a restricted prior class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Agreement of posterior predictions and acquisition decisions over a tested class \(\mathcal P_0\) establishes robustness only over \(\mathcal P_0\). It implies no bound for priors outside that class; weakly identified prediction-relevant directions can remain strongly prior-sensitive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A prior-sensitivity study establishes stability only against the perturbations it actually includes.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P_0\) is the tested prior class.
At least one prediction-relevant direction may be weakly identified by the likelihood.
knowledge_statements.title: Prior Robustness Is Class-Relative

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact prior-to-posterior map for a finite-dimensional Gaussian surrogate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(y\mid\beta\sim N(X\beta,\Sigma)\) and \(\beta\sim N(m_0,V_0)\), the posterior is \(N(m_n,V_n)\), where \[V_n=(V_0^{-1}+X^\top\Sigma^{-1}X)^{-1},\qquad m_n=V_n(V_0^{-1}m_0+X^\top\Sigma^{-1}y).\] These formulas give exact sensitivity to prior location and precision with the likelihood fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a conjugate Gaussian surrogate, prior effects propagate through explicit additions of prior and data precision.
assumptions_latex: \(V_0\succ0\) and \(\Sigma\succ0\).
All displayed matrices and vectors have compatible dimensions.
knowledge_statements.title: Conjugate Gaussian Prior Sensitivity
Prior Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local diagnostic for prior-induced changes in posterior predictions and acquisition decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix observations \(D_t\), likelihood \(L(D_t\mid f)\), and acquisition construction. For priors \(P,Q\) on the latent objective \(f\), let \(\Pi_P,\Pi_Q\) be their posteriors and \(a_P,a_Q\) their acquisition functions on \(X\). Given a probability metric \(d\) and norm \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal A}\), define \[S_{\mathrm{prior}}(P,Q;D_t)=d(\Pi_P,\Pi_Q)+\|a_P-a_Q\|_{\mathcal A}.\] A prior-sensitivity analysis reports this quantity, or its two summands, over a declared class of plausible priors while holding the likelihood, data, and acquisition rule fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prior sensitivity measures how changing only the surrogate prior alters the posterior and acquisition function for fixed observations.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) and \(Q\) yield proper posteriors under the fixed likelihood.
The acquisition functions belong to the domain of \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal A}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_{\mathrm{prior}}(P,Q;D_t)\) separates prior-induced posterior and policy variation.

notation.meaning: alternative priors on the latent objective

children.title: Policy-Solver Diagnostic Interface
children.top_down_role: Checks separating policy behavior from failures of acquisition evaluation or optimization.

children.title: Acquisition-Policy Behavior
children.top_down_role: Observed balance, diversity, and stability of proposals produced by the policy.

knowledge_statements.title: Acquisition-Policy Behavior
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Behavioral representation of the acquisition policy induced by a fitted surrogate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(t\), let \(D_t\) determine a surrogate posterior and acquisition function \(a_t:X\to\mathbb R\). An exact deterministic acquisition policy is represented by \[\pi_t(D_t)\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in X}a_t(x).\] A randomized policy is a Markov kernel \(K_t(\cdot\mid D_t)\) supported on a declared candidate set, with exact maximization requiring \(K_t(M_t\mid D_t)=1\), where \(M_t=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in X}a_t(x)\). Policy behavior is assessed through the sequence of selected points and declared summaries such as predicted utility, posterior uncertainty, and distance from previously evaluated points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An acquisition policy maps the current data to an acquisition maximizer, or to a distribution supported on eligible candidate points.
assumptions_latex: The acquisition function \(a_t\) is well-defined on the feasible domain \(X\).
For exact policies, \(M_t\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_t\) or \(K_t\) provides a mathematically explicit representation of acquisition-policy behavior.

source_refs.source_title: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences

source_witnesses.source_title: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sensitivity of an acquisition policy's proposal distribution to perturbations of its information state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a state distance \(d_D\), a metric \(d_{\mathsf P}\) on proposal laws, and a state class \(\mathcal D\), a policy kernel \(K_t\) is \(L\)-stable when \[d_{\mathsf P}\!\left(K_t(\cdot\mid D),K_t(\cdot\mid D')\right)\le Ld_D(D,D')\quad(D,D'\in\mathcal D).\] Deterministic outputs are represented by Dirac laws. Stability is undefined until the metrics, state class, and tie rule are fixed; switching between tied maximizers need not indicate a defective acquisition criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proposal-law stability bounds policy-output changes under information-state perturbations using declared metrics and tie handling.
assumptions_latex: d_D\text{ and }d_{\mathsf P}\text{ are fixed metrics}.
K_t(\cdot\mid D)\text{ is defined for every }D\in\mathcal D.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d_{\mathsf P}(K_t(\cdot\mid D),K_t(\cdot\mid D'))\le Ld_D(D,D')\text{ characterizes }L\text{-stability.}
knowledge_statements.title: Proposal-Law Stability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spatial allocation summary for realized or randomized acquisition proposals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For proposals \(x_1,\ldots,x_T\), define \[\mu_T=\frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T\delta_{x_t}.\] Then \(\mu_T(A)\) is the fraction of proposals in any measurable \(A\subseteq X\). For policy kernels \(K_t(\cdot\mid D_t)\), define the conditional intended allocation \(\bar\mu_T=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T K_t(\cdot\mid D_t)\). These measures describe allocation, diversity, or concentration but do not alone certify objective performance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Empirical and expected occupation measures summarize where a policy places proposals without by themselves establishing optimization quality.
assumptions_latex: T\ge1.
The proposal space is measurable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mu_T(A)\text{ and }\bar\mu_T(A)\text{ quantify realized and intended proposal frequencies in }A.
knowledge_statements.title: Proposal Occupation Measure

children.title: Acquisition Evaluation Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Reliability of computed acquisition values used to compare candidate designs.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform numerical-evaluation error and its propagation to exact acquisition-value loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a:X\to\mathbb R\) be an exact acquisition and \(\widehat a:X\to\mathbb R\) its numerical approximation. Suppose \[\sup_{x\in X}|\widehat a(x)-a(x)|\le\varepsilon.\] If \(\widehat x\) satisfies \(\widehat a(\widehat x)\ge\sup_{x\in X}\widehat a(x)-\delta\), then \[\sup_{x\in X}a(x)-a(\widehat x)\le2\varepsilon+\delta.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform acquisition-evaluation error ε and computed-acquisition solver error δ bound exact acquisition loss by 2ε+δ.
assumptions_latex: \sup_{x\in X}|\widehat a(x)-a(x)|\le\varepsilon.
\sup_X a\text{ and }\sup_X\widehat a\text{ are finite}.
\widehat a(\widehat x)\ge\sup_X\widehat a-\delta.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Acquisition-Evaluation Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Accuracy Does Not Certify Proposal Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of acquisition validation restricted to the returned point or a noncovering candidate subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{0,1\}\), \(a(0)=0\), \(a(1)=1\), \(\widehat a(0)=0\), and \(\widehat a(1)=-1\). Maximizing \(\widehat a\) returns \(\widehat x=0\), where \(|\widehat a(\widehat x)-a(\widehat x)|=0\), but \[\sup_{x\in X}a(x)-a(\widehat x)=1.\] Thus accuracy only at the returned point, or on a candidate subset omitting a relevant competitor, does not certify proposal accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate acquisition can be exact at its returned point while selecting a point with positive exact-acquisition gap.
assumptions_latex: \widehat x\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in X}\widehat a(x).
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Accuracy Does Not Certify Proposal Accuracy
Acquisition Evaluation Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform-error certificate for numerical acquisition-function evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a:X\to\mathbb R\) be the exact acquisition function and \(\widehat a:X\to\mathbb R\) its numerical approximation. A uniform evaluation certificate of radius \(\varepsilon\ge0\) is a verified bound \[\sup_{x\in X}|\widehat a(x)-a(x)|\le\varepsilon.\] If \(\widehat x\) satisfies \(\widehat a(\widehat x)\ge\sup_{x\in X}\widehat a(x)-\delta\), then it also satisfies \[a(\widehat x)\ge\sup_{x\in X}a(x)-(2\varepsilon+\delta).\] Thus evaluation error and approximate maximization error combine additively into a certified acquisition-value loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform acquisition-evaluation error ε and solver error δ certify that the selected point loses at most 2ε+δ in exact acquisition value.
assumptions_latex: The displayed uniform error bound is valid over the entire feasible domain \(X\).
The suprema of \(a\) and \(\widehat a\) are finite.

notation.meaning: approximate maximization tolerance for the computed acquisition
point returned by the acquisition solver

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The uniform perturbation certificate and the 2ε+δ bound are mathematically correct and appropriately classified, but no inspectable citation is supplied.

children.title: Inner-Solver Quality
children.top_down_role: Quality and repeatability of numerical acquisition maximization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General acquisition-suboptimality certificate for a numerical inner solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(a:X\to\mathbb R\) and a feasible returned point \(\widehat x\), define \[g_a(\widehat x)=\sup_{x\in X}a(x)-a(\widehat x).\] A verified upper bound \(g_a(\widehat x)\le\delta\) certifies \(\delta\)-accurate maximization. If only a finite candidate set \(C\subseteq X\) is evaluated, the observable gap \(\max_{x\in C}a(x)-a(\widehat x)\) is a global certificate only when a valid bound also controls \(\sup_Xa-\max_Ca\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inner-solver quality is certified by a global acquisition-gap bound; a candidate-set gap alone is not generally global.
assumptions_latex: \widehat x\in X.
\sup_{x\in X}a(x)<\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Inner-Solver Gap Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Repeatability Does Not Imply Inner-Solver Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical separation of run-to-run reproducibility from acquisition-value optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{0,1\}\), \(a(0)=0\), and \(a(1)=1\). A deterministic solver returning \(0\) on every run is perfectly repeatable but has gap \(1\). Conversely, a solver may return different elements of a non-singleton exact argmax set and have zero gap on every run. Thus repeatability and acquisition-value accuracy are logically independent absent uniqueness or a separate output-distance criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver can be repeatable and inaccurate, or vary among tied exact maximizers while remaining value-optimal.
assumptions_latex: Solver quality is assessed against the exact acquisition a.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Repeatability neither implies nor is implied by zero acquisition-value gap.}

notation.meaning: exact acquisition optimized by the solver

knowledge_statements.title: Repeatability Does Not Imply Inner-Solver Accuracy
Inner-Solver Quality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Suboptimality certificate for the numerical solver maximizing an acquisition function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an acquisition function \(a:X\to\mathbb R\) and returned point \(\widehat x\in X\), define the inner-solver gap by \[g_a(\widehat x)=\sup_{x\in X}a(x)-a(\widehat x).\] The solver is \(\delta\)-accurate when a verifiable upper bound establishes \(g_a(\widehat x)\le\delta\). If only evaluated candidates \(C\subseteq X\) are available, the observable candidate gap \(\max_{x\in C}a(x)-a(\widehat x)\) is a global certificate only when an additional bound controls \(\sup_{x\in X}a(x)-\max_{x\in C}a(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inner-solver quality is certified by an upper bound on acquisition suboptimality; a candidate-set gap alone is not generally a global certificate.
assumptions_latex: The returned point \(\widehat x\) is feasible.
The acquisition supremum over \(X\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid bound \(g_a(\widehat x)\le\delta\) certifies \(\delta\)-accurate acquisition maximization.

notation.meaning: finite set of evaluated solver candidates

children.title: Policy–Solver Failure Attribution
children.top_down_role: Separation of policy defects from numerical realization failures.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterfactual attribution after fixing the intended exact-policy tie rule and downstream benchmark.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_t=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in X}a_t(x)\), and fix an intended exact-policy distribution \(Q_t\) supported on \(M_t\). For declared downstream loss \(L_t\), policy threshold \(b_t\), and solver-effect tolerance \(\tau_t\ge0\), set \(\ell_t^\star=\int L_t(x)Q_t(dx)\). The intended policy fails the benchmark when \(\ell_t^\star>b_t\). For implemented proposal \(\widehat x_t\), a detrimental numerical realization effect is certified when \(L_t(\widehat x_t)-\ell_t^\star>\tau_t\). Both may hold. If \(Q_t\), \(L_t\), or \(b_t\) is unspecified, or the exact-policy counterfactual is not known accurately enough, this attribution is not identified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Policy–solver attribution requires a declared exact-policy tie rule, downstream loss, benchmark, and sufficiently accurate counterfactual.
assumptions_latex: M_t\ne\varnothing.
L_t, b_t,\text{ and }\tau_t\text{ are fixed before attribution}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ell_t^\star>b_t\text{ diagnoses policy failure, while }L_t(\widehat x_t)-\ell_t^\star>\tau_t\text{ diagnoses a detrimental numerical effect.}

notation.meaning: counterfactual downstream loss of the intended exact policy

knowledge_statements.title: Tie-Rule-Specific Policy–Solver Attribution

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Implemented Proposal Alone Does Not Identify Failure Source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Observational nonidentifiability of policy and solver failure without the intended acquisition counterfactual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{0,1\}\), \(L(0)=1\), \(L(1)=0\), and \(b=1/2\), and observe only \(\widehat x=0\). If the intended acquisition has unique maximizer \(1\), the exact policy meets the benchmark and returning \(0\) is a solver realization failure. If instead the intended acquisition has unique maximizer \(0\), the same implemented proposal is solver-exact but the intended policy fails the benchmark. Hence \(\widehat x\) alone cannot identify the failure source.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The same implemented proposal can arise from a good policy with solver failure or a bad policy with exact solver execution.
assumptions_latex: Only the implemented proposal and downstream loss are observed; the intended acquisition counterfactual is not fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat x\text{ alone does not identify policy versus solver failure.}
knowledge_statements.title: Implemented Proposal Alone Does Not Identify Failure Source
Policy–Solver Failure Attribution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterfactual criterion separating acquisition-policy failure from numerical solver failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_t\) be the intended acquisition, let \(x_t^\star\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in X}a_t(x)\), and let \(\widehat x_t\) be the implemented solver output. For a declared downstream loss \(L_t:X\to\mathbb R\) and tolerance \(\tau\ge0\), attribute failure to the solver when \[L_t(\widehat x_t)-L_t(x_t^\star)>\tau.\] Attribute failure to the policy when \(L_t(x_t^\star)\) itself violates the declared policy-performance threshold. When both conditions hold, attribution is joint; without a certified or sufficiently accurate counterfactual \(x_t^\star\), policy and solver effects are not identifiable from \(\widehat x_t\) alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare the implemented point with an exact acquisition maximizer: excess downstream loss indicates solver failure, while poor exact-policy performance indicates policy failure.
assumptions_latex: The intended acquisition function and downstream loss are fixed for the comparison.
An exact or certified-accurate acquisition maximizer is available as a counterfactual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two counterfactual tests yield solver, policy, joint, or nonidentifiable attribution.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed attribution framework has no citation, depends on which exact maximizer is selected when the argmax is nonunique, and does not formally specify the policy-performance threshold. These choices materially affect attribution.

children.title: Computational Resource Accounting
children.top_down_role: Assessment of modeling and policy overhead relative to black-box evaluation cost.

children.title: Wall-Clock Accounting
children.top_down_role: Elapsed-time assessment across modeling, policy computation, and evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Wall-Clock Accounting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive elapsed-time ledger for one Bayesian-optimization run.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a sequential run with iterations \(t=1,\ldots,T\), partition measured elapsed time into objective evaluation, surrogate modeling, acquisition-policy computation, and residual system time. The wall-clock ledger is \[W_{\mathrm{tot}}=W_{\mathrm{eval}}+W_{\mathrm{model}}+W_{\mathrm{policy}}+W_{\mathrm{sys}},\qquad W_k=\sum_{t=1}^T W_{k,t}.\] Categories must be mutually exclusive under a declared timing convention. If evaluations or computations overlap, elapsed wall time is accounted by intervals or critical-path time rather than by summing concurrent task durations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Wall-clock accounting partitions total elapsed run time into evaluation, modeling, policy, and system components without double-counting concurrent work.
assumptions_latex: Start and end events use a common monotone clock.
The timing convention assigns every elapsed interval exactly once or explicitly handles overlap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The ledger reconciles component times with total elapsed wall time.

notation.meaning: wall time assigned to category k at iteration t

children.title: Resource-Consumption Accounting
children.top_down_role: Assessment of compute, energy, equipment, or personnel consumption.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Consumption Accounting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vector ledger for heterogeneous computational and experimental resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal R\) be a finite set of resource types, such as objective calls, monetary cost, processor time, accelerator time, energy, or memory. For iteration \(t\), record a nonnegative consumption vector \(r_t\in\mathbb R_+^{|\mathcal R|}\). Given an initial consumption vector \(C_0\in\mathbb R_+^{|\mathcal R|}\), cumulative additive consumption through iteration \(T\) is \[C_T=C_0+\sum_{t=1}^T r_t.\] Given component budgets \(B\in\mathbb R_+^{|\mathcal R|}\), the run is resource-feasible through \(T\) exactly when \(C_T\le B\) componentwise. Nonadditive resources, including peak memory, must be recorded with an appropriate aggregator rather than this sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resource accounting accumulates a vector of per-iteration consumptions and compares it componentwise with declared budgets, using separate aggregators for nonadditive resources.
assumptions_latex: Resource types, units, and measurement boundaries are fixed before comparison.
Each additive resource is recorded without omission or duplication.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_T\le B\) characterizes feasibility with respect to all declared additive resource budgets.

notation.meaning: finite set of declared resource types

source_refs.source_title: Simulation-Based Optimization: Parametric Optimization Techniques and Reinforcement Learning

source_witnesses.source_title: Simulation-Based Optimization: Parametric Optimization Techniques and Reinforcement Learning

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint accounting for resource coordinates having additive or peak aggregation laws.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition declared resource coordinates into \(\mathcal R_+\) and \(\mathcal R_{\max}\). For \(r_{t,j}\ge0\), set \[C_{T,j}=C_{0,j}+\sum_{t=1}^T r_{t,j}\quad(j\in\mathcal R_+),\qquad C_{T,j}=\max\{C_{0,j},r_{1,j},\ldots,r_{T,j}\}\quad(j\in\mathcal R_{\max}).\] For declared budgets \(B_j\), resource feasibility is \(C_{T,j}\le B_j\) for every coordinate. Replacing a declared maximum by a sum, or a sum by a maximum, measures a different resource and may change the feasibility verdict.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Additive resources use sums, peak resources use maxima, and feasibility requires every correctly aggregated coordinate to meet its budget.
assumptions_latex: The resource coordinates, units, measurement boundaries, and aggregators are fixed before comparison.
Each consumption is recorded without omission or duplication.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_{T,j}\le B_j\ \forall j\text{ certifies feasibility for the declared mixed ledger.}
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Additive-and-Peak Resource Ledger

children.title: Modeling-Overhead Attribution
children.top_down_role: Resource burden attributable to surrogate fitting or inference.

knowledge_statements.title: Modeling-Overhead Attribution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attribution of computational overhead to surrogate fitting and posterior maintenance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For iterations \(t=1,\ldots,T\), fix a common additive overhead unit and define modeling overhead \(M_t\ge0\) as the amount consumed after data become available and before acquisition calculation begins, solely by surrogate operations declared in advance. These operations may include preprocessing, hyperparameter estimation, factorization, posterior updating, and predictive-cache construction. Total modeling overhead and its share of measured non-evaluation overhead are \[M_{1:T}=\sum_{t=1}^T M_t,\qquad q_M=\frac{M_{1:T}}{M_{1:T}+P_{1:T}+S_{1:T}},\] when the denominator is positive. Shared operations require a declared allocation rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Modeling overhead comprises additive resources spent fitting and maintaining the surrogate, with shared costs assigned by a fixed allocation rule.
assumptions_latex: The overhead unit and measurement boundaries are fixed across iterations.
\(M_{1:T}\), \(P_{1:T}\), and \(S_{1:T}\) use the same additive unit and are mutually exclusive under a declared allocation rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_{1:T}\) and \(q_M\) quantify absolute and relative modeling overhead in the declared unit.

notation.meaning: modeling share of measured non-evaluation overhead

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact dense GP factorization is cubic-time and quadratic-storage, while a fixed-parameter append is quadratic-time.

children.title: Policy-Overhead Attribution
children.top_down_role: Resource burden attributable to acquisition evaluation or candidate selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Policy-Overhead Attribution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attribution of computational overhead to acquisition construction, evaluation, and maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For iterations \(t=1,\ldots,T\), define policy overhead \(P_t\ge0\) as the resources consumed by constructing, evaluating, and optimizing the acquisition rule after the surrogate state is available and before an objective evaluation is launched. Total policy overhead and mean overhead per launched evaluation are \[P_{1:T}=\sum_{t=1}^T P_t,\qquad \overline P=\frac{P_{1:T}}{N_T},\] where \(N_T>0\) is the number of objective evaluations launched. Surrogate updates and objective execution are excluded; shared computations follow a declared allocation rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Policy overhead counts resources used to construct, evaluate, and optimize acquisitions, excluding surrogate updates and objective execution.
assumptions_latex: Policy-stage boundaries and resource units are fixed across runs.
Each shared computation is assigned by a declared allocation rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{1:T}\) and \(\overline P\) quantify total and per-evaluation policy overhead.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative acquisition-policy overhead measured against objective-execution resources in the same additive unit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If cumulative policy overhead is \(P_{1:T}\) and cumulative objective-execution consumption is \(E_{1:T}>0\), both measured with the same additive resource unit and allocation convention, define \[\rho_{P/E}=\frac{P_{1:T}}{E_{1:T}}.\] This ratio compares acquisition-policy computation with objective execution; it is not comparable across runs having different resource units, stage boundaries, concurrency conventions, or shared-cost allocations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The policy-to-evaluation burden ratio compares cumulative policy computation with objective execution under a common accounting convention.
assumptions_latex: P_{1:T}\text{ and }E_{1:T}\text{ use the same additive resource unit and compatible allocation boundaries.}

children.title: Search Termination Recommendation Interface
children.top_down_role: Termination and recommendation choices after or during surrogate-guided search.

children.title: Resource-Bounded Stopping Family
children.top_down_role: Termination based on evaluation count, wall time, or resource consumption.

children.title: Evaluation-Budget Stopping
children.top_down_role: Termination governed by the available number of black-box evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Evaluation-Budget Stopping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stopping rule based on a fixed number of objective evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb N_0\) be the permitted number of charged objective evaluations, and let \(N_t\) be the number already launched or irrevocably committed before iteration \(t\), including completed and in-flight evaluations. If the proposed next batch contains \(b_t\in\mathbb N\) charged evaluations, the evaluation-budget stopping condition is \[N_t+b_t>B.\] Under a no-overshoot convention, the algorithm stops before launching that batch; alternatively, it may reduce the batch to at most \(B-N_t\). For unit batches, stopping occurs once \(N_t=B\). Failed, cancelled, or censored evaluations count toward \(N_t\) exactly when the declared budget convention charges them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop before a proposed evaluation or batch would make the number of launched or committed charged evaluations exceed the allowed count.
assumptions_latex: The evaluation budget \(B\) is fixed before the run.
The counting convention for failed, cancelled, repeated, and parallel evaluations is declared.
\(N_t\) includes every charged evaluation already launched or irrevocably committed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No-overshoot stopping guarantees that the number of launched or committed charged evaluations does not exceed \(B\).

notation.meaning: charged evaluations launched or committed before iteration t
charged size of the proposed next batch

children.title: Cost-Based Stopping
children.top_down_role: Termination governed by cumulative monetary or resource expenditure.

knowledge_statements.title: Cost-Based Stopping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stopping rule based on cumulative realized or committed evaluation cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_c\ge0\) be a total cost budget, let \(C_t\) be cumulative charged cost before iteration \(t\), and let \(\widehat c_t\ge0\) be a certified upper bound on the cost of the proposed next evaluation or batch. The conservative cost-based stopping condition is \[C_t+\widehat c_t>B_c.\] Under a no-overshoot convention, the proposal is not launched when this condition holds. If only expected cost \(\mathbb E[c_t\mid D_t]\) is used, the analogous rule controls expected expenditure and does not by itself guarantee pathwise budget feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop when cumulative charged cost plus a certified bound for the next proposal would exceed budget; expected-cost rules provide only expected control.
assumptions_latex: Costs are nonnegative and measured in a common declared unit.
The charging convention for cancelled, failed, and parallel evaluations is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Using a valid upper cost bound ensures pathwise expenditure does not exceed \(B_c\) under no overshoot.

notation.meaning: cumulative charged cost before iteration t
certified upper bound on proposed additional cost

children.title: Time-Based Stopping
children.top_down_role: Termination governed by wall-clock or operational deadlines.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pathwise completion-feasibility test using a valid duration upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At dispatch time \(s\), suppose \(\widehat U\) is a pathwise-valid upper bound for the proposed evaluation duration, so that \(U\le\widehat U\). Admission under the test \(s+\widehat U\le d\) certifies completion by deadline \(d\). A point prediction or expected duration without such an upper-bound guarantee does not provide this pathwise certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid duration upper bound can certify deadline-safe launch; a mean or point prediction cannot do so by itself.
assumptions_latex: \(U\le\widehat U\) holds for the proposed evaluation.
The deadline requires completion no later than \(d\).

notation.meaning: valid upper bound on evaluation duration

knowledge_statements.title: Hard-Deadline Launch Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dispatch Before Deadline Does Not Ensure Completion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hard-deadline boundary for evaluations with uncertain or nonzero duration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the absolute deadline be \(d\), let an evaluation be dispatched at time \(s<d\), and let its duration be \(U\ge0\). Dispatch-time feasibility \(s<d\) does not imply completion-time feasibility \(s+U\le d\); whenever \(U>d-s\), the evaluation completes after the deadline.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Launching an evaluation before a deadline does not ensure that its result is available by the deadline.
assumptions_latex: The evaluation has nonnegative duration \(U\).
A hard deadline requires completion by \(d\).
knowledge_statements.title: Dispatch Before Deadline Does Not Ensure Completion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational variants for evaluations still running at a reporting deadline or dispatch cutoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d\) be a declared deadline and \(\mathcal P(d)\) the evaluations pending at \(d\). Under a hard reporting deadline, pending work may be cancelled or allowed to continue, but the on-time recommendation must exclude results unavailable by \(d\). Waiting for pending work and reporting after \(d\) is compatible only with the weaker convention that \(d\) is a dispatch cutoff rather than a reporting deadline.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a hard reporting deadline, pending results must be excluded from the on-time recommendation; waiting is valid only under a dispatch-cutoff convention.
assumptions_latex: The deadline is declared as either a reporting deadline or a dispatch cutoff.
A result enters the recommendation only after it is completed and observed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{hard reporting at }d\Longrightarrow\widehat a(d)\text{ is measurable with respect to information available by }d.
knowledge_statements.title: Pending-Evaluation Deadline Policies

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Wall-clock stopping with explicit decision epochs and returned-information convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(t_0\) be the start time, \((t_n)\) the nondecreasing adapted sequence of decision-epoch times, and \(T>0\). With \(\inf\varnothing=\infty\), define
\[
\tau_T=\inf\{n:t_n-t_0\ge T\}.
\]
No action is dispatched at or after \(t_0+T\). Under a hard reporting deadline, the returned recommendation is measurable with respect to results observed by \(t_0+T\); under a dispatch-cutoff convention, actions dispatched earlier may finish later and enter a later report.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Time-based stopping ends dispatch at a declared elapsed-time threshold and must state whether that threshold is also a hard reporting deadline.
assumptions_latex: (t_n)_{n\ge0}\text{ is nondecreasing and adapted to the run history}.
The reporting-deadline or dispatch-cutoff convention is declared.

notation.meaning: Wall-clock time of decision epoch n.

knowledge_statements.title: Elapsed-Time Stopping Index
Time-Based Stopping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Wall-clock stopping for a sequential Bayesian optimization run.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(t_0\) be the run's start time, let \(t_n\) be the time immediately after iteration \(n\), and let \(T>0\) be the allowed elapsed time. The time-based stopping index is \[\tau_T=\inf\{n\geq 0:t_n-t_0\geq T\}.\] No new evaluation is launched at or after \(\tau_T\); the procedure returns the recommendation computed from the information available at \(\tau_T\). If a strict pre-launch rule is required, iteration \(n+1\) is launched only when its predicted completion time does not exceed \(t_0+T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop once elapsed wall-clock time reaches the prescribed limit, and return the recommendation based on information then available.
assumptions_latex: \((t_n)_{n\geq0}\) is nondecreasing.

children.title: Mixed-Resource Stopping
children.top_down_role: Termination under multiple simultaneous resource limits.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Aggregate Accounting Does Not Ensure Componentwise Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a scalar resource score to enforce several hard budgets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let hard-resource budgets be \(B=(1,1)\), current use \(R=(0,0)\), proposed use \(\Delta R=(2,0)\), and weights \(w=(1/2,1/2)\). Then \(w^\top(R+\Delta R)=w^\top B\), while \(R_1+\Delta R_1=2>B_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proposal can satisfy an aggregate resource score while violating an individual hard limit.
assumptions_latex: Both component budgets are hard constraints.
The displayed resource vectors and weights are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w^\top(R+\Delta R)\le w^\top B\ \not\Rightarrow\ R+\Delta R\le B\quad\text{componentwise}.
knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate Accounting Does Not Ensure Componentwise Feasibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed-resource admission separating inviolable limits from penalized consumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition resources into hard indices \(H\) and soft indices \(S\), and choose reserves \(q_j\in[0,B_j]\) for \(j\in H\). Admit proposal \(a\) only if \(R_j+U_j(a)\le B_j-q_j\) for every \(j\in H\). Among admitted proposals, one may optimize a declared score such as \(A_n(a)-\sum_{j\in S}\lambda_jU_j(a)\), where \(\lambda_j\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reserve-aware admission enforces every hard resource componentwise and treats soft resources through declared penalties.
assumptions_latex: \(0\le q_j\le B_j\) for every \(j\in H\).
Each \(U_j(a)\) has the validity required by the declared hard-feasibility semantics.
\(\lambda_j\ge0\) for every \(j\in S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a\text{ admitted}\Longrightarrow R_j+U_j(a)\le B_j-q_j\quad\forall j\in H.
knowledge_statements.title: Reserve-Aware Hard-and-Soft Resource Admission

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Joint Chance Admission by Componentwise Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probabilistic feasibility certificate for multiple hard resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For hard-resource indices \(H\), suppose \(P(\Delta R_j>U_j\mid D_n)\le\delta_j\) and \(R_j+U_j\le B_j\) for every \(j\in H\). Then \[P(R_j+\Delta R_j\le B_j\ \forall j\in H\mid D_n)\ge1-\sum_{j\in H}\delta_j.\] No independence assumption is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Componentwise high-probability increment bounds and a union bound certify simultaneous probabilistic feasibility of all hard resources.
assumptions_latex: \(P(\Delta R_j>U_j\mid D_n)\le\delta_j\) for every \(j\in H\).
\(R_j+U_j\le B_j\) for every \(j\in H\).
\(\sum_{j\in H}\delta_j\le1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P(R_j+\Delta R_j\le B_j\ \forall j\in H\mid D_n)\ge1-\sum_{j\in H}\delta_j.

notation.meaning: allocated violation probability for resource j

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Chance Admission by Componentwise Bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pathwise componentwise pre-launch feasibility using valid increment bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R,B\in\mathbb R^m\), and suppose a proposed action has realized increment \(\Delta R\) satisfying the componentwise pathwise bound \(\Delta R\le U\). If \(R+U\le B\) componentwise, then launching the action certifies \(R+\Delta R\le B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Current use plus valid componentwise increment bounds certifies simultaneous safety for all hard budgets.
assumptions_latex: \(\Delta R_j\le U_j\) for every hard resource.
Hard-resource feasibility is componentwise.

notation.meaning: componentwise pathwise upper bound on the proposed increment

knowledge_statements.title: Simultaneous Hard-Resource Admission Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise stopping and pre-launch conventions for simultaneous hard-resource budgets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(R_n\in\mathbb R_+^m\) be adapted, componentwise nondecreasing cumulative committed use and \(B\in(0,\infty)^m\) the hard-budget vector. If action \(a\) has realized increment \(\Delta R_n(a)\) and a pathwise-valid bound \(\Delta R_n(a)\le U_n(a)\), admit it only when \(R_n+U_n(a)\le B\) componentwise. The safe-admission stopping index is
\[
\tau=\inf\{n:\text{no admissible proposal remains}\},
\]
and its recommendation uses only results available at \(\tau\). Under the distinct post-use exhaustion convention,
\[
\tau_{\mathrm{ex}}=\inf\{n:\exists j,\ R_{j,n}\ge B_j\},
\]
which need not prevent overshoot.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed-resource stopping enforces every hard budget componentwise before launch; post-use exhaustion is a distinct convention that may overshoot.
assumptions_latex: R_n\text{ is adapted and componentwise nondecreasing}.
B_j>0\text{ for every }j.
\Delta R_n(a)\le U_n(a)\text{ componentwise for every admitted action}.
The admissible action set and returned-information convention are declared.

notation.meaning: Valid componentwise bound on the proposed increment.
First decision epoch with no safely admissible proposal.

knowledge_statements.title: Vector Hard-Resource Stopping and Admission
Mixed-Resource Stopping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stopping under several jointly monitored resource budgets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For resources \(j=1,\ldots,m\), let \(R_{j,n}\geq0\) be cumulative consumption after iteration \(n\), and let \(B_j>0\) be its budget. Under disjunctive exhaustion, the stopping index is \[\tau_{\mathrm{mix}}=\inf\{n\geq0:\exists j,\ R_{j,n}\geq B_j\}.\] A candidate evaluation with predicted resource increment \(\widehat{\Delta R}_{j,n+1}\) is admissible only if \(R_{j,n}+\widehat{\Delta R}_{j,n+1}\leq B_j\) for every hard resource. The returned recommendation uses only information collected before stopping.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop when any hard resource budget is exhausted, and launch an evaluation only if all predicted resource limits remain feasible.
assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb{N}\) and \(B_j>0\) for every \(j\).
\(R_{j,n+1}\geq R_{j,n}\) for every resource and iteration.

notation.meaning: cumulative use of resource j after iteration n
