children.title: Covariance Degeneracy Failure Family
children.top_down_role: Identifiability, boundary estimates, duplicate designs, and ill-conditioning.

children.title: Hyperparameter Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Weak identifiability or boundary estimates that distort surrogate behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Hyperparameter Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degenerate covariance limits or nonidentifiability reached during surrogate hyperparameter fitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_\theta\) be the training covariance matrix induced by \(\theta\in\Theta\), and let \(L(\theta)\) be a marginal-likelihood or related fitting criterion. Hyperparameter degeneracy occurs when a boundary sequence \(\theta_m\) satisfies \(\lambda_{\min}(K_{\theta_m})\to0\), or when distinct hyperparameter values induce observationally indistinguishable covariance matrices. Depending on the kernel and design, such behavior can arise from vanishing regularization or particular extreme length-scale limits. Near a singular boundary, covariance solves and log-determinant evaluation become numerically unstable; under nonidentifiability, fitted hyperparameters can vary substantially without a distinguishable fit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hyperparameter degeneracy occurs when boundary parameters make the training covariance nearly singular or when different parameters produce observationally indistinguishable covariance matrices.
assumptions_latex: The training covariance is \(K_\theta\) for \(\theta\in\Theta\).
Hyperparameters are estimated using a marginal likelihood or related criterion \(L(\theta)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A sequence with \(\lambda_{\min}(K_{\theta_m})\to0\), or distinct observationally indistinguishable covariance parameterizations, constitutes hyperparameter degeneracy and can destabilize fitting or prediction.

source_refs.source_title: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences

source_witnesses.source_title: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical nonidentifiability of Matérn variance and range under fixed-domain sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\subset\mathbb R^d\) be bounded with nonempty interior, \(d\le3\), and consider zero-mean stationary Matérn Gaussian processes on \(D\) with common known smoothness \(
u>0\), variance \(\sigma^2\), and range \(ho\), under a parameterization whose correlation argument is proportional to \(\lVert hVert/ho\). Two such process measures are equivalent exactly when \(\sigma_1^2/ho_1^{2
u}=\sigma_2^2/ho_2^{2
u}\). Thus fixed-domain infill cannot consistently distinguish variance and range separately, although the microergodic combination is identifiable under the theorem's regularity conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For fixed-domain Matérn models with known smoothness in dimensions at most three, variance and range are not separately identifiable; their microergodic ratio is identifiable.
assumptions_latex: D\subset\mathbb R^d is bounded with nonempty interior and d\le3.
The processes are stationary Matérn models with the same known smoothness \nu.
The range parameterization is fixed consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equivalent measures occur precisely at equal \sigma^2/\rho^{2\nu}, precluding separate fixed-domain consistent estimation of \sigma^2 and \rho.
knowledge_statements.title: Matérn Fixed-Domain Microergodicity

children.title: Covariance Instability
children.top_down_role: Numerical instability in covariance representations or predictive calculations.

knowledge_statements.title: Covariance Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical failure boundary for Gaussian-process covariance solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=K+\Sigma\) be the symmetric positive-definite covariance used for Gaussian-process conditioning. Covariance instability is approached as the spectral condition number \(\kappa_2(C)=\lambda_{\max}(C)/\lambda_{\min}(C)\) becomes large. In particular, this occurs when \(\lambda_{\min}(C)\downarrow0\) while \(\lambda_{\max}(C)\) remains bounded above and bounded away from zero. For a solve \(C\alpha=y\), perturbations and rounding errors can then be amplified by a factor governed by \(\kappa_2(C)\), materially affecting the computed solve, log determinant, posterior mean, and posterior variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Covariance instability occurs when the covariance condition number is large, allowing numerical or modeling perturbations to be strongly amplified in solves and posterior computations.
assumptions_latex: The regularized training covariance \(C=K+\Sigma\) is symmetric positive definite.
Posterior computation uses linear solves and log-determinant evaluations involving \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: As \(\kappa_2(C)=\lambda_{\max}(C)/\lambda_{\min}(C)\) grows, perturbations and rounding errors can be strongly amplified, producing covariance instability.

notation.meaning: extreme eigenvalues of the covariance matrix

source_refs.source_title: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences

source_witnesses.source_title: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral stabilization of a positive-semidefinite covariance matrix by diagonal loading.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\succeq0\) be symmetric and \(C_\delta=K+\delta I\) with \(\delta>0\). Then \[\lambda_{\min}(C_\delta)=\lambda_{\min}(K)+\delta\ge\delta,\qquad \kappa_2(C_\delta)=\frac{\lambda_{\max}(K)+\delta}{\lambda_{\min}(K)+\delta}\le1+\frac{\lambda_{\max}(K)}{\delta}.\] Thus diagonal loading ensures strict positive definiteness and a finite condition-number bound, although a very small \(\delta\) may still permit severe ill-conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive diagonal loading raises every eigenvalue and bounds the covariance condition number, but insufficient loading can remain numerically unstable.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal Regularization Condition-Number Bound

children.title: Duplicate-Design Ill-Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Covariance degradation associated with repeated or nearly coincident designs.

assumptions_latex: A positive-definite kernel \(k\) is evaluated at training sites \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\).
Two sites coincide, \(x_i=x_j\) with \(i\ne j\), and no positive nugget separates their observations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Duplicate noiseless designs give identical rows of \(K\), so \(K\) is singular; a nugget \(\tau^2>0\) restores eigenvalues of at least \(\tau^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact singularity caused by duplicated inputs under noiseless covariance interpolation.

source_refs.source_title: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_{rs}=k(x_r,x_s)\). If \(x_i=x_j\) for \(i\ne j\), then \(K_{ir}=K_{jr}\) for every \(r\), so the noiseless Gram matrix \(K\) has duplicate rows and is singular. Nearly duplicate sites similarly create a small eigenvalue and a large condition number. Adding independent observation variance \(\tau^2>0\) replaces \(K\) by \(K+\tau^2I\), whose smallest eigenvalue is at least \(\tau^2\); alternatively, exact replicates may be aggregated while retaining their effective noise variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicate noiseless inputs create identical covariance rows and singularity; near duplicates cause ill-conditioning, while a positive nugget or variance-aware aggregation regularizes the system.
knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate-Design Ill-Conditioning

source_witnesses.source_title: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences

children.title: Degeneracy-Induced Prediction Failure
children.top_down_role: Unstable predictions or uncertainty estimates arising from poorly determined parameters.

knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy-Induced Prediction Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Prediction failure propagated from singular or unstable covariance computations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), let \(C=K+\Sigma\) be the training covariance, let \(m_0(X)=(m_0(x_1),\ldots,m_0(x_n))^{\mathsf T}\), and let \(k_x=(k(x,x_1),\ldots,k(x,x_n))^{\mathsf T}\). Ordinary Gaussian-process prediction computes \(m(x)=m_0(x)+k_x^{\mathsf T}C^{-1}(y-m_0(X))\) and \(s^2(x)=k(x,x)-k_x^{\mathsf T}C^{-1}k_x\). If \(C\) is singular, these inverse-based formulas are unavailable without an additional generalized-inverse or regularization convention. If \(C\) is severely ill-conditioned, solve and cancellation errors can cause large changes in \(m(x)\) and severely inaccurate, sometimes negative, computed values of \(s^2(x)\). Acquisition rankings based on these computed quantities are then unreliable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Singular covariance matrices make ordinary inverse-based prediction unavailable, while severe ill-conditioning can destabilize posterior means and produce inaccurate or negative numerical variances and unreliable acquisition rankings.
assumptions_latex: Training inputs are \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), observations form \(y\in\mathbb R^n\), and the prior mean is \(m_0\).
Posterior quantities are computed using solves with \(C=K+\Sigma\) and the test-to-training covariance vector \(k_x\).
The covariance matrix is singular or sufficiently ill-conditioned that solve errors are material.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Singular or materially inaccurate covariance solves can destabilize computed posterior means and variances, thereby invalidating acquisition rankings.

notation.meaning: prior mean vector at the training inputs

source_refs.source_title: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences

source_witnesses.source_title: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative propagation of covariance error into Gaussian-process predictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\succ0\), \(\widetilde C=C+E\), and \(\eta=\lVert C^{-1}E\rVert_2<1\). Then \(\lVert\widetilde C^{-1}-C^{-1}\rVert_2\le \lVert C^{-1}\rVert_2^2\lVert E\rVert_2/(1-\eta)\). Consequently, with \(r=y-m_0(X)\), \(|\widetilde m(x)-m(x)|\le \lVert k_x\rVert_2\lVert r\rVert_2\lVert C^{-1}\rVert_2^2\lVert E\rVert_2/(1-\eta)\) and \(|\widetilde s^2(x)-s^2(x)|\le \lVert k_x\rVert_2^2\lVert C^{-1}\rVert_2^2\lVert E\rVert_2/(1-\eta)\), provided the residual and test covariances are unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Covariance perturbations can produce posterior-mean and variance errors amplified by the squared inverse-covariance norm.
assumptions_latex: C\succ0.
\widetilde C=C+E and \lVert C^{-1}E\rVert_2<1.
The residual vector and test-to-training covariance are unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Prediction-error bounds are amplified by \lVert C^{-1}\rVert_2^2.
knowledge_statements.title: Posterior Sensitivity to Covariance Perturbations

children.title: Acquisition Computation Failure Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by utility mismatch, pathological acquisition geometry, or inaccurate numerical realization.

children.title: Evaluation Allocation Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Evaluation allocation that is excessively local or weakly connected to decision value.

children.title: Premature Exploitation
children.top_down_role: Overly local evaluation allocation before uncertainty has been adequately resolved.

assumptions_latex: The policy selects \(x_{t+1}\) by maximizing a posterior-based acquisition \(a_t\).
There exists an unsampled region \(U\subset\mathcal X\) containing a global optimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(a_t(x)<\sup_{z\notin U}a_t(z)\) for every \(x\in U\) and all sufficiently large \(t\), then the policy never evaluates \(U\) thereafter and may retain positive simple regret.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient allocation-failure condition for permanently excluding an optimal region.

source_refs.source_title: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}a_t(x)\), and let \(U\subset\mathcal X\) be an unsampled region containing a global minimizer \(x^\star\). Premature exploitation occurs if, from some iteration \(T\) onward, \(a_t(x)<\sup_{z\in\mathcal X\setminus U}a_t(z)\) for every \(x\in U\). Then no later evaluation enters \(U\). If all sampled points satisfy \(f(x_i)\ge f(x^\star)+\delta\) for some \(\delta>0\), the simple regret \(r_t=\min_{i\le t}f(x_i)-f(x^\star)\) remains at least \(\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Premature exploitation occurs when the acquisition permanently ranks sampled regions above an unexplored optimal region, allowing simple regret to remain bounded away from zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Premature Exploitation

source_witnesses.source_title: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences

children.title: Unproductive Exploration
children.top_down_role: Evaluation allocation weakly connected to plausible decision improvement.

knowledge_statements.title: Unproductive Exploration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic allocation diagnostic for minimization under a fixed optimality tolerance; it does not by itself establish poor terminal performance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Unproductive exploration at tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\) is diagnosed when a nonvanishing fraction of evaluations remains outside the \(\varepsilon\)-optimal set \(X_\varepsilon\): \[\limsup_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbf{1}\{x_t\notin X_\varepsilon\}>0.\] This condition records persistent allocation away from the declared near-optimal region without asserting that every such evaluation is individually valueless.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exploration is diagnosed as unproductive at a chosen tolerance when a nonvanishing fraction of evaluations remains outside the corresponding near-optimal region.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a design space and \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is minimized.
\(x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f(x)\), \(\varepsilon>0\), and \(X_\varepsilon=\{x\in X:f(x)\le f(x^\star)+\varepsilon\}\).
The Bayesian-optimization policy proposes evaluations \((x_t)_{t\ge1}\subseteq X\).

source_refs.source_title: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences

source_witnesses.source_title: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unproductive Exploration Need Not Harm Simple Regret
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary separating persistent off-target allocation from best-observed terminal performance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{0,1\}\), let \(f(0)=0\) and \(f(1)=1\), and choose \(x_{2k-1}=0\), \(x_{2k}=1\). For every \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\), \(X_\varepsilon=\{0\}\) and the fraction of evaluations outside \(X_\varepsilon\) converges to \(1/2\), yet \(\min_{t\le T}f(x_t)-f(0)=0\) for every \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternating between an optimum and a bad point is persistently off-target by the allocation diagnostic but has zero simple regret.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\varepsilon<1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Unproductive Exploration Need Not Harm Simple Regret

children.title: Exploration–Exploitation Imbalance
children.top_down_role: Policy regimes exhibiting persistent imbalance between local refinement and uncertainty reduction.

assumptions_latex: At iteration \(t\), the acquisition decomposes as \(a_t(x)=E_t(x)+\lambda_tX_t(x)\) on \(X\).
\(E_t:X\to\mathbb{R}\) measures exploitation and \(X_t:X\to[0,\infty)\) measures exploration.
The intended policy uses a reference weight \(\lambda_t^\star>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A component-weight diagnostic, not a universal decomposition of every acquisition function.

source_refs.locator: 2.1.2 Sequential design and nonstationary surrogate modeling p. 34
source_refs.source_title: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exploration–exploitation imbalance is present at iteration \(t\) relative to the declared reference tradeoff \(\lambda_t^\star\) when the implemented maximizers are not all reference maximizers: \[\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in X}\{E_t(x)+\lambda_tX_t(x)\}\not\subseteq\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in X}\{E_t(x)+\lambda_t^\star X_t(x)\}.\] The imbalance is exploration-heavy when \(\lambda_t>\lambda_t^\star\) and exploitation-heavy when \(\lambda_t<\lambda_t^\star\), provided larger weights monotonically favor the declared exploration component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Imbalance occurs when the implemented exploration weight selects proposals that are not optimal under the objective-aligned reference tradeoff.
knowledge_statements.title: Exploration–Exploitation Imbalance

children.title: Allocation-Failure Consequences
children.top_down_role: Search stagnation, wasted evaluations, or missed high-value regions caused by allocation defects.

knowledge_statements.title: Allocation-Failure Consequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simple-regret consequence of permanently excluding a neighborhood of a unique optimum, accounting for all earlier evaluated points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Permanent exclusion of a neighborhood of the unique optimum imposes a simple-regret floor determined jointly by the excluded-region gap and the finitely many earlier evaluations. Define \(\Delta_U:=\inf_{x\in X\setminus U}f(x)-f(x^\star)\) and \(m_0:=\min_{1\le t<t_0}\bigl(f(x_t)-f(x^\star)\bigr)\), with \(m_0:=+\infty\) when \(t_0=1\). Then \[\liminf_{T\to\infty}\bigl(f(\hat x_T)-f(x^\star)\bigr)\ge \min\{\Delta_U,m_0\}>0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If sampling permanently excludes a neighborhood of the unique optimum and no earlier evaluation found that optimum, evaluated-point recommendations retain a positive simple-regret floor determined by the excluded region and the earlier evaluations.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is compact, \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuous, and \(x^\star\) is its unique minimizer.
\(U\) is a neighborhood of \(x^\star\), and there is an integer \(t_0\ge1\) such that \(x_t\notin U\) for every \(t\ge t_0\).
For every \(1\le t<t_0\), \(x_t\ne x^\star\).
For every \(T\ge1\), the recommendation satisfies \(\hat x_T\in\{x_1,\ldots,x_T\}\).

notation.meaning: Recommended evaluated design after T evaluations
Objective gap outside the excluded neighborhood
Smallest objective gap among evaluations preceding permanent exclusion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Persistent Off-Target Allocation Forces Nonvanishing Average Regret
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Average- and cumulative-regret consequence of a nonvanishing fraction of evaluations outside a fixed near-optimal set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_t=f(x_t)-f(x^\star)\ge0\), let \(X_\varepsilon=\{x:f(x)\le f(x^\star)+\varepsilon\}\), and define \(\rho:=\limsup_{T\to\infty}T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbf 1\{x_t\notin X_\varepsilon\}\). If \(\rho>0\), then \[\limsup_{T\to\infty}\frac1T\sum_{t=1}^T r_t\ge\varepsilon\rho>0.\] Hence cumulative regret cannot satisfy \(\sum_{t=1}^T r_t=o(T)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive upper-limiting fraction of evaluations more than epsilon from optimality forces nonvanishing average regret and rules out sublinear cumulative regret.

children.title: Utility–Objective Mismatch

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Policy-level definition covering terminal, cumulative, cost, and risk objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Utility–objective mismatch is the condition that maximizing the implemented one-step acquisition utilities induces a policy \(\pi_a\) that is suboptimal for the declared policy-level objective \(J\): \[J(\pi_a)<\sup_{\pi\in\Pi}J(\pi).\] Equivalently, when an optimizer \(\pi_J\) exists, \(J(\pi_a)<J(\pi_J)\). The definition requires \(J\) to include the intended horizon, evaluation costs, cumulative rewards or losses, and risk functional; disagreement between one-step rankings alone is insufficient unless it changes the induced policy or its objective value.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Myopic Utility Can Be Terminally Suboptimal

Immediate-utility maximization selects \(A\), while the declared two-stage objective gives \(J(B)=2>1=J(A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-step acquisition can reject information gathering that has greater terminal value.
assumptions_latex: The implemented acquisition ranks actions only by immediate utility.
The declared objective includes the stated terminal benefit.

children.title: Flat Acquisition Landscapes

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global acquisition flatness relative to a declared positive acquisition-value scale and numerical tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s_t>0\) be a declared acquisition-value scale and \(\tau_{\mathrm{flat}}\ge0\) a dimensionless resolution. The landscape is globally \((s_t,\tau_{\mathrm{flat}})\)-flat when \[\operatorname{osc}_X(a_t):=\sup_{x,y\in X}|a_t(x)-a_t(y)|\le \tau_{\mathrm{flat}}s_t.\] Equivalently, every \(x\in X\) satisfies \(\sup_{z\in X}a_t(z)-a_t(x)\le\tau_{\mathrm{flat}}s_t\), so acquisition values alone cannot distinguish proposals beyond that declared resolution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An acquisition is numerically flat when its full value range is no larger than a declared scale-adjusted resolution; equivalently, every design is a near-maximizer at that resolution.

\(a_t:X\to\mathbb R\) is bounded.
\(s_t>0\) is a declared acquisition-value scale.
\(\tau_{\mathrm{flat}}\ge0\) is a declared dimensionless resolution.

knowledge_statements.title: Tied Acquisition Maxima
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and tolerance-based ties among global acquisition maximizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The acquisition has tied global maxima when \[M_t:=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in X}a_t(x)\quad\text{satisfies}\quad |M_t|\ge2.\] At value tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), define \(M_t^\varepsilon:=\{x\in X:\sup_{z\in X}a_t(z)-a_t(x)\le\varepsilon\}\). A spatially resolved numerical tie occurs when there are \(x,y\in M_t^\varepsilon\) satisfying \(d(x,y)\ge\delta\), where \(\delta>0\) is the declared separation tolerance. Any unique proposal in either case depends on a tie-breaking rule beyond acquisition value alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Acquisition maxima are tied when at least two distinct designs attain the global value; a numerical tie uses declared value and spatial-separation tolerances.
assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a compact metric space and \(a_t:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is upper semicontinuous.
\(M_t=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in X}a_t(x)\).
For the numerical criterion, \(\varepsilon\ge0\) is a value tolerance and \(\delta>0\) is a separation tolerance.

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary-Attracted Acquisitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric diagnostic; boundary attraction is not intrinsically an objective-performance failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_\delta:=\{x\in X:\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial X)\le\delta\}\). The acquisition is \(\delta\)-boundary-attracted when every global acquisition maximizer lies in this closed boundary layer: \[\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in X}a_t(x)\subseteq B_\delta.\] This geometric condition alone does not imply poor objective performance; such a conclusion requires an additional objective-relative allocation criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An acquisition is boundary-attracted when all of its global maximizers lie within a declared boundary layer; this geometry alone does not establish poor objective performance.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) is compact with nonempty interior and boundary \(\partial X\).
\(a_t:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is upper semicontinuous.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Proposal instability is failure of uniform continuity of the tie-broken proposal map \(P\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vanishing Perturbation with Fixed Proposal Jump
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal example realizing discontinuity of the acquisition proposal map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=[-1,1]\), let \(a(x;\theta)=\theta x\). For every \(\eta>0\), set \(\theta_+=\eta/2\) and \(\theta_-=-\eta/2\). Then \(|\theta_+-\theta_-|=\eta\), while the unique maximizers are \(P(\theta_+)=1\) and \(P(\theta_-)=-1\). Hence proposal separation remains \(2\) as the state perturbation tends to zero.

For \(\varepsilon>0\), suppose \(C_\varepsilon:=\{x\in X:d(x,x^\star)\ge\varepsilon\}\) is nonempty and define \(\gamma_\varepsilon:=a(x^\star)-\sup_{x\in C_\varepsilon}a(x)\). If \(\gamma_\varepsilon>0\) and \(\|b-a\|_\infty<\gamma_\varepsilon/2\), then every maximizer of \(b\) lies in \(B_\varepsilon(x^\star)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive value margin around a unique maximizer prevents uniformly small acquisition perturbations from moving proposals outside the corresponding neighborhood.

knowledge_statements.title: Inner-Solver Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-gap failure criterion for a maximization-type inner problem with a feasible, finite returned point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For outer proposal \(x\), inner-solver failure at tolerance \(\tau_{\mathrm{in}}\) occurs when the returned feasible point has an inner optimality gap exceeding the accepted tolerance: \[g_t(x,z_t^\star(x))-g_t(x,\hat z_t(x))>\tau_{\mathrm{in}}.\] This criterion isolates inner optimization error while treating the inner objective as exactly evaluable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a feasible and valid returned point, the inner solver fails the value-gap criterion when its exact inner-objective gap exceeds the accepted tolerance.
assumptions_latex: For each outer proposal \(x\in X\), \(Z(x)\) is a nonempty feasible inner domain.
\(g_t(x,\cdot):Z(x)\to\mathbb{R}\) attains its maximum at some \(z_t^\star(x)\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{z\in Z(x)}g_t(x,z)\).

children.title: Nested-Estimation Failure
children.top_down_role: Instability or bias in sampling-based acquisition estimates.

knowledge_statements.title: Nested-Estimation Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probabilistic uniform-error criterion for Monte Carlo or other nested acquisition estimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Nested-estimation failure at effort \(m\), tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{est}}>0\), and level \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) occurs when \[\mathbb{P}\!\left(\sup_{x\in X}|\hat a_{t,m}(x)-a_t(x)|>\varepsilon_{\mathrm{est}}\right)>\alpha.\] Alternative error criteria require separately declared assumptions that provide simultaneous control over every acquisition value used by the acquisition optimizer. This condition concerns estimation of the acquisition itself and excludes additional optimization error incurred when maximizing \(\hat a_{t,m}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested estimation fails when the uniform acquisition-estimation error exceeds its declared tolerance with probability greater than the accepted failure level.
assumptions_latex: \(a_t:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is the exact acquisition and \(\hat a_{t,m}:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is a random estimator using effort \(m\).
\(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{est}}>0\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) are declared accuracy and failure levels.
Estimator randomness is represented by probability \(\mathbb{P}\), and the displayed supremum is measurable.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Accuracy Does Not Ensure Uniform Acquisition Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary showing why pointwise estimator control is insufficient for adaptive maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[0,1]\), \(a_m(x)=0\), \(U_m\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\), and \(\hat a_m(x)=\mathbf 1\{|x-U_m|\le m^{-2}\}\). For every fixed \(x\), \(\hat a_m(x)\to0\) in probability, whereas \(\sup_{x\in X}|\hat a_m(x)-a_m(x)|=1\) almost surely for every \(m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Random unit-height spikes can vanish at every fixed candidate while preventing any uniform acquisition accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(U_m\) is uniform on \([0,1]\).
The optimizer may respond to the realized estimated acquisition.

knowledge_statements.title: Missed Acquisition Optima
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer value-gap definition measured against the exact acquisition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A computed proposal \(\hat x_t\) misses the acquisition optimum at tolerance \(\eta\ge0\) when its exact acquisition-value gap satisfies \[\sup_{x\in X}a_t(x)-a_t(\hat x_t)>\eta.\] The condition is independent of whether the miss arose from local convergence, insufficient restarts, inner-solver error, or stochastic acquisition estimation. When \(\eta=0\), every nonmaximizing proposal satisfies the condition; numerical assessment generally uses a positive tolerance scaled to the acquisition's units.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An acquisition optimum is missed when the returned proposal's exact acquisition value lies more than the accepted tolerance below the global maximum.

children.title: Numerical-Failure Attribution
children.top_down_role: Separation of solver error from acquisition-estimation error.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical-Failure Attribution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive certificate bounding acquisition-estimation and computed-acquisition optimization contributions without claiming unique causal attribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the uniform estimation error \(e_t:=\|a_t-\hat a_t\|_\infty\) and the computed-acquisition optimization gap \(o_t:=\hat a_t(\tilde x_t)-\hat a_t(\hat x_t)\). The exact acquisition loss of the returned proposal satisfies \[a_t(x_t^\star)-a_t(\hat x_t)\le 2e_t+o_t.\] Consequently, certified bounds \(e_t\le\bar e_t\) and \(o_t\le\bar o_t\) certify total acquisition loss at most \(2\bar e_t+\bar o_t\). This additive bound does not by itself uniquely identify which numerical mechanism caused an observed loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform acquisition-estimation and computed-acquisition optimization bounds give an additive certificate for total proposal loss, but they do not uniquely determine its cause.
assumptions_latex: \(a_t:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is the exact acquisition, \(\hat a_t:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is its computed approximation, and \(\|a_t-\hat a_t\|_\infty<\infty\).
\(x_t^\star\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in X}a_t(x)\) and \(\tilde x_t\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in X}\hat a_t(x)\).
The computation returns \(\hat x_t\in X\), and all displayed acquisition values are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_t(x_t^\star)-a_t(\hat x_t)\le 2\|a_t-\hat a_t\|_\infty+\hat a_t(\tilde x_t)-\hat a_t(\hat x_t)\).

Thus \(o_t>0\) certifies an optimization contribution, while \(o_t=0\) does not exclude acquisition-estimation error.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Wall-clock boundary where Bayesian-optimization overhead offsets its reduction in objective evaluations.

source_refs.source_title: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a performance target and two procedures: Bayesian optimization and direct search. Let \(c_f>0\) be the cost of one objective evaluation, let \(n_{\mathrm{BO}}\) and \(n_{\mathrm{D}}\) be the respective numbers of evaluations required to attain the target, and let \(H_{\mathrm{BO}}\ge 0\) be the total surrogate-fitting and acquisition-optimization overhead incurred by Bayesian optimization before attaining it. Bayesian optimization has no wall-clock advantage when \[n_{\mathrm{BO}}c_f+H_{\mathrm{BO}}\ge n_{\mathrm{D}}c_f.\] Equivalently, the cheap-objective mismatch boundary is \[n_{\mathrm{D}}-n_{\mathrm{BO}}\le \frac{H_{\mathrm{BO}}}{c_f},\] so the evaluation saving does not exceed the evaluation-equivalent overhead.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed performance target, Bayesian optimization is in the cheap-objective mismatch regime when the evaluations it saves do not compensate for its surrogate and acquisition overhead.
knowledge_statements.title: Cheap-Objective Regime

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalizes the seed's common-cost, zero-comparator-overhead accounting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the total target-attainment costs be \(C_{\mathrm{BO}}=\sum_{i=1}^{n_{\mathrm{BO}}}c_{\mathrm{BO},i}+H_{\mathrm{BO}}\) and \(C_{\mathrm D}=\sum_{j=1}^{n_{\mathrm D}}c_{\mathrm D,j}+H_{\mathrm D}\). Bayesian optimization has no wall-clock advantage precisely when \(C_{\mathrm{BO}}\ge C_{\mathrm D}\). The seed criterion follows when all evaluation costs equal \(c_f\) and \(H_{\mathrm D}=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With heterogeneous evaluation costs or comparator overhead, compare complete target-attainment costs; the seed inequality is a specialization.
assumptions_latex: The performance target, procedures, and cost boundary are fixed.
All evaluation and overhead costs use common units.
Costs are compared consistently pathwise or in expectation.

children.title: Extreme Dimension without Exploitable Structure
children.top_down_role: Search spaces too large for standard global surrogate learning.

knowledge_statements.title: Extreme Dimension without Exploitable Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case Lipschitz-search boundary for globally unstructured high-dimensional domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[0,1]^d\), let \(F_L\) be the class of real-valued \(L\)-Lipschitz functions on \(X\), and require the recommendation after \(n\) evaluations to be an evaluated point. For any deterministic sequential method, consider the locations \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) generated by zero observations and their fill distance \(h_n=\sup_{x\in X}\min_i\lVert x-x_i\rVert_2\). The member \(f(x)=-L\min_i\lVert x-x_i\rVert_2\) of \(F_L\) produces those observations and gives simple regret \(Lh_n\). Since \(n\) Euclidean balls of radius \(h_n\) cover \(X\), \[Lh_n\ge L(nv_d)^{-1/d},\] where \(v_d\) is the unit-ball volume. Thus evaluation requirements grow exponentially in \(d\) at fixed accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without lower-dimensional or additive structure, worst-case Lipschitz optimization needs exponentially many evaluations in dimension to guarantee fixed simple regret.
assumptions_latex: \(d\ge 1\), \(L>0\), and observations are exact.
The final recommendation is one of the evaluated points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Worst-case simple regret is at least \(L(nv_d)^{-1/d}\).

notation.meaning: Class of L-Lipschitz objectives on the unit cube.
Fill distance of the evaluated design.
Volume of the Euclidean unit ball in dimension d.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical information-based Lipschitz global-optimization bound

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind and deterministic exact-observation scope fit the container, and the stated worst-case dimensional dependence is mathematically plausible. No citation is supplied for the exact covering-based Lipschitz lower bound, so this record requires an authoritative theorem or section locator before candidate-review acceptance.

children.top_down_role: Settings where the objective changes materially during the evaluation sequence.

children.title: Objective Drift
children.top_down_role: Temporal changes in the response or decision criterion during optimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Drift
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Time-indexed drift of the latent response surface, distinct from observation noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a decision domain and let \(f_t:X\to\mathbb R\) denote the latent conditional-mean objective at evaluation time \(t\), so that \(Y_t=f_t(X_t)+\varepsilon_t\) with \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_t\mid X_t,t]=0\). Objective drift occurs on an interval \(T\) when the family \(\{f_t:t\in T\}\) is not constant: there exist \(s,t\in T\) and \(x\in X\) such that \(f_s(x)\ne f_t(x)\). Its uniform magnitude between two times is \[\Delta(s,t)=\sup_{x\in X}|f_t(x)-f_s(x)|.\] This definition attributes systematic temporal change to the objective rather than to zero-mean evaluation noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective drift means that the latent conditional-mean response at a fixed decision changes with evaluation time.
assumptions_latex: The conditional mean \(f_t(x)=\mathbb E[Y_t\mid X_t=x,t]\) exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Objective drift is present exactly when \(\Delta(s,t)>0\) for some \(s,t\).

notation.meaning: Latent objective surface at time t.
Uniform drift magnitude between times s and t.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cumulative uniform-magnitude representation of objective drift over a finite horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f_1,\ldots,f_T:X\to\mathbb R\), define \[V_T=\sum_{t=2}^{T}\lVert f_t-f_{t-1}\rVert_\infty.\] Then \(V_T=0\) if and only if \(f_1=\cdots=f_T\), and for \(1\le s<t\le T\), \[\lVert f_t-f_s\rVert_\infty\le\sum_{u=s+1}^{t}\lVert f_u-f_{u-1}\rVert_\infty\le V_T.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A temporal variation budget sums consecutive uniform changes and bounds drift between any two times.
assumptions_latex: \(T<\infty\).
Each consecutive uniform difference is finite.

notation.meaning: Cumulative uniform temporal variation through time T.
Supremum norm over the decision domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Temporal Variation Budget

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abrupt-change representation of a finite sequence of objective surfaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f_1,\ldots,f_T:X\to\mathbb R\), define \[S_T=\sum_{t=2}^{T}\mathbf 1\{f_t\ne f_{t-1}\}.\] The sequence has exactly \(S_T+1\) maximal consecutive intervals on which the objective is constant. Equivalently, a representation by \(K\) consecutive constant regimes has \(S_T\le K-1\), with equality when the representation is maximal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The change count measures abrupt objective drift and equals one less than the number of maximal stationary regimes.
assumptions_latex: \(T<\infty\).
Equality of objectives is pointwise on \(X\).

notation.meaning: Number of consecutive-time changes in the objective surface.

knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise-Stationary Change Count

children.title: Nonstationary Experimental Conditions
children.top_down_role: Changes in equipment, environment, protocols, or operating conditions across evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonstationary Experimental Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition identifying time-varying contextual distributions or context-dependent response laws.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_t\) collect experimental conditions not chosen as components of the decision \(X_t\), and suppose \(Y_t=g(X_t,C_t)+\varepsilon_t\) with conditionally zero-mean \(\varepsilon_t\). Experimental conditions are nonstationary over times \(T\) if either their conditional law changes, \(\mathcal L(C_t\mid X_t=x)\ne\mathcal L(C_s\mid X_s=x)\), or the response law itself depends on time, \(\mathcal L(Y_t\mid X_t=x,C_t=c)\ne\mathcal L(Y_s\mid X_s=x,C_s=c)\), for some admissible \(s,t,x,c\). Consequently, the marginalized objective \[f_t(x)=\int g(x,c)\,dP_t(c\mid x)\] may vary even when \(g\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Experimental conditions are nonstationary when latent context distributions or context-conditioned response laws change over time, potentially changing the marginalized objective.
assumptions_latex: The indicated regular conditional distributions and integral exist.
\(C_t\) is not fully encoded in the surrogate input.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Changing \(P_t(c\mid x)\) can induce a time-dependent marginalized objective \(f_t(x)\).

children.title: Drift-Induced Observation Obsolescence
children.top_down_role: Loss of relevance of earlier observations under evolving objectives or conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: Drift-Induced Observation Obsolescence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies the bias incurred when historical observations are treated as current data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(Y_s=f_s(X_s)+\varepsilon_s\), where \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_s\mid X_s,s]=0\), but a surrogate fitted at time \(t\) treats \(Y_s\) as an observation of \(f_t(X_s)\). The resulting conditional target error is \[\mathbb E[Y_s-f_t(X_s)\mid X_s,s]=f_s(X_s)-f_t(X_s).\] Hence its magnitude is bounded above by \(\Delta(s,t)=\sup_x|f_s(x)-f_t(x)|\). If the drift satisfies \(|f_s(x)-f_t(x)|\le L_t|t-s|\), then the bias of an observation of age \(a=t-s\) is at most \(L_ta\). An observation is \(\eta\)-obsolete when its drift bias exceeds the prescribed tolerance \(\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A historical observation becomes obsolete when temporal drift makes its bias relative to the current objective exceed the modeling tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Observation noise is conditionally zero-mean.
Historical data are reused without explicitly conditioning the surrogate on time.

notation.meaning: Uniform drift between observation and current times.
Temporal Lipschitz bound for the objective.

children.title: Drift Detectability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where sparse or noisy evaluations obscure temporal change.

knowledge_statements.title: Drift Detectability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-theoretic boundary for detecting drift from finitely many noisy observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_0^{(n)}\) be the joint law of \(n\) observations under no drift and \(P_1^{(n)}\) their law under a specified drifting alternative. For every measurable drift test \(\phi\in\{0,1\}\), its type-I and type-II errors satisfy \[P_0^{(n)}(\phi=1)+P_1^{(n)}(\phi=0)\ge 1-\operatorname{TV}\!\left(P_0^{(n)},P_1^{(n)}\right).\] Therefore drift cannot be detected reliably when the two induced observation laws have small total-variation distance. In particular, if their distance is at most \(\delta<1\), no test can make both error probabilities smaller than \((1-\delta)/2\). Drift outside sampled locations is likewise undetectable when it leaves the joint observation law unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Drift is statistically undetectable when drifting and stationary models induce nearly identical distributions for the available observations.
assumptions_latex: Both hypotheses define probability laws on the same observation space.
Detection uses only the \(n\) recorded observations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\operatorname{TV}(P_0^{(n)},P_1^{(n)})\le\delta\), then at least one testing error is at least \((1-\delta)/2\).

notation.meaning: Joint observation law under no drift.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: binary testing bound in total variation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind is appropriate, and the total-variation testing statement is precise and internally consistent. Because no source reference is supplied for the exact binary-testing inequality, an authoritative theorem, proposition, or textbook-section locator is required.

children.title: Evaluation Confounding Failures
children.top_down_role: Uncontrolled variation that prevents reliable surrogate updating or comparison.

children.title: Irreproducible Evaluations
children.top_down_role: Evaluations whose outcomes cannot be reliably reproduced under nominally identical settings.

knowledge_statements.title: Irreproducible Evaluations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Replicate-level irreproducibility at a fixed nominal decision and stated protocol.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y(x,r)\) be the outcome obtained at nominal decision \(x\) under replicate identifier or random seed \(r\), with the declared experimental protocol otherwise fixed. Evaluations are reproducible at \(x\) if there exists a stated tolerance \(\eta\ge0\) such that \[\Pr\bigl(|Y(x,R)-Y(x,R')|\le\eta\bigr)\ge1-\alpha\] for independent protocol-compliant replicates \(R,R'\), where \(\alpha\) is the accepted failure probability. They are irreproducible at \((\eta,\alpha)\) when this inequality fails. If no replicate mechanism or protocol is recorded, reproducibility at that tolerance is not empirically verifiable from single evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluations are irreproducible when independent protocol-compliant repeats at the same nominal decision disagree beyond the accepted tolerance too often.
assumptions_latex: Replicate outcomes use the same declared protocol and nominal decision.
\(R\) and \(R'\) are independent draws from the intended replication mechanism.

notation.meaning: Outcome at decision x under replicate r.

review_flags: tolerance and failure probability are protocol dependent

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided exact binomial certificate for the seed's exceedance-probability criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\) independent protocol-compliant replicate pairs, let \(K=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{|Y_i-Y_i'|>\eta\}\) and \(p=\Pr(|Y-Y'|>\eta)\). For confidence error \(\beta\in(0,1)\), the one-sided Clopper–Pearson lower bound is \(L_\beta=0\) if \(K=0\), and \[L_\beta=F_{\mathrm{Beta}(K,n-K+1)}^{-1}(\beta)\] if \(K>0\). When \(L_\beta>\alpha\), the data certify \(p>\alpha\) with coverage at least \(1-\beta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent replicate pairs can certify irreproducibility when an exact one-sided lower confidence bound for the excessive-discrepancy probability exceeds the accepted rate.
assumptions_latex: The \(n\) replicate pairs are independent and identically distributed under the fixed decision and protocol.
Pair exceedance indicators are Bernoulli with common probability \(p\).
\(\alpha\) is the accepted exceedance probability and \(\beta\) is the confidence error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_\beta>\alpha\Rightarrow p>\alpha\ \text{is certified with confidence at least }1-\beta.

notation.meaning: Number of replicate-pair discrepancies exceeding tolerance
Exact one-sided lower confidence bound for the exceedance probability

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Replication Irreproducibility Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates nonzero randomness from failure of a declared reproducibility tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let independent replicates satisfy \(Y(x,R)\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,\eta/2]\) for \(\eta>0\). Although \(\operatorname{Var}(Y)>0\), \(|Y(x,R)-Y(x,R')|\le\eta/2<\eta\) almost surely, so the evaluation is reproducible at tolerance \(\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random evaluation can remain reproducible when every replicate discrepancy lies within tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Replicates are independent draws from \(\operatorname{Unif}[0,\eta/2]\).
\(\eta>0\) is the declared discrepancy tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Stochasticity Does Not Imply Irreproducibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-moment representation for independent identically distributed replicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Y\) and \(Y'\) are independent protocol-compliant replicates with common finite variance \(\sigma_x^2\), then \[\mathbb E[(Y-Y')^2]=2\sigma_x^2.\] This summary is not equivalent to the seed's tail-probability criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected squared replicate disagreement equals twice within-protocol variance, but variance alone does not determine tolerance-based reproducibility.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\) and \(Y'\) are independent and identically distributed under the same decision and protocol.
\(\operatorname{Var}(Y)=\sigma_x^2<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.title: Mean-Square Replicate Discrepancy

children.title: Confounded Evaluations
children.top_down_role: Evaluations mixed with uncontrolled factors that distort design comparisons.

knowledge_statements.title: Confounded Evaluations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision effects are confounded when uncontrolled context differs systematically with the chosen decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be the chosen decision, \(U\) an unrecorded experimental condition, and \(Y=g(X,U)+\varepsilon\) with \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon\mid X,U]=0\). Evaluations of decision effects are confounded when \(U\) affects the response and its distribution depends on the decision: there exist \(x,x',u,u'\) such that \(g(x,u)\ne g(x,u')\) and \(P(U\mid X=x)\ne P(U\mid X=x')\). The observed regression target is then \[m(x)=\mathbb E[Y\mid X=x]=\int g(x,u)\,dP(u\mid x),\] which combines the effect of changing \(x\) with the effect of changing the distribution of \(U\). Thus comparisons of \(m(x)\) need not identify controlled decision effects.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluations are confounded when response-relevant hidden conditions vary systematically with the selected decision, mixing decision and context effects.
assumptions_latex: The displayed conditional expectation and regular conditional law exist.
The condition \(U\) is neither controlled nor included in the surrogate input.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The observable target \(m(x)\) generally differs from a controlled-context response comparison.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Observed Regression Does Not Identify Controlled Effects Under Confounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructive observational non-identifiability example.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X,U\in\{0,1\}\), \(U=X\) almost surely, and omit observation noise. Under \(g_1(x,u)=x\) and \(g_2(x,u)=u\), both models produce \(Y=X\) and \(m(x)=x\). At controlled context \(u=0\), however, \(g_1(1,0)-g_1(0,0)=1\) while \(g_2(1,0)-g_2(0,0)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identical confounded observations can arise from mechanisms with different controlled decision effects.
assumptions_latex: Only observations of \((X,Y)\) are available.
The latent context satisfies \(U=X\) in the observational data.
knowledge_statements.title: Observed Regression Does Not Identify Controlled Effects Under Confounding

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient design condition eliminating the association component of confounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If assignment is randomized independently of the pre-assignment latent context, \(X\perp U\), then \(P(U\mid X=x)=P(U)\) for every supported \(x\), and \[\mathbb E[Y\mid X=x]=\int g(x,u)\,dP(u).\] This removes decision-dependent context mixing but does not identify context-specific responses without further information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent random assignment makes every decision average over the same context distribution.
assumptions_latex: \(Y=g(X,U)+\varepsilon\) with \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon\mid X,U]=0\).
\(U\) is pre-assignment and \(X\perp U\).
Compared decisions have positive assignment probability or density.

notation.meaning: Independence of assignment and latent context

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Assignment Removes Decision–Context Association

children.title: Uncontrolled Experimental Variation
children.top_down_role: Latent operational or environmental variation affecting observed outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Uncontrolled Experimental Variation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Latent experimental variation that remains after conditioning on the recorded Bayesian-optimization inputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) denote recorded decision variables, \(U\) unrecorded experimental conditions, and \(Y=g(X,U)+\varepsilon\), where \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon\mid X,U]=0\). Uncontrolled experimental variation is present at \(x\) when \[\operatorname{Var}\!\left(g(x,U)\mid X=x\right)>0.\] By conditional variance decomposition, \[\operatorname{Var}(Y\mid X=x)=\operatorname{Var}(g(x,U)\mid X=x)+\mathbb E[\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon\mid X,U)\mid X=x].\] Consequently, fitting a surrogate only on \(X\) merges context variation with intrinsic observation noise. If the law of \(U\mid X=x\) changes across evaluations, this merged residual need not be identically distributed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uncontrolled variation exists when unrecorded conditions change the response after conditioning on all recorded optimization inputs.
assumptions_latex: All displayed conditional second moments are finite.
\(U\) is omitted from the recorded surrogate inputs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uncontrolled context contributes the variance term \(\operatorname{Var}(g(x,U)\mid X=x)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Observational nonidentifiability of omitted-context variation and intrinsic noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the recorded input be constant and let \(Y\sim N(0,1)\). The same observation law arises from \(Y=U\), where \(U\sim N(0,1)\) and \(\varepsilon=0\), and from \(Y=\varepsilon\), where \(g(U)=0\) and \(\varepsilon\sim N(0,1)\). The omitted-context variance is respectively one and zero. Hence \(\mathcal L(Y\mid X)\) alone does not identify \(\operatorname{Var}(g(X,U)\mid X)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identical recorded input-response laws can arise entirely from hidden experimental variation or entirely from intrinsic noise.
assumptions_latex: Only the joint law of recorded inputs and responses is observed.
No context measurement, intervention, or independently justified noise model distinguishes the decompositions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal L(Y\mid X)\text{ does not identify }\operatorname{Var}(g(X,U)\mid X).

notation.meaning: Response contribution from recorded and unrecorded conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: Latent-Variation–Noise Nonidentifiability

children.title: Surrogate-Update Failure
children.top_down_role: Unreliable belief revision caused by irreproducible or confounded observations.

knowledge_statements.title: Surrogate-Update Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by updating an input-only surrogate with observations generated under omitted, varying conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose observations satisfy \(Y_i=g(X_i,U_i)+\varepsilon_i\), but the surrogate assumes \(Y_i=f(X_i)+e_i\) with \(e_i\) identically distributed and conditionally zero-mean given \(X_i\). If \(U_i\) is omitted and \(P(U_i\mid X_i=x)\) varies with \(i\), then no fixed target \(f(x)\) generally satisfies all updates because \[\mathbb E[Y_i\mid X_i=x]=\int g(x,u)\,dP_i(u\mid x)\] is iteration-dependent. Pooling such observations updates the surrogate toward a design-dependent mixture rather than a stable objective. Replication may then reduce reported posterior uncertainty around that mixture without resolving the omitted-condition bias, so acquisition values based on the posterior can become systematically misleading.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Surrogate updating fails when omitted, changing conditions make observations target different response surfaces while the model assumes one fixed objective.
assumptions_latex: The surrogate omits \(U_i\) and assumes a time-invariant conditional mean.
The context-conditioned response \(g(x,u)\) depends nontrivially on \(u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Iteration-dependent \(P_i(U_i\mid X_i=x)\) makes the pooled conditional-mean target generally nonstationary.

notation.meaning: Omitted experimental condition at iteration i.
Iteration-specific conditional law of the omitted condition.
